principal amount subject, of course, to any agreement between the parties.”
36. According to DVC, in a recent decision of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case
of Kerala State Electricity Board and another v Kurien E. Kalathil and Others, [(2018) 4
SCC 793] (KSEB Judgment), the priority of adjustment has been stated as under:
“19. As held in Constitution Bench judgment in Gurpreet Singh's case followed in
BHEL's case, if there is a direction in the decree as to the mode of appropriation
of payment, then appropriation of any payment made by the judgment-debtor has
to be strictly in accordance with the direction contained in the decree. If there is no
such direction in the decree, then the general Principle is that where a judgment-
debtor makes payment without making any indication as to how the payment is to
be adjusted, it is the option of the creditor to make adjustment firstly towards the
interest and then towards the principal. But if the judgment debtor has indicated
the manner in which the appropriation is to be made, then the creditor has no
choice to apply the payment in a different manner. The general Principal of mode
of appropriation firstly in payment of interest and thereafter in payment of principal
amount is subject to the exception i.e. the parties may agree to the adjustment of
the payment in any other manner despite the decree.”

adjusted firstly towards the principal amount and thereafter to LPSC. The Joint

through the PPA, read with the contract between the parties in the form of the Joint
Reconciliation Statement executed between them. In the present case, DVC and
Respondent have specifically agreed to the Joint Reconciliation Statement, which is itself
a contract between the parties. The Hon’ble Supreme Court, in a catena of judgments,
has held that the conduct of parties is a relevant factor in matters of the construction of

the Indian Contract Act, 2003 and not otherwise.

the manner of appropriation of payment made by BYPL, which cannot be unilaterally
altered by DVC by relying upon KSEB Judgment in its letter dated 27.3.2018 since KSEB

reconciliation statement, DVC has in fact raised the bill for Delayed Payment Surcharge
on 6.2.2017 upon BYPL, which is neither disputed nor recalled to date. Thereby, DVC
has explicitly confirmed with the mutually agreed payment mechanism followed by the
parties for 11 years from the signing of the PPA. Such conduct of DVC is in teeth of the
law laid down by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of Kanchan Udyog Judgment.
In light of the above, the expression “unless otherwise agreed by the parties” in clause
(2) of Regulation 59 of Second Amendment Regulations, 2021 applies to the mutually
agreed arrangement between the parties. Accordingly, the mutually agreed payment
mechanism will continue even after the notification of the Second Amendment
Regulations, 2021.
LPS Rules notified by the Ministry of Power (MoP)
42. As noted above, the MoP notified the LPS Rules 2021 on 22.2.2021 and the LPS
Rules 2022 on 3.6.2022. Rules 4 and 5 of the LPS Rules, 2022 are pari materia with
Rules 4 and 5 of the LPS Rules 2021. Rule 5 of LPS Rules provides that “all payments
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Order in Petition No. 319/MP/2019 Page 33 of 46

by a distribution licensee to a generating company or a trading licensee for power
procured from it or by a user of a transmission system to a transmission licensee shall be
first adjusted towards Late Payment Surcharge and thereafter, towards monthly charges,
starting from the longest overdue bill.” LPS Rules are applicable to the parties from the
date of notification, i.e., 22.2.2021 and hence, the mutually agreed methodology between
the parties ceased to operate from the notification of the Rules.
Supreme Court Orders dated 26.3.2014, 6.5.2014 and 3.7.2014 in W.P. Nos 105/2014
43. The Respondent, BYPL, has submitted that the issue of payment and alleged non-
payment owing to its inability to pay, along with related matters, is sub judice before the
Hon’ble Supreme Court in Writ Petition No. 105 of 2014 (filed by the Respondent) and
Contempt Petition No. 141 of 2014 (filed by DVC), which are tagged together. Despite
being aware that the Hon’ble Supreme Court is seized of the issue, DVC has filed the
present Petition seeking adjustment of payment towards LPSC before adjusting the
principal amount, thereby attempting to overreach the pending proceedings. The
Respondent referred to the order 26.03.2024 in W.P. (C) No. 105 of 2014 filed by BYPL
(wherein DVC is arrayed as Respondent No. 8) inter alia directing BYPL to make the
payment of current dues (i.e., with effect from 01.03.2014) which relate to the billing period
from 01.01.2014. Further, the Hon’ble Supreme Court by Order dated 3.7.2014 directed
to continue making monthly payment to the generating and transmission companies on
the basis indicated in the order dated 6.5.2014, while keeping all disputes, including
figures, open for adjudication at a later stage. BYPL has further contended that the
judgments cited by DVC pertain to appropriation of decretal amounts, which are not
applicable to the present case since the amount here arise under contractual
arrangements and not from any decree.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Order in Petition No. 319/MP/2019 Page 34 of 46

44. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and the Respondent
(BYPL). The Respondent has argued that the issue of payment and alleged non-payment
owing to inability to pay is pending adjudication before the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Writ
Petition No. 105 of 2014 and Contempt Petition No. 141 of 2014 (tagged matters), and
therefore, DVC ought not to have filed the present Petition. It has been further contended
that DVC is seeking to overreach the pending proceedings and that the inability to pay
arose on account of a non-cost-reflective tariff determined by the DERC. In this regard,
we are of the view that the pendency of the aforesaid Writ Petition and Contempt Petition
before the Hon’ble Supreme Court does not operate as a bar to the consideration of the
present Petition. The Hon’ble Supreme Court, by its orders dated 26.3.2014, 6.5.2014
and 3.7.2014, directed the Respondent to continue to make recurring monthly payment
to the generating and transmission companies in accordance with the basis indicated
therein and kept all disputes, including those relating to figures, open for determination at
a later stage. Although Writ Petition No. 105 of 2014 was disposed of vide Judgment
dated 06.08.2025, Contempt Petition No. 141 of 2014 is still pending before the Hon’ble
Supreme Court. Further, the Interim Order dated 26.3.2014 passed by the Hon’ble
Supreme Court is still subsisting due to the pendency of C.A. Nos. 4011 and 4012 of 2014
before the Hon’ble Supreme Court.
45. It emerges from above that the Original Methodology followed between the parties
was consistent with the aforementioned Orders passed by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in
W.P. (C) No. 105 of 2014 and connected matters.
46. Further, the Respondent’s plea that its inability to pay the dues to DVC at the
relevant time has been on account of the determination of a non-cost reflective tariff by
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Order in Petition No. 319/MP/2019 Page 35 of 46

49. It is observed that, at the time of signing of the Joint Reconciliation Statement
signed on 11.1.2017 and issuance of Bill dated 06.2.2017, DVC was aware of the law laid
down by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of Gurpreet Singh Judgment and Orders
passed by Hon’ble Supreme Court in W.P. (C) No. 105 of 2014. It is an established
principle of law that ignorance of the law is no excuse. Therefore, having followed the
Original Methodology for appropriation of payment by BYPL for almost 11 years and
acting upon it by raising bills on 06.02.2017, DVC in 2018 cannot unilaterally seek to
change the appropriation methodology by relying on the KSEB Judgment passed on
09.03.2018, which had only reiterated the law already laid down by the Constitution Bench
in the Gurpreet Singh Judgment in 2006.
50. The Commission observes that the issue raised in the present Petition pertains to
the appropriation of payments received from the Respondent towards principal dues and
LPSC. The judgments relied upon by DVC, though relating to decretal amounts,
enunciate the general principle of appropriation as recognised under Section 60 of the
Indian Contract Act, 1872- that, in the absence of a specific instruction from the debtor,
the creditor is entitled to appropriate the payment first towards the interest (or surcharge)
and thereafter towards the principal dues. The said principle, being of general application
in case of a decretal amount, is not applicable in the present regulatory and contractual
context.
Prerogative to indicate the payment adjustment mechanism
51. The next ground of challenge is that in terms of Sections 59 and 60 of the Indian
Contract Act, BYPL have the prerogative to indicate the payment adjustment mechanism
and DVC has acted contrary to its instructions by not providing for adjustment against
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Order in Petition No. 319/MP/2019 Page 37 of 46

current bills first for the payment made after 1.1.2017. Sections 59 and 60 are extracted
as under:
“59. Application of payment where debt to be discharged is indicated- Where a
debtor, owing several distinct debts to one person, makes a payment to him, either
with express intimation, or under circumstances implying, that the payment is to
be applied to the discharge of some particular debt, the payment, if accepted, must
be applied accordingly.
60. Application of payment where debt to be discharged is not indicated. - Where
the debtor has omitted to intimate and there are no other circumstances indicating
to which debt the payment is to be applied, the creditor may apply it at his
discretion to any lawful debt actually due and payable to him from the debtor,
whether its recovery is or is not barred by the law in force for the time being as to
the limitation of suits.”
52. As per Section 59, if a debtor owning several distinct debts to one person makes
a payment to him with the intimation that the payment is to be applied to the discharge of
some particular debt, the payment must be applied accordingly. BYPL has argued that it
clearly indicated to DVC that the amount paid by it was to be adjusted towards the
principal amount first, as this was specifically stated in the payment made. Further, DVC
on 06.2.2017 had raised a Bill for ‘Delayed Payment Surcharge’ in terms of the Joint
Reconciliation Statement dated 11.01.2017, thereby acknowledging that Energy dues
(principal) and LPSC dues (interest) are separate and distinct obligations.
53. The Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of Industrial Credit & Development
Syndicate v. Smithaben H. Patel, [(1999) 3 SCC 80 (Para 14)] inter alia held that “general
rule of appropriation of payments towards a decretal amount is that such an amount is to
be adjusted firstly, strictly in accordance with the directions contained in the decree and
in the absence of such direction, adjustments be made firstly in payment of interest and
costs and thereafter in payment of the principal amount. Such a principle is, however,
subject to one exception, i.e., that the parties may agree to the adjustment of the payment
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Order in Petition No. 319/MP/2019 Page 38 of 46

in any other manner despite the decree. As and when such an agreement is pleaded, the
onus of proving is always upon the person pleading the agreement contrary to the general
rule or the terms of the decree schedule. The provisions of Sections 59 to 61 of the
Contract Act are applicable in cases where a debtor owes several distinct debts to one
person and do not deal with cases in which the principal and interest are due on a single
debt.”.
54. Accordingly, it emerges from the above that Section 59 of the Indian Contract Act
is applicable in the present case, and DVC is bound to abide by the instructions of BYPL
in the matter of appropriation of the payment towards principal dues first.
Doctrine of Past Practice & Unilateral Change in the methodology of adjustment of
dues
55. We have considered the submissions of the parties regarding the petition being
barred by the contract between the parties themselves, as well as the Doctrine of Past
Practice. In this regard, BYPL has contended that, in terms of the Joint Reconciliation
Statement dated 11.1.2017, all payments were to be adjusted first towards the principal
and thereafter towards LPSC, and that this understanding constitutes a binding contract.
BYPL has further argued that DVC cannot alter the agreed methodology of adjustment
unilaterally and that any such change would amount to novation of the contract, requiring
mutual consent under Section 62 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.
56. Per contra, DVC has inter alia contended that DVC is merely exercising its lawful
right of appropriation consistent with the settled legal principle recognised by the Hon’ble
Supreme Court in the KSEB Judgment.
57. We have considered the parties' submissions. In this regard, we are of the view
that the Original Methodology was mutually agreed upon and followed by both DVC and
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Order in Petition No. 319/MP/2019 Page 39 of 46

BYPL. This is evident from the Joint Reconciliation Statement dated 11.1.2017, as well
as the DVC’s Bill dated 06.2.2017 issued to BYPL for the Delayed Payment Surcharge.
Further, as noted above, the KSEB Judgment does not lay down any new law, and the
Hon’ble Supreme Court has merely followed and reiterated the findings of the Constitution
Bench in the Gurpreet Singh Judgment. As such, both parties have mutually signed the
Joint Reconciliation Statement on 11.1.2017, being aware of the law laid down by the
Hon’ble Supreme Court in Gurpreet Singh Judgment as well as the Orders passed by the
Hon’ble Supreme Court in W.P. (C) No. 105 of 2014. Accordingly, in 2018, DVC cannot
unilaterally change the payment appropriation methodology for adjusting payments
towards outstanding LPSC first with effect from February 2017.
58. Any change in the Original Methodology, as evident from the said Joint
Reconciliation Statement, would amount to novation of the contract as per Section 62 of
the Contract Act, wherein mutual agreement of parties is sine qua non. From the facts of
the present case, it is evident from BYPL’s communications dated 08.04.2018 and
21.6.2018 that BYPL did not agree to the change in payment appropriation methodology
proposed by DVC in terms of the KSEB Judgment. In fact, by letter dated 21.06.2018,
BYPL has categorically stated that the payment made by BYPL must be first adjusted
against current dues and thereafter against LPSC.
59. Accordingly, the Original Methodology followed by the parties for appropriation of
payment cannot be altered by DVC’s letter dated 27.3.2018. However, the mutually
agreed past practice between the parties of adjusting the payment by BYPL first towards
principal dues and thereafter towards LPSC can continue only until the notification of the
LPS Rules, 2021 by the MoP on 22.02.2021. Therefore, any payment made by BYPL for
the bills up to 22.2.2021 has to be adjusted towards principal dues first. Thereafter, the
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Order in Petition No. 319/MP/2019 Page 40 of 46

CENTRAL ELECTRICITY REGULATORY COMMISSION
NEW DELHI
Petition No. 147/MP/2026
Coram:
Shri Jishnu Barua, Chairperson

Date of Order: 30th May, 2026
In the matter of
Petition under Sections 17(3) and 17(4) of the Electricity Act, 2003, seeking approval
for creation of security interest over Petitioner’s assets in favour of Respondent No. 3
(who is acting as the security trustee) for the purpose of holding the securities on
behalf of and for the benefit of the lender in terms of the security trustee agreement
dated 25.9.2025 (including its assignees, transferees, novatees) in respect of the
Petitioner’s transmission project.
And
In the matter of
Solapur Transmission Limited (STL),
Samanvay, 600, Tapovan,

Versus
1. Central Transmission Utility of India Limited,
Saudamini, 1st Floor, Plot No.2,

Ahmedabad - 380006
3. Axis Trustee Services Limited,
Axis House, Bombay Dyeing Mills Compound,

Worli, Mumbai - 400025 …Respondents
Parties Present:
Shri Mihir Thakkar, STL
ORDER
The Petitioner, Solapur Transmission Limited (hereinafter referred to as ‘the
Petitioner/STL’), has been granted a transmission licence under Section 14 of the
Order in Petition No. 147/MP/2026 Page 1

Electricity Act, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as ‘the Act’) to develop the Inter-State
Transmission System, viz. “Transmission Scheme for evacuation of 1500 MW RE
injection at Solapur SEZ” (hereinafter referred to as ‘the Transmission System’ or ‘the
Project’), the details of which are specified in the schedule attached to the licence
issued vide Order dated 23.6.2024 in Petition No. 146/TL/2024. The Commission,
vide Order dated 31.5.2024 in Petition No. 147/AT/2024, adopted the competitively
discovered levelised tariff.
2. The Petitioner has filed the present Petition for approval for the creation of
security interest over the Petitioner’s assets, including all movable and immovable
assets, in favour of Respondent No.3, Axis Trustee Services Limited (“Security
Trustee”) and for the benefit of Respondent No.2, Axis Bank Limited (“lender”)
including its successors, transferees, novatees, and assigns for a sum of Rs. 360
crore. The Petitioner has made the following prayers:
“(a) Approve the creation of Security Interest by way of hypothecation/
mortgage/ charge/ pledge/ assignment (as applicable), over the Petitioner’s
Assets to the extent described in this petition, to secure the total commitment to
the lender aggregating to INR 360,00,00,000 /- (Three Hundred Sixty Crores),
in favour of Respondent No. 3 for the benefit of the lender and for its
successors, Subsequent transferees, novatees, assigns and any refinancing
lenders to the Project by way of hypothecation/ assignment/ Mortgage(if any):
(b) Pass any such other/ further order(s)/ direction (s) as this Commission
may deem fit and appropriate in the facts and circumstances of the present
case.”
Submissions of the Petitioner
3. The Petitioner has mainly submitted as under:
(a) The Petitioner, in its capacity as a Transmission Service Provider,
executed a Transmission Service Agreement (hereinafter referred to as ‘the
TSA’) dated 20.3.2024 with the Central Transmission Utility of India Limited
(hereinafter referred to as ‘Respondent No. 1/CTUIL’). Respondent No. 2, Axis
Bank Limited, i.e., the Lender, is a company incorporated under the Companies
Act, 1956. Respondent No. 3 herein, Axis Trustee Services Limited, is a
company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956, and is a Security
Order in Petition No. 147/MP/2026 Page 2

Trustee for the benefit of the lender, and for its subsequent transferees,
assignees, novatees thereof, and any refinancing lenders to the Project, and to
enter into all relevant financing documents pursuant thereto.
(b) The Petitioner, STL, was granted approval for Section 164 of the
Electricity Act, 2003 by the Ministry of Power vide Gazette dated 5.2.2025.
(c) The Petitioner had requested the lender, i.e., Axis Bank Limited to
provide a Rupee Term Loan Facility of up to amount not exceeding in the
aggregate Rs. 360 crore (including certain sub-limits) for part-financing of the
transmission project – Transmission System for Evacuation of Power from RE
Projects in Solapur (1500 MW) SEZ at Solapur in the State of Maharashtra and
reimbursement of excess Promoter Contribution infused by the Promoter for
"the Project". The lender/Axis Bank Limited has granted a Rupee Term Loan
Facility (including certain sub-limits) for a principal amount not exceeding Rs.
360 crore (“the Facility”), on and subject to the terms and conditions set out in
the Facility Agreement dated 25.9.2025, executed between the Petitioner and
the Lender/Axis Bank Limited.
(d) Further, a Security Trustee Agreement dated 25.09.2025 has been
executed between the Petitioner, Respondent No.2/Axis Bank Limited and
Respondent No.3/ Axis Trustee Services Limited.
(e) The Loan Agreement was executed in relation to the Project Facility,
which has been extended by the lender to the Borrower/the Petitioner, on and
subject to the terms and conditions set out in the Loan/ Facility Agreement and
the other financing documents. In terms of the Facility Agreement, the following
documents are the financing documents (“Financing Documents”):
i. Loan Agreement (Facility Agreement)
ii. Security Trustee Agreement (as defined under the Loan Agreement)
(“STA”);
iii. Trust and Retention Account Agreement (as defined under the Loan
Agreement);
Order in Petition No. 147/MP/2026 Page 3

iv. Sponsor’s Undertaking (i.e., undertaking by Torrent Power Limited,
including its successors and permitted assigns and permitted transferees)
(as defined under the Loan Agreement);
v. Security Documents (as defined under the Loan Agreement); and
vi. Any other agreement in relation to the Facility designated as a ‘Financing
Document’ by the Lenders.
(f) In terms of Clause 12.1, 12.2 & 12.5 of the Loan/Facility Agreement, the
lender has the right to sell or transfer (by way of assignment, securitisation,
novation or otherwise) whole or part of the Facility, including any outstanding
payable by the Borrower to the Finance Parties (i.e., Lenders, Escrow Bank and
the Security Trustee) thereunder or any other rights and obligations of the
lenders under the Loan/ Facility Agreement or any other document pursuant
hereto to any Person (as defined in the Loan/ Facility Agreement) in a manner
or under any other such terms and conditions as the lenders may decide,
without any additional obligation on the Borrower. The Borrower shall not be
entitled to directly or indirectly assign, transfer or novate its rights or obligations
under this Agreement in part or in whole or to any person.
(g) In view of the foregoing, subject to the provisions of the Financing
Documents, the lender(s) may assign, convey, or otherwise transfer all or any
part of its right, title, interest in the STA to any other bank or financial institution
and/or any other bank or financial institution which may provide any secured
financial assistance to the Borrower.
(h) Axis Trustee Services Limited/Respondent No. 3 has agreed to act as a
Security Trustee for the benefit of the lender, namely Axis Bank Limited, who
has agreed to finance the Transmission Project of the Petitioner. To provide the
said financing, the lender requires a security to be created over the project
assets, which requires the Commission’s approval.
(i) Pursuant to the terms of the Facility Agreement (Schedule 1 of Sr. no.
26), the secured obligations of Petitioner shall be secured by the following
security package:
“(i) PRIMARY SECURITY
Order in Petition No. 147/MP/2026 Page 4

(a) First charge by way of mortgage on the Mortgaged Properties.
(b) First charge by way of hypothecation over the leasehold rights, tangible
moveable assets, intangible assets, both present and future, in relation to the
Project.
(c) First charge by way of hypothecation over the Current Assets.
(d) First charge by way of hypothecation or equitable assignment or assignment
by way of security on all the right, title, interest, benefits, claims and demands
whatsoever of the Borrower in the Project Documents, including substitution
rights under the TSA and rights under the Transmission License (subject to
consent/ approval of CERC, if applicable). Provided that assignment/ charge on
any of the aforesaid documents shall be intimated to relevant counterparties in
case permission for upfront assignment is available in such document.
(e) First charge by way of hypothecation on all Accounts, DSRA, other
reserves, deposits opened/to be opened and maintained by the Borrower in
relation to the Project and any other bank accounts of the Borrower in relation
to the projects;
(f) Charge by way of pledge over the Pledged Shares, subject to applicable
regulations, including charge over preference shares, compulsorily convertible
debentures / compulsorily convertible preference shares, present and future,
subject to prevailing banking regulations:
Provided that the Borrower shall ensure that the voting rights in relation to the
Pledged Shares do not fall below 30% (thirty percent) at any time until the Final
Settlement Date:
Provided further that in the event applicable regulations do not permit pledge
over 100% (one hundred percent) of the Pledged Shares, pledge to the extent
permissible under applicable regulations shall be provided and for remaining
percentage of the Pledged Shares, a non-disposal undertaking shall be
executed by the sponsor in favour of the Security Trustee to the satisfaction of
Lender, such that pledge and non-disposal undertaking cumulatively constitute
51% (fifty one percent) of equity share capital of the Borrower.
(ii) CORPORATE GUARANTEE
(g) Unconditional and irrevocable corporate guarantee furnished by the
Corporate Guarantor. Provided that the aforesaid corporate guarantee shall fall
away upon occurrence of the CG Expiration Date.
(iii) CONTRACTUAL COMFORT
(h) Non-disposal undertaking in relation to the NDU Shares, including non-
disposal undertaking in relation to 21% (twenty one percent) of preference
shares, compulsorily convertible debentures / compulsorily convertible
preference shares, present and future.”
(j) Accordingly, the Petitioner, has agreed, upon approval of the Commission to
create a Security Interest, as may be required by the lender from time to time, in
terms of the Financing Documents, in favour of the Security Trustee [acting for the
Order in Petition No. 147/MP/2026 Page 5

benefit of the Lender (or any of their assignees, transferees or novates)] by
executing the Security Documents as defined under the Loan Agreement. The
Petitioner has agreed that it shall be lawful for the Lender(s) /Security Trustee (or
any of their assignees, transferees or novates), upon enforcement of the Security
Interest, to enter into and take possession of the properties over which the
Security Interest has been created pursuant to the Financing Documents.
(i) Under the Financing Agreements and on enforcement of the Security Interest, it
shall be lawful for the Lender(s), Security Trustee and their assignees,
transferees, and novates, acting for the benefit of lender(s), to enter into and take
possession of the assets/ properties mortgaged/ charged/ assigned for their
benefit and substitute themselves or any one of them or its nominees for the
Petitioner under any or all of the Transmission Project Document(s).
4. The Petitioner has submitted that the Petitioner is permitted to create
encumbrances over the Transmission Project assets in accordance with Article 15.2.2
of the TSA which provides that the Petitioner may create any encumbrance over all or
part of its receivables, letter of credit or the other assets of the Transmission Project in
favour of the lender or the lender's representative on their behalf, as security for
amount payable under the financing agreements and any other amounts agreed by
the parties, subject to conditions mentioned in TSA. Therefore, in accordance with
Sections 17(3) and (4) of the Act and the provisions of the TSA as quoted above, the
prior approval of the Commission is essential for the creation of a Security Interest
over all the movable and immovable Assets of the Petitioner.
5. Hence, the present Petition has been filed by the Petitioner seeking approval of
the Commission for creation of security by the Petitioner over the Petitioner’s Assets
in favour of the Respondent No. 3 acting for the benefit of the lender and for its
subsequent transferees, assignees, novatees thereof by way of hypothecation/
assignment/ mortgage, to the extent described in this Petition to secure the total
commitment of the Lender aggregating to Rs. 360 crore.
Order in Petition No. 147/MP/2026 Page 6

6. The Petitioner has further submitted that the Commission has consistently
exercised jurisdiction in granting approvals for security creation by transmission
licensees under Section 17 of the Act, particularly in the context of similarly placed
transmission projects. Therefore, the approval sought herein is aligned with regulatory
practice and does not seek to dilute or alter any obligations of the Petitioner under the
TSA. The Petitioner also submitted that the above approval, if granted, shall not affect
the rights and obligations of the Petitioner as the Transmission Licensee.
Hearing dated 7.4.2026
7. The Petition was called out for the hearing on 7.4.2026 after notice to the
Respondents. Vide Record of Proceedings (hereinafter referred to as “RoP”) for the
hearing dated 7.4.2026, the Respondents were granted the opportunity to file their
respective replies.
Hearing dated 6.5.2026
8. During the course of the hearing, the representative of the Petitioner submitted
that no reply has been filed by the Respondents despite notice. Considering the
submissions made by the Petitioner, the matter was reserved for orders.
Analysis and Decision
9. We have considered the submissions made by the Petitioner and perused the
documents placed on record. The Petitioner approached the lender, Axis Bank
Limited, for financing of Petitioner’s Project and availed a Rupee Term Loan
amounting to Rs. 360.00 crore as per the terms and conditions stipulated in the
Facility Agreement with Axis Bank Limited on 25.9.2025. Further, the Petitioner, Axis
Bank Limited, and Axis Trustee Services Limited entered into a Security Trustee
Agreement dated 25.9.2025, wherein Axis Trustee Services Limited is acting as a
Security Trustee for the purpose of holding the security interest and holding the
Order in Petition No. 147/MP/2026 Page 7

securities on behalf of and for the benefit of the Lender (or its assignees, novatees or
transferees).
10. The Petitioner has submitted the break-up of the Project Cost as well as
Financing Plan as per the Facility Agreement dated 25.9.2025, as under:
Particulars Amount (in Rs. crore)
Estimated Project Cost 485
Means of Finance
Sponsor Contribution 125
Rupee Term Loan from Lenders 360
Total 485
11. The transmission projects are capital-intensive projects requiring large capital
investment. These projects are financed through loans. It is a normal practice followed
by financial institutions/the banking industry to ask for sufficient security from the
borrower to back the loan in order to mitigate the credit risk of the lenders. In the
instant case, the lender, Axis Bank Limited, has agreed to provide the Rupee Term
Loan of Rs. 360.00 crore and, for the said purpose, has entered into a Facility
Agreement dated 25.9.2025 with the Petitioner. Further, the Petitioner has executed a
Security Trustee Agreement dated 25.9.2025 with the Security Trustee, Axis Trustee
Services Limited and Axis Bank Limited for the purpose of holding the security interest
and holding the securities on behalf of and for the benefit of the lender (or its
assignees, novatees or transferees).
12. The Petitioner has further submitted that the Petitioner is permitted to create
encumbrances over Project Assets in accordance with Article 15 of the TSA. Under
Article 15.2.2 of the TSA, the Petitioner may create any encumbrance over all or part
of the receivables, or the Transmission Project assets in favour of the lender, i.e.,
Respondent No.2 or their representatives, as security for amounts payable under the
Order in Petition No. 147/MP/2026 Page 8

Financing Agreements and any other amounts agreed by the parties. The relevant
extract of Article 15 of the TSA is as under:
“15.2. Permitted Charges:
15.2.1. Neither Party shall create or permit to subsist any encumbrance over
all or any of its rights and benefits under this Agreement.
15.2.2. However, the TSP may create any encumbrance over all or part
of the receivables, or the Project Assets of the Project in favour
of the Lenders or the Lenders' Representative on their behalf,
as security for amounts payable under the Financing
Agreements and any other amounts agreed by the Parties.
Provided that:
i. the Lenders or the Lenders' Representative on their behalf shall have
entered into the Financing Agreements and agreed in writing to the
provisions of this Agreement; and
ii. any encumbrance granted by the TSP in accordance with this Article
15.2.2 shall contain provisions pursuant to which the Lenders or the
Lender’s Representative on their behalf agrees unconditionally with
the TSP to release from such encumbrances upon payment by the
TSP to the Lenders of all amounts due under the Financing
Agreements.”
13. Sub-sections (3) and (4) of Section 17 of the Act provides as under:
“17. (3) No licensee shall at any time assign his licence or transfer his utility,
or any part thereof, by sale, lease, exchange or otherwise without the prior
approval of the Appropriate Commission.
(4) Any agreement relating to any transaction specified in sub-section (1) or
sub-section (3), unless made with the prior approval of the Appropriate
Commission, shall be void.”
As per the above provisions, a licensee is required to obtain the Commission's
approval for assigning its licence or transferring its utility, or any part thereof, by way
of sale, lease, exchange, or otherwise, and for entering into an agreement relating to
any of these transactions.
14. The Petitioner and the lender, Axis Bank Limited, have appointed Axis Trustee
Services Limited as a Security Trustee for the creation of a Security Interest over all
Order in Petition No. 147/MP/2026 Page 9

the movable and immovable assets of the project. In our view, Axis Trustee Services
Limited needs to be given comfort for the creation of security for the benefit of the
lender, Axis Bank Limited, as the security for the financial assistance provided by it.
We, therefore, accord in-principle approval allowing the Petitioner to create a Security
Interest in favour of Axis Trustee Services Limited by way of mortgage or any other
security document on project assets by execution of an indenture of Mortgage and
financing documents of the Project. The Petitioner is directed to submit a signed copy
of the Indenture of Mortgage for the Project immediately after its execution.
15. This in-principle approval is being granted with the condition that the
transmission licence granted by the Commission to the Petitioner cannot be assigned
in favour of the Security Trustee or nominee of the lender without prior approval of the
Commission at the time of creating rights in favour of such a nominee. Before
agreeing to the assignment of the licence and the assets of the Petitioner to the
nominee of the lender, the Commission will evaluate such a nominee’s expertise in
the development, design, construction, operation, and maintenance of the
transmission lines and their ability to execute the Project and undertake the
transmission of electricity. The licensee, lender, security trustee, and nominee shall
accordingly be jointly required to approach the Commission to seek approval. This will
allow the Commission to satisfy itself of the circumstances necessitating such a
transfer. This decision of ours is in accordance with Regulation 8 of the Central
Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for grant of
Transmission Licence and other related matters) Regulations, 2024, which reads as
under:
“8. Assignment of Licence: In case of default by the licensee in debt
repayment, the Commission may, on an application made by the lenders of the
licensee, assign the licence to a nominee of the lenders.”
Order in Petition No. 147/MP/2026 Page 10

16. In the event of a default by the licensee regarding debt repayment, the
Commission may, upon a joint application submitted by the licensee, lender, Security
Trustee, and nominee, grant approval for the assignment of the licence to a nominee,
contingent upon the satisfactory completion of due diligence procedures.
Consequently, it is imperative to obtain explicit prior approval from the Commission for
the assignment of the licence to the nominee of the Security Trustee or for the transfer
of any assets to them. Finally, the Petitioner is required to submit the financial
documents and statements in accordance with the Commission’s directives.
17. Petition No. 147/MP/2026 is disposed of in terms of the above.

ORDER
This Petition has been filed by the Petitioner, North Eastern Electric Power
Corporation Limited (in short “NEEPCO”) for truing up of tariff for the period 2019-24, in respect
of Agartala Gas Based Power Station (135 MW) (in short, ‘the generating station’), in
accordance with the provisions of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms &
Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2019 (in short, ‘the 2019 Tariff Regulations’) and
determination of tariff of the generating station for the period 2024-29, in accordance with the
provisions of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff)
Regulations, 2024 (in short ‘the 2024 Tariff Regulations’) for the period 2024-29.
2. The generating station with an installed capacity of 135 MW comprises four Gas Turbine
(GT) units of 21 MW each and two Steam Turbine (ST) units of 25.50 MW each. The
beneficiaries of the North-Eastern States have been allocated the full capacity of 135 MW from
the generating station. The generating station, with an installed capacity of 84 MW and
operating in open cycle mode, was declared to be in commercial operation (COD) on 1.8.1998.
The generating station was converted to a Combined Cycle Power Plant with the addition of
Order in Petition No. 39/GT/2025 Page 2 of 86

two Steam Turbine Generating units (STG) each with a capacity of 25.5 MW with effect from
29.7.2015 and 1.9.2015, respectively. Accordingly, the COD of the units of the generating
station are as under:

6. The Commission, vide its Technical Validation (TV) letter dated 1.5.2025, directed the
Petitioner to furnish certain additional information. In compliance with the directions, the
Petitioner filed the additional information, along with the revised tariff forms with the necessary
modifications vide affidavit dated 7.5.2025, after serving a copy on the Respondents. None of
Order in Petition No. 39/GT/2025 Page 4 of 86

the Respondents has filed their replies thereto. The matter was listed for hearing on 27.5.2025,
and the Commission, vide its Record of Proceedings (ROP), directed the Petitioner to file
certain additional information. In compliance with the directions, the Petitioner filed additional
information vide affidavit dated 23.6.2025, after serving a copy on the Respondents. None of
the Respondents has filed a reply thereto. Subsequently, the Petition was listed for hearing on
7.8.2025, and the Commission, after hearing the Petitioner, directed it to file certain additional
information and reserved its order in the Petition. In compliance with the directions, the
Petitioner, vide affidavit dated 1.9.2025, has filed the additional information, after serving a
copy on the Respondents. None of the Respondents has filed their replies thereto.
7. Taking into consideration the submissions of the Petitioner and the documents available
on record, we proceed to examine the claims of the Petitioner on a prudence check, as stated
in the subsequent paragraphs.
Capital Cost
8. Regulation 19 (1) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations provides that the capital cost as
determined by the Commission after prudence check, in accordance with this regulation shall
form the basis of determination of tariff for existing and new generating stations and capital
cost for an existing generating station is governed as per Regulation 19 (3) of the 2019 Tariff
Regulations, which is as follows:
“3) The Capital cost of an existing project shall include the following:
(a) Capital cost admitted by the Commission prior to 1.4.2019 duly trued up by excluding
liability, if any, as on 1.4.2019.
(b) Additional capitalization and de-capitalization for the respective year of tariff as
determined in accordance with these regulations.
(c) Capital expenditure on account of renovation and modernisation as admitted by this
Commission in accordance with these regulations.
(d) Capital expenditure on account of ash disposal and utilization including handling and
transportation facility.
(e) Capital expenditure incurred towards railway infrastructure and its augmentation for
transportation of coal up to the receiving end of generating station but does not include
the transportation cost and any other appurtenant cost paid to the railway; and
Order in Petition No. 39/GT/2025 Page 5 of 86

(f) Capital cost incurred or projected to be incurred by a thermal generating station, on
account of implementation of the norms under Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT)
scheme of Government of India shall be considered by the Commission subject to
sharing of benefits accrued under the PAT scheme with the beneficiaries.
9. Further Regulation 13 of the 2019 Tariff Regulations provides as under:
“13. (1) The Commission shall carry out truing up exercise for the period 2019-24 along with
the tariff petition filed for the next tariff period, for the following:
(a) the capital expenditure including additional capital expenditure incurred up to 31.3.2024,
as admitted by the Commission after prudence check at the time of truing up:
(b) the capital expenditure including additional capital expenditure incurred up to 31.3.2024,
on account of Force Majeure and Change in Law.”
10. In terms of the above, the Petitioner in the Petition has initially claimed the annual fixed
charges based on the opening capital cost of Rs. 68333.64 lakh for the period 2019-24.
However, the order dated 28.7.2023 in Petition No. 32/GT/2020 (Truing up for the period 2014-
19) had approved the closing capital cost of Rs. 65293.48 lakh, on a cash basis, as on
31.3.2019. In response to the various queries regarding the variation sought vide TV Letter
dated 1.5.2025, the Petitioner modified tariff forms, changed the opening capital cost to Rs.
65293.48 lakh, and accordingly modified the related calculations. Further, the order dated
26.10.2023 in Petition No. 246/GT/2020 (determination of tariff for the period 2019-24) has also
considered the opening capital cost of Rs. 65293.48 lakh, as on 1.4.2019, for the determination
of tariff for the period 2019-24. Accordingly, in terms of Regulation 19(3) of the 2019 Tariff
Regulations, the closing capital cost of Rs. 65293.48 lakh, on a cash basis, as on 31.3.2019,
has been considered as the opening capital cost, as on 1.4.2019, for truing up the tariff for the
period 2019-24.
Additional Capital Expenditure
11. Regulation 25 of the 2019 Tariff Regulations provides as follows:
“25. Additional Capitalisation within the original scope and after the cut-off date:
(1)The additional capital expenditure incurred or projected to be incurred in respect of an
existing project or a new project on the following counts within the original scope of work
and after the cut-off date may be admitted by the Commission, subject to prudence check:
(a)Liabilities to meet award of arbitration or for compliance of the directions or order of any
statutory authority, or order or decree of any court of law;
Order in Petition No. 39/GT/2025 Page 6 of 86

(b)Change in law or compliance of any existing law;
(c) Deferred works relating to ash pond or ash handling system in the original scope of work;
(d)Liability for works executed prior to the cut-off date;
(e)Force Majeure events;
(f) Liability for works admitted by the Commission after the cut-off date to the extent of
discharge of such liabilities by actual payments; and
(g)Raising of ash dyke as a part of ash disposal system.
(2)In case of replacement of assets deployed under the original scope of the existing project
after cut-off date, the additional capitalization may be admitted by the Commission, after
making necessary adjustments in the gross fixed assets and the cumulative depreciation,
subject to prudence check on the following grounds:
(a)The useful life of the assets is not commensurate with the useful life of the project and
such assets have been fully depreciated in accordance with the provisions of these
regulations;
(b)The replacement of the asset or equipment is necessary on account of change in law or
Force Majeure conditions;
(c) The replacement of such asset or equipment is necessary on account of obsolescence
of technology; and
(d)The replacement of such asset or equipment has otherwise been allowed by the
Commission.”
12. Regulation 26 of the 2019 Tariff Regulations provides as follows:
“26. Additional Capitalisation beyond the original scope:
(1)The capital expenditure, in respect of existing generating station or the transmission
system including communication system, incurred or projected to be incurred on the
following counts beyond the original scope, may be admitted by the Commission, subject
to prudence check:
(a) Liabilities to meet award of arbitration or for compliance of order or directions of any
statutory authority, or order or decree of any court of law;
(b) Change in law or compliance of any existing law;
(c) Force Majeure events;
(d) Need for higher security and safety of the plant as advised or directed by appropriate
Indian Government Instrumentality or statutory authorities responsible for national or
internal security;
(e) Deferred works relating to ash pond or ash handling system in additional to the original
scope of work, on case to case basis
Provided also that if any expenditure has been claimed under Renovation and
Modernisation (R&M) or repairs and maintenance under O&M expenses, the same shall
not be claimed under this Regulation;
(f) Usage of water from sewage treatment plant in thermal generating station “
(2) In case of de-capitalisation of assets of a generating company or the transmission
licensee, as the case may be, the original cost of such asset as on the date of
decapitalisation shall be deducted from the value of gross fixed asset and corresponding
loan as well as equity shall be deducted from outstanding loan and the equity respectively
in the year such de-capitalisation takes place with corresponding adjustments in cumulative
depreciation and cumulative repayment of loan, duly taking into consideration the year in
which it was capitalised.”
Order in Petition No. 39/GT/2025 Page 7 of 86

14. The COD of the open cycle (GT) of the generating station is 1.8.1998. However, with
the introduction of two additional Steam Turbine generating units with effect from 29.7.2015
Order in Petition No. 39/GT/2025 Page 9 of 86

and 1.9.2015, the COD of the combined cycle generating station (i.e., only STG) is 1.9.2015.
Accordingly, the STG cut-off date is 31.3.2018.
15. The Petitioner has claimed additional capital expenditure of various items under the
relevant Regulations of the 2019 Tariff Regulations. The analysis and decisions made for each
of the items claimed are based on the submissions of the Parties and documents placed on
record. Further, the admissibility of the claims is done by exercising a prudence check of the
claims made by the Petitioner with relevant documentary evidence submitted to substantiate
the claim of additional capital expenditure.
16. For additional capital expenditure items claimed under Regulation 25(1)(a) of the 2019
Tariff Regulations which is for additional capital expenditure items within original scope of work
and after the cut-off date for liabilities to meet award of arbitration or for compliance of the
directions or order of any statutory authority, or order or decree of any court of law, the claim
is allowed if the Petitioner has corroborated the claim with relevant documentary evidence
indicating the liabilities to meet the award of arbitration or compliance of the directions or order
of any statutory authority. Similarly, for items claimed under Regulation 25(1)(f) of the 2019
Tariff Regulations which is for additional capital expenditure items within original scope of work
and after the cut-off date for Liability for works admitted by the Commission after the cut-off
date to the extent of discharge of such liabilities by actual payments, the claim is allowed after
prudence check of the supporting documents furnished by the Petitioner to justify the claim.
17. For additional capital expenditure items claimed under Regulation 25(2)(a) of the 2019
Tariff Regulations, which permits replacement of assets which have completed their useful life
and have been fully depreciated or become unreliable due to aging, lack of spare parts, and
harsh site condition, the claim is allowed subject to prudence check and verification of actual
capitalization and requires the Petitioner to furnish supporting documentation including life
completion evidence, procurement details, and justification. The Commission has been
Order in Petition No. 39/GT/2025 Page 10 of 86

considering the claims under this regulation on verification of details of old assets which are
being replaced from Form- I (Details of Assets De-capitalized during the period), wherein the
details of the year put to use of the asset, gross block and corresponding depreciation
recovered are provided. Further, if the gross block of the old asset is not provided, the
Commission derives the assumed deletion value of the same. In the instant petition, the
Petitioner has provided the details of most of the items replaced under this head in Form- I and
the same is considered. For the items for which the required details are not provided by the
Petitioner, the method of assumed deletion is considered.
18. For additional capital expenditure items claimed under Regulation 25(2)(c) of the 2019
Tariff Regulations, which is for the replacement of the asset on account of obsolescence of
technology, the obsolescence certificate from OEM or by the competent authority, as submitted
by the Petitioner, is considered to ascertain the claim. Further details of the old asset which
are being replaced are verified from Form-I (Details of Assets De-capitalized during the period),
wherein the details of put to use of the asset, gross block and corresponding depreciation
recovered are provided. In the instant petition, the Petitioner has provided the details in support
of obsolescence and for assets replaced under this head in Form- I and the same is considered.
For the items for which the required details are not provided by the Petitioner, the method of
assumed deletion is considered.
19. For additional capital expenditure items claimed under Regulation 25(2)(d) of the 2019
Tariff Regulations, which is for replacement of assets within original scope of works and after
the cut-off date, which was otherwise been allowed by the Commission, the claim is allowed if
the work was previously allowed during the determination of tariff for the period 2019-24 in
order dated 26.10.2023 in Petition No. 246/GT/2020. Moreover, for claims that were not part
of the said order, and the Petitioner has referred to previous orders for the same generating
Order in Petition No. 39/GT/2025 Page 11 of 86

station, the claims are allowed after a prudence check of the documentary evidence submitted
by the Petitioner.
20. For the additional capital expenditure items claimed under Regulation 26(1)(b) of the
2019 Tariff Regulations which is for additional capital expenditure beyond the original scope
due to change in law or compliance of any existing law, the claim is allowed if the Petitioner
has submitted sufficient justification for corroborating the claim as a mandatory requirement as

27. As per the consistent methodology adopted by the Commission in its orders, the
expenditure on replacement of assets, if found justified, is allowed for the purpose of tariff,
provided that the capitalization of the said asset is followed by de-capitalization of the
gross value of the old asset. However, in certain cases, where the decapitalization is
proposed to be effected during the future years to the year of capitalization of the new
Order in Petition No. 39/GT/2025 Page 25 of 86

asset, the decapitalization of the old asset for the purpose of tariff is shifted to the very
same year in which the capitalization of the new asset is allowed. Such de-capitalization
which is not a book entry in the year of capitalization is termed as “Assumed Deletion”.
Further, in the absence of the gross value of the asset being de-capitalized, the same is
calculated by de-escalating the gross value of the new asset at the rate of 5% per annum
till the year of capitalization of the old asset.

Present Petition
6. The Petitioner has filed the present Petition for truing up of the tariff of the
generating station for the period 2019-24 in accordance with Regulation 13 of the 2019
Tariff Regulations, which provides as under:
“13. Truing up of tariff for the period 2019-24: (1) The Commission shall carry out
the truing up exercise for the period 2019-24 along with the tariff petition filed for the
next tariff period, for the following:
(1a) The input price of coal or lignite from the integrated mine(s) of the generating
station(s) for the tariff period 2019-24 shall be trued up for the capital expenditure
including additional capital expenditure incurred up to 31.3.2024, as allowed by the
Commission;
the capital expenditure including additional capital expenditure incurred up to
31.3.2024, on account of Force Majeure and Change in Law, as admitted by the
Commission.
a. the capital expenditure including additional capital expenditure incurred up to
31.3.2024, as admitted by the Commission after prudence check at the time of truing
up:
Order in Petition No. 701/GT/2025 Page 3 of 62
7 01/GT/2025

b. the capital expenditure including additional capital expenditure incurred up to
31.3.2024, on account of Force Majeure and Change in Law.
(2) The generating company or the transmission licensee, as the case may be, shall
make an application, as per Annexure – I, to these regulations, for carrying out truing
up exercise in respect of the generating station or a unit thereof of the transmission
system or an element thereof by 30.11.2024.
(3) The generating company or the transmission licensee, as the case may be, may
make an application for interim truing up of tariff in the year 2021-22, if the annual fixed
cost increased by more than 20% over the annual fixed cost as determined by the
Commission for the respective year of the tariff period:
Provided that if the actual additional capital expenditure falls short of the projected
additional capital expenditure allowed under provisions of Chapter 7 of these
regulations, the generating company or the transmission licensee, as the case may
be, shall not be required to file any interim true up petition for this purpose and shall
refund to the beneficiaries or the long term customers, as the case may be, the excess
tariff recovered corresponding to the projected additional capital expenditure not
incurred at the bank rate as on 1st April of the respective years, under intimation to the
Commission:
Provided further that the generating company or the transmission licensee shall submit
the complete details along with the calculations of the refunds made to the
beneficiaries or the long term customers, as the case may be, at the time of truing up.
(4) After truing up, if the tariff already recovered exceeds or falls short of the tariff
approved by the Commission under these regulations, the generating company or the
transmission licensee, shall refund to or recover from, the beneficiaries or the long
term customers, as the case may be, the excess or the short fall amount along with
simple interest at the rate equal to the bank rate as on 1st April of the respective years
of the tariff period in six equal monthly instalments.
(4a) After truing up, if the input price already recovered exceeds or falls short of the
input price approved by the Commission under these regulations, the excess or the
shortfall amount shall be refunded or recovered, as the case may be, by the generating
company along with simple interest at the rate equal to the bank rate as on 1st April
of the respective years of the tariff period in six equal monthly instalments:
Provided that the generating company shall refund such excess amount or recover the
shortfall amount from the beneficiaries based on scheduled energy.”

8. The Petition was heard on 28.8.2025 wherein the Commission directed the
Petitioner to submit additional information, and parties were further directed to
complete the pleadings. In compliance, the Petitioner has filed the additional
information vide affidavit dated 9.10.2025. The Respondent, UPPCL, has filed its reply
vide affidavit dated 1.11.2025, and the Petitioner has filed its rejoinder to the said reply
vide affidavit dated 27.11.2025. Pursuant to the hearing on 9.12.2025, the order in the
Petition was reserved. Based on the submissions of the parties and the documents
on record, we proceed with truing up the tariff of the generating station for the period
2019-24, after a prudence check, as stated in the subsequent paragraphs.
Capital Cost
9. Regulation 19 of the 2019 Tariff Regulations provides as under:
“19. Capital Cost: (1) The Capital cost of the generating station or the transmission
system, as the case may be, as determined by the Commission after prudence check
in accordance with these regulations shall form the basis for determination of tariff for
existing and new projects.
Order in Petition No. 701/GT/2025 Page 5 of 62
7 01/GT/2025

(2) The Capital Cost of a new project shall include the following:
(a) The expenditure incurred or projected to be incurred up to the date of commercial
operation of the project;
(b) Interest during construction and financing charges, on the loans (i) being equal to
70% of the funds deployed, in the event of the actual equity in excess of 30% of the
funds deployed, by treating the excess equity as normative loan, or (ii) being equal to
the actual amount of loan in the event of the actual equity less than 30% of the funds
deployed;
(c) Any gain or loss on account of foreign exchange risk variation pertaining to the loan
amount availed during the construction period;
(d) Interest during construction and incidental expenditure during construction as
computed in accordance with these regulations;
(e) Capitalised initial spares subject to the ceiling rates in accordance with these
regulations;
(f) Expenditure on account of additional capitalization and de-capitalisation determined
in accordance with these regulations;
(g) Adjustment of revenue due to sale of infirm power in excess of fuel cost prior to the
date of commercial operation as specified under Regulation 7 of these regulations;
(h) Adjustment of revenue earned by the transmission licensee by using the assets
before the date of commercial operation;
(i) Capital expenditure on account of ash disposal and utilization including handling
and transportation facility;
(j) Capital expenditure incurred towards railway infrastructure and its augmentation for
transportation of coal upto the receiving end of the generating station but does not
include the transportation cost and any other appurtenant cost paid to the railway;
(k) Capital expenditure on account of biomass handling equipment and facilities, for
co-firing;
(l) Capital expenditure on account of emission control system necessary to meet the
revised emission standards and sewage treatment plant;
(m) Expenditure on account of fulfilment of any conditions for obtaining environment
clearance for the project;
(n) Expenditure on account of change in law and force majeure events; and
(o) Capital cost incurred or projected to be incurred by a thermal generating station,
on account of implementation of the norms under Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT)
scheme of Government of India shall be considered by the Commission subject to
sharing of benefits accrued under the PAT scheme with the beneficiaries.
(3) The Capital cost of an existing project shall include the following:
(a) Capital cost admitted by the Commission prior to 1.4.2019 duly trued up by
excluding liability, if any, as on 1.4.2019;
(b) Additional capitalization and de-capitalization for the respective year of tariff as
determined in accordance with these regulations;
(c) Capital expenditure on account of renovation and modernisation as admitted by
this Commission in accordance with these regulations;
(d) Capital expenditure on account of ash disposal and utilization including handling
and transportation facility;
(e)Capital expenditure incurred towards railway infrastructure and its augmentation for
transportation of coal up to the receiving end of generating station but does not include
the transportation cost and any other appurtenant cost paid to the railway;
(f) and Capital cost incurred or projected to be incurred by a thermal generating station,
on account of implementation of the norms under Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT)
scheme of Government of India shall be considered by the Commission subject to
sharing of benefits accrued under the PAT scheme with the beneficiaries.
(4) The capital cost in case of existing or new hydro generating station shall also
Order in Petition No. 701/GT/2025 Page 6 of 62
7 01/GT/2025

include:
(a) cost of approved rehabilitation and resettlement (R&R) plan of the project in
conformity with National R&R Policy and R&R package as approved; and
(b) cost of the developer’s 10% contribution towards Rajiv Gandhi Grameen
Vidyutikaran Yojana (RGGVY) and Deendayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana
(DDUGJY) project in the affected area.
(5) The following shall be excluded from the capital cost of the existing and new
projects:
(a) The assets forming part of the project, but not in use, as declared in the tariff
petition;
(b) De-capitalised Assets after the date of commercial operation on account of
replacement or removal on account of obsolescence or shifting from one project to
another project: Provided that in case replacement of transmission asset is
recommended by Regional Power Committee, such asset shall be decapitalised only
after its redeployment; Provided further that unless shifting of an asset from one
project to another is of permanent nature, there shall be no de-capitalization of the
concerned assets.
(c) In case of hydro generating stations, any expenditure incurred or committed to be
incurred by a project developer for getting the project site allotted by the State
Government by following a transparent process;
(d) Proportionate cost of land of the existing project which is being used for generating
power from generating station based on renewable energy; and
(e) Any grant received from the Central or State Government or any statutory body or
authority for the execution of the project which does not carry any liability of
repayment.”
10. The Commission vide order dated 16.4.2024 in Petition No. 450/GT/2020
(pertaining to truing up of tariff for the period 2014-19), approved the closing capital
cost of Rs.123835.89 (net of un-discharged liabilities of Rs.572.04 lakh) as on
31.3.2019. Subsequently, the Commission vide order dated 31.12.2024 in Review
Petition No. 23/RP/2024 in Petition No. 450/GT/2024 revised the tariff of the
generating station for the 2014-19 tariff period, considering the closing capital cost of
Rs.124680.51 lakh as on 31.3.2019. The Petitioner, in the instant Petition, has also
claimed the opening capital cost of Rs.124680.51 lakh as on 1.4.2019. Accordingly,
the same is considered as opening capital cost as on 1.4.2019, for the purpose of
truing up the tariff for the period 2019-24, in accordance with Regulation 19(3) of the
2019 Tariff Regulations
Additional Capital Expenditure:
11. Regulations 25 and 26 of the 2019 Tariff Regulations provides as under:
Order in Petition No. 701/GT/2025 Page 7 of 62
7 01/GT/2025

“25. Additional Capitalisation within the original scope and after the cut-off date:
(1) The additional capital expenditure incurred or projected to be incurred in respect
of an existing project or a new project on the following counts within the original scope
of work and after the cutoff date may be admitted by the Commission, subject to
prudence check:
(a) Liabilities to meet award of arbitration or for compliance of the directions or order
of any statutory authority, or order or decree of any court of law;
(b) Change in law or compliance of any existing law;
(c) Deferred works relating to ash pond or ash handling system in the
original scope of work;
(d) Liability for works executed prior to the cut-off date;
(e) Force Majeure events;
(f) Liability for works admitted by the Commission after the cut-off date to
the extent of discharge of such liabilities by actual payments; and
(g) Raising of ash dyke as a part of ash disposal system.
(2) In case of replacement of assets deployed under the original scope of the existing
project after cut–off date, the additional capitalisation may be admitted by the
Commission, after making necessary adjustments in the gross fixed assets and the
cumulated depreciation, subject to prudence check on the following grounds:
(a) The useful life of the assets is not commensurate with the useful life of the project
and such assets have been fully depreciated in accordance with the provisions of
these regulations.
(b) The replacement of the assets or equipment is necessary on account of change in
law or Force Majeure conditions;
(c) The replacement of such assets or equipment is necessary on account of
obsolescence of technology; and
(d) The replacement of such assets or equipment has otherwise been allowed by the
Commission.
26. Additional Capitalisation beyond the original scope
(1) The capital expenditure, in respect of existing generating station or the
transmission system including communication system, incurred or projected to be
incurred on the following counts beyond the original scope, may be admitted by the
Commission, subject to prudence check:
(a) Liabilities to meet award of arbitration or for compliance of order or
directions of any statutory authority, or order or decree of any court of law;
(b) Change in law or compliance of any existing law;
(c) Force Majeure events;
(d) Need for higher security and safety of the plant as advised or directed by
appropriate Indian Government Instrumentality or statutory authorities responsible for
national or internal security;
(e) Deferred works relating to ash pond or ash handling system in additional to the
original scope of work, on case to case basis:
Provided also that of any expenditure has been claimed under Renovation and
Maintenance (R&M) or repairs and maintenance under O&M expenses, the same shall
not be claimed under these Regulations;
(f) Usage of water from sewage treatment plant in thermal generating station.
(2) In case of de-capitalisation of assets of a generating company or the transmission
licensee, as the case may be, the original cost of such asset as on the date of
decapitalisation shall be deducted from the value of gross fixed asset and
corresponding loan as well as equity shall be deducted from outstanding loan and the
equity respectively in the year such de-capitalisation takes place with corresponding
adjustments in cumulative depreciation and cumulative repayment of loan, duly taking
into consideration the year in which it was capitalised.”
Order in Petition No. 701/GT/2025 Page 8 of 62
7 01/GT/2025

15. The Petitioner has claimed additional capitalisation of Rs. 60.52 lakh in the year
2019-20 towards DDCMIS PG Test of Unit-1,2 &4 under Regulation 27 read with
Regulation 25(1)(f) in exercise to the Power to relax in terms of Regulation 76 of the
2019 Tariff Regulations. In justification, the Petitioner has submitted that the
Commission vide order dated 21.3.2017 in Petition No. 336/GT/2014 allowed Rs
40.00 lakh on account of PG Test of DDCMIS System, whose R&M was done in the
period 2009-14 and was approved earlier by the Commission in order dated
17.10.2012 in Petition No. 229/2009. The Petitioner has also submitted that the PG
test of DDCMIS could not be carried out during the period 2014-19 as M/s BHEL could
not mobilise the required resources for the same, and the work was finally carried out
successfully in the year 2019-20. Further, the Petitioner has submitted that the
variation between the projected and actual costs is due to a long-time gap between
the award and execution of the work; the projected cost of PG Test for the work was
based on the original awarded contract in the year 2010. The original contract had no
provision for GST in it, and the actual expenditure incurred and paid to BHEL was as
per the terms and conditions of the awarded contract and the imposition of GST.
16. The matter has been considered. It is observed that the order dated 21.3.2017
in Petition No. 336/GT/2014 had approved additional capital expenditure claimed
under this head amounting to Rs. 40.00 lakh, under Regulation 15 (1) of the 2014
Tariff Regulations, however the work could not be carried out during the period 2014-
19 as M/s BHEL could not mobilise required resources for the same, and the work
was finally carried out successfully in year 2019-20. Further, on a prudence check of
the justification submitted by the Petitioner regarding the variation in the projected and
actual cost, which was due to a long time gap between the award and execution of
Order in Petition No. 701/GT/2025 Page 11 of 62
7 01/GT/2025

the work, the expenditure is allowed under Regulation 25(1)(f) along with Regulation
27 of the 2019 Tariff Regulations.
Real Time Monitoring of AAQMS
17. The Petitioner has claimed additional capital expenditure of Rs. 7.24 lakh in
2019-20 under Regulation 26(1)(b) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations for Real Time
Monitoring of Ambient Air Quality Monitoring System (AAQMS). Since the additional
capital expenditure claimed under this head had already been approved by the
Commission vide order dated 17.4.2024 in Petition No. 445/GT/2020, in which the
Petitioner had furnished the CPCB letter dated 5.2.2014, directing the SPCBs/PCCs
to require highly polluting industries to install online effluent quality monitoring
systems. Accordingly, to comply with the said direction, the Petitioner has incurred
additional capital expenditure. Hence, the claim of the Petitioner is allowed under
Regulation 26(1)(b) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations.
Automatic Generation Control-AGC
18. The Petitioner has claimed additional capital expenditure of Rs.17.36 lakh,
Rs.0.91 lakh, and (-) Rs.0.50 lakh (cost adjustment) in 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-
24, respectively, towards the AGC system under Regulation 26(1)(b) of the 2019 Tariff
Regulations. In justification, the Petitioner has submitted that the said expenditure has
been claimed based on the directions of the Commission in its order dated 2.8.2019
in Petition No. 319/RC/2018.
19. The matter has been considered. It is observed that in an order dated 2.8.2019
in Petition No. 319/RC/2018, the Commission had directed as under:
“All thermal ISGS stations with installed capacity of 200 MW and above and all hydro
stations having capacity exceeding 25 MW excluding the Run-of-River Hydro Projects
irrespective of size of the generating station and whose tariff is determined or adopted
by CERC are directed to install equipment at the unit control rooms for transferring the
Order in Petition No. 701/GT/2025 Page 12 of 62
7 01/GT/2025

required data for AGC as per the requirement to be notified by NLDC. NLDC shall
notify the said requirements within one month of this order”
20. It is therefore evident that the additional capital expenditure claimed by the
Petitioner is for compliance to the above directions. This, according to us, is a change
in law event and therefore, the claim of the Petitioner is allowed under Regulation
26(1)(b) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations.
Gen. Relay Panel for 110 MW Unit 1&3
21. The Petitioner has claimed additional capital expenditure of Rs. 46.13 lakh and
Rs. 8.41 lakh in 2019-20 and 2020-21, respectively, towards Gen. Relay Panel for 110
MW Unit#1&3 under Regulation 25(2)(c) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations. Since the
additional capital expenditure claimed under this head had already been approved by
the Commission vide order dated 17.4.2024 in Petition No. 445/GT/2020, the same is
allowed. However, it is noticed that the Petitioner has not submitted the
decapitalisation value of the old asset, despite the directions vide order dated
17.4.2024 in Petition No. 445/GT/2020 to furnish the gross value of old replaced
assets. Accordingly, an assumed deletion has been considered in respect of the
claimed expenditure as mentioned in paragraph 58 of this order.
Online Energy Monitoring System
22. The Petitioner has claimed additional capitalisation of Rs. 14.60 lakh in the year
2019-20 under Regulation 26(1)(b) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations. The Petitioner has
submitted that the Online Energy Monitoring System was installed in compliance of
CEA (Installation & Operation of Meters), Regulations, 2006 at the instant station to
replace the obsolete Energy Monitoring System in order to monitor the Station
Auxiliary Power consumption of the generating station for optimisation of the same.
Order in Petition No. 701/GT/2025 Page 13 of 62
7 01/GT/2025

23. The matter has been examined. It is noticed that the Petitioner has also claimed
the same expenditure towards an online energy monitoring system under capital
spares, which are separately allowed under O&M expenses on a consumption basis.
Considering the nature of work, the same forms part of O&M expenses and is
considered under capital spares only. Hence, the same is not allowed under additional
capital expenditure.
ABT Upgradation
24. The Petitioner has claimed additional capitalisation of Rs. 19.83 lakh in the year
2020-21 under Regulation 25(2)(c) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations ABT upgradation.
The Petitioner has stated that the operating system of the ABT server was based on
Windows Server 2003, for which support in terms of software updates, security
patches, etc., was not available due to its obsolescence and end of life. Further, the
Petitioner has submitted that, to run and regulate the Station Load as per schedule on
a real-time basis, in line with the provisions of the latest DSM Regulations and Grid
Code, the ABT system was upgraded.
25. The matter has been examined. The Petitioner has submitted the lifecycle
policy of Windows Server 2003 by Microsoft regarding the declaration of obsolescence
and end of life of Windows Server 2003 (EOL July 2015). Since the expenditure is
claimed under regulation 25(2)(c) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations, considering the
submission of the Petitioner regarding the obsolescence and the necessary proof
attached, the expenditure is allowed. However, the Petitioner has not submitted the
decapitalisation value of the old asset; accordingly, an assumed deletion has been
considered in respect of the claimed expenditure as stated under paragraph 58.
Order in Petition No. 701/GT/2025 Page 14 of 62
7 01/GT/2025

Steam Generator (BHEL make 110MW) UNIT-1
26. The Petitioner has claimed additional capitalisation of Rs. 6.51 lakh in the year
2022-23 under Regulation 25(1)(a) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations towards a steam
generator in compliance with order of Dy. Commissioner, Commercial Tax, Govt. of
UP on 31.3.2022. The Petitioner has submitted that the above expenditure was
incurred in compliance with the order of the State Govt. of UP, through Dy.
Commissioner, Commercial Tax, while disposing of the matter of entry tax on the
machinery brought to plant premises during R&M of Units in the year 2003-04. The
initial order was passed on 31.3.2006, against which a revised order was passed on
30.7.2017. The final order with respect to the entry tax was settled by the order of Dy.
Commissioner, Commercial Tax. Govt. of UP on 31.3.2022. The Petitioner has
provided a copy of the challan dated 27.3.2023, deposited with the Department of
Commercial Tax, Govt. of UP, treasury.
