ORDER
The Petitioner, Adani Energy Solutions Limited (hereinafter referred to as “the
Petitioner”) and KPS III HVDC Transmission Limited (herein after referred to as “ Co-
Petitioner”) have filed the present Petition under Sections14 and 15 of the Electricity
Act, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as “the Act”) read with the Central Electricity
Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for Grant of
Transmission License and other related matters) Regulations, 2024 (hereinafter
Order in Petition No. 27/TL/2026 Page 2

referred to as “the 2024 Transmission Licence Regulations”) for the grant of
transmission licence to establish the transmission project for “Transmission System
for Evacuation of Power from potential renewable energy zone in Khavda area of
Gujarat under Phase-V (8 GW): Part C” on a Build, Own, Operate and Transfer
Basis (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) consisting of following elements:
S. No. Name of the Transmission Element Scheduled COD
in months from
Effective Date
1. Establishment of 2500 MW, ± 500 kV KPS3
(HVDC) [VSC] terminal station (2x1250 MW) at a
suitable location near KPS3 substation with
associated interconnections with 400 kV HVAC
Switchyard*
2. Establishment of 2500 MW, ± 500 kV South
Olpad (HVDC) [VSC] terminal station (2x1250
MW) along with associated interconnections with
400 kV HVAC Switchyard of South Olpad S/s*
3. Establishment of KPS3 (HVDC) S/s along with
2x125 MVAR, 420 kV bus reactors along with
associated interconnections with HVDC 48 months from
Switchyard*. The 400kV bus shall be established in SPV transfer
2 sections through 1 set of 400 kV bus
sectionaliser to be kept normally OPEN. 400/33 kV,
2x50 MVA transformers for exclusively supplying
auxiliary power to HVDC terminal.
4. KPS3 - KPS3 (HVDC) 400 kV 2xD/C (Quad
ACSR/AAAC/AL59 moose equivalent) line along
with the line bays at both substations
5. ±500 kV HVDC Bipole line between KPS3
(HVDC) and South Olpad (HVDC) (with
Dedicated Metallic Return) (capable to evacuate
2500 MW)
*The 400 kV interconnections (along with all associated equipment/ bus extension, etc.)
between HVDC and HVAC switch yards shall be implemented by the TSP.
Note:
i. The 1250 MW pole-1 shall emanate from 400 kV bus section 1 of KPS3 (HVDC) and
terminate at South Olpad S/s. Similarly, the 1250 MW pole-2 shall emanate from 400 kV
bus section 2 of KPS3 (HVDC) and terminate at South Olpad S/s.
ii. HVDC System will be designed with 100% power reversal capability as well as black
start, automatic grid restoration and dynamic reactive power support capability.
iii. The rated power transmission capacity as well as the rated transmission voltage shall
be defined and guaranteed at the rectifier DC Bus.
Order in Petition No. 27/TL/2026 Page 3

iv. TSPs of KPS3 shall provide space for scope at Sl. No. 4 as per the above scope.
v. TSP of South Olpad S/s shall provide space for scope at Sl. No. 2 as per above scope
ensuring:
(a) indicative total space requirement for HVDC terminal station of size 400 m x 300 m.
The AC switchyard connection and DC overhead line shall be from 300 m side of
rectangular plot.
(b) the width of the approach road and access road shall be at least 10 m for
facilitating smooth transportation of HVDC equipment including converter
transformer and with access road all around the space for HVDC.
(c) the spatial arrangement for proposed space for HVDC terminal and the layout
proposed for the current AC GIS transmission scheme is such that Bus duct length
required for interconnection between AC GIS station and HVDC terminal is
minimum to the extent possible in linear manner and the layout of the AC line
termination gantries should be such that there is no crossing of present/ future AC
lines and HVDC line near the termination ends of both AC and HVDC yards.
vi. Implementation timeline: 48 months from SPV transfer.”
2. Based on the competitive bidding carried out by the PFC Consulting Limited
(PFCCL), in its capacity as the Bid Process Coordinator (BPC), in accordance with
the Guidelines issued by the Ministry of Power, Government of India under Section
63 of the Act, Adani Energy Solutions Limited was declared a successful bidder with
the lowest quoted annual transmission charges of Rs. 23,917.69 million per annum.
3. The Commission, after considering the application of the Petitioner in light of
the provisions of the Act and the Transmission Licence Regulations, in its order
dated 9.5.2026, prima facie proposed to grant a transmission licence to the
Petitioner. The relevant extracts of the order dated 9.5.2026 are extracted as under:
“34. Considering the material on record, we are prima facie of the view that
the co-Petitioner, KPS III HVDC Transmission Limited, satisfies the conditions
for the grant of an inter-State transmission licence under Section 15 of the
Act, read with the Transmission Licence Regulations for construction,
operation, and maintenance of the transmission system as described in para
1 of this order. We, therefore, direct that a public notice in two daily digital
newspapers and on the Commission`s website under clause (a) of sub-
section (5) of Section 15 of the Act be published to invite suggestions or
objections to the grant of a transmission licence aforesaid. The objections or
suggestions, if any, shall be filed by any person before the Commission by
18.5.2026.”
Order in Petition No. 27/TL/2026 Page 4

4. A public notice under Sub-section (5) of Section 15 of the Act was published
in all editions of The Hindu (English) and Amar Ujala (Hindi) on 13.5.2026. No
suggestions/ objections have been received from members of the public in response
to the public notice.
Hearing dated 19.5.2026
5. The matter was called out for the hearing on 19.5.2026. During the course of
the hearing, the representative of the Petitioner submitted that no objection had been
received in response to the public notice published by the Commission under sub-
section (5) of Section 15 of the Act.
6. As regards the grant of a transmission licence, Clauses (13) and (14) of
Regulation 5 of the 2024 Transmission Licence Regulations provide as under:
“(13) The Commission may, after consideration of the further suggestions
and objections, if any, received in response to the public notice in terms of
Clause (12) of this Regulation, grant licence to the applicant in Form-III
appended to these regulations or for reasons to be recorded in writing,
reject the application.
(14) The Commission shall before granting licence or rejecting the
application under the provisions of this Regulation provide an opportunity of
hearing to the applicant, CTUIL, the concerned DICs, or the person who
has filed suggestions and objections, or any other interested person.”
7. In our order dated 9.5.2026, we had proposed to grant a transmission licence
to the Petitioner company and directed the issue of public notice. In response to the
public notice, no suggestions/ objections have been received. CTUIL, in its letter
dated 22.12.2025, has recommended granting a transmission licence to the
Petitioner. We find that the Petitioner company meets the requirements of the Act
and the Transmission Licence Regulations, 2024, for the grant of a transmission
licence for the subject Transmission System mentioned in paragraph 1 of this order.
Order in Petition No. 27/TL/2026 Page 5

Considering the submissions of the Petitioner and CTUIL, we direct that a
transmission licence be granted to the Petitioner, KPS III HVDC Transmission
Limited, to establish the transmission project for “Transmission System for
Evacuation of Power from potential renewable energy zone in Khavda area of
Gujarat under Phase-V (8 GW): Part C” on a Build, Own, Operate and Transfer basis
as per the details given in paragraph 1 above.
8. The grant of the transmission licence to the Petitioner (hereinafter referred to
as “the licensee”) is subject to the fulfilment of the following conditions throughout
the period of the licence:
(a) The transmission licence shall, unless revoked earlier, remain in force for
a period of 25 years from the date of issue;
(b) The transmission licensee shall comply with the provisions of the Central
Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms, and Conditions for
grant of Transmission Licence and other related matters) Regulations,
2024 or any subsequent enactment thereof during the period of
subsistence of the licence;
(c) The licensee may make an application, two years before the expiry of the
initial licence period, for the grant of the transmission licence for another
term in accordance with Regulation 9 (2) of the 2024 Transmission
Licence Regulations, which shall be considered by the Commission in
accordance with law;
Order in Petition No. 27/TL/2026 Page 6

(d) The licensee shall not enter into any contract for or otherwise engage in
the business of trading in electricity during the period of subsistence of
the transmission licence;
(e) The licensee shall have the liability to pay the license fee in accordance
with the provisions of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission
(Payment of Fees) Regulations, 2012, as amended from time to time or
any subsequent enactment thereof. Delay in payment or non-payment of
the licence fee or a part thereof for a period exceeding sixty days shall be
construed as a breach of the terms and conditions of the licence;
(f) The licensee shall comply with the directions of the National Load
Despatch Centre under Section 26 of the Act, or the Regional Load
Despatch Centre under sub-section (3) of Section 28 or sub-section (1) of
Section 29 of the Act, as may be issued from time to time for maintaining
the availability of the transmission system;
(g) The licensee shall remain bound by the provisions of the Central
Electricity Regulatory Commission (Standard of Performance of inter-
State transmission licensees) Regulations, 2012 or subsequent
enactment thereof;
(h) The licensee shall provide the non-discriminatory open access to its
Transmission System for use by any other licensee, including a
distribution licensee or an electricity trader, or generating company or any
other person in accordance with the Act; the Central Electricity Regulatory
Commission (Open Access in inter-State Transmission) Regulations,
Order in Petition No. 27/TL/2026 Page 7

2008; the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and
General Network Access to the inter-State Transmission System)
Regulations, 2023; the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Indian
Electricity Grid Code) Regulations, 2023, as amended from time to time
or any subsequent re-enactments thereof;
(i) The licensee shall not undertake any other business for optimum
utilisation of the Transmission System without prior intimation to the
Commission and shall comply with the provisions of the Central Electricity
Regulatory Commission (Sharing of Revenue Derived from Utilization of
Transmission Assets for other business) Regulations, 2020;
(j) The licensee shall remain bound by provisions of the Central Electricity
Regulatory Commission (Sharing of inter-State Transmission Charges
and Losses) Regulations, 2020, as amended from time to time;
(k) The licensee shall remain bound by the provisions of the Act, the Rules
and Regulations framed thereunder, in particular the 2024 Transmission
Licence Regulations, the Grid Code, the Standards specified by the
Central Electricity Authority, orders and directions of the Commission
issued from time to time;
(l) The licensee shall ensure the execution of the Project as per the
Technical Standards and Grid Standards of CEA;
(m) The licensee shall submit all such reports or information as may be
required under 2024 Transmission Licence Regulations, Standard of
Order in Petition No. 27/TL/2026 Page 8

Performance Regulations or any other regulation of the Commission or as
per the directions of the Commission as may be issued from time to time;
(n) The licensee shall ensure that the EPC contract for the execution of work
under the scope of the project is awarded through a competitive bidding
process.
9. CTUIL and the Central Electricity Authority shall monitor the execution of the
Project and bring to the Commission's notice any lapse on the part of the licensee in
meeting the schedule for further appropriate action in accordance with the provisions
of the Transmission Service Agreement executed between the licensee and the
Nodal Agency, the Act, and the Transmission Licence Regulations.
10. It is expected that while carrying out the survey, the Petitioner has complied
with the provisions of clauses 2.5.7.3, 2.5.7.4, and 2.5.7.5 of the RfP. The Petitioner
will comply with the provisions of the bidding documents and the TSA for the
commissioning of the Project within the SCOD in letter and spirit.
11. An extract copy of this order is to be sent to CTUIL, CEA, and BPC for
information and necessary action.
12. Petition No. 27/TL/2026 is allowed in terms of the above.
Sd/- sd/- sd/- sd/-

ORDER
The instant Petition has been filed by Power Grid Corporation of India Limited
(PGCIL) (hereinafter referred to as “the Petitioner”), a deemed transmission licensee,
for the truing up of the transmission tariff for the 2019-24 period under the Central
Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2019
(hereinafter referred to as “the 2019 Tariff Regulations”) and the determination of the
transmission tariff for the 2024-29 period under the Central Electricity Regulatory
Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2024 (hereinafter referred to
as “the 2024 Tariff Regulations”) in respect of the following assets under “Northern
Region System Strengthening Scheme-XVIII” in the Northern Region (hereinafter
referred to as “the transmission project”):
Asset-I: Combined Assets: One circuit of 400 kV D/C Dehradun-Bagpat Line along
with associated bays at both ends. Part of the second circuit of 400 kV D/C Dehradun-
Bagpat Transmission Line as 400 kV S/C Roorkee-Dehradun Line from Dehradun
end and partly as 400 kV S/C Saharanpur-Bagpat Line from Bagpat end using part
of one circuit of 400 kV D/C Roorkee-Saharanpur Line (under-NRSS XXI) at
intersection point along with associated bays at Dehradun and Bagpat end;
Asset-II: 400/220 kV, 315 MVA ICT-I at Dehradun and associated bays with 1
number 220 kV line bay, 400/220 kV, 315 MVA ICT-II at Dehradun and associated
bays with 1 number 220 kV line bay, and 80 MVAr bus reactor at Dehradun and
associated bays; and
Asset-III: 4 number 220 kV bays at Dehradun Substation.
Order in Petition No. 561/TT/2025 Page 3 of 74

The Petitioner has combined Assets I, II, and III during the 2019-24 tariff period and
claimed a combined tariff, and as such has termed them ‘Combined Assets’ for the
2019-24 and 2024-29 tariff periods. However, we have allowed individual tariffs for
Assets I, II and III and termed them jointly as the “transmission assets” in this order for
the 2019-24 and 2024-29 tariff periods. The reasons for doing so are mentioned in the
subsequent paragraph of this order.
2. The Petitioner has made the following prayers in the instant Petition:
“a) Approve the trued-up Transmission Tariff for 2019-24 block and transmission tariff
for 2024-29 block for the asset covered under this petition, as per para 16 and 17 above.
b) Admit the capital cost claimed and additional capitalization incurred during 2019-24
and projected additional capitalization to be incurred during 2024-29.
c) Allow the petitioner to recover the shortfall or refund the excess Annual Fixed
Charges, on account of Return on Equity due to change in applicable Minimum
Alternate/Corporate Income Tax rate as per the Income Tax Act, 1961 (as amended
from time to time) of the respective financial year directly without making any application
before the Commission as provided in Tariff Regulations, 2019 and Tariff Regulations,
2024 as per para 16 and 17 above for respective block.
d) Approve the reimbursement of expenditure by the beneficiaries towards petition filing
fee, and expenditure on publishing of notices in newspapers in terms of Regulation 94
(1) Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff)
Regulations, 2024, and other expenditure (if any) in relation to the filing of petition.
e) Allow the petitioner to bill and recover RLDC fees & charges and Licensee fee,
separately from the respondents in terms of Regulation 94 (3) and (4) Central Electricity
Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2024.
f) Allow the petitioner to bill and adjust impact on Interest on Loan due to change in
Interest rate on account of floating rate of interest applicable during 2024-29 period, if
any, from the respondents.
g) Allow the petitioner to file a separate petition before the Commission for claiming the
overall security expenses and consequential IOWC on that security expenses as
mentioned at para 24 above.
h) Allow the petitioner to file a separate petition before the Commission for claiming the
overall insurance expenses and consequential IOWC on that insurance expenses as
mentioned at para 24 above.
i) Allow the petitioner to file a separate petition before the Commission for claiming the
overall capital spares at the end of tariff block as per actual as mentioned at Para 24
above.
j) Allow the petitioner to claim expenses of CTUIL borne by POWERGRID through a
separate petition as mentioned at para 25 above.
Order in Petition No. 561/TT/2025 Page 4 of 74

k) Allow the Petitioner to bill and recover GST on Transmission Charges separately from
the respondents, if GST on transmission is levied at any rate in future. Further, any taxes
including GST and duties including cess etc. imposed by any statutory/Govt./municipal
authorities shall be allowed to be recovered from the beneficiaries and
l) Allow to continue the recovery of annuity payment being done for State Forest
Authority directly from the beneficiaries as allowed by the Commission vide order dated
31.03.2021 in Petition No. 104/TT/2020.
m) Pass such other relief as the Commission deems fit and appropriate under the
circumstances of the case and in the interest of justice.”
Background
3. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
a. The Investment Approval (the IA) and expenditure sanction for the
transmission project were accorded by the Board of Directors of the Petitioner

price level. Subsequently, the Revised Estimate Cost (RCE) for the transmission
project was approved by the Board of Directors of the Petitioner at its 339th
meeting held on 29.3.2017, and conveyed vide Memorandum dated 31.3.2017,
with an estimated cost of ₹84166 lakh, including the IDC of ₹17620 lakh, based
on the October 2016 price level.
b. The scope of the transmission project is as follows:

tariff for Asset-III vide order dated 30.11.2017 in Petition No. 55/TT/2017, filed
Order in Petition No. 561/TT/2025 Page 6 of 74

Review Petition No. 8/RP/2018 seeking approval of the COD and tariff for
Asset-III in terms of the proviso (ii) to Regulation 4(3) of the Central Electricity
Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2014
(hereinafter referred to as “the 2014 Tariff Regulations”), and for allowing the
annuity paid by the Petitioner to the Forest Department for 35 years as per
the Relief and Rehabilitation Policy of the Government of Uttar Pradesh. The
Commission, vide its order dated 12.6.2018, disposed of Review Petition No.
8/RP/2018, rejecting the prayer for approval of the COD of Asset-III,
reiterating its earlier observations, and directed the Petitioner to raise the
issue of annuity at the time of filing the tariff Petition for Asset-III, matching
the COD of the downstream transmission system of PTCUL.
g. The Commission, vide order dated 31.3.2021 in Petition No. 104/TT/2020,
approved the COD of Asset-III under proviso (ii) to Regulation 4(3) of the
2014 Tariff Regulations, trued up the Annual Fixed Charges (AFC) for the
transmission assets for the 2014-19 tariff period, and determined the AFC for
the 2019-24 tariff period for the Combined Assets.
4. The Respondents are the distribution and transmission licensees and the power
departments, mainly the beneficiaries of the Northern Region, that are procuring
transmission services from the Petitioner.
5. The Petitioner has served a copy of the Petition on the Respondents and notices
regarding the filing of this Petition have been published in the newspapers in
accordance with Section 64 of the Electricity Act, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as “the
Act”). No comments or suggestions have been received from the general public in
response to the aforesaid notices published in the newspapers by the Petitioner. PTCUL
has filed its reply to the Petition vide affidavit dated 22.1.2026.
Order in Petition No. 561/TT/2025 Page 7 of 74

6. The hearing in this matter was held on 17.2.2026, and the order was reserved.
7. This order is issued considering the submissions made by the Petitioner vide
affidavits dated 8.11.2024, 13.11.2025, 24.12.2025 and 3.3.2026; reply filed by PTCUL
vide affidavit dated 22.1.2026, and the rejoinder filed by the Petitioner to the reply of
PTCUL vide affidavit dated 2.3.2026.
8. Having heard the parties and perused the material available on record, we
proceed to dispose of the Petition.
9. It is observed that the Petitioner has claimed the AFC, subsequent capital cost
and the Additional Capital Expenditure (ACE) in respect of the Combined Assets for
truing up of the tariff for the 2019-24 tariff period and the determination of the tariff for
the 2024-29 tariff period.
10. The Commission, vide Record of Proceedings (RoP) dated 17.2.2026, observed
that according to the Petitioner, the downstream network associated with Asset-III,
owned by PTCUL, is yet to be commissioned, and sought clarification on how Asset-III
has been combined with the other assets to claim the AFC in the instant Petition.
11. In response, the Petitioner, vide affidavit dated 3.3.2026, has submitted that the
Commission, vide order dated 31.3.2021 in Petition No. 104/TT/2020, had approved the
capital cost and the transmission tariff for the 2019–24 tariff period for the Combined
Assets under the transmission project and the same has been duly considered while
filing this truing-up Petition for the 2019–24 tariff period as well as the tariff Petition for
the 2024–29 tariff period.
12. We have considered the Petitioner’s submissions. The Commission, vide order
dated 31.3.2021 in Petition No. 104/TT/2020, approved the COD of Asset-III as
4.2.2017 under proviso (ii) to Regulation 4(3) of the 2014 Tariff Regulations and trued
up the AFC for the 2014-19 tariff period. The Commission, vide order dated 31.3.2021,
Order in Petition No. 561/TT/2025 Page 8 of 74

also directed the Petitioner and PTCUL to explore the possibility of using the existing
unutilised bays for the 220 kV D/C Mori-Dehradun Transmission Line, with suitable
modifications, if required, rather than constructing new bays. Once Asset-III is put to
use for the 220 kV D/C Mori-Dehradun Transmission Line or for any other purpose, the
tariff for the asset will be recovered from the PoC pool. The Petitioner, vide affidavit
dated 3.3.2026, has submitted that Asset-III remains unutilised and has not been put to
use because the downstream transmission system owned by PTCUL is yet to be
commissioned.
13. In light of the above discussions, we are of the view that the transmission assets
ought not to be combined for the purpose of truing up the AFC for the 2019-24 tariff
period and for determining the AFC for the 2024-29 tariff period, as the downstream
transmission system owned by PTCUL, associated with Asset-III, is yet to be
commissioned and Asset-III remains unutilised. Accordingly, in the instant order, the
truing up of the tariff for the 2019-24 tariff period and the determination of the tariff for
the 2024-29 tariff period are done on an individual asset basis, rather than for the
Combined Assets.

23. The Petitioner, vide affidavit dated 24.12.2025, has submitted that the
Commission, vide order dated 31.3.2021 in Petition No. 104/TT/2020, disallowed the
excess Initial Spares amounting to ₹21.45 lakh for Asset-I under the head Transmission
Line. Further, Initial Spares for the transmission project claimed are within the limit
specified under Regulation 13 of the 2014 Tariff Regulations and the restricted Initial
Spares of ₹21.45 lakh under Transmission Line have been added back in the opening

capital cost as on 1.4.2019 for the 2019-24 tariff period. The Petitioner has prayed to
allow the Initial Spares as claimed in the present Petition.
24. We have considered the Petitioner’s submissions. The Appellate Tribunal for
Electricity (APTEL), in its judgement dated 14.9.2019 in Appeal No. 74 of 2017,
observed that, for the purpose of a prudence check, the Commission may restrict Initial
Spares to the cost of the individual asset, and later, at the time of truing up, the Initial
Spares shall be allowed as per the overall project cost. The relevant portion of the
judgment dated 14.9.2019 is extracted hereunder:
“8.13. ……… We do not agree with this methodology of restricting initial spares asset
/ element wise as adopted by the Central Commission. The Central Commission to
have a prudence check on the initial spares, being restricted based on the individual
asset wise cost initially, but subsequently ought to have allowed as per the ceiling limits
on the overall project cost basis during the true-up.”
25. Therefore, in accordance with the APTEL’s aforesaid judgment dated 14.9.2019,
the Initial Spares are to be allowed as per the norms on the overall project cost. The
overall project cost of the transmission assets can ideally be arrived at only when the
transmission assets are combined. However, as noted above in this order, Asset-III has
not yet been put to regular use. Further, in this order, the truing up of the AFC for the
2019-24 tariff period concerning the transmission assets is allowed on an individual
basis, not on a combined basis.
26. In view of the above, it is observed that the Initial Spares are not required to be
recalculated based on the overall project cost, in accordance with APTEL’s judgment
dated 14.9.2019 for the 2019-24 tariff period. Accordingly, the Petitioner’s claim for
adding back the additional Initial Spares of ₹21.44 lakh based on the overall project cost
is hereby rejected.

Act, 1961. Section 115 JB (2) of the IT Act, 1961, defines book profit as the net profit in
the Statement of Profit and Loss prepared in accordance with Schedule-III of the
Companies Act, 2013, subject to some additions and deductions as mentioned in the IT
Act, 1961. Since the Petitioner has been paying the MAT rates of the respective financial
years, the notified MAT rates for the respective financial years shall be considered as

(1) The additional capital expenditure in respect of a new project or an existing

scope of work, after the date of commercial operation and up to the cut-off date may be
admitted by the Commission, subject to prudence check:
(a) Payment made towards admitted liabilities for works executed up to the
cut-off date;
(b) Works deferred for execution;
(c) Procurement of initial capital spares within the original scope of work, in
accordance with the provisions of Regulation 23 of these regulations;
(d) Payment against the award of arbitration or for compliance with the
directions or order of any statutory authority or order or decree of any court
of law;
(e) Change in law or compliance with any existing law which is not provided
for in the original scope of work;
(f) For uninterrupted and timely development of Hydro projects, expenditure
incurred towards developing local infrastructure in the vicinity of the power
plant not exceeding Rs. 10 lakh/MW shall be considered as part of capital
cost and in case the same work is covered under budgetary support
provided by Government of India, the funding of such works shall be
adjusted on receipt of such funds;
Provided that such expenditure shall be allowed only if the expenditure
is incurred through Indian Governmental Instrumentality; and
(g) Force Majeure events.
Provided that in case of any replacement of the assets, the additional capitalization
shall be worked out after adjusting the gross fixed assets and cumulative depreciation of

67. Regulation 18 of the 2024 Tariff Regulations provides as follows:
“18. Debt-Equity Ratio: (1) For new projects, the debt-equity ratio of 70:30 as

treated as normative loan:
Provided that:
i. where equity actually deployed is less than 30% of the capital cost, actual
equity shall be considered for determination of tariff:
ii. the equity invested in foreign currency shall be designated in Indian
rupees on the date of each investment:
iii. any grant obtained for the execution of the project shall not be considered
as a part of capital structure for the purpose of debt: equity ratio.
Explanation.-The premium, if any, raised by the generating company or the
transmission licensee, as the case may be, while issuing share capital and
investment of internal resources created out of its free reserve for the funding of
the project, shall be reckoned as paid up capital for the purpose of computing
return on equity, only if such premium amount and internal resources are actually
utilised for meeting the capital expenditure of the generating station or the
transmission system.
(2) The generating company or the transmission licensee, as the case may be,
shall submit the resolution of the Board of the company or the approval of the
competent authority in other cases regarding the infusion of funds from internal
resources in support of the utilization made or proposed to be made to meet the
capital expenditure of the generating station or the transmission system including
communication system, as the case may be.

69. Regulation 33 of the 2024 Tariff Regulations provides as follows:
"33. Depreciation: (1) Depreciation shall be computed from the date of commercial
operation of a generating station or unit thereof or a transmission system or element
thereof including communication system. In the case of the tariff of all the units of a
generating station or all elements of a transmission system including the
communication system for which a single tariff needs to be determined, the
depreciation shall be computed from the effective date of commercial operation of
the generating station or the transmission system taking into consideration the
depreciation of individual units:
Provided that the effective date of commercial operation shall be worked
out by considering the actual date of commercial operation and installed capacity of
all the units of the generating station or capital cost of all elements of the
transmission system, for which a single tariff needs to be determined.
(2) The value base for the purpose of depreciation shall be the capital cost of the
asset admitted by the Commission. In case of multiple units of a generating station
or multiple elements of a transmission system, the weighted average life for the
generating station or the transmission system shall be applied. Depreciation shall be
chargeable from the first year of commercial operation. In the case of commercial
operation of the asset for a part of the year, depreciation shall be charged on a pro
rata basis.
(3) The salvage value of the asset shall be considered as 10%, and depreciation
shall be allowed up to the maximum of 90% of the capital cost of the asset:
Provided that the salvage value for IT equipment and software shall be
considered as NIL and 100% value of the assets shall be considered depreciable;
……….
Provided also that any depreciation disallowed on account of lower
availability of the generating station or unit or transmission system, as the case may
be, shall not be allowed to be recovered at a later stage during the useful life or the
extended life.
(4) …………
Order in Petition No. 561/TT/2025 Page 39 of 74

(5) Depreciation for Existing Projects shall be calculated annually based on the
Straight Line Method and at rates specified in Appendix-I to these regulations for the
assets of the generating station and transmission system:
Provided that the remaining depreciable value as on 31st March of the
year closing after a period of 12 years from the effective date of commercial
operation of the generating station or transmission system, as the case may be, shall
be spread over the balance useful life of the assets;
………
(6) Depreciation for New Projects shall be calculated annually based on the Straight
Line Method and at rates specified in Appendix-II to these regulations for the assets
of the generating station and transmission system:
Provided that the remaining depreciable value as on 31st March of the
year closing after a period of 15 years from the effective date of commercial
operation of the generating station or the transmission system, as the case may be,
shall be spread over the balance useful life of the assets;
…………
(7) In the case of the existing projects, the balance depreciable value as on 1.4.2024
shall be worked out by deducting the cumulative depreciation as admitted to by the
Commission up to 31.3.2024 from the gross depreciable value of the assets.
(8) The generating company or the transmission licensee, as the case may be, shall
submit the details of capital expenditure proposed to be incurred during five years
before the completion of useful life along with proper justification and proposed life
extension. The Commission, based on prudence check of such submissions, shall
approve the depreciation by equally spreading the depreciable value over the
balance Operational Life of the generating station or unit thereof or fifteen years,
whichever is lower, and in case of the transmission system shall equally spread the
depreciable value over the balance useful life of the Asset or 10 years whichever is
higher.
(9) In case of de-capitalization of assets in respect of generating station or unit
thereof or transmission system or element thereof, the cumulative depreciation shall
be adjusted by taking into account the depreciation recovered in tariff by the de-
capitalised asset during its useful service.

worked out for the transmission assets as per the rates of depreciation specified in the
2024 Tariff Regulations. The transmission assets shall complete 12 years of their useful

ORDER
The Petitioners, Indian Energy Exchange Limited (IEX), Power Exchange India
Limited (PXIL) and Hindustan Power Exchange Limited (HPX), have filed the present
Petitions under Section 66 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and in compliance with the
directions issued by the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) vide
Order dated 28.04.2025 in Suo-motu Petition No. 08/SM/2024, seeking approval of
the pre-specified slots in the Term Ahead Market (TAM), Green Term Ahead Market
(G-TAM) and High Price Term Ahead Market (HP-TAM) on their respective Exchange
Platforms.
2. The Petitioners have made the following prayers:
In Petition No. 674/RC/2025
a. Consider the pre-specified time slots as proposed in para 8(e) for TAM, HPTAM
and GTAM.
b. Approve the pre-specified time slots uniformly at all the Power Exchanges.
c. Pass such further order or orders as may be considered necessary in the facts
and circumstances of the case.
In Petition No. 754/RC/2025
a. Grant approval for the time slots as detailed in paragraphs 11 and 12 of this
Petition.
b. Pass any such other relief(s)/ Order(s) that this Hon’ble Commission may deem
fit.
In Petition No. 753/RC/2025
a. Allow the present petition;
Order in Petition Nos. 674/RC/2025, 754/RC/2025 & 753/RC/2025 Page 3 of 25

b. Approve the pre-specified time slots as proposed in Para 10 and 11 of this
Petition for trading of contracts in Term Ahead Market (TAM), Green Term
Ahead Market (GTAM), and High Price Term Ahead Market (HPTAM) at the
Petitioner’s Exchange platform;
c. Pass such other and further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit
and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case and in the interest
of justice.
Submissions of the Petitioner(s):
In Petition No. 674/RC/2025
3. The Petitioner, Indian Energy Exchange Limited (IEX), was granted permission
to set up, operate and commence exchange operations vide Commission’s order
dated 31.08.2007 and 09.06.2008 and has been in operation since 27.06.2008.
4. The Commission has issued the following directions to the Power Exchanges
vide Order dated 28.04.2025 in Petition No. 08/SM/2024 with respect to changes in
the Intra-day (ITD), Day Ahead Contingency (DAC) and the Term Ahead Contracts
(TAM) (including Any Day Single-Sided (ADSS)) in their Power Exchanges as under:
“32. Therefore, the Commission directs the power exchanges to discontinue the
provision of user-defined time slots (including hourly slots), in TAM, including
Green TAM and High-Price TAM, within a week from the date of this order. The
power exchanges shall allow only the established pre-specified slots on the
exchange platform for TAM contracts, including Green TAM and High-Price
TAM. However, all such contracts traded before the date of this Order shall
continue to be valid.
33. On the second issue of different durations of established pre-specified time
slots to be allowed on the power exchanges, we have considered the concerns
raised by some of the stakeholders regarding varying peak periods, load
profiles, and generation portfolio mix across different states. Accordingly, we
direct the power exchanges as under:
(i) For TAM and HP-TAM: Power exchanges to carry out consultation
with market participants on the selection of pre-specified time slots from
within RTC, Peak/Off-Peak hour, Solar/Non-Solar hour, Day/Night, that
they propose to notify on their respective platforms. Post consultation,
the power exchanges shall approach the Commission for approval on
the pre-specified slots, within a month from the date of this Order.
Order in Petition Nos. 674/RC/2025, 754/RC/2025 & 753/RC/2025 Page 4 of 25

(ii) For G-TAM: Power exchanges to carry out consultation with market
participants on the selection of pre-specified time slots based on the
generation profile of different technologies. Post consultation, the power
exchanges shall approach the Commission for approval on the pre-
specified slots, within a month from the date of this Order.
34. The Commission also directs the NLDC to declare the timings of the Solar/
Non-Solar hours at regular intervals. With regard to Peak/Off-Peak hours, the
CERC Tariff Regulations 2024-29 provide for the declaration of region-wise
peak and off-peak hours at regular intervals by the respective RLDCs.
…”
5. The Petitioner has submitted the compliance report, vide affidavit dated
05.05.2025, with respect to directions in para 32, 38, 41(a), 41(b), 47(b), 47(c) and 62
of the order dated 28.04.2025 in Petition No. 08/SM/2024.
6. The petitioner has made the present submission in compliance with the
directions issued in para 33(i) and 33(ii) w.r.t pre-specified time slots in TAM, HPTAM
and GTAM segments at IEX.
7. The Petitioner proposed the pre-specified time slots for TAM, HP-TAM and GTAM
(Hydro) vide Public Notice dated 13.05.2025, as under:
S. No. Contract Delivery Hours
1 Peak 18-24 hrs.
2 Night 00-06 hrs.
3 Morning 06-09 hrs.
4 Day 09-18 hrs.
5 Solar 06-18 hrs.
6 Non-solar 00-06, 18-24 hrs.
7 RTC 00-24 hrs.
8. The Petitioner proposed the above slots based on the trend observed in the
Market Clearing Price (MCP) of the Day Ahead Market (DAM) at IEX v/s the national
net demand during FY 2024-25. The Petitioner presented trend analysis of hourly
weighted average MCP (Rs./unit) in DAM and the hourly average net demand (GW)
of the country at the national level during FY 2024-25, which shows that the average
prices in the DAM largely peaks when the national net demand peaks, and the prices
reduce when the net demand is at a declining trajectory during the day. The Petitioner
Order in Petition Nos. 674/RC/2025, 754/RC/2025 & 753/RC/2025 Page 5 of 25

has submitted that the two follow each other and are reflective of the market scenario
as far as the demand-supply patterns are concerned.
9. Based on the observed demand and price behaviour, the Petitioner proposed
various time slots as under:
• Peak slot proposed by Petitioner is 18-24 hours, as the average peak price
when the demand is consistently high, i.e., for 18-24 hours, is observed to
be Rs. 6.3/unit.
• Night slot proposed by the Petitioner is for hours that have a declining
trend of net demand and prices, i.e., 00-06 hrs. Average prices during these
hours are observed to be Rs. 3.9/unit.
• Morning slot is proposed to be during 06-09 hours. As in this time period,
net demand starts to increase along with the commencement of RE
generation and the reduction of baseload generation. The average price
starts to increase and is observed at Rs. 4.6/unit.
• Day slot is proposed to be during 09-18 hours. The net demand is at its
lowest, with the lowest average market price at Rs. 3.3/unit once the RE
generation peaks.
• Solar slot is proposed as 06-18 hours.
• Non-solar slot as 00-06 & 18-24 hours, in line with the present designation
by the Grid-India in their daily Power Supply Position report.
10. In compliance with the direction of the Commission, the Petitioner issued public
notice on 13.05.2025, inviting suggestions from the stakeholders by 22.05.2025, on
the selection of pre-specified time slots from within RTC, Peak/Off-Peak hour,
Solar/Non-Solar hour, Day/Night, that it proposes to notify on its platform. At the
request of stakeholders, the due date for receiving suggestions was extended to
26.05.2025.
11. In response to the Petitioner’s notice, suggestions were received from the
following stakeholders:
(i) Shree Cement Limited
Order in Petition Nos. 674/RC/2025, 754/RC/2025 & 753/RC/2025 Page 6 of 25

(ii) Noida Power Company Limited (NPCL)
(iii) Jammu & Kashmir SLDC (JKSLDC)
(iv) Rajasthan Urja Vikas & IT Services Limited (RUVITL)
(v) Punjab State Power Corporation Limited (PSPCL)
(vi) DB Power Limited (DBPL)
(vii) Andhra Pradesh Transco & Discoms
(viii) BSES Yamuna Power Limited (BYPL)
(ix) BSES Rajdhani Power Limited (BRPL)
(x) UP Power Corporation Limited (UPPCL)
12. The suggestions from the above stakeholders on pre-specified time slots
proposed by Petitioner are summarised as under:
a) “Peak hours” be different for summers and winters.
b) “Peak hours” be bifurcated into “evening peak” (18-24 hrs) and “late-night peak”
(00-03 hrs).
c) DISCOMS should be allowed to customise RTC blocks for better operational
flexibility.
d) Time slots be configured region-wise (North, South, East, West, North-east)
and reviewed annually based on demand patterns and seasonal variations.
e) BESS facilities should be allowed to participate in non-solar hours.
f) Flexibility to power exchanges/ market participants to define contract hours/
custom-delivery slots.
g) UPPCL has opposed the removal of user-defined time-slots in TAM, HPTAM,
as it would affect their state’s diverse needs. It would lead to greater reliance
on RTM purchases, increasing their financial risk. A hybrid approach, limited,
user-defined slots can help support liquidity and operational flexibility.
h) RUVITL recommended that market participants be allowed the flexibility to
define custom delivery slots in 2-hour intervals, which would enable more
granular demand-supply matching, better integration of variable renewable
energy, and customised scheduling based on specific regional needs or
operational constraints.
Order in Petition Nos. 674/RC/2025, 754/RC/2025 & 753/RC/2025 Page 7 of 25

13. The Order dated 28.04.2025 in Petition No. 8/SM/2024 requires peak/off-peak
hours to be based on the region-wise peak and off-peak declared by RLDCs at regular
intervals in accordance with the CERC Tariff Regulations 2024-29. In this regard, the
Petitioner has submitted that the peak hours declared by RLDCs are announced
monthly and revised from time to time, if necessary, and that they vary across regions
depending on weather conditions, geographical factors, and regional demand profiles.
As against this, TAM contracts at IEX provide for power trading on an advance basis
up to three months. Therefore, the region-wise peak/off-peak declared by RLDCs may
not be feasible for Exchange-based contracts and may also fragment liquidity in TAM
contracts.
14. With respect to G-TAM, the Petitioner has proposed that the Renewable Energy
(RE) Seller be allowed to create a profile within the Delivery hrs. 00-24 hours as is
being done at present. The reason attributed by the Petitioner is that, in GTAM,
contracts are designed in a manner to accommodate the variable nature of RE
generation by requiring them to place bids in MWh irrespective of time slots.
15. The Petitioner has submitted that the stakeholders are largely aligned with all
the contract delivery hours except for the peak slot, which is based on their own state-
level requirements. The Petitioner has further submitted that a few stakeholders have
suggested several combinations of peak slots for day and night hours, and a few have
requested to provide region-wise contracts and time slots. One of the stakeholders
has suggested retaining user-defined slots with some flexibility.
16. The Petitioner seeks approval of the proposed time slots for TAM/HP-
TAM/GTAM (Hydro) and for GTAM, except ADSS, as detailed below:
a) TAM/HPTAM/GTAM (Hydro)
S.N. Contract Delivery Hours
1 Peak 18-24 hrs.
2 Night 00-06 hrs.
3 Morning 06-09 hrs
4 Day 09-18 hrs.
Order in Petition Nos. 674/RC/2025, 754/RC/2025 & 753/RC/2025 Page 8 of 25

5 Solar 06-18 hrs.
6 Non-solar 00-06, 18-24 hrs.
7 RTC 00-24 hrs.
b) GTAM
Particulars Delivery hrs.
RE Seller to create profile* within the 00-24 hrs.
‘Delivery hrs.’
*Bidding in MWh
The Petitioner has submitted that only the pre-defined slots will be made available at
the IEX platform, as approved by the Commission, and that all existing slots, including
the hourly slot, will be discontinued.
In Petition No. 754/RC/2025
17. The Petitioner, Power Exchange India Limited (PXIL), was granted permission
to set up, operate and commence exchange operations vide Commission’s order
dated 27.05.2008 in Petition No. 21/2008 and has been in operation since 22.10.2008.
18. The Commission issued directions to the Power Exchanges vide Order dated
28.04.2025 in Petition No. 08/SM/2024 with respect to changes in the Intra-day (ITD),
Day Ahead Contingency (DAC) and the Term Ahead Contracts (TAM) (including Any
Day Single-Sided (ADSS)) in the Power Exchanges, which are produced in para 4 of
this order.
19. In compliance with the above directions, the Petitioner discontinued the
provision of user-defined time slots in TAM, G-TAM and HP-TAM contracts and issued
a circular dated 05.05.2025 to this effect. The Petitioner further filed an affidavit dated
27.05.2025, evidencing compliance with the Commission’s directions.
20. The Petitioner has submitted that it had addressed a letter dated 14.05.2025 to
Grid India, seeking information regarding applicable time slots for Term Ahead Market
contracts. The response received from Grid India vide letter dated 29.05.2025 was
placed on record by an affidavit dated 04.06.2025.
Order in Petition Nos. 674/RC/2025, 754/RC/2025 & 753/RC/2025 Page 9 of 25

21. In accordance with the directions of the Commission in Petition No. 8/SM/2024,
the Petitioner issued a Public Notice dated 21.05.2025 inviting comments and
suggestions from stakeholders on the proposed pre-specified time slots for TAM, HP-
TAM and G-TAM contracts. In response to the said public notice, comments were
received from the following stakeholders:
(i) BSES Rajdhani Power Limited (“BRPL”)
(ii) BSES Yamuna Power Limited (“BYPL”)
22. The comments/ feedback from the above stakeholders on pre-specified time
slots proposed by Petitioner are summarised as follows:

23. The Petitioner seeks approval of time slots applicable in Daily, Weekly and
Monthly Contracts for transacting in Green and Conventional power that were
approved in Petition no 229/MP/2021 dated 07.06.2022 and in High Price power that
were approved in Petition no 170/MP/2023 dated 21.09.2023. The pre-specified time
slots proposed by the Petitioner are as under:
a) For TAM/ HPTAM/ GTAM (for sale of power from Hydro/ Wind/ Biomass/
Waste-to-Energy):

b) For G-TAM (Solar), the proposed time slots are:

*Considering the early sunrise hours and late sunset hours in the North-

In Petition No. 753/RC/2025
24. The Petitioner, Hindustan Power Exchange Limited (HPX), was granted
permission to set-up, operate and commence exchange operations vide
Commission’s order(s) dated 12.05.2021 & 27.06.2022 and has been in operation
since 06.07.2022.
25. The Petitioner submitted an affidavit dated 30.05.2025 in compliance with
the Commission’s following directions, vide Order dated 28.04.2025 in Suo Motu
Petition no. 8/SM/2024:
“63. Considering the directions given in the relevant sections of this Order, the
Commission directs all the power exchanges to submit the compliance report (as
applicable) on affidavit within the stipulated timelines. The power exchanges are
also directed to amend the Business Order in Petition No. 8/SM/2024 Page 18
Rules, Rules, and Bye-Laws, wherever necessary, with intimation to the
Commission. Needless to mention, if any discrepancy is noticed or if it appears
that the revised Business Rules, Rules and Bye-Laws do not conform to the
Regulations and/or to this Order in any respect, necessary action shall be taken
for such compliance.”
26. Further, the Hon’ble Commission was pleased to pass certain other
directions to all the Power Exchanges with respect to revision of Intra-Day, Day
Ahead Contingency (DAC), Term Ahead Market (TAM) (including Any Day Single
Sided or ADSS) contracts. The relevant directions are produced in para 4 of this
order.
Order in Petition Nos. 674/RC/2025, 754/RC/2025 & 753/RC/2025 Page 12 of 25

27. In terms of the above directions, the Petitioner invited suggestions/
comments from stakeholders on the selection of pre-specified time slots in the
Term Ahead Market (TAM), Green Term Ahead Market (GTAM), and High Price
Term Ahead Market (HPTAM) contracts vide its circular dated 20.05.2025. In
response to the Petitioner’s circular, comments were received from the following
stakeholders:
(i) Rajasthan Urja Vikas & IT Services Limited (RUVITL)
(ii) BSES Yamuna Power Limited (BYPL)
(iii) BSES Rajdhani Power Limited (BRPL)
28. The stakeholders RUVITL, BRPL, and BYPL have submitted detailed
proposals, including suggested time-slot tables, to reflect regional and seasonal
demand variations. The key points are as follows:
i. RUVITL submitted that a uniform slot structure may not align with the specific
needs of all participants, especially in large and climatically diverse states like
Rajasthan.
ii. BRPL and BYPL both pointed out that since region-wise peak hours vary, Power
Exchanges should create region-specific peak slots (as detailed in their
submitted tables), such as NR peak for summer: 21:00–24:00 hrs and winter:
18:00–20:00 hrs.
iii. RUVITL submitted that market participants should be allowed the flexibility to
define custom delivery slots in 2-hour intervals to enable more granular
demand-supply matching.
iv. BRPL and BYPL suggested extending the morning hour from 6:00 to 10:00
hours to better align with actual demand patterns.
v. All three stakeholders maintain that modifications are required to better align
with actual demand patterns and seasonal requirements observed across
various regions.
Order in Petition Nos. 674/RC/2025, 754/RC/2025 & 753/RC/2025 Page 13 of 25

vi. RUVITL contended that customising slots will contribute to better integration of
variable renewable energy, improved market efficiency, and grid stability.
29. The Petitioner, after considering the consultations and feedback from various
stakeholders, along with the time slots, also considered the monthly peak hours
published by the Regional Load Despatch Centres (RLDCs) in terms of the CERC
(Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2024–29, which mandate the RLDCs to
publish region-wise peak and off-peak hours at regular intervals. The Petitioner has
submitted that, as peak and off-peak hours vary across states and regions depending
on local climatic conditions, generation profiles, and consumption patterns, many
stakeholders have emphasised the need for two-hourly slots to improve demand-
supply matching, facilitate better renewable energy integration, and cater to local
variations in demand and generation profiles.
30. The Petitioner has proposed the following set of pre-specified time slots, after
due stakeholder consultation and internal evaluation for approval:
S.No. Contract Delivery Slot 1 Delivery Slot 2 Delivery Slot 3
1 Day 08:00-10:00 10:00-14:00 14:00-18:00
2 Night/ Morning 00:00-02:00 02:00-05:00 05:00-08:00
3 Peak 17:00-19:00 18:00-24:00 19:00-24:00
4 RTC 00:00-24:00
5 Solar 06:00-18:00
6 Non-Solar 00:00-06:00, 18:00-24:00
31. The Petitioner has further proposed to incorporate two-hourly slots across the
TAM, GTAM, and HPTAM segments, citing stakeholder recommendations.
32. The Petitioner has submitted that only the above-mentioned pre-specified slots,
as may be approved by this Hon’ble Commission, shall be made available on its
trading platform.
Order in Petition Nos. 674/RC/2025, 754/RC/2025 & 753/RC/2025 Page 14 of 25

Hearing dated 31.07.2025
33. During the course of hearing in Petition No. 674/RC/2025, the representative
of the Petitioner (IEX) submitted that the instant Petition has been filed in compliance
with the directions issued by the Commission vide its order dated 28.4.2025 in Suo-
motu Petition No. 08/SM/2024 for approval of the pre-specified slots in the TAM,
GTAM and HPTAM at IEX. The Commission directed the Petitioner (IEX) to implead
NLDC (Grid India) as a party to the Petition and directed the impleaded Respondent
to file its reply in the Petition.
34. In response to the specific observation of the Commission regarding the
position of the other exchange(s), the learned counsel present on behalf of the
Hindustan Power Exchange Limited (HPX) submitted that HPX has also filed a similar
Petition before the Commission, whereas, learned counsel present on behalf of Power
Exchange of India Limited (PXIL) submitted that PXIL would be filing a similar Petition
shortly.
35. Having regard to the aspect involved in the matter, the Commission deemed it
appropriate to take up the present matter along with a similar Petition already filed by
HPX and the one to be filed by PXIL.
Reply of the Respondent (Grid India) dated 27.08.2025 in Petition No.
674/RC/2025
36. The Respondent, Grid India, in its reply, stated that it has submitted the inputs
dated 29.05.2025 to the Commission in pursuance of the directions issued under
clause 34 of the Suo Moto order in the Petition No. 8/SM/2024, which is summarised
below:
i. Peak hours, as declared by RLDCs, are region-specific, based on weather,
geography, and regional demand patterns. These are announced monthly and
revised weekly in advance.
ii. Peak hours declared by various RLDCs for April 2025 (as tabulated below)
show that no common national 4-hour peak hour slot can be defined. States
peak at different times based on their demand curve. Therefore, imposing
uniform peak hours across India would hinder buyers from optimising their
Order in Petition Nos. 674/RC/2025, 754/RC/2025 & 753/RC/2025 Page 15 of 25

power procurement strategies with their actual demand profiles. Allowing
region-wise peak slots in TAM would lead to liquidity fragmentation.
Region Peak Hours
Northern Region 18:30 to 21:30 hours
22:00 to 23:00 hours
Southern Region 06:00 to 08:00 hours
18:30 to 20:30 hours
Western Region 18:00 to 20:00 hours
22:00 to 23:00 hours
Eastern Region 19:00 to 21:00 hours
22:00 to 24:00 hours
Northeastern Region 18:00 to 22:00 hours
iii. Trading under TAM is currently permitted up to 90 days in advance (Petitions
have been filed by Power Exchanges to extend the same to 11 months)
whereas peak and off-peak hours are declared only a month in advance by the
RLDCs. As the visibility of peak and off-peak hours for future months is not
there during the trading hours, it would be impractical for the participants to
engage in such contracts.
iv. Market Clearing Price (MCP) of the Day Ahead Market (DAM) follows all India
net demand curve. The pressure on the market price occurs during the non-
solar hours of the country as a whole and not on a regional basis. Hence, it
would be more appropriate to structure the contracts as solar and non-solar
hours rather than peak and off-peak hours, as the former has a better influence
on the demand supply curve.
v. Contract executed under GTAM is a national contract, and therefore, creation
of the GTAM contract should be based on national solar and non-solar hours
rather than regional peak and off-peak hours.
37. The peak hours declared by RLDCs in accordance with the Tariff Regulations
2024 vary region to region depending upon weather, geography, and regional demand
Order in Petition Nos. 674/RC/2025, 754/RC/2025 & 753/RC/2025 Page 16 of 25

patterns. As per the Tariff Regulation, the hours of Peak and Off-Peak periods during
a day (for the month) are to be declared by the concerned RLDC at least a week in
advance (before commencement of the month). Since Term Ahead Contracts on the
Power Exchanges platform provide contracts up to 90 days in advance (with Petitions
filed by Power Exchanges to extend to 11 months), the lack of visibility of the peak/off-
peak hours for the entire trading horizon makes participation in such contracts difficult.
Grid India submitted a diurnal plot of all India demand met for the years 2022, 2023,
and 2024, which depicted the monthly variation in the timing of the All-India peak
demand met.
38. A single peak hour slot at the all India level may not be helpful for the states to
cater for their peak demand, as each state is achieving peak demand at a different
time. Grid India further stated that, during the stakeholder consultation held by the
Petitioner, stakeholders proposed different peak and off-peak hours based on their
respective operational constraints. Therefore, imposing a uniform peak hour slot would
hinder buyers from optimising their power procurement strategies, while allowing
region-wise peak hour slots in the Term Ahead Market (TAM) may lead to liquidity
fragmentation.
39. Grid India, in its submission, reiterated Petitioner’s observation that the Day
Ahead Market (DAM), Unconstrained Market Clearing Price (UMCP) follows the Net
demand curve. Grid India further added that pressure on market price is more
pronounced during non-solar hours. Accordingly, it would be more appropriate to
design contracts based on solar and non-solar hours. The non-solar hours, as
proposed by the Petitioner in two separate slots (00–06 hours and 18–24 hours), may
be categorised.
40. With respect to the Green Term-Ahead Market (GTAM), Grid India has
submitted that for sources other than hydro, the proposed time-slot contracts cover
the entire 00:00–24:00 hrs period, requiring Renewable Energy sellers to create a
bidding profile for the day. This approach is considered appropriate, as the time-slot
structure for GTAM-hydro has been aligned with that of TAM contracts.
Order in Petition Nos. 674/RC/2025, 754/RC/2025 & 753/RC/2025 Page 17 of 25

41. Grid India has submitted that in compliance with the directions of the
Commission in its Suo Moto Order in Petition No. 8/SM/2024, the solar and non-solar
hours shall be declared at regular intervals. Power Exchanges may align their contract
design with such categorisation of solar and non-solar hours.
Hearing dated 28.08.2025
42. The Commission admitted Petition Nos. 753/RC/2025 and 754/RC/2025, after
hearing the learned counsels and representatives for the parties. Regarding the
comments filed by Grid India (GCIL), the Petitioner, IEX, submitted that it had no
objection to the same. Learned counsel for the Petitioner, PXIL, sought two days’ time
to file a response to the comments of Grid India, while the counsel for HPX submitted
that a copy of the GCIL’s comments had not yet been received. Consequently, the
Commission directed HPX to implead GCIL as a party and file a revised memo of
parties within two days. Furthermore, GCIL was directed to provide a copy of its
comments to all Petitioners, and the Petitioners were permitted to file their respective
responses thereafter.
Petitioner’s (IEX) response dated 09.09.2025 to Grid India’s Reply dated
27.08.2025 in Petition No. 674/RC/2025
43. The Petitioner has submitted that it agrees with the observations of the
Respondent (GCIL) and believes that the region-wise peak/ off-peak hours proposed
to be declared by RLDCs may not be feasible for Exchange-based contracts and may
also fragment liquidity in the TAM contracts. Additionally, it is necessary to ensure
adequate visibility of pre-defined slots for market participants to trade these contracts.
44. In response to Grid India’s suggestion of designing contracts based on solar
hours and non-solar hours as declared at regular intervals by NLDC, the Petitioner
submitted that IEX has also proposed pre-defined slots in order to cater to the specific
requirements of participants during peak, night, morning and day hours characterised
by the trend of Market clearing prices and net demand of the country in addition to the
solar and non-solar hours. The Petitioner stated that the above combinations in
tandem may help participants fulfil their requirements through the market.
Order in Petition Nos. 674/RC/2025, 754/RC/2025 & 753/RC/2025 Page 18 of 25

Reply of the Respondent (Grid India) dated 18.09.2025 in Petition No.
754/RC/2025
45. The Respondent, in compliance with the directions, submitted its reply in the
Petition No. 754/RC/2025, which is summarised in para(s) 36-39 & 41 of this order.
46. The Respondent has further submitted that the creation of GTAM contracts
should be based on national solar and non-solar hours rather than regional peak and
off-peak hours, as GTAM is a national contract. Considering the nature of the
generation technologies that will participate in the GTAM contracts, it was further
stated that, other than hydro, renewable energy sellers may place their bids based on
daily generation for the entire 00:00 – 24:00 hours period. However, GTAM-hydro
timeslots may be aligned with those of TAM contract timeslots.
Reply of the Respondent (Grid India) dated 18.09.2025 in Petition No.
753/RC/2025
47. The Respondent, in compliance with the directions, submitted its reply in the
Petition No. 753/RC/2025, which is summarised in para(s) 36-39, 41 & 46 of this order.
48. In addition, the Respondent submitted that the fragmentation of Day, Night and
Morning Contracts into 3 delivery slots and the introduction of two hourly slots across
these segments, as proposed by the Petitioner, might result in liquidity fragmentation;
hence, a common delivery slot would be preferable under a contract.
Hearing dated 01.10.2025
49. The learned counsel for the Petitioner, PXIL in Petition No.754/RC/2025,
prayed for an additional two weeks to file a response to the comments given by GCIL.
Whereas, learned counsel for the Petitioner, HPX, in Petition No. 753/RC/2025,
submitted that, while HPX is primarily aligned with the GCIL’s comments, GCIL, inter
alia, has also suggested that the Power Exchanges may align their contract design
Order in Petition Nos. 674/RC/2025, 754/RC/2025 & 753/RC/2025 Page 19 of 25

with the categorisation of solar and non-solar hours. However, exchanges’ existing
contracts, as already approved by the Commission, do not have such categorisation.
The learned counsel for the HPX further submitted that the matter may be listed, if
required.
50. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsels and
representatives for the Petitioners, the Commission permitted the Petitioners to file
their respective response to GCIL’s comments, if not filed already, within a week.
Thereafter, the Commission reserved the matters for order.
51. Subject to the above, the Commission reserved the matters for order. However,
the matters shall be listed for the hearing, if required.
Petitioner’s (PXIL) response dated 07.10.2025 to Grid India’s Reply dated
18.09.2025 in Petition No. 754/RC/2025
52. With regard to observations of the Respondent in respect of GTAM contracts,
the Petitioner submitted that the Hydro segment differs from the Solar segment;
however, since these sources remain schedulable, the timeslots of the Hydro segment
are proposed to be aligned with TAM and GTAM except for the Solar segment. This
would ensure that Hydro timeslots remain aligned with TAM contract timeslots while
facilitating Solar and Non-Solar categorisation for renewable energy generation.
Accordingly, for Hydro, the time slots are retained like TAM.
Petitioner’s (HPX) response dated 09.10.2025 to Grid India’s reply dated
18.09.2025 in Petition No. 753/RC/2025
53. The Petitioner submitted that HPX is primarily aligned with the comments/
suggestions of the Respondent. However, the Petitioner has reservations since the
proposal made by the Respondent may not be practical and has cited the following
reasons for the same:
(i) In the absence of fixed solar and non-solar hours, there will be practical
difficulties for market participants in scheduling, trading, and settlement of
Order in Petition Nos. 674/RC/2025, 754/RC/2025 & 753/RC/2025 Page 20 of 25

contracts on the exchanges. Presently, T+90 days contracts are being traded,
and if NLDC is to declare solar and non-solar hours periodically, participants
will face challenges in entering into long-duration contracts without uniformity
in these hours. There may be scenarios where solar hours differ from one
month to another, creating inconsistencies and operational complexities for
both the exchanges and market participants.
(ii) With respect to the fixation of non-solar hours from 1800 to 0600 hours, it is
submitted that this duration of twelve hours encompasses the evening peak,
night, as well as a portion of the morning peak hours (considering seasonal
variations). The demand profile and requirement of utilities across these sub-
segments vary significantly as evident from GCIL submission dated
18.09.2025. Hence, it would be practically difficult for any utility to enter in to
such contract.
54. The Petitioner prayed that, keeping in view the different peaks and off-peak due
to seasonal variation, the approval may be granted to the proposed timeslots in the
Petition and the same may be aligned in Solar and Non-Solar Categories.
Analysis and Decision
55. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioners, namely, Indian Energy
Exchange Limited (IEX), Power Exchange India Limited (PXIL) and Hindustan Power
Exchange Limited (HPX), the comments/ suggestions of the stakeholders and the
observation of Grid India, along with the reply of the Petitioners.
56. The relevant extract from the Commission’s Order dated 28.04.2025 in Petition
No. 8/SM/2024 is as under:
“…………..
33. On the second issue of different durations of established pre-specified time
slots to be allowed on the power exchanges, we have considered the concerns
raised by some of the stakeholders regarding varying peak periods, load
profiles, and generation portfolio mix across different states. Accordingly, we
direct the power exchanges as under:
(i) For TAM and HP-TAM: Power exchanges to carry out consultation
with market participants on the selection of pre-specified time slots from
Order in Petition Nos. 674/RC/2025, 754/RC/2025 & 753/RC/2025 Page 21 of 25

within RTC, Peak/Off Peak hour, Solar/Non-Solar hour, Day/Night, that
they propose to notify on their respective platforms. Post consultation,
the power exchanges shall approach the Commission for approval on
the pre-specified slots, within a month from the date of this Order.
ii) For G-TAM: Power exchanges to carry out consultation with market
participants on the selection of pre-specified time slots based on the
generation profile of different technologies. Post consultation, the power
exchanges shall approach the Commission for approval on the pre-
specified slots, within a month from the date of this Order.
34. The Commission also directs the NLDC to declare the timings of the Solar/
Non-Solar hours at regular intervals. With regard to Peak/Off-Peak hours, the
CERC Tariff Regulations 2024-29 provide for the declaration of region-wise
peak and off-peak hours at regular intervals by the respective RLDCs.
…………”
57. We recall that the core intent behind proposing pre-specified timeslots in TAM
contracts is to align with the conditions specified in the Commission’s Orders dated
07.06.2022, 07.06.2022 & 30.12.2022 in Petition Nos. 219/MP/2021, 229/MP/2021 &
206/MP/2022, and to avoid the scope of any manipulation by restricting the slots to a
fixed specification.
58. Grid India, in its inputs dated 29.05.2025 to the Commission on the directions
issued under clause 34 of the Suo Moto order in the Petition no. 8/SM/2024 proposed
to structure the TAM contracts as solar and non-solar hours rather than peak and off-
peak, mainly because of the following reasons:
(i) A common four-hour peak hour slot cannot be defined at the national level
for bidding at power exchanges because each state reaches its peak
demand at a different time based on its demand curve;
(ii) Imposing uniform peak hours across all regions would hinder buyers from
optimising their power procurement strategies with their actual demand
profiles;
(iii) Region-wise peak hour slot will lead to liquidity fragmentation in TAM;
Order in Petition Nos. 674/RC/2025, 754/RC/2025 & 753/RC/2025 Page 22 of 25

(iv) Low visibility of peak and off-peak hours for future months because peak and
off-peak hours are declared only a month in advance by the RLDCs, while
power exchanges offer contracts in TAM up to 3 months in advance; and
(v) Pressure on market price is during the non-solar hours of the country as a
whole and not on a regional basis.
It was further pointed out that the contracts executed under GTAM are national
contracts; hence, creation of GTAM contracts should be based on national solar and
non-solar hours rather than regional peak and off-peak hours.
59. We find merit in Grid India’s suggestion for structuring TAM contracts based on
Solar and Non-Solar hours instead of Peak and Off-Peak hours. With regard to the
various slot structures and recommendations submitted by all the Power Exchanges
and stakeholders, the Commission has observed that while the exchanges and
stakeholders have proposed region-specific peak hours, two-hourly delivery slots, and
seasonally adjusted variations, such proposals are not aligned with the objectives of
pre-specified time slots in TAM, GTAM and HPTAM envisaged in the Order dated
28.04.2025 in Petition No. 8/SM/2024.
60. Allowing region-wise or multiple sub-slots within a contract category would
fragment liquidity, reduce market depth in each slot, impair price discovery and
reintroduce the very complexity the said Suo Moto order sought to eliminate.
Moreover, as highlighted by Grid India, regional peak and off-peak hours vary month-
to-month, and visibility of these hours over the full trading horizon of Term Ahead
Contracts (up to 90 days, with proposals to extend to 11 months) is not feasible;
adopting such a variable structure would make participation in these contracts
impractical. At the same time, a single uniform “all-India peak” slot may not accurately
reflect the demand profile of all States. In view of these factors, the Commission is of
the considered view that the TAM contract design should be structured on national-
level Solar and Non-Solar hours, as declared by Grid India.
61. The Petitioners have largely agreed that region-wise peak/ off-peak hours may
not be feasible for exchange-based forward contracts and could fragment liquidity,
Order in Petition Nos. 674/RC/2025, 754/RC/2025 & 753/RC/2025 Page 23 of 25

while certain stakeholders proposed region-specific or seasonal peak slots and even
two-hourly customisation.
62. With regard to the pre-specified time slots, we have considered the proposals
received from the power exchanges and the flexibility requirements of market
participants. We have also considered the inputs from Grid India that, due to wide
regional variations in peak and off-peak hours, a common four-hour peak slot cannot
be defined at the national level for bidding on power exchanges. Accordingly, we have
decided on the following pre-specified time slots for TAM/ HP-TAM/ GTAM (Hydro):
S. No. Contract Duration
1 RTC Contracts 00-24 hrs.
2 Solar Contracts 06-18 hrs.
2(a) Morning Contracts 06-09 hrs.
2(b) Day Contracts 09-18 hrs.
3 Non-Solar Contracts 18-06 hrs
3(a) Evening Contracts 18-24 hrs.
3(b) Night Contracts 00-06 hrs.
63. Broadly, we approve three types of pre-specified time slots for TAM contracts,
namely, RTC, Solar and Non-Solar contracts. Under Solar and Non-solar contracts,
there shall be further classification of contracts as shown in the table above. These
time slots are based on the prevailing national solar and non-solar hours. However,
we direct Grid India to issue a detailed procedure for separately notifying solar and
non-solar hours on a national basis, factoring in regional variation as far as possible.
On the Grid India notifying solar hours and non-solar hours, the solar contracts and
non-solar contracts as indicated above shall stand modified as per the time slots
stipulated by Grid India.
64. We direct all the power exchanges to offer contracts in TAM/ HP-TAM/ GTAM
(Hydro) with the pre-specified time slots as indicated in paragraphs 62 & 63 of this
order, by notifying market participants well in advance. Moreover, subsequent to the
changes to national solar and non-solar hours by Grid India, power exchanges shall
Order in Petition Nos. 674/RC/2025, 754/RC/2025 & 753/RC/2025 Page 24 of 25

be required to align their contracts in TAM accordingly. Power exchanges shall notify
market participants in advance of changes to the time slots.
65. Regarding the pre-specified time slots for contracts in GTAM (other than
Hydro), the Commission has received comments from stakeholders to allow flexibility
to the RE Generators in order to match the bids with their generation profile. After
carefully considering the proposals received from the Power Exchanges and
stakeholders' suggestions, the Commission intends to allow RE generators (other than
Hydro) to create their profiles based on various technologies within the pre-specified
time slots for the contract types specified for TAM in paragraphs 62 & 63 of this order.
The Commission also directs Grid India to examine the need for continuation of such
profile-based bidding, while at the same time ensuring that this flexibility is not misused
to customise bidding strategies for reasons other than operational needs of RE
technologies, and submit a report for consideration of the Commission within two
months from the date of this Order.
66. The directions to the power exchanges pertaining to pre-specified time slots for
TAM/ HP-TAM/ GTAM (Hydro) and GTAM (other than Hydro) contracts shall come
into effect within a week from the date of the Order. However, all such contracts traded
or entered into before the date of this Order shall continue to be valid.
67. In view of the above, all the power exchanges are directed to amend their
Business Rules, Rules, and Bye-Laws, and submit a compliance report on affidavit
within the stipulated timelines. Needless to mention, if any discrepancy is noticed or if
it appears that the revised Business Rules, Rules and Bye-Laws do not conform to the
Regulations and/or to this Order in any respect, necessary action shall be taken for
such non-compliance.
68. Petition Nos. 674/RC/2025, 754/RC/2025 & 753/RC/2025 are disposed of in
terms of the above directions.

Background
3. The present Petition is a consequence of the earlier Petition No. 513/TL/2024
filed by the Petitioner seeking the grant of the transmission licence for the Project.
Vide order dated 18.12.2025 in Petition No. 513/TL/2024, the Commission observed
that the proposed transmission scheme could result in a redundant transmission
asset without visibility of its utilization as one of the applicants, namely ACME Clean
Energy Private Limited had withdrawn its GNARE application of 2182 MW and the
other applicant, Avaada Greenh2 Private Limited (700 MW GNARE) had expressed
its intention to shift to the intra-State system. Therefore, the Commission was of the
considered view that it was premature to grant a transmission licence for the instant
scheme as it did not fulfil the requirement prescribed under Section 38(2)(c) of the
Act. Accordingly, the Commission referred the proposal back to the National
Committee on Transmission (NCT) for reconsideration on the basis of its likely
utilisation and impact on consumers, with liberty to the Petitioner to approach the
Commission after the decision of NCT. The relevant extract of the order is as under:
Order in Petition No. 125/TL/2026 Along with 34/IA/2026
Page 5

“34. The Act mandates that an inter-State transmission system is required to
be developed in an efficient and economical manner. However, the instant
transmission scheme may result in a redundant transmission asset without any
visibility of its utilisation. Therefore, we are of the considered view that it is
premature to consider the grant of a transmission licence for the instant
transmission scheme, as it does not fulfil the requirement prescribed under
Section 38(2)(c) of the Act. Therefore, we find it appropriate to refer the
proposal for the instant transmission scheme back to the NCT for
reconsideration on the basis of its likely utilisation and impact on the
consumers in the absence of any application for its use by the bulk consumers.
Accordingly, we direct the Petitioner and the CTUIL to approach the NCT with
the observations as made in this Order. After the decision of the NCT, the
Petitioner is granted liberty to approach the Commission, if so advised.”
