ORDER
The Petitioner Company, Greenko Energies Private Limited, has filed the present
Petition for the upgradation of its inter-State trading licence in electricity from Category
‘III’ to Category ‘I’.
2. By order dated 22.1.2008 in Petition No. 61 of 2007, Sri Balaji Biomass Power
Private Limited (now known as Greenko Energies Private Limited), was granted a
category 'A ' trading licence to trade in electricity as an electricity trader in whole of
Order in Petition No. 136/TD/2026
Page 1 of 11

India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir in accordance with the Central Electricity
Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for grant of Trading licence
and other related matters) Regulations, 2004 (hereinafter referred to as “ the Trading
Licence Regulations, 2004”).
3. Pursuant to the Central Electricity Regulation Commission (Procedure, Terms
and Conditions for grant of Trading licence and other related matters) Regulations,
2009 (hereinafter referred to as the “Trading Licence Regulations, 2009”), which came
into effect on 16.2.2009, Category ‘A’ licenses (up to 100 MUs) were converted to
Category ‘IV’ licenses (not more than 100 MUs) under Regulation 15 of the Trading
Licence Regulations, 2009.
4. Subsequently, the Petitioner approached the Commission for up-gradation of its
trading licence from Category ‘IV’ to Category ‘III’ and the Commission vide Order
dated 19.2.20216 in Petition No. 212/MP/2015, up-graded the Category ‘IV’ to
Category ‘III’ in accordance with the the "Trading Licence Regulations, 2009, subject
to the terms and conditions contained in the licence.
5. The Petitioner has submitted that in view of the improvement in power demand,
the competitive dynamics of Power Exchanges, the anticipated growth in the power
market, and the prospective business potential in power trading, Greenko Energies
Private Limited seeks an up-gradation of its existing trading licence from Category ‘III’
to Category ‘I’. The Petitioner has submitted that it intends to engage in trading
activities up to a quantum of 7,000 MUs annually. The Petitioner has further stated that
its trading volumes have shown a consistent increase over the last financial year,
which warrants an upgrade of the category of the licence.
Order in Petition No. 136/TD/2026
Page 2 of 11

Hearing dated 25.3.2026
6. The matter was called out for the hearing on 25.3.2026. The learned counsel for
the Petitioner reiterated the submissions made in the instant Petition. Vide Record of
Proceedings (“the RoP”) dated 25.3.2026, the Petitioner was directed to submit, on
affidavit, within two weeks, a duly signed and audited special balance sheet prepared
within 30 days of the filing of the petition, with all pages, including the Auditor’s Report,
financial statements, notes, and schedules, duly authenticated by the Auditor. The
Petitioner was further directed to demonstrate compliance with the requirements of net
worth, current ratio, and liquidity ratio for the grant of a Category I licence in
accordance with the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020, based on the duly certified,
audited special balance sheet.
7. In compliance with the RoP dated 25.3.2026, the Petitioner vide affidavit dated
9.4.2026, has submitted the information called for. The Petitioner has submitted that
its Balance Sheet is dated 31.1.2026, which is within 30 days immediately preceding
the date of filing of the instant Petition, i.e. 2.3.2026. With regard to the Petitioner’s net
worth, the Petitioner has submitted that it exceeds the stipulated minimum of Rs. 50
crore or Rs. 75 crore (for between 7000 MUs to 10,000 MUs and beyond 10,000 MUs
respectively) is required for a Category I trading licence. In terms of Regulation 9 (2)
of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020, the Commission may consider relaxation of
the minimum norms under liquidity ratio and current ratio in view of the significantly
higher net worth of the Petitioner. The Petitioner company is financially sound with
respect to liquidity for carrying out electricity trade on account of its high net worth
[more than 100% of stipulated trade on account of its high net worth]. The Petitioner
prayed to exercise the Power to Relax enshrined in Regulation 23 of the Trading
Order in Petition No. 136/TD/2026
Page 3 of 11

Licence Regulations, 2020, in terms of Section 66 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and the
proviso to Regulation 9(2) to relax the requirement of the minimum 1:1 current ratio
and liquidity ratio.
Hearing dated 24.4.2026
8. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the
directions issued vide RoP dated 25.03.2026 have been duly complied with, and
requested that the matter be reserved for orders. Considering the submissions made
the matter was reserved for the Order.
Analysis and Decision
9. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner. Regulation 9(4) of the
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for
Grant of Trading License and other Related Matters) Regulations, 2020 (the Trading
Licence Regulations 2020) provides as under:
“(4) The Trading Licensee shall make an appropriate application accompanied
by prescribed fees for up-gradation of its licence to a higher category or down-
gradation of its licence to a lower category in order to fulfil the conditions of these
regulations in accordance with the procedure specified in Regulation 15 of these
regulations.”
10. Regulation 15(1) of the Trading Licence Regulations 2020 provides as under:
“15(1) Upgradation of licence:
(a) The Trading Licensee may at any time during a particular year apply for a
higher category licence on the basis of the volume proposed to be traded in a
particular Year.
(b) The Trading Licensee shall file an application before the Commission for
upgradation of its licence to a higher category as soon as he expects the trading
volume to exceed the trading volume limit specified for the Trading Licensee’s
existing category.
(c) The Trading Licensee shall be granted an opportunity of being heard by the
Commission before taking a decision on the application
Order in Petition No. 136/TD/2026
Page 4 of 11

(d) The Trading Licensee shall be required to submit the audited special
balance sheet to support the compliance of Net Worth requirement for higher
category licence.
(e) The Trading Licensee shall pay licence fee applicable to the higher category
licence if in a particular Year the licence has been upgraded:
Provided that in case a Trading Licensee has already paid licence fee
applicable for its existing lower category licence in a particular year, then the
Trading Licensee shall have to make payment equivalent to difference of fee
applicable for higher category licence and fee already paid for existing licence
category.”
11. The Petitioner has filed the instant Petition for the upgradation of its inter-State
trading licence in accordance with the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020. On perusal
of the Petition, the Petitioner, being an existing trading licensee, fulfils all technical
requirements for the grant of a Category ‘I’ inter-State trading licence. As regards the
net worth requirements for Category ‘I”, Regulation 3 (3) of the Trading Licence
Regulations, 2020 provides that a person applying for a Category ‘I’ trading licence
should have a net worth of Rs. 50 crore and should have maintained a minimum
current ratio and liquidity ratio of 1:1 on the date of the Audited Special Balance Sheet
accompanying the Petition.

and liquidity ratio have been worked out as under:

Order in Petition No. 136/TD/2026
Page 7 of 11

15. As per the above special audited balance sheet dated 31.01.2026, the
Petitioner fulfils the requirement of net worth for the grant of Category-I trading
licensee. However, the Petitioner does not meet the requirement of the current and
liquidity ratios specified in Regulation 3(3)(b) of the Trading Licence Regulations. As
per Regulation 9 of the Trading Licence Regulations, the trading licensee is required
to maintain the current and liquidity ratios of 1:1 at all times. Relevant portion of
Regulation 9 of the Trading Licence Regulations is extracted as under:
“9. Obligations of the Trading Licensee the Trading Licensee shall be subject to
the following obligations, namely:
(1) The Trading Licensee shall comply with the requirements of laws in force
and, in particular, the Act, the Rules and the Regulations, Grid Code, orders
and directions issued by the Commission from time to time and any of the State
Electricity Regulatory Commissions in accordance with law.
(2) The Trading Licensee shall maintain the Net Worth in accordance with
Regulation 3 of these regulations at all times and shall maintain Current Ratio
of 1:1 and Liquidity Ratio of 1:1 at the end of every financial year: Provided that
if the current ratio or the liquidity ratio at the end of the financial year is less than
1:1, then the Trading Licensee shall be required to maintain additional Net
Worth of 100% of the Net Worth stipulated for the respective category of trading
licence.”
16. Since the Petitioner is not fulfilling the requirement of the current and liquidity
ratios, the Commission, vide Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 25.3.2026,
directed the Petitioner to file the status of the current and liquidity ratios. The Petitioner
has submitted that its net worth is larger than the stipulated minimum of Rs. 50 crore
or Rs. 75 crore required for Category I trading licence and has prayed to relax the
minimum norms under liquidity and current ratios in view of the significantly higher net
worth of the Petitioner in terms of Regulation 9 (2) of the Trading Licence Regulations,
2020. The Petitioner company is financially sound with respect to liquidity for carrying
Order in Petition No. 136/TD/2026
Page 8 of 11

out electricity trade on account of its high net worth [more than 100% of stipulated
trade on account of its high net worth].
17. The Commission, upon perusal of the submissions and Audited Special
Balance sheet as on 31.01.2026, observed that although the Petitioner does not fulfil
the current and liquidity ratios requirement, as stipulated under the applicable
Regulations, the Petitioner possesses a net worth of ₹4,81,805.41 lakh, which is
several times higher than the minimum net worth required for a Category-I trading
licence. The Petitioner meets other criteria for the grant of a trading licence as required
under the Trading Licence Regulations. It is noted that in similar situated cases, the
Commission, in various Petitions filed by the utilities, particularly, vide order dated
27.5.2019 in Petition No. 219/TD/2018 in the case of M/s NTPC Ltd. and recently vide
order dated 7.7.2025 in Petition No. 557/TD/2025 in the case of M/s Reliance
Industries Ltd., relaxed the liquidity ratio requirement, as the company demonstrated
financial soundness for conducting electricity trade and fulfilled all other necessary
criteria. The relevant paras of the order dated 7.0.2025 are extracted as under:
“16. Since the Petitioner is not fulfilling the requirement of the liquidity ratio, the
Commission, vide Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 05.06.2025 and RoP
dated 10.06.2025, directed the Petitioner to file the status of the liquidity ratio. The
Petitioner vide its affidavit dated 16.06.2025 has submitted that the Commission, in its
order dated 27.05.2019 in Petition No. 219/TD/2019, granted a Category I Trading
Licence to M/s. NTPC Ltd. This decision was made by relaxing the liquidity ratio
requirement, as the company demonstrated financial soundness in terms of liquidity
for conducting electricity trade and fulfilled all other necessary criteria.
17. The Commission, upon perusal of the submissions, observed that although the
Petitioner does not fulfil the liquidity ratio requirement as stipulated under the
applicable Regulations, the Petitioner possesses a net worth of ₹4,96,804 lakh, which
is several times higher than the minimum net worth required for a Category-I trading
license. In view of the substantial financial strength demonstrated by the Petitioner, the
Commission, in exercise of its powers under Regulation 17 of the Central Electricity
Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for grant of Trading
Licence and other related matters) Regulations, hereby relaxes the requirement of the
liquidity ratio in the present case. However, as specified under Regulation 9(2) of
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for grant
Order in Petition No. 136/TD/2026
Page 9 of 11

of trading licence and other related matters) Regulations, 2020, the Petitioner shall be
required to maintain the additional net worth of 100% of the net worth stipulated for the
respective category of trading licence.”
In light of the above and the substantial financial strength demonstrated by the
Petitioner, the Commission, in exercise of its powers under Regulation 23 of the
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for grant
of Trading Licence and other related matters) Regulations, 2020, hereby relaxes the
requirement of the current and liquidity ratios in the present case. However, as
specified under Regulation 9(2) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission
(Procedure, Terms and Conditions for grant of trading licence and other related
matters) Regulations, 2020, the Petitioner shall be required to maintain the additional
net worth of 100% of the net worth stipulated for the respective category of trading
licence.
18. On consideration of the above facts, after an examination, we find that the
Petitioner meets the requirements as specified in the Trading Licence Regulations for
the grant of a Category 'I' trading licence, Accordingly, we approve the upgradation of
the inter-State trading licence of the Applicant from Category ‘III’ to Category ‘I’ with
effect from the date of issuance of the order. The licensee shall remain bound by the
terms and conditions contained in the various orders issued from time to time and
provisions of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020. The licensee shall further comply
with the provisions of the Payment of Fees Regulations and Trading Licence
Regulations, 2020, as amended from time to time.
19. Let an extract copy of this order be sent to the Central Government (Ministry of
Power) and the Central Electricity Authority in terms of sub-section (7) of Section 15
of the Electricity Act, 2003, for their information and record.
Order in Petition No. 136/TD/2026
Page 10 of 11

20. We direct that the necessary endorsement be made on the licence issued to
the applicant with regard to the change of Category of the licensee.
21. Petition No. 136/TD/2026 is allowed in terms of the above.

5. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner, BPC, and CTUIL and
perused the documents available on record. Section 63 of the Act provides as under:
“Section 63: Determination of tariff by bidding process: Notwithstanding
anything contained in section 62, the Appropriate Commission shall adopt the
tariff if such tariff has been determined through transparent process of bidding
in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Central Government.”
6. The Ministry of Power, Government of India, has notified the “Tariff based
Competitive bidding Guidelines for Transmission Service” and “Guidelines for
Encouraging Competition in Development of Transmission Projects‟ (hereinafter
referred to as “the Guidelines‟) under Section 63 of the Act vide Resolution No.
15/1/2017-Trans dated 10.8.2021, as amended from time to time. The salient features
of the Guidelines are as under:
(a) The Guidelines are applicable for the procurement of transmission
services for transmission of electricity through tariff based competitive bidding
for selection of the Transmission Service Provider (TSP) for new transmission
system on a Build, Own, Operate and Transfer basis.
Order in Petition No. 132/AT/2026

(b) For procurement of the transmission services required for any inter-State
transmission Project, the Central Government shall notify the CTUIL or any
Central Government Organization/ Central Public Sector Undertaking or its
wholly owned subsidiary (Special Purpose Vehicle) to be the Bid Process
Coordinator (BPC), who would be responsible for the coordinating the bid
process.
(c) The BPC shall prepare the bid documents in accordance with the
Guidelines and obtain approval of the Appropriate Government, or alternatively,
the BPC can use the Standard Bid Documents notified by the Ministry of Power.
Any material deviation from the Standard Bidding Documents shall be made
only with the prior approval of the Appropriate Government. Intimation about
initiation of the bidding process shall be sent by the BPC to the Appropriate
Commission.
(d) For the procurement of the transmission services under the guidelines,
BPC shall adopt a single stage two envelope tender process featuring Request
for Proposal (RfP). The entire bidding process shall be conducted online
through electronic medium under e-reverse bidding framework.
(e) The RfP notice should be published in at least two national newspapers,
website of the BPC and preferably in trade magazines also, so as to accord it
wide publicity. The bidding shall necessarily be by way of International
Competitive Bidding (ICB). For the purpose of issue of RfP, minimum conditions
to be met by the bidder shall be specified in the RfP.

declared as the successful bidder.
12. BPC, in their evaluation report has confirmed the following:
i. The levelised tariff for this project based on CERC norms works out to
Rs. 1562.34 million per annum. This has been computed based on the
estimated cost as communicated by the Cost Committee constituted by
CEA and methodology for calculation of tariff as per CERC norms.
ii. The entire bid process has been carried out in accordance with the
"Tariff based Competitive Bidding Guidelines for Transmission Service"
and "Guidelines for encouraging competition in development of the
Transmission Projects" issued by Ministry of Power, Govt, of India under
Section 63 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and as amended from time to time.
13. After detailed discussions on the evaluation report prepared by BPC, the
Order in Petition No. 132/AT/2026
Page 19

BEC decided the following:
i. 'Enerica Infra 1 Private Limited' is the successful Bidder after the
conclusion of the e-reverse auction process with the lowest Quoted
Transmission Charges of Rs. 1562.34 million per annum.
ii. The quoted tariff is lower than the Levelised Tariff estimated as per
CERC norms. The quoted tariff discovered through e-reverse auction
process is acceptable.
iii. In view of (i) and (ii) above, 'Enerica Infra 1 Private Limited' may be
issued Letter of Intent (Lol).
BEC has also issued a separate certificate in this regard (Annexure-C).”
24. Bid Evaluation Committee (BEC), vide its certificate dated 31.10.2025, certified
as under:
“It is hereby certified that:
1. The entire bid process has been carried out in accordance with the "Tariff
based Competitive Bidding Guidelines for Transmission Service" and
"Guidelines for encouraging competition in development of the Transmission
Projects" issued by Ministry of Power, Govt, of India under Section 63 of the
Electricity Act, 2003 and as amended from time to time.
2. Enerica Infra 1 Private Limited has emerged as the Successful Bidder after
the conclusion of e-reverse bidding process with the lowest Quoted
Transmission Charges of Rs. 1562.34 million per annum.
3. The quoted tariff is lower than the Levelised Tariff calculated based on
CERC norms considering the Capital Cost for the Project ‘Transmission
system for Evacuation of Power from RE Projects in Morena SEZ in Madhya
Pradesh- Phase I (2500 MW)’ as assessed by Cost Committee. The quoted
tariff discovered through e-reverse bidding process is acceptable.”
25. In the light of the discussions in the preceding paragraphs, it emerges that the
selection of the successful bidder and the discovery of the annual transmission charges
of the Project have been carried out by the BPC through a transparent process of
competitive bidding in accordance with the Guidelines issued by the Ministry of Power,
Government of India, under Section 63 of the Act. BEC has certified that the process
is in conformity with the Ministry of Power Guidelines. BEC, in its certificate dated
Order in Petition No. 132/AT/2026
Page 20

31.10.2025, has certified that Enerica Infra 1 Private Limited has emerged as the
successful bidder after the conclusion of the e-reverse auction with the lowest
transmission charges of Rs. 1562.34 million per annum. It is noted that the quoted tariff
of Rs. 1562.34 million per annum is lower (~40.82% Lower) than the estimated CERC
levelised tariff (Rs. 2639.99 million per annum). Based on the BEC certification, we
approve and adopt the single annual transmission charge of Rs. 1562.34 million per
annum as per the final offer of the successful bidder, subject to the grant of
transmission licence to the Petitioner company. The transmission charges shall remain
valid throughout the period covered in the TSA.
26. The sharing of the transmission charges by the designated ISTS customers
(DICs) shall be governed by the provisions of the Central Electricity Regulatory
Commission (Sharing of inter-State Transmission Charges and Losses) Regulations,
2020, as amended from time to time.
27. Extract copy of this order shall be sent to the Nodal agency, CTUIL.
28. Petition No. 132/AT/2026 is disposed of in terms of the above.
Sd/- sd/- sd/- sd/-
(Ravinder Singh Dhillon) (Harish Dudani) (Ramesh Babu V.) (Jishnu Barua)

CENTRAL ELECTRICITY REGULATORY COMMISSION
NEW DELHI
Petition No. 856/MP/2025 along with IA 129/2025
Coram:
Shri Jishnu Barua, Chairperson
Shri Ramesh Babu V., Member
Shri Harish Dudani, Member
Shri Ravinder Singh Dhillon, Member
Date of Order: 13.05.2026
In the Matter Of:
Petition under Section 79(1)(c) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 42 of
the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network
Access to the Inter-State Transmission System) Regulations, 2022 inter alia seeking
directions to the Central Transmission Utility of India.
AND
In the Matter Of:
ACME Cleantech Solutions Private Limited (ACME)
Plot No, 152, Kanhai Colony,
Sector 44, Gurugram, Haryana 122003 …Petitioner
Versus
Central Transmission Utility of India Limited (CTUIL)
First Floor, Saudamini, Plot No.- 2,
Sector- 29 Near IFFCO Chowk, Metro Station
Gurugram, Haryana 122001 …Respondent
Parties Present:
Shri Venkatesh, Advocate, ACSPL
Shri Shryeshth Sharma, Advocate, ACSPL
Shri Akash Lamba, Advocate, ACSPL
Shri Kunal Veer Chopra, Advocate, ACSPL
Ms. Priya Dhankar, Advocate, ACSPL
Shri Manav Bhatia, Advocate, ACSPL
Shri Shubham Arya, Advocate, CTUIL
Order in Petition Number 856/MP/2025 and IA 129/2025
Page 1

Ms. Pallavi Saigal, Advocate, CTUIL
Ms. Kaavya Madaan, Advocate, CTUIL
Ms. Priyansi Jadiya, CTUIL
Shri Swapnil Verma, CTUIL
ORDER
The instant petition has been filed under Section 79(1)(c) of the Electricity Act,
2003 read with Regulation 42 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission
(Connectivity and General Network Access to the Inter-State Transmission System)
Regulations, 2022 (‘GNA Regulations’) inter alia seeking directions to the CTUIL to
allow change of the source of connectivity with partial conversion from Land BG route
to LoA route.
2. The Petitioner has made the following prayers vide the instant Petition:
(a) Direct CTUIL to decide the Petitioner’s application dated 15.09.2025 for change
of source of connectivity from solar to wind as per Regulation 9.3 of the GNA
Regulations (inserted by way of the Third Amendment) forthwith without any
delay and preconditions including the delay on account of transition;
(b) Direct CTUIL to issue final grant of connectivity to the Petitioner in accordance
with Regulation 9 of GNA Regulations;
(c) Direct CTUIL to evaluate the documents submitted by Petitioner towards
compliance of Regulation 11A based on wind source and allow conversion of
connectivity from Land BG route to LoA route as requested by Petitioner.
(d) Direct CTUIL to restrain from taking any coercive action against the Petitioner,
including under Regulation 11B of the GNA Regulations; and
(e) Pass any other or further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and
proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case and in the interest of
justice.
Petitioner has also sought the following interim reliefs vide the instant Petition:
(a) Pass an ad-interim ex-parte order restraining the Respondent from taking any
coercive action against the Petitioner, including under Regulation 11B of the GNA
Regulations, during the pendency of the present Petition; and
(b) Pass any other or further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and
proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case and in the interest of
justice.
Order in Petition Number 856/MP/2025 and IA 129/2025
Page 2

3. Petitioner vide IA Number 129/2025 has made the following prayers:
(a) Allow the present Application;
(b) List, hear and consider the Petition bearing No. 856/MP/2025 titled ACME
Cleantech Solutions Private Limited v. Central Transmission Utility of India
Limited for urgent hearing on 09.12.2025 or 11.12.2025, whichever is
convenient to this Hon’ble Commission, in terms of the directions of the Hon’ble
High Court vide order dated 05.12.2025;
(c) In continuation of the interim relief sought before this Hon’ble Commission in
the present petition, it is most humbly prayed that this Hon’ble Commission stay
the letter dated 04.12.2025 issued by CTUIL thereby revoking the in-principle
grant of connectivity of the Applicant’s 400 MW Project.
And/or
(d) Pass any other order(s)/direction(s) as deemed necessary in the interest of
justice and equity.
Submissions of the Petitioner:
4. Petitioner has submitted as under:
(a) On 12.01.2024, the Petitioner applied for the grant of connectivity for a 400
MW solar project under the LAND BG route at the Pachora PS in Madhya
Pradesh. Petitioner also furnished a bank guarantee in lieu of Land dated
12.01.2024, amounting to Rs. 40 Crore. CTUIL granted in-principle
connectivity to the Petitioner on 10.04.2024. Thereafter, Petitioner submitted
Conn-BG1, Conn-BG2, and Conn-BG3 on 09.05.2024. Accordingly, under
Regulation 9 of the GNA Regulations, CTUIL was obligated to issue final
connectivity to the Petitioner by 14.05.2024, i.e., 15 days from the date of
submission of the bank guarantee by the Petitioner. However, CTUIL has not
to date issued final connectivity to the Petitioner.
(b) Petitioner is obligated to submit land documents within 18 months of issuance
of an in-principle grant of connectivity or within 12 months of issuance of a
final grant of Connectivity, whichever is earlier, as per Regulation 11A of the
GNA Regulations. The Petitioner may also convert its connectivity from the
Land BG route to the LoA route by submitting a valid LoA in terms of
regulation 5.8(xi)(a) of the GNA Regulations; however, such conversion is
Order in Petition Number 856/MP/2025 and IA 129/2025
Page 3

also allowed post issuance of the final grant in terms of regulation 11A (4) of
the GNA Regulations.
(c) In the instant case, Petitioner is required to submit the above documents by
10.10.2025, being 18 months from the issuance of the in-principle grant of
Connectivity issued on 10.04.2024.
(d) In the meantime, the Petitioner participated in the bidding conducted by NTPC
by way of Request for Selection bearing no.
NTPC/RECS/202324/Hybrid/BOO8 dated 19.07.2023 for selection of ISTS-
connected wind-solar hybrid power projects (Tranche-I). It is pertinent to
highlight that the Petitioner was selected as the successful bidder by NTPC by
way of the LoA dated 11.01.2024 for the development of a 400 MW wind-solar
hybrid project (300 MW contracted capacity), comprising 300 MW of solar
capacity and 100 MW of wind capacity. Petitioner on 07.05.2025 raised a
request to NTPC for a change in location and point of interconnection of the
wind component in the LoA issued by NTPC. NTPC, in response, issued
Amendment No. 3 dated 22.08.2025, amending Clause 7.0 of the LoA to
record the changed project location.
(e) Accordingly, the Petitioner was desirous of converting the in-principle
connectivity granted by way of letter dated 10.04.2024 from the Land BG
route to the LoA route for 100 MW and the Land Route for the balance 300
MW. Additionally, the Petitioner was also desirous of changing the source of
connectivity from solar to wind.
(f) Petitioner vide its letter dated 05.05.2025 and 8.5.25 sought amendment of
the project location to coincide with the project location of the wind
component under the LoA. CTUIL, vide its letter dated 29.05.2025, stated
that the project location can only be amended once the Petitioner attains the
status of connectivity grantee upon execution of the connectivity agreement.
(g) CTUIL vide its email dated 05.08.2025, requested the Petitioner to submit its
land-readiness compliances under Regulation 11A(1) of GNA Regulations, in
relation to the Petitioner’s 400 MW Project
Order in Petition Number 856/MP/2025 and IA 129/2025
Page 4

(h) Commission on 09.09.2025 issued the Third Amendment, whereby inter alia
Regulation 9.3 was inserted to permit a change in the source of connectivity
even prior to the grant of final connectivity. Petitioner, vide its email dated
15.09.2025, issued a letter requesting CTUIL to issue a final grant of
connectivity to the Petitioner, permit the Petitioner to change the source of
connectivity under the Third Amendment,
(i) Regulation 11A (2) of the GNA Regulations (inserted vide the second
amendment effective from 15.07.2024) permits conversion of connectivity
granted under the Land BG route to the LoA route. Further, as per Para 5(xiii)
of the Detailed Procedure for Connectivity and General Network Access
(GNA) to the ISTS approved by this Commission vide order dated 14.10.2022
(“Detailed Procedure”) permitted applicants who have been granted
connectivity to ISTS for the generation projects based on particular
renewable energy source(s) to change to another renewable energy
source(s) for the same granted connectivity in part or full, subject to approval
by CTUIL.
(j) Prior to the Third Amendment, while conversion from the Land BG route to
the LoA route was permitted for applicants of connectivity, a change in source
was permitted only for entities that are a “connectivity grantee,” i.e. those
entities whose Cat-1 is signed. This direction is in accordance with the order
dated 12.05.2024, 09/MP/2024 titled Acme Cleantech Solutions Private
Limited & Anr. vs. Central Transmission Utility of India Limited, . Since, in the
present case, CTUIL had inordinately delayed the grant of final connectivity
to the Petitioner, the Petitioner could not have changed the source of the in-
principle connectivity granted to it prior to the Third Amendment.
(k) However, this Commission on 09.09.2025 issued the Third Amendment,
whereby Regulation 9.3 has been inserted, permitting change of source of
connectivity within 18 months of the grant of in-principle connectivity or 18
months prior to the effective date of GNA, whichever is later. In the present
case, the 18-month period from the grant of in-principle connectivity expired
on 10.10.2024, and the 18-month period prior to the effective date of
connectivity was on 30.10.2024. Accordingly, the Petitioner immediately after
Order in Petition Number 856/MP/2025 and IA 129/2025
Page 5

issuance of the Third Amendment, i.e., on 15.09.2025, applied for a change
in source of connectivity from solar to wind.
(l) However, CTUIL vide its email dated 07.10.2025 stated that it would process
the source change request of the Petitioner as per Regulation 9.3 of GNA
Regulations, upon completion of the transition of already granted
Connectivity(ies) to solar and non-solar access, as per the Third Amendment,
which would require more than 3 months in line with Regulation 5.11(b).
CTUIL, on the same date, issued another email to the Petitioner calling upon
the Petitioner to submit the land documents as per the original source in
terms of Regulation 11A of the GNA Regulations, by 10.10.2025, failing which
CTUIL would initiate action under Regulation 11B of the GNA Regulations.
(m) Petitioner is a serious developer and not a fly-by-night operator. Petitioner
vide its email dated 08.10.2025 submitted the requisite land and project
documents in compliance with Regulation 11A of the GNA Regulations, albeit
for the changed source of the project. Petitioner, vide its email dated
08.10.2025, submitted the LoA granted to the Petitioner by NTPC and the
documents substantiating the procurement of the requisite quantum of land
for 300 MW.
(n) However, since the source of connectivity granted to the Petitioner has not
been changed from solar to wind either on account of delay in grant of final
connectivity by CTUIL or on account of transition from GNA Regulations to
the Third Amendment (both of which are beyond the control of the Petitioner),
CTUIL vide its email dated 10.10.2025 has refused to accept the documents
submitted by the Petitioner.
(o) As a result, CTUIL has been treating the Petitioner as non-compliant with the
obligation under Regulation 11A of the GNA Regulations and threatening to
take coercive action against the Petitioner under Regulation 11B of the GNA
Regulations. This is despite the fact that there is no non-compliance or
contravention attributable to the Petitioner, and Regulation 11B of the GNA
Regulations is not applicable to the Petitioner (since the Petitioner is not a
connectivity grantee under the GNA Regulations).
Order in Petition Number 856/MP/2025 and IA 129/2025
Page 6

(p) Petitioner submitted that these issues or similar other issues may arise in the
transition pursuant to the Third Amendment, and this Commission may
consider resolving such issues by dovetailing the pre-amendment GNA
Regulations 2022 with the Third Amendment, enabling a smoother transition
window and eradicating the possibility of any coercive action against
generators akin to the case of the Petitioner.
Hearing dated 10.11.2025
5. During the hearing, learned counsel for Petitioner submitted the facts of the case.
6. Considering the submission made by the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the
Commission directed as under:
“
(a) Admit and issue notice to the Respondent, subject to just exceptions.
(b) The Petitioner was directed to file, on an affidavit, why the land documents, for 300
MW capacity for which a source change from solar to wind is sought, are submitted
in the name of four different SPVs. Further to clarify, whether the 100 MW wind
capacity is also being developed by any SPV. File the current status of
implementation of each project.
(c) The Respondent (CTUIL) was directed to file information as under, along with its
reply, if any, within two weeks, with a copy to the Petitioner, who may file its
rejoinder, if any, within a week thereafter:
(i)Reason for not issuing the final grant of connectivity to the Petitioner and reasons
for linking configuration change with solar/ non solar access finalisation.
(ii)Expected timeline for the effectiveness of the Petitioner’s GNA.”
Submissions vide IA 129/2025 :
7. The Petitioner has made the following submissions vide IA dated 06.12.2025:
(a) Application was filed seeking urgent hearing in terms of the directions passed
by the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi vide order dated 05.12.2025 in W.P. (C) No.
18486 of 2025 (“Writ Petition”). The Hon’ble High Court vide its order inter alia
passed the following directions:
“Considering the submissions made before this Court, the CERC is requested
to take up the petitioner’s application for interim stay on the next date, i.e., 09th
December, 2025, or 11th December, 2025.It is directed that status quo shall be
maintained and no precipitative action or steps shall be taken by the respondent
Order in Petition Number 856/MP/2025 and IA 129/2025
Page 7

no. 1 qua the bank guarantees submitted by the petitioner or with respect to the
electricity connectivity granted to the petitioner. It is clarified that the present
status quo order is being passed for a limited period till the matter is taken up
for hearing and considered by the CERC.”
(b) The need to approach the Hon’ble High Court was necessitated because of the
act of CTUIL to attempt to invoke the Bank Guarantee and revoke the grant of
in-principle connectivity for the Applicant’s 400 MW project at the Pachora
Pooling Station in Madhya Pradesh.
(c) The revocation of the in-principle connectivity, as conveyed by CTUIL vide its
letter dated 04.12.2025, has grave and immediate consequences on the ongoing
project development activities. In particular, lenders strictly require an active and
subsisting grant of connectivity before undertaking the disbursement of loan
amounts. In the absence of such connectivity, no financial institution will disburse
funds, thereby jeopardising the financial closure process and crippling the ability
to undertake even essential project activities.
(d) The revocation thus threatens to bring the entire 400 MW project to a standstill,
causing irreversible financial and contractual harm. Therefore, in the interest of
justice and to prevent frustration of the pending Petition itself, the operation of
the revocation letter dated 04.12.2025 issued by CTUIL, thereby revoking the in-
principle grant of connectivity of the Applicant’s 400 MW Project, warrants an
immediate stay by this Commission.
Submissions of CTUIL:
8. The Respondent-CTUIL vide affidavit dated 08.12.2025 submitted as under:
(a) CTU vide letter dated 10.04.2024 issued intimation for in-principle grant of
connectivity for 400 MW (Solar Project) at Pachora PS (Existing), identifying
Augmentation (other than ATS) under Part-1: Rajgarh Phase-I (Commissioned),
Part-2: Rajgarh Phase-II (SCOD-14.02.2026), and Part-3: Rajgarh Phase-III
(part System) (tentatively by 31.01.2027). For the implementation of Part-3, the
scheme “Transmission system for Evacuation of Power from RE Projects in
Rajgarh (1500 MW) SEZ in MP- Phase III and Evacuation of Power from RE
Projects Neemuch (1000 MW) SEZ in MP--Phase II”, has been awarded on
25.10.2025 to RNTL with SCOD of 29.09.2027.
Order in Petition Number 856/MP/2025 and IA 129/2025
Page 8

(b) As per GNA Regulations (prior to the Third Amendment), the final grant had to
be issued along with the firm start date of connectivity, which could only be
ascertained after the award of all elements of the required transmission system.
(c) As per Regulation 11A (1), REGS/ESS/RPPD are required to submit land
documents within 18 months of an in-principle grant or 12 months of a final grant,
whichever is earlier, failing which revocation under Regulation 11B (1) follows.
Accordingly, the due date for submission of the land documents was 10/10/2025,
but the applicant failed to submit them. Thus, even after the 3rd amendment, the
final grant could not be issued due to the non-submission of land documents for
compliance with Regulation 11A(1), rendering the connectivity liable for
revocation under Regulation 11B(1). Subsequently, the connectivity granted to
M/s ACSPL was revoked by CTU vide letter dated 04.12.2025 on account of non-
compliance with Regulation 11(A) & 11(B) of the GNA Regulations.
(d) As per Regulation 9.3.4, applications received for seeking a change in source
from solar to non-solar (wind) can only be processed after ascertaining the extent
of non-solar access, which has not been granted to any other entity (in line with
Regulation 9.3.4). That the same can be ascertained upon completion of the
transition of already granted Connectivity to solar and non-solar access, as per
the 3rd amendment. Applicant sought source change from Solar to Wind (Non-
Solar) vide e-mail dated 15.09.2025 (after the notification of Third Amendment to
the GNA Regulations), and hence the applicant was advised to submit land
documents as per the original grant (Solar) vide CTUIL’s e-mail dated
07.10.2025, in order to avoid noncompliance with provisions of the GNA
Regulations.
(e) Petitioner’s Connectivity has been revoked vide CTUIL letter dated 04.12.2025.
However, as per the latest commissioning schedule for the elements identified
for grant of connectivity to M/s ACSPL, the timeline for the effectiveness of the
Petitioner’s GNA would have been as follows: for 350 MW, it is 30.04.2026, and
for 50 MW, it is 29.09.2027.
Submissions of Petitioner:
9. Petitioner, vide affidavit dated 08.12.2025, submitted as under:
Order in Petition Number 856/MP/2025 and IA 129/2025
Page 9

a) Regarding submissions of land documents in the name of a subsidiary, it is
submitted that Proviso to Regulation 15.1 of the GNA Regulations permits
connectivity granted to a parent company to be utilised by its subsidiary and vice
versa. Further, the acquisition of land for the execution of projects is a time-
consuming process. Any developer starts acquiring land in the initial stages, prior
to PPA signing, so that the project can be completed in a timely manner in
accordance with the PPA timelines. In view of the above, the Petitioner had also
begun acquiring land in the name of its various SPVs, as the land acquisition
process takes substantial time. Accordingly, land has been acquired in different
SPVs with a view to utilising it in its multiple projects.
b) Regarding 100 MW wind capacity being developed by any SPV, it is submitted
that the balance 100 MW of wind capacity for which in-principle connectivity has
been granted to the Petitioner is part of a hybrid project developed through a
subsidiary of the connectivity grantee. The said subsidiary has already executed
the power purchase agreement, and the corresponding solar component of the
said hybrid project is being developed at Bikaner-III.
c) Further, regarding the current status of the implementation of the project,
Petitioner has submitted that:
(i) Petitioner is installing 100 WTGS of 4 MW each for the project. Out of this, the
Petitioner has entered into a contract and issued a purchase order to SANY for
the procurement of 41 WTGs. The Petitioner is in the process of placing an
order for balance WTGs.
(ii) Petitioner is required to procure land at 100 locations for the installation of the
WTGs. Out of this, the Petitioner has entered into a lease deed for 44 locations,
and the Petitioner is in the process of entering into a lease deed for the
remaining 56 locations. It is pertinent to note that the lease deeds executed for
44 locations clearly state that the leased land is for a wind power project.
Further, the land required for setting-up the PSS has been fully acquired by the
Petitioner.
(iii) The Petitioner has also issued purchase orders for the procurement of other
electrical and grid infrastructure, namely:
Order in Petition Number 856/MP/2025 and IA 129/2025
Page 10

(iv) The Petitioner has undertaken foundation works for 31 locations out of 109 and
erected 5 towers. However, the stringing work is pending due to the pendency
of Section 68 approval.
(v) The foundation works for MCR & switchgear and building works for the same
are in progress.
(vi) Petitioner, vide its letter dated 05.05.2025, sought amendment of the project
location to coincide with the project location of the wind component under the
LoA, but CTUIL vide its letter dated 29.05.2025 stated that the project location
can only be amended once the Petitioner attains the status of connectivity
grantee after execution of the connectivity agreement.
Hearing dated 11.12.2025
10. During the hearing, learned counsel for Petitioner submitted that CTUIL has
initiated the steps for revocation of the Petitioner’s connectivity and invocation of
Bank Guarantees (BGs) during the pendency of the instant Petition. Being
aggrieved by this, the Petitioner approached the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi in
Writ Petition (C) No. 18486 of 2025, wherein the Hon’ble High Court vide order
dated 5.12.2025 has directed that the status quo be maintained and no
precipitative steps shall be taken by CTUIL qua the invocation of the BGs and the
Order in Petition Number 856/MP/2025 and IA 129/2025
Page 11

revocation of the in-principle connectivity granted to the Petitioner for a limited
period till the Petitioner’s application is taken up for hearing and considered by this
Commission. Accordingly, the present IA 129/2025 has been filed. He also
apprised the Commission that the Petitioner’s grievance is squarely covered now
by the order dated 8.12.2025 in Petition No. 14/SM/2025, whereby the
Commission has exercised its power to remove difficulties for effective
implementation of the Third Amendment to the GNA Regulations, 2022, and,
according to the Petitioner, nothing survives in the matter. In the alternative, the
learned senior counsel pressed for interim relief, including a stay on the revocation
of the in-principle grant of connectivity to the Petitioner.
Learned counsel for the Respondent, CTUIL, submitted that the compliance
affidavit dated 10.11.2025 filed by CTUIL comprehensively addresses the
queries and issues involved in the matter, and as such, no separate reply has
been filed in the matter. He further submitted that the connectivity of the
Petitioner was revoked prior to the Hon’ble High Court’s order, and as such, the
Petitioner cannot take the benefit of the order passed by the Commission in
Petition No. 14/SM/2025.
11. After hearing the parties, the Commission directed the issuance of notice on the
IA. The Respondent, CTUIL, was also directed to file its written note/ submissions
to the IA, with a copy to the Petitioner, and, in the meantime, the interim direction
issued by the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi vide order dated 5.12.2025 shall
continue till the next date of hearing.
Written Note by CTUIL:
12. Respondent CTUIL vide written submissions dated 22.12.2025 has submitted as
below:
a) On 08.12.2025, this Commission passed a Suo-moto Order in 14/SM/2025,
wherein it was recognised that the Applicant shall be given at least one chance
to change source(s) under Regulation 9.3, post the effectiveness of the Third
Amendment. In view of the foregoing, it was stated that the Third Amendment
to the GNA Regulations introduced a transition framework under which all
existing Connectivity must first be transitioned to solar and non-solar access.
Until this transition exercise is completed, CTUIL cannot conclusively ascertain
the quantum of non-solar access that has already been allocated and the
Order in Petition Number 856/MP/2025 and IA 129/2025
Page 12

balance, if any, that remains available for consideration of source-change
requests.
b) ACME sought a change of source from solar to wind (non-solar) vide email
dated 15.09.2025, i.e., after the Third Amendment was notified. Since the

system studies, as required, and approve or reject the change of renewable energy
source(s) within 30 days of application by the Applicant. Upon approval of such a change

the changed renewable energy source(s), and the Nodal Agency shall then incorporate

9.3.3 An Applicant covered under clause (xi)(b) of Regulation 5.8 of these regulations who

solar hour access shall be permitted only to the extent the non-solar hour access
has not been granted to another entity(ies).

the Right of First Refusal (ROFR) period ( 9.9.25 plus 3 months plus 75 days) and
after expiry of the ROFR period is required to be clarified.
I. During the transition period, i.e., till 21.02.2026, the following steps may
take place:
Step-1 : An entity with solar source ‘A’ eligible to seek a change of source
under Regulation 9.3 of the GNA Regulations makes an application for source
change during the ROFR period. It has yet to be converted into an entity with
solar hour access.

Step-2 : Another entity ‘B’ makes an application for non-solar access at a
substation at which ‘A’ is connected, based on the tentative list of non-solar
access declared by CTUIL on its website, during the ROFR period.
Step-3: Another entity ‘C’ with solar source exercised its ROFR rights and
made an application under Regulation 5.11 (a) to seek non-solar access.
For the above-said applications, applications under Step-1 shall have to be processed
within 30 days of the date of application. Then the Application under Step-3 shall be
processed after completion of the ROFR period. Application under Step-2 shall be
processed after completion of the processing of applications under Step-3.
II. Cases after completion of the ROFR period
(A) After completion of the ROFR period, the following steps may take place:
Step-1 : All entities with solar source would be converted to entities with specific
solar hour access in terms of the Regulations.
Step-2 : Non-solar hour access of an entity ‘A’ ( which has been converted as an
entity with solar hour access on expiry of ROFR period) under Step (1) is sought
for by another entity ‘B’.
Step-3 : Entity with solar-hour access ‘A’, applies for source change after step (2)
has been carried out.
In case an entity under Step 1 which has been declared as an entity with solar hour
access, applies for change of source ( change from solar to wind or ESS requiring
non-solar hour access) after its non-solar hour access has been sought for by another
entity ‘B’, then application of ‘B’ shall be processed followed by application at Step-3
and in case ‘B’ is granted non-solar capacity of ‘A’, something which has been
committed to another entity (‘B) cannot be given back to ‘A’ if it makes application
under Step 3.

’B’ makes an application for non-solar access of entity ‘A’ on 5.3.2026. Entity ‘A’
applies for a change of source to wind on 20.3.2026.

consider the application of ‘A’ for a source change from solar to wind.

Regulation 5.11(a) on 1.11.2025 (during ROFR period) on tentative locations, or

(iv) The minimum capacity for conversion of Connectivity shall be 50 MW.
”
As per the above, an entity that has been issued a final grant of Connectivity and
has also been issued an LOA becomes eligible to submit an application for
conversion of part or full capacity, and, in case a part capacity is converted, an
elaborate procedure is to be followed by CTUIL. Further, if a change of source is
also sought, the application for such a change in source may be submitted prior
to or along with the application under Regulation 11A(4). In the instant case, the
above-said clause is not applicable, as the Petitioner was not issued the final grant
of Connectivity. Even presuming that the final grant was issued to the Petitioner,
the above-said LOA with the changed configuration would not become an eligible
document until the source change is approved by CTUIL.
41. We are of the view that the provision of conversion from LAND BG to LOA route
can be exercised by an entity in terms of the provisions of the Regulations. Since,
in the instant case, Petitioner has not been issued a final grant of Connectivity, it
is not eligible to apply for conversion under Regulation 11A(4) for the LAND BG to
LOA route. Also, in the instant case, the LOA was issued much earlier in January
2024; the Petitioner chose to amend the location as late as August 2025.
42. Considering the above discussions, we note that Petitioner was required to furnish
the land documents for the 400 MW solar project by 10.10.2025. As a result, it
claims to have furnished land documents for Wind for 300 MW connectivity. It did
not furnish land documents for 100 MW Connectivity, but instead furnished an LOA
of WIND. Accordingly, we direct as under:
(a) We have already directed under Issue No.1 that the source change application
for the Petitioner be processed within 30 days of the issue of this Order. CTUIL
shall issue the final grant of Connectivity upon processing the source change
application. In case of rejection by CTUIL in terms of Regulation 9.3.2 on
Order in Petition Number 856/MP/2025 and IA 129/2025
Page 32

technical grounds, the connectivity quantum of 400 MW shall be revoked, and
LAND BG and Conn-BGs shall be dealt with in terms of the GNA Regulations
(b) Considering the transition case, we allow, as a one-time dispensation, that if
CTU permits the source change application for Petitioner, CTU shall process
the land documents furnished by the Petitioner for a 300 MW Connectivity
quantum.
(c) In case CTU permits the source change application, Petitioner shall be given a
one-time dispensation of 15 days from the date of source change permission
by CTU, to furnish the land documents for 100 MW Connectivity quantum.
Since last date to furnish the land documents is already over on 10.10.2025
and Petitioner did not furnish the land documents as per the Regulations,
Petitioner would be required to deposit compensation for delay in submission
of land documents @ 5% of Land BGfor 100 MW Connectivity (Rs 50 lacs)
starting from 10.10.2025 till the allowed time to furnish the land documents for
such quantum. If the Petitioner fails to furnish the compensation amount within
the specified timeline, the connectivity quantum of 100 MW shall be revoked,
and the LAND BG and Conn-BGs with respect to the quantum of connectivity
revoked shall be dealt with in terms of the GNA Regulations
(d) In case the land documents under clause (b) or clause (c) are not in order or
the petitioner is unable to furnish the land documents under clause (c) the
Connectivity quantum corresponding to appropriate land documents furnished
by the Petitioner shall be retained and balance Connectivity shall be revoked,
and LAND BG and Conn-BGs with respect to the quantum of connectivity
revoked shall be dealt with in terms of the GNA Regulations
43. Issue No. 2 and Issue No 3 are answered accordingly.
Issue No.4: Whether Petitioner can be allowed conversion of connectivity from
the Land BG route to the LoA route?
44. We have already noted under Issue No.2 that Petitioner becomes eligible for
conversion from LAND BG or Land route to LOA/PPA route only after final grant of
connectivity has been issued and subject to other conditions as per Regulation
11A(4). Accordingly, Petitioner shall be eligible to apply for such conversion under
regulation 11 A(4) of the GNA Regulation on issuance of final grant of Connectivity,
Order in Petition Number 856/MP/2025 and IA 129/2025
Page 33

provided subject to meeting any other conditions as required under the GNA
Regulations.
Issue No. 5: Whether the letter dated 04.12.2025 issued by CTUIL, thereby
revoking the in-principle grant of connectivity of the Applicant’s 400 MW
Project, is required to be stayed?
45. We note that CTUIL revoked the Connectivity of 400 MW of the Petitioner vide
letter dated 4.12.2025 quoted as under:
Order in Petition Number 856/MP/2025 and IA 129/2025
Page 34

As per the above, CTUIL stated that since the Petitioner failed to furnish the land
documents, the Connectivity is revoked.
46. Petitioner approached the Delhi High Court against the invocation of the Bank
Guarantee and revocation of Connectivity. Hon’ble High Court of Delhi vide order
dated 05.12.2025 in W.P. (C) No. 18486 of 2025 (“Writ Petition”) directed as under:
“Considering the submissions made before this Court, the CERC is requested
to take up the petitioner’s application for interim stay on the next date, i.e., 09th
December, 2025, or 11th December, 2025. It is directed that status quo shall
be maintained and no precipitative action or steps shall be taken by the
respondent no. 1 qua the bank guarantees submitted by the petitioner or with
respect to the electricity connectivity granted to the petitioner. It is clarified that
the present status quo order is being passed for a limited period till the matter
is taken up for hearing and considered by the CERC.”
47. The Petition was listed for hearing on 11.12.2025, where vide ROP it was
directed that the interim direction issued by the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi vide
order dated 5.12.2025 shall continue till the next date of hearing.
48. The Order in the main petition and the IA was reserved for Order during the
next hearing on 23.12.2025.
49. We are of the considered view that the letter dated 4.12.2025 issued by CTU
revoking the Connectivity is required to be set aside, keeping in view that we
have directed CTU to process the application of source change, issue a final
grant of Connectivity and process the land documents, apart from giving time
to the Petitioner to furnish land documents for 100 MW Connectivity with
payment of compensation. In case Petitioner fails to comply with the directions
under this Order, CTU may take action in terms of the GNA Regulations.
Order in Petition Number 856/MP/2025 and IA 129/2025
Page 35

50. Issue No. 5 is addressed accordingly.
51. Petition No 856/MP/2025 and IA 129/2025 are disposed of in terms of the
above.

CENTRAL ELECTRICITY REGULATORY COMMISSION
NEW DELHI
Petition No. 7/MP/2026
along with
IA Nos. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026
Coram:
Shri Jishnu Barua, Chairperson
Shri Ramesh Babu V, Member
Shri Harish Dudani, Member
Date of Order: 13.05.2026
In the matter of:
Petition under Sections 79(1)(c), 79(1)(f) and 79(1)(k) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with
Regulation 42 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General
Network Access) Regulations, 2022 (as amended) and Regulation 65 of the Central
Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business Regulations), 2023, seeking
directions to Central Transmission Utility of India Limited to consider the documents
furnished by Prerak Greentech Solar Private Limited as compliance of the Financial
Closure requirement under Regulation 11A(2) of the GNA Regulations, 2022 (as amended)
or, in the alternative, to communicate the firm start date of Connectivity and grant a period
of 06 (six) months prior thereto for achieving Financial Closure.
And in the matter of:
Prerak Greentech Solar Private Limited
L-11, First Floor, Green Park Extension,
New Delhi, Delhi-110016 ……Petitioner
Versus
Central Transmission Utility of India Limited,
Floors No. 5th -10th, IRCON International Tower, Tower 1,
Plot No. 16, Institutional Area,
Sector-32, Gurugram, Haryana-122003 ……Respondent
Order in Petition No. 7/MP/2026 along with IA Nos. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026 Page 1

Parties Present: Shri Basava Prabhu Patil, Sr. Advocate, PGSPL
Shri Nishant Kumar, Advocate, PGSPL
Shri Animesh Kumar, Advocate, PGSPL
Dr. Sumit Kumar, Advocate, PGSPL
Ms. Palak Joshi, Advocate, PGSPL
Shri Shikhar Khanna, Advocate, PGSPL
Shri Shubham Arya, Advocate, CTUIL
Ms. Pallavi Saigal, Advocate, CTUIL
Ms. Kaavya Madan, Advocate, CTUIL
Ms. Shree Dwivedi, Advocate, CTUIL
Ms. Muskan Aggarwal, CTUIL
Shri Swapnil Verma, CTUIL
Shri Ranjeet Singh Rajput, CTUIL
ORDER
The present Petition has been filed by Prerak Greentech Solar Private Limited
(hereinafter referred to as the “Petitioner”/”Prerak”) seeking directions to Central
Transmission Utility of India Limited (CTUIL) to consider the documents furnished by the
Petitioner as compliance of the Financial Closure requirement under Regulation 11A(2) of
the GNA Regulations, 2022 (as amended) or, in the alternative, to communicate the firm
start date of Connectivity and grant a period of 06 (six) months prior thereto for achieving
Financial Closure. The Petitioner has made the following prayers in Petition No.
7/MP/2026:
(a) Allow the present Petition; and
(b) Exercise the power to remove difficulty under Regulation 42 of the Central Electricity
Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access) Regulations, 2022 (as
amended) and consequently, direct CTUIL to consider Prerak Greentech Solar Private
Limited being compliant with the requirement to achieve Financial Closure under Regulation
11A(2) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network
Access) Regulations, 2022 (as amended) in view of the documents shared by it on
28.08.2025 and 27.11.2025; or
(c) Direct Central Transmission Utility of India Limited to intimate the ‘firm’ start date of
Connectivity to Prerak Greentech Solar Private Limited which will be upon the
operationalization of the Common Transmission System pertaining to the Prerak Greentech
Solar Private Limited’s Connectivity, and consequently, grant Prerak Greentech Solar Private
Limited the statutory period of 06 (six) months prior to such firm date to comply with the
requirements of Regulation 11A(2) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission
(Connectivity and General Network Access) Regulations, 2022 (as amended); and/or
(d) pass any other or further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the
facts and circumstances of the present case and in interest of justice.
Interim Relief Sought:
Order in Petition No. 7/MP/2026 along with IA Nos. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026 Page 2

(a) List the present Petition at the earliest convenient date as per the convenience of this Hon’ble
Commission;
(b) Direct Central Transmission Utility of India Limited to not take any coercive actions against
Prerak Greentech Solar Private Limited including revocation / cancellation of the Connectivity
dated 03.05.2024 granted to the Petitioner at 220 kV Bhadla-III PS till the disposal of the
present Petition; and/or
(c) pass any other or further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the
facts and circumstances of the present case and interest of justice.
2. The Petitioner has also filed an IA bearing No. 2/IA/2026 and has made the following
prayers:
(a) List the present Petition at the earliest convenient date as per the convenience of this Hon’ble
Commission;
(b) Direct Central Transmission Utility of India Limited to not take any coercive actions against
Prerak Greentech Solar Private Limited including revocation / cancellation of the Connectivity
dated 03.05.2024 granted to the Petitioner at 220 kV Bhadla-III PS till the disposal of the
present Petition; and/or
(c) Pass any other or further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in
the facts and circumstances of the present case and in interest of justice.
3. The Petitioner has also filed an IA bearing No. 7/IA/2026 and has made the following
prayers:
(a) Urgently list and allow the present Application;
(b) Stay the operation and effect of letter dated 31.12.2025 issued by the Respondent/ CTUIL
revoking the Connectivity of 400 MW granted to the Applicant at Bhadla-III PS;
(c) Direct the Respondent to not take any coercive action against the Applicant including creation
of any third-party rights in relation to the Applicant’s Connectivity dated 03.05.2024 of 400
MW at Bhadla-II PS till the disposal of the present Petition;
(d) Direct the Respondent to refund the amount of Rs. 11,50,00,000/- (Rupees Eleven Crores
Fifty Lakhs Only) paid by the Applicant on 02.01.2026 in lieu of encashment of Conn-BGs
dated 25.04.2024;
(e) Restore the status quo ante prevailing as on 30.12.2025 in respect of the Petitioner’s
Connectivity during the pendency of the captioned Petition;
(f) Take on record the additional documents annexed with this application in respect of
subsequent events that have taken place after the filing of the Subject Petition; and/or
(g) Pass any other or further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in
the facts and circumstances of the present case and in interest of justice.
Submissions of the Petitioner:
4. The Petitioner has mainly submitted as under:
(a) The Petitioner is a Solar Park Developer and has been granted Connectivity/ GNA of
400 MW at Bhadla-III PS. The Petitioner intends to utilise the above-mentioned
Connectivity/ GNA for the evacuation of power from the 335 MW solar component of a
renewable energy project being developed by one of its affiliates, i.e., ABC CT RE Park
Order in Petition No. 7/MP/2026 along with IA Nos. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026 Page 3

(01) Private Limited (“ACRPPL”) at Chocra Village, Sheo Tehsil, Barmer District,
Rajasthan.
(b) The Petitioner, by way of its application dated 26.08.2022, applied for the grant of
Stage-II Connectivity of 400 MW at 220 kV Bhadla-III PS. The Stage-II Connectivity
was granted by CTUIL on 26.10.2022 w.e.f. 31.12.2024. A Transmission Agreement
for Connectivity dated 16.11.2022 was executed between the Petitioner and CTUIL.
Conn-BG1 of Rs. 50 Lakhs and Conn-BG2 of Rs. 3 Crores were duly furnished by the
Petitioner on 21.11.2022.
(c) The Petitioner vide its application dated 17.12.2022 applied for the grant of Long-Term
Access (“LTA”) of 400 MW; and submitted the requisite bank guarantee of Rs. 40
Lakhs dated 16.12.2022.
(d) Pursuant to the coming into effect of the GNA Regulations, the Petitioner, by way of its
letter dated 03.05.2023, requested the transition of its 400 MW Connectivity at Bhadla-
III PS as per Regulation 37.1 of the GNA Regulations.
(e) CTUIL, by way of its letter dated 14.11.2023, issued the in-principle grant of
Connectivity to the Petitioner at Bhadla-III PS w.e.f. 30.09.2025. Thereafter, the
Petitioner, in terms of Regulation 8 of the GNA Regulations, provided the requisite
Conn-BG3 dated 12.12.2023 to the tune of Rs. 8 Crores to CTUIL on 13.12.2023.
(f) Upon the request made by the Petitioner, the earlier provided Conn-BGs were released
by CTUIL, and in place of the same, the Petitioner had furnished fresh Conn-BGs dated
25.04.2024 (Conn-BG1, Conn-BG2 and Conn-BG3) to CTUIL.
(g) CTUIL, by way of its letter dated 03.05.2024, issued the final grant of Connectivity of
400 MW at Bhadla-III PS. As per the final grant for Connectivity, the start date was
16.08.2025, subject to the availability of the transmission system of Connectivity.
(h) The start date of Connectivity was subsequently extended by CTUIL, and this was
apprised and conveyed to the Petitioner in various JCC Meetings of Northern Region
(“NR”). As per the 35th JCC Meeting of NR held on 24.09.2025, the final start date of
Connectivity of the Petitioner at Bhadla-III PS is 28.02.2026, while the Connectivity is
likely to be operationalised upon commissioning of the common transmission system,
i.e. 30.09.2026.
(i) The RE Project is being developed under the ‘Selection of RE Power Generators for
Order in Petition No. 7/MP/2026 along with IA Nos. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026 Page 4

Supply of 3000 MW Firm and Dispatchable Power from ISTS-Connected Renewable
Energy (RE) Power Projects Anywhere in India (NTPC-TRANCHE-II) on a Built-Own-
Operate basis’ dated 31.10.2023. The tariff discovered under the PPA has been duly
adopted by this Commission, and a back-to-back power supply agreement has also
been executed by NTPC with the buying entities. Therefore, the said RE Project has
all necessary regulatory approvals in place for its effectiveness.
(j) The Petitioner has executed the ISA dated 05.12.2025 with ACRPPL, granting it the
right to utilise the abovementioned Connectivity at Bhadla-III PS, along with the
dedicated transmission line being developed by the Petitioner from the Project to
Bhadla-III PS.
(k) Regulation 11A (2) of the GNA Regulations provides, inter alia, that an applicant being
a Renewable Energy Generating Station (“REGS”) or a renewable power park
developer, to which an in-principle grant of Connectivity has been issued, is required
to achieve Financial Closure for the capacity covered under such Connectivity at least
six (06) months prior to the Scheduled Commercial Operation Date (“SCOD”) or the
start date of Connectivity, whichever is later.
(l) Regulation 11A (2) of the GNA Regulations highlights that in order to achieve the
Financial Closure, an applicant can either submit: (i) a loan sanction letter or proof of
first disbursal of the loan amount; or (ii) a board resolution (if internal funding is planned
for 100% of the project cost).
(m) Regulation 11B (2) of the GNA Regulations provides that in the event of failure to
achieve such Financial Closure within the stipulated time frame, the Connectivity
granted to the applicant will stand revoked and the bank guarantee furnished by the
applicant will be encashed.
(n) In view of the provisions under the GNA Regulations, the Petitioner was required to
achieve Financial Closure within six (06) months prior to the start date of Connectivity.
Accordingly, CTUIL, by way of its email dated 21.07.2025, highlighting the start date
of Connectivity to be 28.02.2026, requested the Petitioner to submit the Financial
Closure documents as per Regulation 11(A)(2) of the GNA Regulations before
28.08.2025.
(o) The Petitioner, in due compliance with Regulation 11A(2) of the GNA Second
Amendment Regulations, opted to provide the loan sanction letter issued by its lender
Order in Petition No. 7/MP/2026 along with IA Nos. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026 Page 5

bank and inter alia by way of its e-mail dated 28.08.2025 to CTUIL, provided the
following documents towards Financial Closure:
(i) Undertaking dated 28.08.2025 towards achieving Financial Closure;
(ii) In-principle sanction letter dated 26.08.2025 for line of credit commitment of
minimum Rs. 175 crore issued by Kotak Mahindra Bank Limited; and
(iii) Net worth certificate dated 28.08.2025 issued by its Auditor.
(p) CTUIL, after around 03 (three) months, by way of its e-mail dated 18.11.2025,
requested the Petitioner to provide the sanction for the term loan to fund the Project
within 07 (seven) days, failing which CTUIL will be constrained to take steps under
Regulation 11B of the GNA Regulations.
(q) The GNA Regulations do not envisage that the requirement under Regulation 11A(2)
will be fulfilled only upon the final loan sanction letter, rather, it merely stipulates a loan
sanction letter.
(r) The Petitioner, by way of its application dated 17.05.2024, sought approval from the
Central Electricity Authority (“CEA”) under Section 68 of the Electricity Act for laying of
an overhead transmission line from the Project (i.e., 335 MW solar component) till
Bhadla-III PS. However, to date, the said application has not been processed by CEA
on account of the pendency of W.P. (C) No. 838 of 2019 titled “M.K. Ranjitsinh & Ors.
v. Union of India” (“GIB Writ Petition”) before the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India, which
has been reserved for Judgment on 29.11.2025.
(s) The Petitioner was unable to provide the final loan sanction letter on account of the
pendency of approval under Section 68 of the Electricity Act for laying of overhead
transmission line; and the associated uncertainty in issuance of the said approval.
(t) This Commission issued the Third Amendment GNA Regulations, which were made
effective from 09.09.2025. Notably, as per Regulation 11A(2) of the said Regulations,
the Petitioner was required to achieve the Financial Closure 06 (six) months prior to
the ‘firm’ start date of Connectivity. Further, as per Regulation 10.5 of the GNA
Regulations (as amended), said ‘firm’ start date of Connectivity was intrinsically
dependent upon the commissioning of the associated transmission system.
(u) The Petitioner, relying upon the GNA Third Amendment Regulations, by way of its e-
mail dated 20.11.2025, requested CTUIL to confirm the ‘firm’ start date of Connectivity,
Order in Petition No. 7/MP/2026 along with IA Nos. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026 Page 6

as the lenders are requesting the same.
(v) Further, the Petitioner, by way of abundant caution and its commercial wisdom,
decided to develop the Project by internal funding, i.e., the second option under
Regulation 11A (2) of the GNA Regulations. Accordingly, the Petitioner, by way of its
e-mail dated 27.11.2025 to CTUIL, provided the following documents towards
Financial Closure:
(i) Undertaking dated 27.11.2025 towards achieving Financial Closure;
(ii) Net-worth certificate dated 05.11.2025 of the Petitioner’s affiliate, i.e., Imperia
Holdings (DIFC) Limited;
(iii) Net worth certificate dated 28.08.2025 of the Petitioner;
(iv) Board Resolution dated 25.11.2025 issued by the Petitioner’s affiliate for
providing financial assistance of Rs. 180 crore towards the development of the
Project; and
(v) Board Resolution dated 25.11.2025 issued by the Petitioner for approval of
acceptance of financial commitment of Rs. 180 Crore towards the development
of the Project.
(w) Considering that the Petitioner has already furnished documents demonstrating
internal group funding commitments, sufficient net worth, and undertakings confirming
Financial Closure, this Commission ought to direct CTUIL to consider the Petitioner as
compliant with the requirement to furnish Financial Closure documents under
Regulation 11A(2) of the GNA Regulations.
(x) For the purpose of development of the solar component of the RE Project (i.e., the 335
MW solar component), the Petitioner has already acquired approx. 1515 acres of land,
i.e., 90% of the total land required for development of the Project.
(y) As per the final grant of Connectivity dated 03.05.2024, the start date of the Petitioner’s
Connectivity is contingent upon the availability of the transmission system for
Connectivity as highlighted therein. It is relevant to highlight that despite the request
made by the Petitioner, CTUIL has not yet communicated the firm start date of
Connectivity to the Petitioner, which will be upon the operationalisation of the common
transmission system. Further, during the 35th JCC Meeting held on 24.09.2025, CTUIL
has categorically stated that the Connectivity is likely to be operationalised w.e.f.
Order in Petition No. 7/MP/2026 along with IA Nos. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026 Page 7

30.09.2026 upon commissioning of the common transmission system.
(z) As the ‘firm’ start date of Connectivity is intrinsically dependent upon the
operationalisation of the common transmission system, which is entirely within the
domain and responsibility of CTUIL, and since the said date has been repeatedly
revised and remains uncertain even as on date, there exists no justification whatsoever
for insisting upon the Petitioner to submit the Financial Closure documents in absence
of such ‘firm’ start date of Connectivity.
(aa) The Petitioner has been given to understand that CTUIL is not considering the
documents shared by the Petitioner on 27.11.2025 in compliance with Regulation
11A(2) of the GNA Regulations and will take steps under the GNA Regulations,
including revocation of Connectivity under Regulation 11B of the GNA Regulations.
Therefore, there is an imminent threat of revocation of the Petitioner’s 400 MW
Connectivity at Bhadla-III PS, and invocation of Conn-BGs furnished by the Petitioner
towards such Connectivity. Being aggrieved by the abovementioned conduct of CTUIL,
the Petitioner is constrained to file the present Petition before this Commission.
Hearing dated 23.12.2025:
5. The extracts of the RoP for the hearing dated 23.12.2025 held under Petition (Diary)
No. 641/2025, along with IA (Diary) No. 642/2025, are as under:
“The matter, along with the IA, was mentioned by the learned senior counsel for the Petitioner,
citing the urgency therein.
2. The learned senior counsel submitted that the present Petition has been filed inter alia
seeking directions upon the Respondent, CTUIL, to (i) treat the Petitioner as having complied
with the requirement to achieve Financial Closure under Regulation 11A(2) of the GNA
Regulations (as amended) on the basis of the documents already furnished on 28.8.2025 and
27.11.2025, respectively; and/or (ii) in the alternative, direct CTUIL to communicate the ‘firm’
start date of Connectivity and consequently grant the Petitioner statutory period of six months
prior to such firm date to comply with Regulation 11A(2) of the GNA Regulations (as amended);
and, (iii) pending final adjudication of the present Petition, restrain CTUIL from taking any
coercive actions against the Petitioner, including revocation of the Connectivity granted on
3.5.2024. The learned senior counsel further submitted that the Petitioner has also moved IAs
(Diary) Nos. 642/2025 seeking grant of interim reliefs and direction to CTUIL not to take any
coercive action against the Petitioner in any manner whatsoever, including
revocation/cancellation of the Connectivity dated 3.5.2024 granted to the Petitioner at 220 kV
Bhadla-III PS till the disposal of the present Petition.
3. Considering the submissions made by the learned senior counsel for the Petitioner, the
Commission directed that notice be issued to the Respondent to file its reply within a week, with
a copy to the Petitioner, who may file a rejoinder thereof within two days thereafter.”
Submissions of the Petitioner in 7/IA/2026:
Order in Petition No. 7/MP/2026 along with IA Nos. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026 Page 8

6. The Petitioner has submitted as under:
(a) CTUIL, in complete disregard of the procedural discipline, rather than filing its
response in the Subject Petition along with the said IA, unilaterally revoked the
Applicant’s Connectivity by way of its letter dated 31.12.2025 without any separate
notice or prior warning regarding such revocation.
(b) Further, immediately thereafter, CTUIL, in an uncanny haste, on 01.01.2026, issued
notices to the Lenders for encashment of the Conn-BGs dated 25.04.2024 (“Conn-
BGs”) furnished by the Applicant aggregating to an amount of Rs. 11,50,00,000/-
(Rupees Eleven Crores Fifty Lakhs Only).
(c) In order to avoid any impact on its credit rating and large-scale ramifications, the
Applicant under duress was constrained to deposit an amount of Rs. 11,50,00,000/-
(Rupees Eleven Crores Fifty Lakhs Only), without prejudice to its rights under the
Subject Petition, to CTUIL on 02.01.2026, and by way of its letter requested CTUIL
to withdraw the notices invoking the Conn-BGs. Accordingly, CTUIL withdrew its
requests for encashment of Conn-BGs.
(d) The present Application has been filed seeking a stay on the operation,
implementation and effect of CTUIL's letter dated 31.12.2025, till final adjudication of
the Subject Petition by this Commission, along with consequential reliefs thereof.
(e) The obligation to furnish documents evidencing Financial Closure arises six months
prior to the firm start date of Connectivity. In the present case, no firm start date has
ever been communicated by CTUIL, and the same remains contingent upon the
operationalisation of the common transmission system, which is presently expected
to be operationalised w.e.f. 30.09.2026. Thus, even assuming that the common
transmission system becomes operational w.e.f. 30.09.2026, the Petitioner would be
entitled to achieve Financial Closure up to 30.03.2026.
(f) Regulation 11A(2) of the GNA Regulations expressly recognises a loan sanction
letter, proof of first disbursal of the loan amount, or a copy of a Board resolution
(where internal funding is planned for 100% of the project cost) as valid documents
for demonstrating Financial Closure. Notably, the GNA Regulations do not prescribe
the nature or format of the loan sanction letter required for compliance.
(g) Accordingly, the Applicant duly submitted an in-principle loan sanction letter issued
by its lender bank on 28.08.2025, i.e., within the prescribed timeline, thereby fully
complying with the requirements of Regulation 11A(2).
Order in Petition No. 7/MP/2026 along with IA Nos. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026 Page 9

(h) There was no occasion for CTUIL to keep the matter in abeyance without any reason
for more than 2 months and to revert as belatedly as on 18.11.2025 for the very first
