Order in Petition No. 7/MP/2026 along with IA Nos. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026 Page 24

prior to the scheduled date of commercial operation or start date of Connectivity,
whichever is later. The start date of connectivity intimated to the Petitioner is 28.2.2026,
and hence the last date to achieve financial closure comes as 28.8.2025.
25. Petitioner has submitted that it is yet to be provided with the ‘firm’ start date of
Connectivity by CTUIL as contemplated in the GNA Regulations (as amended vide third
amendment), since, as per the 35th JCC Meeting held on 24.09.2025, the Connectivity
is likely to be made effective from 30.09.2026.
26. Let us compare the provisions of the GNA Regulations to see whether there was any
change with respect to the last date to achieve financial closure.
(a) GNA Regulations (prior to the third amendment) provide as under:
“7. In-principle Grant of Connectivity by the Nodal Agency
7.1 In the event the Nodal Agency after the interconnection study undertaken in
accordance with Regulation 6.1 of these regulations, determines that no augmentation is
required, the Nodal Agency shall intimate in-principle grant of Connectivity to the Applicant
within 60 days from the last day of the month in which the application had been received
along with details such as terminal bay(s), already available or to be developed under
ISTS through CTU, and minimum design features for dedicated transmission lines to be
constructed by the Applicant.
7.2 In case the Nodal Agency, after the interconnection study undertaken in accordance
with Regulation 6.1 of these regulations, determines that augmentation (with ATS or
without ATS) is required, the Nodal Agency shall intimate in-principle grant of Connectivity
to the Applicant within 90 days from the last day of the month in which the application had
been received:
Provided that intimation for in-principle grant of Connectivity shall mention the ATS and
terminal bay(s), estimated cost of such ATS and terminal bay(s), minimum design features
for dedicated transmission lines to be constructed by the Applicant and the likely date of
start of Connectivity:
Provided further that the firm date of start of Connectivity shall be confirmed at the
time of final grant of Connectivity.”
As per above, the firm date of start of connectivity was to be confirmed at the time
of final grant of Connectivity. Hence, the start date of Connectivity intimated in the
final grant of Connectivity was the firm start date of Connectivity, and the same was
based on the SCOD of the augmentation.
(b) The third amendment to the GNA Regulations issued on 31.08.2025, effective from
9.9.2025, provided as under:
“28.4. The word “firm” shall be inserted before the words “start date of Connectivity” occurring
at multiple places in clause (2) and clause (3) of Regulation 11A of the Principal Regulations.”
Order in Petition No. 7/MP/2026 along with IA Nos. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026 Page 25

“18.1. Regulation 9.1 of the Principal Regulations shall be substituted as under:
9.1 Within 15 days of receipt of Conn-BG1, Conn-BG2 and Conn-BG3, as applicable, the
Nodal Agency shall intimate the final grant of Connectivity to the entity that has been
intimated the in-principle grant of Connectivity. The intimation shall contain, inter alia, the
following:
(a) Name of the ISTS sub-station or switchyard of the generating station or switchyard of
the entity covered under Regulation 17.1(iii) of these regulations, as the case may be,
where Connectivity is granted.
(b) The coordinates of the ISTS substation, terminal bay location, and Single Line
Diagram for the ISTS substation where Connectivity is granted, as per the following:
(i) In case of an ISTS sub-station which has been declared under commercial operation,
the final coordinates of the ISTS substation, terminal bay location and Single Line
Diagram shall be furnished;
(ii)In case of an ISTS sub-station which is under-construction, the tentative or final
coordinates of the ISTS substation, terminal bay location, and Single Line Diagram,
as available with the Nodal Agency;
(iii) In case Connectivity is granted at an ISTS sub-station other than that covered under
sub-clause (i) or (ii) of this clause, the tentative or final coordinates of the ISTS
substation, terminal bay location, and Single Line Diagram shall be furnished as per
Regulation 10.5 of these regulations;
(c) The broad design features of the dedicated transmission lines including voltage level.
(d) Start date of Connectivity, tentative or firm, as available. In case the tentative Start
date of Connectivity is furnished in the final grant of Connectivity, the firm Start date of
Connectivity shall be intimated as per Regulation 10.5 of these regulations.
….
22.1..
10.5 Confirmation of firm Start Date of Connectivity, coordinate of the ISTS substation,
terminal bay location, and Single Line Diagram to the Applicant:
(a) For applicants, where Connectivity is granted with augmentation (with ATS or
without ATS), the Nodal Agency, within 6 (six) months of final grant of
Connectivity, shall intimate to such entity the firm timeline for completion of
augmentation, ATS, terminal bay(s), and firm date of start of Connectivity based
on scheduled date of commercial operation of such elements.
……”
As per the above, a concept of furnishing a ‘tentative’ start date of connectivity in the
‘final grant of Connectivity’ has been introduced. It has been provided that the ‘firm
start date of Connectivity’ shall be confirmed under Regulation 10.5, which shall be
based on the scheduled date of commercial operation of elements of augmentation.
27. On perusal of the GNA Regulations prior to third amendment and after third
amendment, we observe that there is no change with respect to last date to achieve
financial closure under Regulation 11A(2) since prior to third amendment ‘start date of
Order in Petition No. 7/MP/2026 along with IA Nos. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026 Page 26

As per the above, during the 35th JCC, it was recorded that the start date of connectivity
under the GNA Regulation is 28.02.2026 (final) and the connectivity is likely to be
operationalised upon the commissioning of the common transmission system, i.e.
30.09.2026. According to the Petitioner, its start date should be considered to be
30.9.2026.
29. We are of the considered view that the firm start date of connectivity stands intimated
to the Petitioner in terms of the GNA regulations, which is 28.02.2026. We do not agree
with the argument of the Petitioner that the firm start date of Connectivity should have
been revised based on the actual implementation status of augmentation. GNA
Regulations provide a clear distinction between ‘firm start date of Connectivity’ and
‘effective date of GNA’, where, on actual completion of augmentation, ‘effective date of
GNA’ is achieved. There is no provision to revise the firm start date of Connectivity
based on its actual implementation status, and accordingly, the contention of the
Petitioner that it is yet to be provided with the ‘firm’ start date of Connectivity by CTUIL
is rejected.
30. As per the above discussions and in terms of Regulation 11A(2) of the GNA
Regulations, Petitioner’s firm start date of Connectivity is 28.2.2026 and accordingly,
Petitioner was required to achieve financial closure by 28.8.2025.
31. Issue No.1 is answered accordingly.
Issue No. 2: Whether Petitioner meets the requirement of achieving Financial Closure
under Regulation 11A(2) of the GNA Regulations, in light of the documents submitted on
28.08.2025 and 27.11.2025. Whether the Commission ought to exercise its powers to
remove difficulties under Regulation 42 of the GNA Regulations to treat Petitioner as
compliant with the requirement of Financial Closure under Regulation 11A(2)? Whether
the Petitioner is entitled to a refund of Rs. 11.50 Crore paid by the Petitioner in lieu of
encashment of Conn-BGs?
Issue No.3: Whether the operation and effect of the letter dated 31.12.2025 issued by
the Respondent/ CTUIL revoking the Connectivity of 400 MW granted to the Applicant at
Bhadla-III PS is required to be stayed or quashed?
32. Let us peruse the documents required to be furnished to show compliance with
Regulation 11A(2). Regulation 11A(2) of the GNA Regulations prior to 3rd amendment
is quoted as under:
“…
11A. Conditions subsequent to be satisfied by the Connectivity Grantee
Order in Petition No. 7/MP/2026 along with IA Nos. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026 Page 28

(1) ….
(2) An applicant which is REGS (other than Hydro generating station), ESS (excluding
PSP) or Renewable power park developer to which final grant of connectivity has been
issued, shall have to achieve the financial closure for the capacity of such Connectivity,
latest by 6 months prior to the scheduled date of a commercial operation or start date of
Connectivity of such applicant, whichever is later:
Provided that such an applicant shall submit proof of Financial Closure of the project (with
copy of the loan sanction letter or proof of first disbursal of the loan amount) or copy of
the board resolution (if internal funding is planned for 100% of the project cost) to CTU
within 15 days of achieving the financial closure:
..”.
As per the above, the following documents shall be accepted as proof of financial
closure:
(i) Copy of the loan sanction letter or proof of the first disbursal of the loan amount
or
(ii) Copy of Board resolution (if internal funding is planned for 100% of the project
cost).
33. We have also perused Advisory dated 3.2.2025 issued by the CTUIL, quoted as under:
“Advisory for conditions subsequent to be satisfied by Connectivity Grantee under
GNA Regulations
[Rev-1 dated: 03.02.2025]
1. Documents to be submitted in satisfaction of conditions subsequent by the
Connectivity Grantee (under Regulation 11A of the GNA Regulations, 2022)
..
1.2. Financial Closure:
Land/Land BG route: An applicant which is REGS (other than Hydro generating station), ESS
(excluding PSP), or Renewable power park developer to which an in-principle grant of
connectivity has been issued shall have to achieve the financial closure for the capacity of
such Connectivity, latest by 6 months prior to the scheduled date of a commercial operation
or start date of Connectivity of such applicant, whichever is later.
LOA/PPA route: In case of REGS (other than Hydro generating station) or ESS (excluding
PSP) granted Connectivity under LoA route, the SCOD for the above clause shall be
considered as the SCOD as extended by REIA/ Distribution licensee / authorized agency on
behalf of distribution licensee, subject to the condition that any extension in timeline to
achieve FC due to extension in SCOD shall not be allowed more than 12 months from original
timeline as per initial SCOD.
Land/Land BG route to LOA route: Further, the entities who were earlier granted Connectivity
under Land or Land BG route and converted the Connectivity to LoA route, shall achieve FC
latest by 6 months prior to Start date of Connectivity.
LoA/PPA route to Land/Land BG route: In case applicant is granted Connectivity under
Order in Petition No. 7/MP/2026 along with IA Nos. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026 Page 29

As per above, we note that the document is titled “In-Principle sanction letter regarding
line of credit commitment” in place of “loan sanction letter”.
37. CTUIL, vide e-mail dated 18.11.2025, requested the Petitioner to submit revised
documents. Relevant extract of CTUIL e-mail dated 18.11.2025 is as under:
“In the furtherance of trailing mail regarding financial closure, Please find below
observations on the submitted documents:
1. Applicant has submitted an in-principle letter regarding line of credit commitment from
the Kotak Mahindra Bank. Please submit a sanction for term loan to fund the project.
It is requested to submit revised documents within 7 days to avoid any consequences as
stipulated under Regulation 11B of the GNA Regulations 2022.”
As per the above, CTUIL requested the Petitioner to submit the revised documents
within 7 days to avoid any consequences as stipulated under Regulation 11B of the
GNA Regulations.
38. Petitioner, vide e-mail dated 27.11.2025, furnished new documents substantiating the
Financial Closure. The relevant extract of Petitioner’s e-mail dated 27.11.2025 is as
under:
“Please find attached the revised below-mentioned documents for Financial Closure with
respect to the financial closure (FC) of 400 MW Renewable Power Park of M/s Prerak
Greentech Solar Private Limited having CTU application no: SW..1671216520154 dated
17/12/2022 as:
• Executed UDFC Copy
• Net-worth certificate of Connectivity Grantee (Prerak Greentech)
• Net-worth Certificate of Affiliate (DIFC)
• Board Resolution for Financial/Equity Commitment of Prerak Greentech
• Board Resolution of Affiliate (DIFC) for Fund Commitment to Prerak
Greentech
• Board Resolution of Connectivity Grantee (Prerak Greentech) for Fund
acceptance from DIFC
In case of any requirement, we would be happy to assist.”
As per the above, the Petitioner submitted the above six documents, including the
Board Resolutions dated 25th November 2025 and undertaking dated 27.11.2025.
Order in Petition No. 7/MP/2026 along with IA Nos. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026 Page 32

resources.
40. CTUIL, vide letter dated 31.12.2025, revoked the 400 MW connectivity granted to the
Petitioner. The relevant extract of the CTUIL letter dated 31.12.2025 is as under:
“Sub: Revocation of Connectivity due to non-compliance of Reg 11A(2) for
Connectivity application (SW9990894382- M029_D001 A007- 1671216520154) of M/s
Prerak Greentech Solar Private Limited
Ref.: i. Intimation for in-principle grant of 400 MW Connectivity issued by CTUIL vide letter
Ref. No. C/CTU/N/5/Conn-INT-1A/SW... 1671216520154 dated 14/11/2023
ii. Intimation for final grant of 400 MW Connectivity issued by CTUIL vide letter Ref. No.
C/CTU/N/5/Conn-INT-1C/SW... 1671216520154 dated 03/05/2024
Dear Sir,
This is with reference to your application no. SW9990894382-M029_D001_A007-
1671216520154 for connectivity of 400 MW in Bhadla III PS, Rajasthan. As per Regulations
11A (2) of CERC GNA Regulations, REGS (other than Hydro), ESS (excluding PSP) or
RPPD shall have to achieve Financial Closure latest by 6 months prior to the scheduled
date of a commercial operation or start date of Connectivity of such applicant, whichever is
later.
The application was reverted for clarification in the documents submitted for the Financial
Closure vide email dated 18-Nov-25. However, instead of submission of documents
towards clarification on the query of CTUIL, you have submitted a revised UD_FC along
with new documents which are of a later date beyond the due date for compliance of Reg.
11A (2). As you have failed to comply with the provisions of Regulation 11A (2) of
GNA regulation, Connectivity Granted against application no. SW9990894382-
M029_D001 A007-1671216520154 is hereby revoked with immediate effect in line with
Reg 11A (2) of GNA Regulations, 2022. Further, the treatment of submitted Bank
Guarantees shall be as per the prevailing CERC Regulations and directions issued from
time to time.
As per the above, CTUIL has revoked the connectivity granted to the Petitioner as the
revised FC documents submitted by the Petitioner were of ‘a later date beyond the due
date’ of 28.08.2025. However, CTUIL has not commented on the correctness of the
revised FC documents submitted by the Petitioner.
41. Petitioner has contended that it has furnished the required Board Resolution within the
due date, i.e. firstly, on 28.08.2025 and secondly on 27.11.2025, i.e. within 10 days
after notification of the discrepancy by CTUIL on 18.11.2025. On both occasions, the
very same Board Resolution has been submitted, issued within the due date for
achieving financial closure and is not of a later date beyond the due date, and no
infirmities have been pointed out by CTUIL in the said Board Resolution. Petitioner has
also stated that it was unable to provide the final loan sanction letter on account of the
Order in Petition No. 7/MP/2026 along with IA Nos. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026 Page 34

pendency of approval under Section 68 of the Electricity Act for the laying of an
overhead transmission line, and the associated uncertainty regarding the issuance of
the said approval.
42. We have considered the submissions of Petitioner and Respondent, CTUIL, in this
regard. We note that Petitioner furnished an Undertaking on 28.8.2025 stating its
financial closure through a loan (Rs 175 crore) and equity (Rs 39 crore). However, in
lieu of a ‘loan sanction letter’, the petitioner furnished an “In-Principle sanction letter
regarding line of credit commitment’ and the Petitioner has also conveyed its inability
to furnish a final loan sanction letter due to pending Section 68 approval. We agree that
CTU has rightly contended that “In-Principle sanction letter regarding line of credit
commitment” does not meet the requirement of Regulation 11A(2).
43. We do not agree with the petitioner’s contention that it furnished a Board resolution on
28.8.2025, which should have been considered by CTUIL for meeting Financial
Closure, as we have already noted that the petitioner had itself furnished an undertaking
dated 28.8.2025 for project funding mainly through a loan; therefore, it cannot argue
that it was funding the entire project through equity on 28.8.2025.
44. Petitioner has argued that CTU itself belatedly pointed out a discrepancy in its in-
principle sanction letter, and Petitioner furnished revised documents – revised Board
resolution and revised undertaking within 10 days of pointing out this discrepancy by
CTU, and hence should not be penalised by revocation of Connectivity.
45. We note that once Petitioner furnished an undertaking on 28.8.2025 stating that it has
achieved financial closure through a loan, it cannot contend that the Board Resolution
dated November 2025 stating funding through equity is only a minor deficiency to be
considered under removal of deficiency. We are of the considered view that CTUIL has
rightly revoked the Petitioner's Connectivity, having not considered the documents
furnished by the Petitioner, thereby changing the entire basis of the Financial Closure.
Such documents are to be considered fresh documents, and since the last date to
achieve financial closure had already passed, and to furnish financial closure
documents was already over, CTUIL rightly revoked the Connectivity.
46. Petitioner has placed its reliance on this Commission’s order dated 05.12.2025 in
Petition Nos. 768/MP/2025 and 769/MP/2025 seeking that its Connectivity should not
be revoked on payment of compensation charges. The relevant extract of the order
dated 05.12.2025 in Petition Nos. 768/MP/2025 and 769/MP/2025 are as under:
Order in Petition No. 7/MP/2026 along with IA Nos. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026 Page 35

“27. We have considered the submissions of Petitioners and the information on
record. As per the submission of the Petitioners, they have achieved the financial
closure within the stipulated time i.e. on 21.06.2025 against the last date of 25.06.2025
in case of 768/MP/2025 and on 23.06.2025 against the last date of 26.06.2025 in case
of 769/MP/2025, but have failed in timely submission of documents and submitted it
after delay of 54 and 56 days respectively.
28. It is also noted that CTU vide its email dated 16.01.2025 intimated AGEL that its due
date for submission of financial closure documents is 25.06.2025 and therefore requested
AGEL to submit financial closure documents in line with Regulation 11A (2) of GNA
Regulations, 2022. Similarly, CTU, vide its email dated 16.01.2025, intimated SRPL that
the due date for submission of financial closure documents is 26.06.2025 and therefore
requested SRPL to submit the financial closure documents in line with Regulation 11A(2)
of the GNA Regulations, 2022. However, neither of the petitioners has furnished any
justification for the delay in submission of the FC documents after a delay of 54/ 56 days,
despite being reminded by CTUIL vide its e-mail communication dated 16.01.2025, well in
advance. Petitioners have only submitted that they have achieved the financial closure and
substantially complied with the extant GNA Regulations of this Commission.
30.Petitioners have submitted that the renewable parks have achieved substantial
progress. In the case of SRPL (769/MP/2025), the Park has been charged and
commissioned. Various RE generators in the park have commissioned their respective RE
generation capacities of 990 MW and are injecting power into the grid. Further, in the case
of AGEL (768/MP/2025), substantial progress towards the implementation of the Park (i.e.,
the pooling substation and line) has been achieved and is targeted for completion by
December 2025. Therefore, we find that the instant Petitions are fit cases for exercising the
power to relax and the power to remove difficulty to condone the delay in furnishing
proof/copies of financial closure documents in terms of the first proviso to Regulation 11A(2)
of the GNA 2nd Amendment Regulations 2024 by the petitioners. The relevant extracts of
GNA Regulations are as under:
…..
32. Accordingly, we condone the delay in furnishing proof/ copy of financial closure
documents in terms of the first proviso to Regulation 11A(2) of the GNA 2nd Amendment
Regulations 2024 by the petitioners, subject to payment of compensation equivalent to 5%
of the total Conn BGs amount submitted by the petitioners within 15 days of this Order. The
amount received by the CTUIL under the aforementioned compensation shall be utilised to
reduce the monthly transmission charges under the 2020 Sharing Regulations. On receipt
of the compensation amount from the petitioners, CTUIL is directed to reinstate/ restore the
connectivity of the Petitioners. However, this order shall not be treated as a precedent,
having been decided keeping in view the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case.”
As per the above, submission of the requisite financial closure document with a delay
was permitted, subject to payment of compensation equivalent to 5% of the total Conn
BGs.
47. We note that the Petitioner has indicated that it had already acquired 94% of the land
towards development of the project, and the project is planned to be commissioned by
March 2027. Further, the petitioner has indicated that it has signed an Implementation
Service Agreement (ISA) with ABC CT RE Park (01) Private Limited for utilising 335
MW out of 400 MW Solar Park connectivity. Petitioner has also submitted that
revocation of connectivity would result in abandonment of the project, despite having
Order in Petition No. 7/MP/2026 along with IA Nos. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026 Page 36

sufficient means and measures to set up the project through multiple modes. which is
already in the advanced stage of construction presently. Considering the same, we find
that the Petitioner's case is a fit case for the exercise of the powers to relax and remove
difficulties. However, since there is a delay at the Petitioner’s end in achieving the
financial closure and in submitting the requisite documents towards financial closure,
we are of the view that such relaxation can only be allowed with payment of
compensation for such delay.
48. In light of the above discussions, in exercise of the Power conferred under Regulations
41 and 42 of the GNA Regulations, we are of the view that the Regulation 11A(2) of the
GNA Regulations shall be relaxed to the extent that the Financial Closure documents
submitted by the Petitioner vide e-mail dated 27.11.2025 shall be considered by CTUIL
for scrutinising, if they comply with requirement of Regulation 11A(2) of the GNA
Regulations, subject to payment of compensation by the Petitioner as per subsequent
paragraphs. Accordingly, the revocation letter issued by CTUIL dated 31.12.2025 shall
stand quashed.
49. In light of the above discussions, we direct as under:
(a) CTUIL is directed to check the correctness of the documents submitted by the
Petitioner vide e-mail dated 27.11.2025 within a period of 15 days of issue of this
Order and convey the same to the Petitioner.
(b) The compensation amount for delay in achieving financial closure shall be calculated
based on the principles followed in the Order dated 05.12.2025 in Petition Nos.
768/MP/2025 and 769/MP/2025, which provides for payment of compensation
equivalent to 5% of total Conn-BGs amount submitted by the Petitioner. Accordingly,
the amount of compensation shall be calculated as 5% of the total Conn-BGs. The
amount of compensation shall be calculated by CTUIL and conveyed to the
Petitioner within a period of 15 days from the issuance of this Order.
(c) In case the financial closure documents furnished by the Petitioner are found in
Order by the CTUIL, the amount as calculated by CTUIL under clause (b) above
shall be adjusted from the amount deposited by the Petitioner in lieu of encashment
of Conn-BGs (Rs 11.5 Crore). The balance amount after adjustment of the
compensation amount shall be returned to the Petitioner within a period of 7 days
thereafter.
(d) The amount collected by the CTUIL under the aforementioned compensation shall
Order in Petition No. 7/MP/2026 along with IA Nos. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026 Page 37

be utilised to reduce the monthly transmission charges under the 2020 Sharing
Regulations.
(e) Petitioner shall furnish the Conn-BGs (Conn-BG1, Conn-BG2, Conn-BG3, as
applicable), within a period of 15 days of confirmation of the correctness of
documents under Clause (a) by the CTUIL. If the Petitioner fails to re-furnish the
Conn-BGs within the stipulated timelines as mentioned above, CTUIL shall revoke
the connectivity within a period of 7 days of the lapse of a period of 15 days allowed
for re-furnishing the Conn-BGs.
50. The Petition No. 7/MP/2026 along with IA No. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026 stands disposed
of in terms of above.
Sd/ Sd/ Sd/
(Harish Dudani) (Ramesh Babu V) (Jishnu Barua)
Member Member Chairperson
CERC Website S. No. 300/2026
Order in Petition No. 7/MP/2026 along with IA Nos. 2/IA/2026 and 7/IA/2026 Page 38

items.subject: Non-compliance with the provisions of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for grant of trading licence and other related matters) Regulations, 2020.
items.pdf_text:
Petition No.10/SM/2026
Coram:
Shri Jishnu Barua, Chairperson
Shri Ramesh Babu V., Member
Shri Harish Dudani, Member
Shri Ravinder Singh Dhillon, Member
Date of Order: 13th May, 2026
In the matter of
Non-compliance with the provisions of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission
(Procedure, Terms and Conditions for grant of trading licence and other related
matters) Regulations, 2020.
And
In the matter of
Instinct Infra & Power Limited,
C-201, Naraina Industrial Area, Phase-1,
New Delhi-110 028
…Respondent
ORDER
Vide order dated 7.9.2005 in Petition No. 15/2005, Instinct Infra & Power Limited
(formerly known as ‘Instinct Advertising & Marketing Ltd’) was granted an inter-State
trading licence for Category ‘A’ for trading in electricity in India, in accordance with the
application made under sub-section (1) of Section 15 of the Electricity Act, 2003 (the
‘Act’) read with the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and
Conditions for grant of Trading licence and other related matters) Regulations, 2004.
Hereinafter, Instinct Infra & Power Limited shall be referred to as the ‘licensee/
Respondent’.
Order in Petition No. 10/SM/2026 Page 1 of 8

2. Pursuant to the notification of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission
(Procedure, Terms and Conditions for grant of trading licence and other related
matters) Regulations, 2009, the trading licence granted to the licensee was re-
categorized as Category ‘IV’. The licence was further upgraded from Category ‘IV’ to
Category ‘III’ vide order dated 28.2.2013 in Petition No. 11/RC/2013. Consequent to
the enactment of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms
and Conditions for grant of trading licence and other related matters) Regulations,
2020, and subsequent amendments thereof (in short ‘the Trading Licence Regulations,
2020’), the Respondent’s category was revised to Category IV vide order dated
4.3.2024 in Petition No. 313/TD/2023. In the said order, it was also made clear that the
licensee shall remain bound by the terms and conditions mentioned in the order dated
7.9.2005. At present, the Respondent holds a Category IV trading licence granted in
terms of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020.
3. Regulations 9(3) and 9(4) of the Trading Licence Regulations,2020 provide as
under:
“9. Obligations of the Trading Licensee:
(3) The Trading Licensee shall not exceed at any point of time 110 percent
of the volume of trading authorized during a Year under the licence granted
to him.
(4) The Trading Licensee shall make an appropriate application
accompanied by prescribed fees for up-gradation of its licence to a higher
category or down-gradation of its licence to a lower category in order to
fulfil the conditions of these regulations in accordance with the procedure
specified in Regulation 15 of these regulations.”
4. Regulation 15 of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020 provides for the
procedure for upgradation or downgradation of trading licence. Relevant clauses of the
Order in Petition No. 10/SM/2026 Page 2 of 8

same are extracted as under:
“15. Procedure for upgradation of licence or down-gradation of licence
or compliance of Net Worth criteria for Category I Trading Licensee
(1) Upgradation of licence:
(a) The Trading Licensee may at any time during a particular year
apply for a higher category licence on the basis of the volume
proposed to be traded in a particular Year.
(b) The Trading Licensee shall file an application before the
Commission for upgradation of its licence to a higher category as soon
as he expects the trading volume to exceed the trading volume limit
specified for the Trading Licensee’s existing category.”
As per Regulation 9 (3), the trading licensee is obligated not to exceed at any
point in time 110 percent of the volume of trading authorized during a Year under the
licence granted to him. Further, in case, the licensee foresees that the trading volume
might be exceeding the permissible limits during a year, then he is required to file an
application of upgradation of its licence under the provisions of Regulation 15(1)(b)
of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020 as soon as he expects the trading volume
to exceed the trading volume unit as mentioned in its existing category.
5. Regulations 11(2), (4) and (5) and Regulation 12(2) and (3) of Trading Licence
Regulations, 2020 provide as under:
“11. Submission of Information:
(2) Furnish monthly information through Forms IV-A, IV-B, IV-C, IV-D, IV-
E, IV-F, IVG and IV-H in respect of inter-State trading, intra-State trading
on the basis of the inter-State trading licence, trading through power
exchanges, Banking of electricity, short-term, long-term trading and
Cross Border Trade of Electricity, so as to reach the Commission before
15th of the succeeding month:
Provided that the information sent to the Commission, shall be posted on
the website of the Trading Licensee by 15th of the succeeding month,
Order in Petition No. 10/SM/2026 Page 3 of 8

and such report shall be available on the website for not less than five
Years;
(4) Submit annual return of inter-State transactions detailing:
(a) total volume transacted (in MUs and Rupees) and the total trading
margin charged thereon,
(b) total volume transacted in intra-State transactions on the basis of
the inter-state trading licence (in MU and Rupees),
(c) total volume transacted on Power Exchange and the total trading
margin charged thereon,
(d) total volumes of Renewable Energy Certificates transacted,
(e) complete list of Buyers and Sellers in the above categories,
certified by Chartered Accountant or Cost Accountant by 31st May
every Year as per Form IV-J;
(5) Submit to the Commission copies of the Annual Reports including
Directors’ report, Auditors’ report, Balance Sheet and Profit and Loss
Account pertaining to inter-State and intra-State trading on the basis of
the inter-State trading licence, segment of the business along with all the
Schedules and notes to the accounts, not later than nine months after the
close of the Year to which they relate and shall keep them posted on its
website or in any authorized website for a period of at least five Years;
12. Standards of Performance:
(2) Till such time the standards of performance are specified under clause
(1), the Trading Licensee shall furnish to the Commission the
performance details for each Year in the format prescribed by the
Commission in Form V, appended to these regulations by 30th April
immediately following the Year ending on 31st March.
(3) The Trading Licensee shall display on its website (i) the volume of
inter-State and intra-State trading on the basis of the inter-State trading
licence, if any, on monthly basis; (ii) trading licences held by it; (iii)
petitions filed before the Commission and the orders including interim
orders, if any, issued by the Commission to ensure dissemination of
information to its clients.”
6. It has been observed that repeated reminder letters/emails dated 21.4.2025,
20.5.2025, 9.12.2025, 23.12.2025, 30.12.2025, 16.1.2026, and 17.2.2026 were
issued to the Respondent for providing the requisite information in terms of
Regulations 11(2), 11(4), 11(5), 12(2) and 12(3) of the Trading Licence Regulations,
2020 and the Respondent was directed to apply for upgradation of its trading licence
Order in Petition No. 10/SM/2026 Page 4 of 8

from Category IV to Category III. However, the Respondent has neither furnished the
required information nor filed a Petition for upgradation of his licence in terms of the
Trading Licence Regulations, 2020.
7. Regulations 17(7), (8), (10), (11) and (12) of Trading Licence Regulations,
2020 enumerate specific acts constituting contravention and non-compliance by a
Trading Licensee as under:
“17. Contravention by Trading Licensee
(7) Delay or non-submission of monthly transaction information sought
under clause (2) of Regulation 11;
(8) Failure to comply with Regulation 15 of these regulations
(10) Non-submission or delay in submission of any report required to be
submitted by the Trading Licensee under any of the regulations
mentioned in clause (1) of this regulation;
(11) Delay in submission of any other information sought by the
Commission;
(12) Failure to make mandatory disclosures or reporting in accordance
with the provision to clause (2) of Regulation 11 of these regulations on
Trading Licensee’s website.”
8. Regulation 18 of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020 provides for the
procedure for taking cognizance of the contraventions as under:
“18. Procedure for taking cognizance of the contraventions
(1) The Commission, on being satisfied on the basis of the information in
its possession or on basis of the information submitted by any person that
a prima facie case exists against any Trading Licensee with respect to
any of the provisions of Regulation 17, may initiate Suo-motu
proceedings against the Trading Licensee and may direct the Trading
Licensee to submit such information and explanation as may be
considered necessary for the purpose of the proceeding:
Provided that the proceedings for non-payment of fee shall be initiated
if the Trading Licensee fails to deposit the fees and surcharge, if any,
Order in Petition No. 10/SM/2026 Page 5 of 8

within seven days of the expiry of due date of payment as per the
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Payment of Fee)
Regulations, 2012:
Provided further that the licence shall be deemed to be suspended
after expiry of fifteen days from the due date of payment and shall
remain suspended till the payment of fees and surcharge, if any, is
made or suspension is withdrawn.
(2) No penalty shall be imposed on the Trading Licensee without giving
it an opportunity of being heard.
(3) The penalties, if any, shall be imposed in accordance with Regulation
19 of these regulations.”
9. Section 19 of the Act provides that:
“19. Revocation of licence
(1) If the Appropriate Commission, after making an enquiry, is satisfied
that public interest so requires, it may revoke a licence in any of the
following cases, namely: -
(a) where the licensee, in the opinion of the Appropriate Commission,
makes wilful and prolonged default in doing anything required of him
by or under this Act or the rules or regulations made thereunder;
(b) where the licensee breaks any of the terms or conditions of his
licence the breach of which is expressly declared by such licence to
render it liable to revocation;
(c) where the licensee fails, within the period fixed in this behalf by his
licence, or any longer period which the Appropriate Commission may
have granted therefor –
(i) to show, to the satisfaction of the Appropriate Commission, that
he is in a position fully and efficiently to discharge the duties and
obligations imposed on him by his licence;
(ii) or to make the deposit or furnish the security, or pay the fees
or other charges required by his licence;
(d) where in the opinion of the Appropriate Commission the financial
position of the licensee is such that he is unable fully and efficiently to
discharge the duties and obligations imposed on him by his licence.
(2) Where in its opinion the public interest so requires, the Appropriate
Commission may, on application, or with the consent of the licensee,
Order in Petition No. 10/SM/2026 Page 6 of 8

revoke his licence as to the whole or any part of his area of distribution
or transmission or trading upon such terms and conditions as it thinks fit.
(3) No licence shall be revoked under sub-section (1) unless the
Appropriate Commission has given to the licensee not less than three
months’ notice, in writing, stating the grounds on which it is proposed to
revoke the licence, and has considered any cause shown by the licensee
within the period of that notice, against the proposed revocation.
(4) The Appropriate Commission may, instead of revoking a licence
under sub-section (1), permit it to remain in force subject to such further
terms and conditions as it thinks fit to impose, and any further terms and
conditions so imposed shall be binding upon and be observed by the
licensee and shall be of like force and effect as if they were contained in
the licence.
(5) Where the Commission revokes a licence under this section, it shall
serve a notice of revocation upon the licensee and fix a date on which
the revocation shall take effect.
(6) Where the Appropriate Commission has given notice for revocation of
licence under sub-section (5), without prejudice to any penalty which may
be imposed or prosecution proceeding which may be initiated under this
Act, the licensee may, after prior approval of that Commission, sell his
utility to any person who is found eligible by that Commission for grant of
licence.”
Accordingly, in terms of Section 19 of the Act read with the Trading Licence
Regulations, 2020, where the licensee, in the opinion of the Commission, makes
willful and prolonged default in doing anything required of him by or under the Act or
the Rules or the Regulations, the Commission may revoke the licence after serving a
notice of not less than three months.
10. The Respondent has not complied with the directions of the Commission
issued vide letters/ emails dated 21.4.2025, 20.5.2025, 9.12.2025, 23.12.2025,
30.12.2025, 16.1.2026, and 17.2.2026. The Respondent was abundantly cautioned
vide the aforesaid letters/ emails that non-compliance with the directions of the
Commission would ultimately attract penal provisions in terms of the Act as well as
Order in Petition No. 10/SM/2026 Page 7 of 8

the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020, including the revocation of his trading licence.
However, the Respondent has been recurrently acting in non-compliance with the
Trading Licence Regulations, 2020. In our prima facie view, the licensee is not entitled
to hold a licence when he has failed to make mandatory disclosures or to report and
also failed to upgrade its trading licence, in violation of the Trading Licence
Regulations, 2020. Accordingly, we direct the Respondent to file its response within
two months, as to why its inter-State trading licence should not be revoked for willful
default in making mandatory disclosures/ reporting, as well as for not upgrading its
trading licence. This order shall also be treated as notice under sub-section (3) of
Section 19 of the Act, and if no reply is received within three months and unless
otherwise directed by the Commission, the licence of the licensee shall stand revoked
after expiry of the period of three months from the date of issue of this order.

(Ravinder Singh Dhillon) (Harish Dudani) (Ramesh Babu V.) (Jishnu Barua)

The Petitioner, SR and ER Power Transmission Limited (hereinafter referred to
as “SRERPTL”), has filed the present Petition for the grant of a transmission licence
under Sections 14, 15 and 79 (1) (e) of the Electricity Act, 2003 (hereinafter referred to
as “the Act”) read with the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure,
Terms, and Conditions for grant of Transmission Licence and other related matters)
Regulations, 2024 (hereinafter referred to as “the Transmission Licence Regulations”)
to establish the inter-State transmission system for the “Strengthening between SR

to as “the Project”) consisting of the following elements:

2. The Petitioner has made the following prayers:
“(a) Grant Transmission License to the Applicant ; and
(b) Allow the sharing and recovery of Transmission Charges for Inter-State
Transmission System for “Inter-Regional Strengthening between SR Grid and
ER Grid” as per Sharing of Inter-state Transmission Charges and Losses CERC
Regulations 2020 and any other amendment thereon issued from time to time
by CERC.
(c) Pass such other order / orders, as may be deemed fit and proper in the facts
& circumstances of the case.”
Hearing dated 25.3.2026 and 24.4.2026
3. Notice was issued to the parties to file their respective replies and rejoinders.
Order in Petition No. 121/TL/2026
Page 5

Vide Record of Proceedings for the hearing (hereinafter referred to as “RoP”) dated
25.3.2026, the PFCCL was directed to submit, the complete Bid Evaluation Report,
including details of bidders at the RFQ and RFP stages, their quoted tariffs, evaluation
by the Bid Evaluation Committee (BEC), and minutes of meetings, along with the
comparative analysis of levelised tariff in accordance with the applicable CERC Tariff
Regulations based on the benchmarking capital cost assessed by the CEA/CTUIL, with
detailed calculations, and the recommendations of the Cost Committee along with
detailed cost estimates, underlying assumptions, and justification. After hearing the
Petitioner’s representative on 24.4.2026, the matter was reserved for order.
4. In compliance with the directions vide RoP dated 25.3.2026, PFCCL filed the
requisite information sought vide letter dated 2.4.2026. The same has been taken on
record.
5. The Petitioner has submitted that in accordance with the “Guidelines for
Encouraging Competition in Development of Transmission Projects” and “Tariff Based
Competitive Bidding Guidelines for Transmission Service” (hereinafter referred to as
“the Guidelines”) issued by the Ministry of Power, Government of India, under Section
63 of the Act, PFC Consultancy Limited (hereinafter referred to as “PFCCL”) was
notified by the Ministry of Power, Government of India, vide Gazette Notification. No.
CG-DL-E-24052025-263324 dated 21.5.2025 as the Bid Process Coordinator
(hereinafter referred to as “BPC”) for the purpose of selection of bidder as the
Transmission Service Provider (hereinafter referred to as “TSP”) to establish the “Inter-
Regional Strengthening between SR Grid and ER Grid” on a Build, Own, Operate and
Transfer basis.
Order in Petition No. 121/TL/2026
Page 6

6. PFCCL, in its capacity as the BPC, initiated the bid process on 23.6.2025 and
completed the same on 3.2.2026 in accordance with the Guidelines. Power Grid
Corporation of India Limited was selected as the successful bidder, having quoted the
lowest transmission charges of Rs. 3118.60 million per annum to provide transmission
services to the beneficiaries of the transmission system.
7. The RfP was issued on 23.6.2025. At the RfP (Technical and Financial) stage,
six bidders, namely, (i) Adani Energy Solutions Limited; (ii) Dilip Buildcon Limited; (iii)
Enerica Infra 1 Private Limited; (iv) Power Grid Corporation of India Limited; (v)
Resonia Limited, and (vi) The Tata Power Company Limited, submitted their offers.
The RfP (Technical) bids of the bidders were opened by the Bid Opening Committee
at the Central Electricity Authority on 6.11.2025 in the presence of a representative of
the bidders. Based on the recommendation of the Bid Evaluation Committee (“BEC”),
the RfP (Financial) Bids-Initial Price Offer of the bidders were opened on 5.12.2025.
The Lowest Initial Price Offer discovered (Best Deal) on the MSTC portal was Rs.
3150.00 million per annum. The details of the quoted transmission charges by the
bidders are as under:

8. As per Clause 3.5.1 of the RfP document, initial offers shall be ranked on the
Order in Petition No. 121/TL/2026
Page 7

9. The e-reverse was conducted on the MSTC portal on 9.12.2025 and was
concluded on the same day. Two bidders participated in the e-reverse auction. The
following bidders were qualified to participate in the e-reverse auction. The following

10. As per the Bid Evaluation Report dated 11.12.2025, Power Grid Corporation of
India Limited emerged as the successful bidder with the lowest quoted transmission
charges of Rs. 3118.60 million per annum. BEC, vide its certificate dated 11.12.2025,
has certified that the entire bid process has been carried out in accordance with the
Guidelines issued by the Ministry of Power under Section 63 of the Act. BEC has
further certified that the transmission charges discovered through the e-reverse auction
are acceptable.
11. Consequent to its selection as the lowest bidder, a Letter of Intent (hereinafter
referred to as “LoI”) was issued to Power Grid Corporation of India Limited on
Order in Petition No. 121/TL/2026
Page 8

15.12.2025, which was accepted by Power Grid Corporation of India Limited. Under
the terms of RfP and the Letter of Intent, the successful bidder is obligated to
accomplish the following tasks:
a) Provide Contract Performance Guarantee in favour of Central Transmission
Utility of India Limited (CTUIL);
b) Execute Share Purchase Agreement and Transmission Service Agreement;
c) Acquire, for the Acquisition Price, 100% equity share of SR and ER Power
Transmission Limited from PFCCL along with all its related assets and
liabilities;
d) Make an application to this Commission for the adoption of transmission
charges, as required under Section 63 of the Act; and
e) Apply to this Commission for the grant of a transmission licence.
12. Power Grid Corporation of India Limited has furnished the Contract
Performance Guarantee (hereinafter referred to as “CPG”) in favour of the Nodal
Agency, i.e., CTUIL, for Rs. 55.00 crore on 3.2.2026 and has acquired a hundred per
cent equity holding in SR and ER Power Transmission Limited on 3.2.2026. The
Petitioner entered into a Transmission Service Agreement (TSA) with CTUIL on
3.2.2026.
13. Section 14 of the Act provides that the Appropriate Commission may, on an
application made under Section 15 of the Act, grant a licence to any person to transmit
electricity as a transmission licensee in any area as may be specified in the licence.
The word “person” has been defined in Section 2 (49) of the Act to include any
company or body corporate or association or body of individuals, whether incorporated
or not, or artificial juridical person. The Petitioner has been incorporated under the
Order in Petition No. 121/TL/2026
Page 9

Companies Act, 2013. The main objective of the Petitioner Company is as under:
“To develop Power System Network, To plan, promote and develop an
integrated and efficient power transmission system network in all its aspects
including planning, investigation, research, design and engineering, preparation
of preliminary, feasibility and definite project reports, construction, operation
and maintenance of transmission lines, sub-stations, load dispatch stations
and communication facilities and appurtenant works, coordination of integrated
operation of state, regional and national grid system, execution of turn-key jobs
for other utilities/organizations and wheeling of power in accordance with the
policies, guidelines and objectives laid down by the Central Government from
time to time”
14. Section 15 (1) of the Act provides that every application under Section 14 of
the Act shall be made in such manner and in such form as may be specified by the
Appropriate Commission and shall be accompanied by such fees as may be prescribed
by the Central Government. The Commission has specified the Transmission Licence
Regulations in this regard. Regulation 4 (1) of the Transmission Licence Regulations
provides that eligibility for the grant of a licence for inter-State transmission of electricity
is contingent upon the entity being selected either through the competitive bidding
process under Section 63 of the Electricity Act, 2003 or by the Central Government or
its authorised agency to implement a project under the regulated tariff mechanism.
Regulation 10 (1) of the Transmission Licence Regulations provided that, in case the
licensee has been selected for implementation of the project in accordance with the
competitive bidding guidelines, the transmission tariff in terms of the Transmission
Service Agreement shall be adopted by the Commission under Section 63 of the Act.
The Project under consideration has been identified for development under competitive
bidding by a competent authority, and the selection of the Project developer has been
certified to have been made in accordance with the Guidelines for competitive bidding.
15. Regulation 5 of the Transmission Licence Regulations, 2024 provides for the
procedure for granting of a transmission licence as under:
Order in Petition No. 121/TL/2026
Page 10

“(1) The application for the grant of licence shall be made to the Commission
in Form-I appended to these regulations and shall be accompanied by such
fee as may be prescribed by the Central Government from time to time under
sub-section (1) of section 15 of the Act.
(2) The application shall be supported with an affidavit in accordance with
Regulation 17 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of
Business) Regulations, 2023.
(3) The applicant shall submit the original application in electronic form along
with enclosures on the e-filing portal of the Commission and electronically
serve a copy of such application on all the concerned DICs of the project and
the Central Transmission Utility. The application shall be served through e-mail
on the concerned DICs of the project who are not registered on the e-filing
portal of the Commission.
(4) The applicant shall also upload the complete application along with
annexures on its website, in English. The applicant shall also upload on its
website, the details as per Form-I and Form-II appended to these regulations
in the Indian language of the State or the Union Territory where an element of
the project or concerned transmission line is situated or proposed to be
situated. The application shall be kept posted on the website of the applicant
till such time the application is disposed of by the Commission.
(5) The applicant shall, within 3 working days of filing the application, publish a
notice of its application in Form-II appended to these regulations in at least two
leading daily digital newspapers, one in English language and another in the
Indian language of the State or Union Territory where an element of the project
or concerned transmission line is situated or proposed to be situated, inviting
comments from the general public. The notice shall also be kept posted on the
website of the applicant.
(6) The Registry of the Commission shall carry out a preliminary scrutiny of the
application and convey the defects, if any, as far as possible within 7 days of
receipt of the application. The defects shall be rectified by the applicant within
a period of 7 days from the date of such intimation from the Registry of the

notice in terms of Clause (5) of this Regulation submit to the Commission on

Page 11

affidavit the details of the notice published, names of the digital newspapers in

and enclosing the relevant pages of the publication of notice.

20. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner, BPC, and CTUIL. The
proviso to Clause 2.15.2 of the RfP provides that “if for any reason attributable to the
BPC, the said activities are not completed by the Selected Bidder within the above
period of ten (10) days as mentioned in this clause, such period of 10 days shall be
extended, on a day-to-day basis till the end of the Bid validity period”. As per the above
provision, the selected bidder was required to complete all the activities, including the
acquisition of the SPVs, by 26.12.2025. Though the LoI was issued on 15.12.2025,
BPC, vide its letter dated 2.2.2026, in terms of Clause 2.15.2 of the RfP, extended the
date up to 3.2.2026 for completion of all activities by the successful bidder. The
selected bidder furnished the Contract Performance Guarantee in favour of the Nodal
Agency (CTUIL) for Rs. 55.00 crore on 3.2.2026 and acquired a hundred per cent
equity-holding in the applicant company on 3.2.2026 after execution of the Share

issuance of the acquisition of the SPV to the successful bidder. The successful bidder,
namely Power Grid Corporation of India Limited, acquired the SPV on 3.2.2026.

Petitioner satisfies the conditions for the grant of an inter-State transmission licence

construction, operation, and maintenance of the transmission system as described in
para 1 of this order. We, therefore, direct that a public notice in two daily digital

Section 15 of the Act be published to invite suggestions or objections to the grant of a
transmission licence aforesaid. The objections or suggestions, if any, shall be filed by
any person before the Commission by 22.5.2026.

provisions of the TSA, the applicable provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003, and the
Transmission Licence Regulations, as framed and notified by the Commission.
23. It is observed that as per Article 5.1.1 of the TSA, the TSP, at its own cost and
expense, shall be responsible for designing, constructing, erecting, testing, and
commissioning each element of the Project by scheduled COD in accordance with the
various regulations of the Central Electricity Authority regarding Technical Standards
and Grid Standards, Prudent Utility Practices and other applicable laws. Further, Article
5.4 of the TSA provides that the TSP shall ensure that the Project is designed, built

This Petition has been filed by the Petitioner, NTPC Limited (“NTPC”), for

4. The Petition was heard on 24.6.2025, wherein it was observed that the
Petitioner had also claimed a supplementary tariff towards the Modified System of
Emission Control System (“ECS”), which was commissioned on 15.8.2022. The
Commission, therefore, directed that in respect of the supplementary tariff
determination towards the ECS, the Petitioner is at liberty to file a separate Petition in
accordance with the provisions of the applicable Tariff Regulations, based on the
actual capital expenditure duly certified by the auditor.
5. The Respondent, Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Company Limited (“TNPDCL”)
and the Respondent, Kerala State Electricity Board Limited (“KSEBL”) have filed their
replies to the Petition vide replies dated 1.9.2025 and 2.7.2025 respectively, and the
Petitioner has filed its rejoinder to the said replies vide affidavits dated 15.9.2025. The
matter was again heard on 28.10.2025, and the Petitioner was directed to submit
certain additional information, and the order was reserved in the Petition with the
Order in Petition No. 627/GT/2025 Page 4 of 56

consent of the parties. In compliance with the Commission's directions, the Petitioner
has filed the additional information vide affidavit dated 17.11.2025. In addition to this,
the Petitioner, vide the affidavit dated 3.11.2025, also placed on record certain
documents and certificates that were unintentionally omitted while filing the Petition
and for accuracy and completeness of records in the Petition. Based on the
submissions of the parties and the documents on record, we proceed to truing up the
tariff of the generating station for the period 2019-24, after a prudence check, in the
subsequent paragraphs.
Capital Cost
6. Regulation 19(1) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations provides that the capital cost as
determined by the Commission after a prudence check in accordance with this
regulation shall form the basis of the determination of the tariff for existing and new
projects. Regulation 19(3) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations provides that the capital cost
of an existing project shall include the following:
(3) The Capital cost of an existing project shall include the following:
(a) Capital cost admitted by the Commission prior to 1.4.2019 duly trued up by
excluding liability, if any, as on 1.4.2019;
(b) Additional capitalization and de-capitalization for the respective year of tariff as
determined in accordance with these regulations;
(c) Capital expenditure on account of renovation and modernisation as admitted by
this Commission in accordance with these regulations;
(d) Capital expenditure on account of ash disposal and utilization including handling
and transportation facility;
(e)Capital expenditure incurred towards railway infrastructure and its augmentation for
transportation of coal up to the receiving end of generating station but does not include
the transportation cost and any other appurtenant cost paid to the railway;
(f) and Capital cost incurred or projected to be incurred by a thermal generating station,
on account of implementation of the norms under Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT)
scheme of Government of India shall be considered by the Commission subject to
sharing of benefits accrued under the PAT scheme with the beneficiaries.
Order in Petition No. 627/GT/2025 Page 5 of 56

7. The order dated 25.9.2021 in Petition No. 220/GT/2020 (pertaining to truing up
of tariff for the period 2014-19), approved the closing capital cost of Rs.157587.03 (net
of undischarged liabilities) as on 31.3.2019. The said amount was considered the
opening capital cost as on 1.4.2019 for the determination of the tariff for the period
2019-24, in terms of the order dated 17.11.2021 in Petition No. 444/GT/2020. The
Petitioner, in the instant Petition, has also claimed the opening capital cost of Rs
157587.03 lakh as on 1.4.2019. Accordingly, the same is considered as opening
capital cost as on 1.4.2019, for the purpose of truing up the tariff for the period 2019-
24, in accordance with Regulation 19(3) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations.
Additional Capital Expenditure:
8. Regulations 25 and 26 of the 2019 Tariff Regulations provide as under:
“25. Additional Capitalisation within the original scope and after the cut-off date:
(1) The additional capital expenditure incurred or projected to be incurred in respect of
an existing project or a new project on the following counts within the original scope of
work and after the cutoff date may be admitted by the Commission, subject to prudence
check:
(a) Liabilities to meet award of arbitration or for compliance of the directions or
order of any statutory authority, or order or decree of any court of law;
(b) Change in law or compliance of any existing law;
(c) Deferred works relating to ash pond or ash handling system in the
original scope of work;
(d) Liability for works executed prior to the cut-off date;
(e) Force Majeure events;
(f) Liability for works admitted by the Commission after the cut-off date to
the extent of discharge of such liabilities by actual payments; and
(g) Raising of ash dyke as a part of ash disposal system.
(2) In case of replacement of assets deployed under the original scope of the existing
project after cut – off date, the additional capitalisation may be admitted by the
Commission, after making necessary adjustments in the gross fixed assets and the
cumulated depreciation, subject to prudence check on the following grounds:
(a) The useful life of the assets is not commensurate with the useful life of the
project and such assets have been fully depreciated in accordance with the
provisions of these regulations.
(b) The replacement of the assets or equipment is necessary on account of
change in law or Force Majeure conditions;
Order in Petition No. 627/GT/2025 Page 6 of 56

(c) The replacement of such assets or equipment is necessary on account of
obsolescence of technology; and
(d) The replacement of such assets or equipment has otherwise been allowed
by the Commission.
26. Additional Capitalisation beyond the original scope
(1) The capital expenditure, in respect of existing generating station or the transmission
system including communication system, incurred or projected to be incurred on the
following counts beyond the original scope, may be admitted by the Commission,
subject to prudence check:
(a) Liabilities to meet award of arbitration or for compliance of order or
directions of any statutory authority, or order or decree of any court of law;
(b) Change in law or compliance of any existing law;
(c) Force Majeure events;
(d) Need for higher security and safety of the plant as advised or directed by
appropriate Indian Government Instrumentality or statutory authorities
responsible for national or internal security;
(e) Deferred works relating to ash pond or ash handling system in additional to
the original scope of work, on case to case basis:
Provided also that of any expenditure has been claimed under Renovation and
Maintenance (R&M) or repairs and maintenance under O&M expenses, the
same shall not be claimed under these Regulations;
(f) Usage of water from sewage treatment plant in thermal generating station.
(2) In case of de-capitalisation of assets of a generating company or the transmission
licensee, as the case may be, the original cost of such asset as on the date of
decapitalisation shall be deducted from the value of gross fixed asset and
corresponding loan as well as equity shall be deducted from outstanding loan and the
equity respectively in the year such de-capitalisation takes place with corresponding
adjustments in cumulative depreciation and cumulative repayment of loan, duly taking
into consideration the year in which it was capitalised.”
9. The year-wise projected additional capital expenditure allowed vide the order
dated 17.11.2021 in Petition No. 444/GT/2020, for the 2019-24 tariff period, was Rs.
5681.14 lakh. The same is summarised as under:

Assumed Deletions
49. As per the consistent methodology adopted by the Commission, the
expenditure on replacement of assets, if found justified, is allowed for the purpose of
tariff, provided that capitalisation of the new asset is followed by the de-capitalisation
of the gross value of the old asset. However, in certain cases where de-capitalisation
is proposed to be affected in the future, i.e. the year of capitalisation of the new asset,
the decapitalisation of the old asset, for the purpose of tariff, is considered in the same
year in which the capitalisation of the new asset is allowed. Such de-capitalisation,
which is not reflected as a book entry in the year of capitalisation, is termed “Assumed
Deletion”. Therefore, the methodology of arriving at the fair value of the decapitalised
asset, i.e., escalation rate of 5% per annum from the COD has been considered in
order to arrive at the gross value of the old asset under consideration as on COD as
100% and escalated it @5% per annum, till the year, during which additional capital
expenditure is claimed against the replacement of the same. The amount claimed for
the additional capital expenditure against the asset is multiplied by the derived ratio
based on the above values, i.e., the value in the year of COD divided by the value in
the capitalised year.
50. In the present Petition, the Petitioner has claimed additional capital expenditure
on a replacement basis under Regulation 25(2)(c) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations, but
has not furnished the de-capitalised value of the old assets. The Petitioner was asked
to furnish the corresponding de-capitalised value of the assets capitalised. In
response, the Petitioner has submitted that there is no corresponding de-capitalisation
against the assets done in the same year. Accordingly, the de-capitalised value of the
assets/ works has been calculated in terms of the above-mentioned methodology. The
‘Assumed deletions’ allowed for the purpose of tariff are as under:

admitted by the Commission. In case of multiple units of a generating station or multiple

or claimed as a part of additional capitalisation or consumption of stores and spares
and renovation and modernization.”
(a) Water Charges
81. The first proviso to Regulation 35(1)(6) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations states
that the water charges are to be allowed based on water consumption, depending
upon the type of plant, the type of cooling water system, etc., subject to a prudence
check. The Petitioner has claimed water charges based on the water drawl and rates
as notified by the Irrigation & CAD Department, Government of Telangana State, for
the period 2019-24. The Petitioner, in its additional submission in response to the TV
letter dated 5.6.2025, had submitted as follows:
Order in Petition No. 627/GT/2025 Page 39 of 56

“…Plant Load Factor (PLF) varies over time. During periods of high PLF and increased
power generation, water consumption also rises accordingly.
Furthermore, even when the plant is under shutdown or undergoing overhauling,
auxiliary equipment continues to operate, requiring water for cooling and other
essential purposes. In view of the above, water consumption has been calculated
based on 100% of the normative value.
…
It is also submitted that NTPC Ramagundam also have to pay water pumping
charges/Power charges, which are included in the “water charges calculation sheet” in
the revised Excel file “Appendix-I_rev….”
82. TNPDCL, vide its reply, had submitted that the TV Letter dated 5.6.2025, had
sought various clarifications and documents with respect to water charges and in the
absence of such proof or justification, the same may be rejected. KSEBLL has also
submitted that the year-wise variation in the claimed water charges is not adequately
justified in the petition. The Petitioner, vide its rejoinders, has submitted that the water
charges claimed are based on the tariff fixed by the State Government, and the same
are not within the Petitioners control but constitute statutory levies.
83. The matter has been considered. The Petitioner, in its additional submission
filed vide affidavit dated 17.11.2025, has placed on record auditor-certified details of
water charges, along with month-wise summaries of water charges and year-wise
power charges. The Petitioner had also provided the actual water drawl vis-à-vis the
normative consumption as per the MoEF&CC notification dated 7.12.2015. During the
prudence check, it is observed that the specific water consumption for plants installed
before 2017 is limited to 3.5 m3/MWh, and the actual consumption is within the
prescribed limit of the MoEF&CC notification.
84. Further, the order dated 25.9.2021 in Petition No. 220/GT/2020, had allowed
the recovery of the power charges/ pumping charges paid to the irrigation & CAD
Department, Government of Telangana. Also, the Petitioner has submitted that the
raw water for NTPC Ramagundam is sourced from the storage reservoir of NTPC,
Order in Petition No. 627/GT/2025 Page 40 of 56

ORDER
The instant Petition has been filed by Power Grid Corporation of India Limited
(hereinafter referred to as “the Petitioner/ PGCIL”) for truing up of the transmission tariff
for the 2019-24 tariff period under the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms
and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2019 (hereinafter referred to as “the 2019 Tariff
Regulations”) and the determination of the transmission tariff for the 2024-29 tariff period
under the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff)
Regulations, 2024 (hereinafter referred to as “the 2024 Tariff Regulations”) with respect
to the following assets (hereinafter referred to as “the transmission assets/ Combined
Asset”) under the “Transmission System Strengthening Associated with Mundra UMPP
(Part-B)” (hereinafter referred to as “the transmission project”) in the Western Region.
Asset No. Asset Name
400kV D/C Mundra UMPP – Bhuj (Triple Snowbird) Circuit -2 Transmission

UMPP Switchyard and 400kV Bhuj Pooling Station.
2. The Petitioner has made the following prayers in the instant Petition:
Page 2 of 45
Order in Petition No. 748/TT/2025

a) “Approve the trued-up Transmission Tariff for 2019-24 block and transmission tariff for
2024-29 block for the assets covered under this petition, as per para 15 and 16 above.
b) Admit the capital cost claimed, and additional capitalization incurred during 2019-24.
c) Allow the petitioner to recover the shortfall or refund the excess Annual Fixed Charges,
on account of Return on Equity due to change in applicable Minimum Alternate/Corporate
Income Tax rate as per the Income Tax Act, 1961 (as amended from time to time) of the
respective financial year directly without making any application before the Commission
as provided in Tariff Regulations 2019 and Tariff Regulations, 2024 as per para 15 and
16 above for respective block.
d) Approve the reimbursement of expenditure by the beneficiaries towards petition filing fee,
and expenditure on publishing of notices in newspapers in terms of Regulation 94 (1)
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations,
2024, and other expenditure (if any) in relation to the filing of petition.
e) Allow the petitioner to bill and recover RLDC fees & charges and Licensee fee separately
from the respondents in terms of Regulation 94 (3) and (4) Central Electricity Regulatory
Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2024.
f) Allow the petitioner to bill and adjust impact on Interest on Loan due to change in Interest
rate on account of floating rate of interest applicable during 2024-29 period, if any, from
the respondents.
g) Allow the petitioner to file a separate petition before the Commission for claiming the
overall security expenses and consequential IOWC on that security expenses as
mentioned at para 21 above.
h) Allow the petitioner to file a separate petition before the Commission for claiming the
overall insurance expenses and consequential IOWC on that insurance expenses as
mentioned at para 21 above.
i) Allow the petitioner to file a separate petition before the Commission for claiming the
overall capital spares at the end of tariff block as per actual as mentioned at Para 21
above.
j) Allow the petitioner to claim expenses of CTUIL borne by POWERGRID through a
separate petition as mentioned at para 22 above.
k) Allow the Petitioner to bill and recover GST on Transmission Charges separately from
the respondents, if GST on transmission is levied at any rate in future. Further, any taxes
including GST and duties including cess etc. imposed by any statutory/Govt./municipal
authorities shall be allowed to be recovered from the beneficiaries.
and pass such other relief as the Commission deems fit and appropriate under the
circumstances of the case and in the interest of justice.”
Background
3. The brief facts of the case are as under:
a) The Investment Approval (the IA) for the implementation of the transmission
Page 3 of 45
Order in Petition No. 748/TT/2025

project was accorded by the Board of Directors (BOD) of the Petitioner in its 330th
meeting held on 20.7.2016 vide Memorandum No. C/CP/PA1617-07-0D-IA004
dated 22.7.2016, at an estimated cost of ₹30094.00 lakh, including the Interest
During Construction (IDC) of ₹1804.00 lakh, based on the April 2016 price level.
Subsequently, the RCE (Revised cost estimates) for the transmission project was
approved by BoD of the Petitioner’s Company vide Memorandum No. PA1920-
08-0S-RCE004 dated 4.11.2019, at an estimated cost of ₹33166.00 lakh,
including IDC of ₹1350.00 lakh based on the March 2019 price level.
b) The scope of the transmission project was approved in the 36th Standing
Committee Meeting of Power System Planning of the Western Region
constituents held on 29.8.2013, and the same was further ratified in the 24th
WRPC Meeting held on 9.10.2013. The project was further discussed in the 38th
Standing Committee Meeting of Power System Planning of Western Region
constituents held on 17.7.2015.
c) The entire scope of work has been completed and covered under the instant
transmission project as under:
i) Mundra UMPP – Bhuj Pool 400 kV D/C Line (triple snowbird): 95 kms.
ii) Extension of 400 kV Bhuj Pooling Station – 400 kV line bays: 2 nos.
iii) Extension of 400 kV Mundra UMPP Switchyard – 400 kV line bays: 2 nos.
d) The Commission, vide its order dated 13.1.2020 in Petition No. 387/TT/2018, had
determined the transmission tariff for Asset-1 from its COD (20.3.2019) to
31.3.2019. As per the IA dated 20.7.2016, Asset-1 was scheduled to be put into
commercial operation on 20.12.2018, however, it was commissioned on
20.3.2019, with a time-over-run of 3 months (90 days), which was condoned by
the Commission in its aforesaid order. Subsequently, the Commission vide its
order dated 30.1.2022 in Petition No. 142/TT/2021, had trued-up the transmission
Page 4 of 45
Order in Petition No. 748/TT/2025

tariff for the 2014-19 tariff period and determined the transmission tariff for the
2019-24 tariff period with respect to the Asset-1.
e) The Commission vide order dated 3.1.2022 in Petition No. 684/TT/2020, had
determined the transmission tariff with respect to Asset-2 from its COD (2.4.2019)
to 31.3.2024. As per the IA dated 22.7.2016, Asset-2 was scheduled to be put into
commercial operation on 20.12.2018, however, it was commissioned on 2.4.2019,
with a time-over-run of (104 days), which was partially condoned by the
Commission in its aforesaid order.
f) The Petitioner has filed the instant Petition for truing up of the transmission tariff
for the 2019-24 tariff period with respect to the transmission assets and the
determination of the transmission tariff for the 2024-29 tariff period with respect to
the Combined Asset implemented in the Western Region. The details are as
