Gurugram, Haryana 122003
…Respondent No. 1
2. SJVN Ltd. (SJVN)
6th Floor, Tower-1,
NBCC Office Complex, East Kidwai Nagar,
New Delhi – 110023
…Respondent No. 2
Parties Present:
Shri Amit Kapur, Advocate, Ganeko
Shri Shubham Arya, Advocate, CTUIL
Ms. Pallavi Saighal, Advocate, CTUIL
Ms. Shree Dwivedi, Advocate CTUIL
ORDER
The instant Petition is filed by the Petitioner(s) namely Ganeko-1 and Ganeko-
2 consequent to the Show Cause Notices dated 29.07.2025 issued by CTUIL about
revocation of Connectivity at the Mandsaur PS and Solapur PS.
2. The Petitioner(s) have made the following prayers vide the main Petition:
(a) Admit and allow the present Petition;
(b) Quash the letters dated 29.07.2025 issued to the Petitioners, Ganeko One
Energy Pvt. Ltd. & Ganeko Two Energy Pvt. Ltd. by Respondent No. 1, Central
Transmission Utility of India Ltd.;
(c) Invoke this Hon’ble Commission’s “Power to Relax” and “Power to Remove
Difficulties” in terms of the GNA Regulations to alleviate the difficulty in
implementing Regulation 11(A)(4) by allowing the swapping of LoAs issued
under the same bid, against each of the Connectivity granted to the Petitioners,
Ganeko One Energy Pvt. Ltd. & Ganeko Two Energy Pvt. Ltd. and directing
Respondent No.1, Central Transmission Utility of India Ltd. to consider the same,
in the following manner:-
i. Allow Ganeko Two Energy Pvt. Ltd. to rely on the PPA executed based
on the underlying Base LoA for conversion of the Connectivity granted
to Ganeko Two Energy Pvt. Ltd. at Solapur PS.
ii. Allow Ganeko One Energy Pvt. Ltd. to submit the Greenshoe LoA in
place of the Base LoA, against Ganeko One Energy Pvt. Ltd.‘s
Connectivity which has already been converted.
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 2

(d) Issue appropriate directions to Respondent No. 1, Central Transmission Utility of
India Ltd. for allowing the conversion of the Connectivity granted to the
Petitioners, Ganeko One Energy Pvt. Ltd. and Ganeko Two Energy Pvt. Ltd. from
the Land-BG route to LOA/PPA route; and
(e) Pass such other and further order or orders as this Hon'ble Commission deems
appropriate under the facts and circumstances of the present case.
3. The Petitioner(s) have made the following prayers vide the IA 67/2025 dated
04.08.2025:
(a) Allow the present Application and urgently list the present Petition filed by the
Applicant;
(b) Direct Respondent No. 1, Central Transmission Utility of India Ltd. not to take
any coercive steps in furtherance of the Show Cause Notices dated 29.07.2025
till the final disposal of the present Petition; and
(c) Pass any such further orders as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit in the
facts and circumstances of the present case
4. The Petitioner(s) have made the following prayers vide the IA 133/2025 dated
13.12.2025:
(a) Allow the present Application and urgently list the present Petition filed by the
Applicants, Ganeko One and Ganeko Two;
(b) Direct Respondent No. 1, Central Transmission Utility of India Ltd. not to take
any actions prejudicial to the rights and interests of the Applicants, Ganeko One
and Ganeko Two;
(c) Restrain Respondent No. 1, Central Transmission Utility of India Ltd. from
taking any coercive action against the Applicants, Ganeko One and Ganeko
Two with respect to the 300 MW Connectivity granted at Mandsaur PS, Madhya
Pradesh and Solapur PS, Maharashtra, respectively, during the pendency of
the present petition; and
(d) Pass any such other and further Order as this Hon'ble Commission may deem
appropriate in the facts and circumstances of the case.
Submissions of Petitioner(s):
5. The Petitioner has primarily made the following submissions:
(a) Ganeko-1 and Ganeko-2 had been granted 300 MW Connectivity each, by
CTUIL and have thereafter executed the Connectivity Agreement on 09.12.2024
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 3

and 07.01.2025, respectively, consequent to the completion of the following
steps, as stipulated under the GNA Regulations:
Date Particulars
17.04.2024 Ganeko-1 submitted its application to CTUIL seeking
Connectivity at the Mandsaur PS located in the State of
Madhya Pradesh for a quantum of 300 MW under Regulation
5.1(xi)(c) of the GNA Regulations.
02.07.2024 Ganeko-2 submitted its application to CTUIL seeking
Connectivity at the Solapur PS located in the State of
Maharashtra for a quantum of 300 MW under Regulation
5.1(xi)(c) of the GNA Regulations.
15.07.2024 CTUIL intimated the in-principle grant of Connectivity to
Ganeko-1 for 300 MW at the Mandsaur PS.
21.10.2024 CTUIL intimated the in-principle grant of Connectivity to
Ganeko-2 for 300 MW at the Solapur PS.
11.11.2024 CTUIL intimated the final grant of Connectivity to Ganeko-1 for
300 MW at the Mandsaur PS.
09.12.2024 CTUIL intimated the final grant of Connectivity to Ganeko-2 for
300 MW at the Solapur PS.
(b) Ganeko-1 emerged as the successful bidder under the SJVN RfS and was
awarded the Base LoA on 28.10.2024 for 140 MW contracted capacity. On
10.12.2024 it sought conversion of its Connectivity at Mandsaur PS from the
Land-BG route to the LoA/PPA route and release of the Rs. 30 Crore Bank
Guarantee, which was allowed by CTUIL on 31.12.2024 and land BG was
returned.
(c) As on 31.12.2024, when CTUIL allowed Ganeko-1’s change in eligibility route,
only the Base LoA dated 28.10.2024 existed for supply of the Contracted
Capacity of 140 MW with the ISTS Interconnection Point at Mandsaur PS, and
the Greenshoe option for an additional Contracted Capacity of 140 MW at
Solapur PS was still under consideration. Subsequently, on 03.02.2025, SJVN
awarded the Greenshoe LoA to Ganeko-1, resulting in two subsisting LoAs: the
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 4

Base LoA for 140 MW at Mandsaur PS and the Greenshoe LoA for 140 MW at
Solapur PS, intended to be implemented by Ganeko-2.
(d) SJVN vide its letter dated 24.02.2025 had intimated Ganeko-1 that SJVN had
signed the PSA with UPPCL and further requested Ganeko-1 to inter alia,
proceed further for signing of the PPA, based on the underlying Base LoA dated
28.10.2024. At this juncture, it is relevant to note the Start Date of Connectivity
granted to Ganeko-1 and Ganeko-2, respectively: -
Entity Location Scheduled Start Date of
Commissioning Date Connectivity
of Augmentation
Ganeko-1 Mandsaur PS 15.10.2026 31.03.2027
Ganeko-2 Solapur PS 20.03.2026 31.12.2026
Based on the above, the Connectivity granted to Ganeko-2 by CTUIL was
scheduled to commence earlier than the Connectivity granted to Ganeko-1.
However, while SJVN had already signed the PSA with UPPCL tying up the
Contracted Capacity awarded to Ganeko-1 under the Base LoA with the Delivery
Point at Mandsaur PS, SJVN was unable to tie up the Contracted Capacity
awarded to Ganeko-1 under the Greenshoe LoA with the Delivery Point at
Solapur PS, as on such date.
(e) In the interest of timely commissioning of the Project, given recent cases where
transmission systems are inevitably delayed due to force majeure events and
in line with the provisions of the Bidding Guidelines, SJVN RfS and the PPA,
which stipulate that the commencement of power supply has to be one within
24 months from the date of execution of the PPA, on 27.02.2025, Ganeko-1
responded to SJVN’s letter dated 24.02.2025 referencing the Base LoA and
stated that Ganeko-1 intended to adhere to the stipulated timelines by duly
executing the PPA within 30 days from signing of the Power Supply Agreement.
(f) On 17.03.2025, Ganeko-1 wrote to SJVN and inter alia informed that:
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 5

(i) In line with Clause 4.1.6 of the RfS and Clause 10(v) of the Base LoA, Ganeko-
1 had nominated its subsidiary, Ganeko-2 as the Project SPV for signing the PPA
with SJVN, for the Contracted Capacity of 140 MW and implementation of the
Project. It is pertinent to mention here that:
• Ganeko-1 and Ganeko-2 were earlier affiliates and wholly owned
subsidiaries of Ganeko Solar Pvt. Ltd. (“Ganeko Solar”).
• For the purposes of implementing the Project awarded under the Base
LoA and for the purposes of execution of the PPA, Ganeko-2 was brought
under Ganeko-1.
(ii) There would be a change in location of the proposed Project, wherein the
Delivery Point, i.e., ISTS Interconnection Point was the Solapur PS (and not the
Mandsaur PS, intimated earlier).
(g) On 18.03.2025, SJVN, issued amendment No. 1 to the Base LoA awarded to
Ganeko-1, revising the project location, including the ISTS Interconnection Point
to Solapur PS (from Mandsaur PS). Pursuant to this, on 20.03.2025, Ganeko-2
and SJVN executed the PPA based on the underlying Base LoA with the ISTS
Interconnection Point at Solapur PS.
(h) On 23.05.2025, Ganeko-1 requested SJVN to amend the Delivery Point, i.e.,
the ISTS Interconnection Point, mentioned in the Greenshoe LoA to Mandsaur
PS in place of Solapur PS. The above request was accepted by SJVN and
Amendment No. 1 to the Greenshoe LoA was issued by SJVN on 03.06.2025
revising the project location to Mandsaur PS instead of Solapur PS.
(i) On 02.06.2025, Ganeko-2 requested CTUIL for Conversion of the 300 MW
Connectivity granted to Ganeko-2 at the Solapur PS from the Land-BG route to
the LoA/PPA route by relying on the PPA signed by Ganeko 2 and release the
Bank Guarantee amounting to Rs. 30 Cr. furnished to CTUIL by Ganeko-2 on
29.04.2024, in view of Regulation 11(A)(4) of the GNA Regulations which allows
for conversion of Connectivity from the Land-BG route to the LoA/PPA route.
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 6

(j) CTUIL while scrutinising Ganeko-2’s request, observed that the PPA on the basis
of which Ganeko-2 was seeking the conversion of Connectivity from the Land-
BG route to the LoA/PPA route was premised on the Base LoA, based on which
CTUIL had already converted the Connectivity granted to Ganeko-1 by CTUIL
on 31.12.2024. On 29.07.2025, CTUIL unfairly issued the Show Cause Notices
to Ganeko-1 and Ganeko-2, respectively threatening revocation of Ganeko’s
connectivity and initiation of blacklisting proceedings.
(k) CTUIL’s allegation that Ganeko-1 and Ganeko-2 have allegedly violated the
undertakings provided in the Connectivity Applications submitted by Ganeko-1
and Ganeko-2, while seeking the grant of Connectivity is based on an incorrect
factual premise. Alleged mistake/anomaly arose due to an inadvertent omission
on the part of Ganeko to inform CTUIL at the relevant point in time about the
amendments to the Base LoA and Greenshoe LoA carried out by SJVN at the
behest of Ganeko. Such omission on the part of Ganeko in failing to report the
above in a timely manner was neither wilful nor intentional. It is a settled position
of law that substantive relief cannot be denied to a party on account of procedural
technicalities.
(l) All along there were two LoAs, i.e., the Greenshoe LoA and the Base LoA
awarded by SJVN to Ganeko-1 relatable to the Connectivity granted by CTUIL
to Ganeko-1 and Ganeko-2 at Mandsaur PS and Solapur PS respectively. No
unlawful advantage or benefit ensured to Ganeko-1 and Ganeko-2.
(m) Ganeko requested SJVN to amend the Base LoA factoring in ground realities,
viz:
(i) The Connectivity granted to Ganeko-2 by CTUIL at Solapur PS was
scheduled to commence earlier than the Connectivity granted to Ganeko-1
by CTUIL at Mandsaur PS.
(ii) SJVN had already signed the PSA with UPPCL tying up the Contracted
Capacity awarded to Ganeko-1 under the Base LoA with the Delivery Point
at Mandsaur PS, SJVN was unable to tie up the Contracted Capacity
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 7

awarded to Ganeko-1 under the Greenshoe LoA with the Delivery Point at
Solapur PS, as on such date.
(iii) With a view to ensuring that the project investments are not adversely
affected, generating stations and transmission systems are planned in a
manner so as to ensure that both elements are commissioned in tandem.
Accordingly, since there was greater visibility of the Connectivity granted to
Ganeko-2 at the Solapur PS, Ganeko-2’s Project at Solapur was prioritised.
(iv) Recent cases where the commissioning of transmission systems are
routinely delayed due to force majeure events, consequentially delaying the
commissioning of generating assets.
(n) The undertaking provided by Ganeko-1 and Ganeko-2 is only relatable to the
time of initial application. Thus, the same would only be relatable to the
documents submitted when Ganeko-1 and Ganeko-2 initially applied for the
Connectivity on 17.04.2024 and 02.07.2024, respectively. No such undertaking
was provided by Ganeko-1 and Ganeko-2 while submitting its request for
conversion of the subsisting Connectivity from the Land-BG route to the LoA/PPA
route.
(o) CTUIL’s allegations regarding Ganeko’s failure to inform CTUIL about the
amendment in the Base LoA vis-à-vis the project location from Mandsaur to
Solapur until 20.06.2025 are based on an incorrect premise. Ganeko’s purported
failure to keep CTUIL informed of all the developments relating to the Projects,
more particularly the fact that the Base LoA and the Greenshoe LoA had been
amended by SJVN, was a mere oversight which was neither wilful nor intentional.
The amendments to the Base LoA and the Greenshoe LoA carried out by
SJVN/Ganeko were in consonance with the contractual framework subsisting
between SJVN and Ganeko, pursuant to the bidding conducted under the SJVN
RfS. Ganeko followed all contractual procedures and provisions in toto, all along.
(p) Ganeko took all measures in line with Prudent Utility Practices to resolve the
alleged mistakes or anomalies pointed out by CTUIL and to ensure that project
development activities were not hampered; however, despite the same, on
29.07.2025, CTUIL arbitrarily and unfairly issued Show Cause Notices to
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 8

Ganeko-1 and Ganeko-2, threatening revocation of Connectivity and initiation of
blacklisting proceedings.
(q) The alleged anomalies pointed out by CTUIL in the Show Cause Notice were
neither intentional nor wilful but attributable to a genuine oversight and mistake
in failing to report project related developments to CTUIL at the relevant points
of time. Such oversight cannot be broad-stroked as ‘fraud’, especially
considering that no damage has been caused to CTUIL, nor has the sanctity of
the process for grant of Connectivity been disturbed.
(r) Notwithstanding the issuance of the Show Cause Notices, the record
demonstrates that Ganeko acted in a fair, transparent, and bona fide manner in
its dealings with CTUIL, SJVN, and other governmental instrumentalities, in
consonance with the contractual framework governing the Base LoA and
Greenshoe LoA and with the objective of timely project commissioning in line
with Prudent Utility Practices. At all material times, the Base LoA and Greenshoe
LoA subsisted and were mappable to the Connectivity granted to Ganeko-1 and
Ganeko-2 at Mandsaur PS and Solapur PS, respectively, and Ganeko on its own
accord clarified the purported anomalies and sought engagement with CTUIL to
resolve any alleged discrepancies. However, CTUIL failed to consider these
clarifications and instead arbitrarily issued Show Cause Notices.
(s) While the GNA Regulations are admittedly silent on the aspect of
replacing/swapping of LoA/PPA issued under the same bid, once submitted for
conversion from Land-BG route to LoA route, there is no contrary provisions
contained in the GNA Regulations which prohibit the same. In fact, the 1st Proviso
to Regulation 15.1 of the GNA Regulations allow for the Connectivity granted to
a parent company may be utilised by its subsidiary company and vice versa.
Thus, allowing such a dispensation by relaxing Regulation 11(4)(A) of the GNA
Regulations would be in consonance with the spirit of the GNA Regulations,
which allows transferability and interchangeability of Connectivity so long as
there is a parent-subsidiary relationship existing.
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 9

(t) In the present Petition and the genuine difficulty faced by Ganeko and CTUIL in
effectuating the provisions of the GNA Regulations, it is humbly submitted that
this Hon’ble Commission ought to exercise its ‘Power to Remove Difficulty’ and
‘Power to Relax’ as prescribed under Regulations 42 and 41 of the GNA
Regulations to grant relief sought for in the present Petition by Ganeko.
(u) Ganeko-1 and Ganeko-2 have made significant investments towards project
development work, viz: -

Submissions vide IA No 67/2025:
6. The Petitioners vide IA No. 67/2025 dated 04.08.2025 has reiterated its submission
under the main Petition and prayed for urgent listing and direction to CTUIL not to take
any coercive steps in furtherance of show cause Notice dated 29.07.2025 till the final
disposal of the present Petition.
Hearing dated 07.08.2025:
7. During the hearing, learned Counsel for Petitioner made submissions about the issues
raised in the Petition. The learned counsel for the Respondent, CTUIL, submitted that
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 11

the present Petition filed by the Petitioners is premature, as CTUIL is yet to take a
decision on the inquiry relating to the impugned Show Cause Notices issued to the
Petitioners. Considering the submissions of the Petitioners and Respondent, CTUIL,
the Commission deemed it appropriate to let CTUIL first conclude its inquiry after
following due process in respect of the impugned Show Cause Notices. After inquiry,
if CTUIL finds that the connectivity/Petitioner is required to be revoked/blacklisted,
CTUIL shall not implement the same for 10 days so that the Petitioner may approach
the Commission against the such a decision of CTUIL.
Hearing dated 10.09.2025, 14.10.2025 and 11.11.2025:
8. During the hearing dated 10.09.2025, matter was adjourned on request by learned
counsel for CTUIL, as inquiry in respect to Show Cause Notice was not concluded.
Further, during the hearing dated 14.10.2025 and 11.11.2025 learned counsel for
CTUIL prayed additional time for concluding inquiry citing that CTUIL is formulating a
comprehensive procedure for blacklisting. Accordingly, matter was adjourned with
direction to expedite inquiry and file conclusion within three weeks without fail.
Submissions of CTUIL:
9. CTUIL vide affidavit dated 08.12.2025 submitted an inquiry report dated 05.12.2025
stating that as per the inquiry, Ganeko One Energy Pvt. Ltd (Ganeko-1) and Ganeko
Two Energy Pvt. Ltd (Ganeko-2) are not liable for any "transgression" or "fraud" as per
the CTU Procedure for Inquiry and therefore no action for blacklisting would be
required. However, Ganeko-1 & Ganeko-2 shall be liable for actions in terms of the
applicable provisions of GNA Regulations, 2022 in light of the findings of CTUIL in the
ordinary course. Although considering the directions of this Commission vide RoP
dated 07.08.2025, such actions would not be implemented for 10 days. The findings
of the report are as below:
“Show Cause Notices dated 29.07.2025 issued to M/s Ganeko One Energy
Private Limited (G1) and M/s Ganeko One Energy Private Limited (G2)
…
C. Issues raised by CTU in its show cause notices dated 29.07.2025
Issue 1: Violation of Undertakings qua G1 and G2
Issue 2: Concealment of material information qua G1
Issue 3: Eligibility Condition not satisfied for considerable time by G1
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 12

…
27. Conclusion (G1):
(i) The cumulative effect of these violations is that G1 failed to maintain valid
eligibility, misrepresented its compliance status, and breached its commitments
to CTU in terms of the provisions of the GNA Regulations, 2022 and the
undertakings and affirmations submitted as a part of the Connectivity Application
and supporting Affidavit.
(ii) Accordingly, CTU is of the view that appropriate action be taken qua the G1’s
connectivity in light of the violations namely, concealment of material change,
interim absence of eligibility, and breach of undertaking.
(iii) The findings regarding Fraud or Transgression and the consequential actions, if
any have been dealt separately in Section ‘J’ below.
…..
I. Conclusion (G2):
(i) CTU observes that G2’s conduct constitutes a clear breach of its undertaking
and reliance on an exhausted eligibility document.
(ii) Accordingly, CTU is of the view that appropriate action may be taken qua the
G2’s connectivity in light of the violations and breach of undertaking submitted

c) The attempt to distinguish between the Base LoA and its subsequent amendment
is equally misconceived. The amended LoA flows from the same Base LoA, which

subsequent amendment of project location by the bidding agency does not revive,

ground that an alternative eligibility document continues to subsist.

the LoA inapplicable to the Connectivity granted at Mandsaur.

that the relevant Connectivity be continuously supported by a valid document
applicable to that Connectivity. It is an admitted position that between 18.03.2025
(when the Base LoA ceased to support the Mandsaur Connectivity) and 20.06.2025
(when the Greenshoe LoA was submitted), Ganeko-1’s Connectivity at Mandsaur

findings in the Inquiry Report regarding absence of fraud or intent to deceive are
misplaced. CTUIL has consistently distinguished between absence of fraud and
existence of regulatory non-compliance. The GNA Regulations, 2022 are
compliance-based and mandate continuous satisfaction of eligibility conditions,
independent of intent. While the Inquiry Report records that the omission was not
fraudulent, it does not negate the fact that Ganeko-1 failed to maintain eligibility for
its Connectivity at Mandsaur during the relevant period. The violations have in fact
been admitted by Ganeko itself, though erroneously categorised as oversight or

……

dated 31.12.2024.

from Land BG route to LOA/PPA route along with an PPA dated 20.03.2025 referred at 3 above. On

LOA dated 03.06.2025 along with an amendment for change in location from Solapur to Mandsaur and

other LOA is not envisaged/ permitted under GNA Regulations, 2022 and its amendments thereof.

(a) GANEKO TWO has sought a change in eligibility route (from BG route to LoA/PPA route)
through submission of a document (i.e. PPA) already utilized and exhausted by GANEKO ONE
for its own change in eligibility route (from BG route to LoA/PPA route).

Solapur on 18.03.2025 appears to have resulted in a situation wherein GANEKO ONE could
not have fulfilled the eligibility criteria as per the CERC GNA Regulations.

without the support of any eligibility criteria/documents (i.e. either LoA-PPA or Land or 8G) for the
period between 18.03.2025 and 20.06.2025
(g) GANEKO TWO had executed a PPA for establishment of project at Solapur, on GANEKO ONE's
LoA, as a SPV company. As such, the said PPA appears to have been executed only in relation
to the LoA issued to GANEKO ONE and could never have been allowed to be an eligibility
document for GANEKO TWO as the same LoA had already been exhausted by GANEKO ONE.
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 27

From the aforesaid, it appears prima facie that GANEKO ONE is in violation of undertakings and
circumvented the requirement for exclusive use of eligibility documents. It is imperative to state that the
actions of GANEKO ONE appear to be misleading and constitute willful misrepresentation.
Accordingly, GANEKO ONE is hereby called upon to please clarify and show cause within 15 (fifteen)
days from the date of this notice as to why connectivity of GANEKO ONE should not be revoked along
with all associated consequences and why proceedings for blacklisting should not be initiated against
GANEKO ONE for failing to meet and maintain the criteria of eligibility required of Connectivity grantee;
for suppression of material facts and information pertaining to the eligibility documents submitted by
GANEKO ONE to sustain its connectivity application and grant; attempt to commit fraud upon CTU in
order to sustain the connectivity granted; and clear and abject default of the undertaking submitted as
a part of the connectivity application wherein GANEKO ONE has undertaken that documents (if any)
submitted at any stage in order to meet the eligibility conditions "shall not be used as eligibility
documents for any other Connectivity application.
Failure to address any other breaches or illegal conduct in this notice shall not prejudice CTUIL's rights
to take appropriate action in the future.
Nothing stated herein shall be deemed a waiver of any rights or remedies available under law, conduct
or equity, all of which are expressly reserved.
…”
Show Cause Notice dated 29.7.25 to Ganeko-2 is same as issued to Ganeko-1 except
following quoted paras:
“From the aforesaid, it appears prima facie that GANEKO TWO is in violation of undertakings and
circumvented the requirement for exclusive use of eligibility documents. It is imperative to state that the
actions of GANEKO TWO appear to be misleading and constitute willful misrepresentation.
Accordingly, GANEKO TWO is hereby called upon to please clarify and show cause within 15 (fifteen)
days from the date of this notice as to why connectivity of GANEKO TWO should not be revoked along
with all associated consequences and why proceedings for blacklisting should not be initiated against
GANEKO TWO for failing to meet and maintain the criteria of eligibility required of Connectivity grantee;
for suppression of material facts and information pertaining to the eligibility documents submitted by
GANEKO TWO to sustain its connectivity application and grant; attempt to commit fraud upon CTU in
order to sustain the connectivity granted; and clear and abject default of the undertaking submitted as
a part of the connectivity application wherein GANEKO TWO has undertaken that documents (if any)
submitted at any stage in order to meet the eligibility conditions "shall not be used as eligibility
documents for any other Connectivity application.
Failure to address any other breaches or illegal conduct in this notice shall not prejudice CTUIL's rights
to take appropriate action in the future.
Nothing stated herein shall be deemed a waiver of any rights or remedies available under law, conduct
or equity, all of which are expressly reserved…”
24. We note that CTUIL vide the abovesaid show cause notice proposed twin actions - one
of blacklisting and other of revocation of Connectivity for Ganeko-1 and Ganeko-2. We
note that on the issue of blacklisting, CTU has filed a comprehensive inquiry report dated
05.12.2025, vide which CTUIL did not find any transgression or fraud, accordingly, no
consequential action on blacklisting was initiated. However CTU concluded that Ganeko-
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 28

1’s Connectivity shall be liable for necessary actions and Ganeko-2’s Connectivity may
be revoked . Accordingly, CTUIL revoked connectivity of both Ganeko-1 and Ganeko-2
vide letter dated 16.12.2025 w.e.f. 26.12.2025 citing violations of 2022 GNA Regulations,
non-sustenance of eligibility conditions and breach of undertakings.
25.Now we shall analyse if the show-cause notice issued by CTUIL is in Order. We have
perused the GNA Regulations ( prior to third amendment) which provides as under:
“5.8 (xi) In case of Applicants which are REGS (other than Hydro generating station)
or ESS (excluding Pumped Storage Plant (PSP)) the following documents shall be
submitted:
(a) Letter of Award (LOA) by, or Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) entered into with, a
Renewable Energy Implementing Agency or a distribution licensee or an authorized agency
on behalf of distribution licensee consequent to tariff based competitive bidding, as the case
may be:
Provided that in case of Applicants being multi-located REGS, the details of locations and
capacity at each location, duly certified by the Renewable Energy Implementing Agency or
the distribution licensee, as the case may be, shall be submitted.
Or
(b) Registered Title Deed as a proof of Ownership or lease rights or land use rights for 50%
of the land required for the capacity for which Connectivity is sought;
Provided that for States where State Government issues Government Order for allotment of
Land to the Nodal Agency identified for development of Renewable energy in the State,
which in turn issues Advance Possession of land to the project developer, such Government
Order allotting land to the Nodal Agency accompanied with Advance Possession letter
issued in the name of Applicant of Connectivity, shall be considered as a valid document
towards Land Use Rights subject to the condition that the said documents shall be submitted
for at least 50% of the land required for the capacity for which Connectivity is sought;
OR
(c) For a capacity up to 1000 MW - Bank Guarantee of Rs. 10 lakh/MW and for a capacity
more than 1000 MW - Bank Guarantee of Rs. 100 Crore plus Rs. 5 lakh/MW for capacity
over and above 1000 MW, in lieu of ownership or lease rights or land use rights of land for
50% of the land required for the capacity for which Connectivity is sought subject to
provisions of Regulations 11A and 11B of these regulations; or
…
11A: Conditions subsequent to be satisfied by the Connectivity Grantee:
…
(1) An applicant which is REGS (other than Hydro generating station) or ESS (excluding
PSP) covered under sub-clause (c) of Clause (xi) of Regulation 5.8 or Renewable power
park developer covered under sub-clause (c) of Clause (vii) Regulation 5.8, shall submit
documents for land in terms of sub-clause (b) of Clause (xi) or sub-clause (b) of Clause (vii)
of Regulation 5.8 of these regulations, as the case may be, within 18 months of issuance of
an in-principle grant of Connectivity or within 12 months of issuance of a final grant of
Connectivity, whichever is earlier. The Bank Guarantee submitted under subclause (c) of
Clause (vii) or under sub-clause (c) of Clause (xi) of Regulation 5.8 of these regulations shall
be returned within 7 days of submission of stipulated documents as proof of Ownership or
lease rights or land use rights.
…
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 29

(4) In case of Applicants which have been granted Connectivity under clauses (xi)(b) or (xi)(c)
of the Regulation 5.8 but are subsequently covered under clause (xi)(a) of the Regulation
5.8, the requirement of furnishing the documents in accordance with Clauses (1) to (3) shall
be the same as applicable to the entities covered under clause (xi)(a) of Regulation 5.8.
11B. Consequences of non-fulfilment of conditions under Regulation 11A:
(1) If the Connectivity grantee covered under clause (xi)(c) of Regulation 5.8 or Renewable
power park developer covered under clause (vii)(c) of Regulation 5.8 of these regulations,
fails to submit the documents in accordance with Clause (1) of Regulation 11A of these
regulations, its Connectivity shall be revoked, Bank Guarantee of Rs 10 lakh/MW submitted
in lieu of land shall be encashed and Conn-BG1, Conn-BG2 and Conn-BG3 shall be treated
in terms of Regulation 24.2 or Regulation 24.3 of these regulations, as applicable.
16. Treatment of Connectivity Bank Guarantee:
16.1. Conn-BG1 shall be returned within 30 days of declaration of commercial operation of
full capacity by the Connectivity grantee.
16.2. Conn-BG2 and Conn-BG3 shall be returned in five equal parts over five years
corresponding to the generation capacity which has been declared under commercial
operation by the Connectivity grantee:
24.6 Revocation of Connectivity:
(1)
(a)Connectivity shall be revoked for the corresponding capacity, if the Connectivity and
corresponding GNA has been made effective in terms of Clause (a) of Regulation 22.4 of
these regulations and the Connectivity grantee fails to achieve COD either in full or in parts
on or before,
(i)the scheduled date of commercial operation of the generation project, for cases
covered under clause (xi)(a) of the Regulation 5.8, as intimated at the time of making
application for grant of Connectivity or as extended or delayed commissioning
permitted by the Renewable Energy Implementing Agency or the distribution licensee
or the authorized agency on behalf of distribution licensee, as the case may be.
(ii)six months after the scheduled date of commercial operation as intimated at time of
making application for grant of Connectivity, for cases covered under clause (xi)(b) or
(xi)(c) of the Regulation 5.8.
(b) In case of Applicants which have been granted Connectivity under clause (xi)(b) or (xi)(c)
of the Regulation 5.8 but are subsequently covered under clause (xi)(a) of the Regulation
5.8, the last date for declaration of COD shall be the SCOD of the project or as extended or
delayed commissioning permitted by the Renewable Energy Implementing Agency or the
distribution licensee or the authorized agency on behalf of distribution licensee, as the case
may be.
As per the above, an applicant covered under LAND BG route may get converted to
LOA/PPA route under Regulation 11A(4). The entity covered under LAND BG route is
required to furnish Land documents under Regulation 11A(1) within specified timeline
and seek release of LAND BG on submission of such land documents. However as a
consequence of conversion from LAND BG to LOA route under Regulation 11A(4) such
entity seeks release of LAND BG on submission of eligible LOA/PPA since under
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 30

LOA/PPA route it is not required to furnish land documents. Accordingly, after
acceptance of route change request of Ganeko-1, Land BG amounting to Rs. 30 crores
were released, otherwise it would have been released on submission of land documents
in November’25, subject to conditions that land documents were complete and in order.
26. We note that as per the GNA Regulations an LOA or PPA associated with such LOA,
which has been used to seek Connectivity under Regulation 5.8(xi)(a) cannot be used
again by another entity to seek another Connectivity. This is similar to situation where an
entity uses certain land documents to seek Connectivity under Regulation 5.8(xi)(b) and
uses the same documents to seek another Connectivity. Any conversion sought under
Regulation 11A(4) to route of regulation 5.8(xi)(a) is same as seeking Connectivity under
Regulation 5.8(xi)(a). Same document cannot be used to seek two Connectivities.
27. Petitioner has argued that it got the Base LOA amended to get the location changed by
SJVN (REIA) and hence it is not the same LOA. We disagree with such proposition of
the Petitioner. In such a situation an entity would get LOA amended a number of times
and seek Connectivity for each such LOA and block the Connectivity since under such
LOA amended ‘n’ number of times, project shall be installed only at one location. As soon
as LOA gets amended, the previous LOA becomes infructuous.
28.We have also perused application for 300MW connectivity at Mandsaur by Ganeko-1 as
under:
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 31

entity to go against the Regulations and its undertakings by availing the benefit of an
exhausted document. Further assessment of suitability of project for a particular LOA or
while seeking Connectivity is solely on Petitioner, and it should have been more prudent
when it itself proposed the location to SJVN each time.
31. Petitioner has argued that it had two LOAs in hand at all points in time. We do not agree
this argument of Petitioner. As concluded earlier a Petitioner may have ‘n’ number of
LOAs or PPAs in hand. But he cannot avail benefits of Connectivity using an exhausted
document. This is similar to situation wherein connectivity obtained based on LoA/ PPA
route and those LoA/ PPA got terminated.
32.In light of above discussions we are of the view that show cause issued by CTUIL against
Ganeko-1 is in order and there is no direction to set aside such show-cause notice
against Ganeko-1 since Ganeko-1 was without any eligibility document as on 18.3.2025.
33.Now we proceed to analyse if show cause issued to Ganeko-2 is in Order or not. The
relevant extracts of Ganeko-2’s connectivity application is as under:
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 33

As per the above, Ganeko-2 at the time of application was aware that LoA/ PPA that
has been used by any other applicant shall not be used as eligibility document.
34. CTU vide the show-cause notice to Ganeko-2 has stated that Ganeko-2 is in violation of
undertakings and circumvented the requirement for exclusive use of eligibility
documents. CTU has noted that Ganeko-2 furnished a PPA signed by Ganeko-2 against
Base LOA which has already been utilised by Ganeko-1. In facts and circumstances of
the case, we are of the view that CTU rightly issued show-cause to Ganeko-2 seeking
explanations. Accordingly, the Prayer of the Petitioner to set aside show cause notices
dated 29.7.2025 against Ganeko-1 and Ganeko-2 are not acceded to.
35.Issue No. 1 is addressed accordingly.
Issue No.2 : Whether there is a requirement to allow swapping of LoAs issued under
the same bid, against each of the Connectivity granted to the Petitioners, Ganeko
One Energy Pvt. Ltd. & Ganeko Two Energy Pvt. Ltd. and consequentially, Whether
directions are required to be issued to CTUIL for allowing the conversion of the
Connectivity granted to the Petitioners, Ganeko One Energy Pvt. Ltd. and Ganeko
Two Energy Pvt. Ltd. from the Land-BG route to LOA/PPA route.
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 34

36. Petitioner(s) have submitted that the GNA Regulations are admittedly silent on the
aspect of replacing/swapping of LoA/PPA issued under the same bid, once submitted for
conversion from Land-BG route to LoA route, there is no contrary provisions contained
in the GNA Regulations which prohibit the same. In fact, the 1st Proviso to Regulation
15.1 of the GNA Regulations allow for the Connectivity granted to a parent company may
be utilized by its subsidiary company and vice versa. Thus, allowing such a dispensation
by relaxing Regulation 11(4)(A) of the GNA Regulations would be in consonance with
the spirit of the GNA Regulations, which allows transferability and interchangeability of
Connectivity so long as there is a parent-subsidiary relationship existing. Petitioner has
stated that in the present Petition a genuine difficulty is faced by Ganeko and CTUIL in
effectuating the provisions of the GNA Regulations, and that this Commission ought to
exercise its ‘Power to Remove Difficulty’ and ‘Power to Relax’ as prescribed under
Regulations 42 and 41 of the GNA Regulations to grant relief sought for in the present
Petition by Ganeko. Since Ganeko One’s Connectivity has already been converted from
the Land-BG route to the LoA/PPA route by utilising the Base LoA, while Ganeko Two’s
request for conversion on the basis of the PPA founded on the same Base LoA is no
longer feasible as the Base LoA stands exhausted, though Ganeko One continues to
house the unutilised Greenshoe LoA. In these facts and circumstances, it is submitted
that this Commission may invoke its Power to Relax and Power to Remove Difficulty by
allowing Ganeko Two to rely on the PPA executed under the Base LoA for conversion of
its Connectivity at Solapur PS and permitting Ganeko One to submit the Greenshoe LoA
in place of the Base LoA against its Connectivity at Mandsaur PS.
37. Petitioner has also submitted that in the alternative, this Commission may grant a one-
time dispensation by directing CTUIL to consider Ganeko Two’s withdrawal of its earlier
conversion request and allow it to continue under the Land-BG route, and permit Ganeko
One to furnish a Land-BG in support of its Connectivity.
38. CTUIL has submitted that subsequent withdrawal of the conversion request is purely
post-facto and does not efface or cure the breach already committed. Regulatory
compliance under the 2022 GNA Regulations is required to be contemporaneous and
cannot be retrospectively regularised upon detection of a violation. Compliance with land
milestones under Regulation 11(A)(1) is irrelevant to the issue of breach of undertaking
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 35

and does not legitimise an impermissible attempt to convert eligibility route on the basis
of an exhausted LoA/PPA. While CTUIL has recorded that no fraud or mala fide intent is
established, it has consistently distinguished absence of fraud from regulatory non-
compliance.
39. We have perused the submissions of Petitioner and Respondents. We note that Base
LOA issued for Mandsaur PS got amended as Solapur PS . Greenshoe LOA was
amended from Solapur PS to Mandsaur PS. Petitioner is seeking to permit it to swap
the two LOAs against the two Connectivities .
40. We note that Petitioner sought Connectivity on LAND BG route knowing fully well that it
is required to furnish land documents within a stipulated timeline. It chose to convert to
LOA route and sought early return of LAND BG without furnishing Land documents. Later
Petitioner itself made such LOA an infructuous document.
41. We would like to clarify that when an entity seeks connectivity, it should make itself aware
of the regulations and be serious in implementing the project. The routes have been
provided so that all kinds of projects can seek Connectivity. But conversion from land
route to LOA route should not be seen as a way out to not furnish the land documents.
Without land, in any case entity would not be able to implement the project. We are of
the view that since Petitioner was granted Connectivity on Land BG route, it should
satisfy the condition of furnishing the land documents. We have already concluded in
Issue No1 that Petitioner was in violation of its undertakings while using exhausted
documents. Hence, we reject the prayer of Petitioners to permit it to swap the LOAs for
purpose of converting its connectivity from LAND BG to LOA route. Hence no direction
is required to be issued to CTUIL to consider LOA or PPA for conversion of Connectivity
of Petitioner from LAND BG to LOA. The issue of whether Petitioner’s Connectivity
should be revoked or not is dealt with in next issue herein.
42. Issue No. 2 is addressed accordingly.
Issue No.3 : Whether Connectivity of Ganeko-1 and Ganeko-2 shall be revoked in
terms of letter dated 16.12.25 issued by CTUIL? What consequential directions are
required to be issued to Petitioners to retain the Connectivity?
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 36

43.We have perused the revocation letter dated 16.12.2025 issued by CTUIL quoted as
under:
Connectivity revocation letter issued to Ganeko-1:
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 37

Connectivity revocation letter issued to Ganeko-2:
As per above, CTUIL after detailed inquiry has found following violations inter alia
including breach of the 2022 GNA Regulations by the Petitioner(s) as under:
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 38

a) Failure to maintain eligibility conditions from 18.03.2025 onwards in respect of
Ganeko-1 rendering the connectivity ineligible.
b) Concealment of material change in location in the LOA from Mandsaur to Solapur
until 20.06.2025 by Ganeko-1.
c) Breach of undertaking and accompanying affidavit submitted along with the
connectivity application of Ganeko-1 by permitting use of eligibility documents in
another application by Ganeko-2.
d) Breach of undertaking and accompanying affidavit submitted along with the
connectivity application by Ganeko-2 while attempting to utilize an eligibility
document that is PPA dated 20.03.2025 linked to LOA already exhausted by
Ganeko-1.
44. Now let us analyse if Connectivity of Ganeko-1 has been rightly revoked or not. We have
already noted in Issue No.1 that as on 18.3.2025, the LOA basis on which Connectivity
of Ganeko-1 was surviving got exhausted. Hence the Connectivity of Ganeko-1 becomes
liable for revocation as on 18.3.2025. We note that CTUIL has rightly revoked
Connectivity of Ganeko-1.
45. Now let us analyse if Connectivity of Ganeko-2 has been rightly revoked or not. We note
that Ganeko-2 was granted Connectivity basis LAND BG at Solapur PS. Gankeo-2
entered into PPA under the Base LOA utilised by Ganeko-1. As such Ganeko-2 as an
independent entity could have entered into any number of PPAs as a company. The issue
arose since Ganeko-2 submitted such a PPA for conversion from LAND BG to LOA/PPA
route to seek return of LAND BG. We note that CTUIL have not accepted the PPA and
did not convert the LAND BG to PPA route. We also note that Ganeko-2 furnished the
land documents to CTUIL on 13.11.25. We note that Ganeko-2 was in breach of its
undertakings by furnishing PPA whose LOA was already utilised by Ganeko-1, we are of
the view that Ganeko-2 was liable of revocation on this count. Accordingly, we note that
CTUIL has rightly revoked Connectivity of Ganeko-2.
46.The Petitioner(s) have submitted the status of the projects as under:
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 39

As per above, we note that both Ganeko-1 and Ganeko-2 have ploughed in
sufficient amount of investment towards land acquisition and procurements towards
their individual project development.
47. Petitioner(s) have stated that they have submitted land documents for 50% of land
required for connectivity granted under land BG and sufficient investments have been
made for timely implementation of projects. We also note that Ganeko-2 has signed PPA
with SJVN for which PSA has been signed with procurer.
Order in Petition Number 728/MP/2025 along with related IAs Page 40

CENTRAL ELECTRICITY REGULATORY COMMISSION
NEW DELHI
Petition No. 92/TD/2026
Coram:
Shri Jishnu Barua, Chairperson
Shri Ramesh Babu V., Member
Shri Harish Dudani, Member
Shri Ravinder Singh Dhillon, Member
Date of Order: 4th May, 2026
In the matter of
Application under Sections 14 and Section 15(1) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with
Regulation 6 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and
Conditions for Grant of Trading Licence and other Related Matters) Regulations, 2020,
for grant of an inter-state trading license.
And
In the matter of
EKI Energy Service Limited,
Registered Office: - 325-C, Prem Trade Centre,
Opposite Gujarati Girls College, Maharani Road, Indore - 452007.
Address for Correspondence:
EKI EMBASSY, A35,
Scheme 78 Part 1- Phase 2,
Indore – 452010, Madhya Pradesh. …Petitioner
Parties present:
Shri Tabrez Malawat, Advocate, NTPL
Shri Syed Hamza, Advocate, NTPL
Shri Sourajit Sarkar, Advocate, NTPL
Ms. Rupali Jain, Advocate, NTPL
ORDER
The Petitioner, EKI Energy Service Limited (hereinafter referred to as “the
Petitioner”), incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956 has made the present
Order in Petition No. 92/TD/2026
Page 1 of 10

Application under Sections 14 and 15 (1) of the Electricity Act, 2003 (hereinafter
referred to as “the Act”) read with Regulation 6 of the Central Electricity Regulatory
Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for the Grant of Trading Licence and
other related matters) Regulations, 2020 (hereinafter referred to as “the Trading
Licence Regulations”), amended from time to time, for the grant of a Category ‘IV’
trading licence for inter-State trading in electricity across India.
Hearing Dated 7.4.2026
2. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner mainly reiterated the
submissions made in the Petition and submitted that the Petitioner satisfies all the
criteria for the grant of a Category ‘IV’ trading licence as stipulated in the Trading
Licence Regulations and prayed for the grant of a trading licence to the Petitioner.
3. The Petitioner, vide Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 07.04.2026,
was directed to submit the following information and clarification:
“(a) Clarify the present legal status of the Petitioner company, in view of the
discrepancy between the description in the petition as a “Private Limited Company”
and the Annual Audited Financial Statements as on 31.3.2025 reflecting the status as
a Listed Public Limited Company, and to place on record documents confirming the
current legal status of the company.
(b) Furnish the detailed Schedules and Notes to Accounts, forming an integral
part of the Audited Special Balance Sheet as on 31.12.2025, including complete
particulars of loans and advances extended to associates and related parties as
defined under the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020, duly prepared in accordance
with the financial reporting framework prescribed under the Companies Act, 2013, in
compliance with Clause 3(b) of the Regulations.
(c ) Confirm that the professionals whose profiles have been submitted are
engaged on a full-time basis, in compliance with Regulation 3(2) of the Trading
Licence Regulations, 2020.
(d) An affidavit to the effect that it shall not carry out the business of transmission
of electricity during the subsistence of the inter-State trading licence, if granted by the
Commission.”
Order in Petition No. 92/TD/2026
Page 2 of 10

3. The Petitioner has filed a compliance affidavit dated 18.04.2026, furnishing the
requisite information and clarification called for as under:
(a) With regard to the legal status of the Company, the Petitioner is a Public
Limited Company listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange as disclosed and
highlighted at Pages 127 and 227 of the Petition. Any inadvertent reference to
the Petitioner as a 'Private Limited Company' in the Petition is a typographical
error and therefore, may be read as 'Public Limited Company'.
(b) In compliance with Clause 3(b) of the Trading Licence Regulations, the
supporting documents are placed on record. These include the Audited Special
Balance Sheet as on 31.12.2025, prepared under the Companies Act, 2013,
along with its Schedules and Notes to Accounts, including details of all loans
and advances extended to related parties and associates as defined under the
said Regulations.
(c) With regard to the engagement of professionals, the individuals, whose
profiles have been submitted, are employed on a full-time basis, in compliance
with Regulation 3(2) of the Trading Licence Regulations
4. The Petitioner, has vide its additional affidavit dated 18.4.2026,
submitted that it shall not, directly or indirectly, engage in or carry on the business of
transmission of electricity at any time during the subsistence of the inter-State trading
licence, if granted.
Order in Petition No. 92/TD/2026
Page 3 of 10

5. We have perused the documents available on record. Regulation 6 of the
Trading Licence Regulations provides for the procedure for the grant of a trading
licence as under:
“6. Procedure for grant of licence
(1) Any person desirous of undertaking inter-State trading in electricity shall
make an application to the Commission for grant of licence in the manner
specified in Form-I appended to these regulations and such application shall
be accompanied by-
(a) Such application fee as prescribed by the Central Government from
time to time and shall be paid as per the procedure specified in Central
Electricity Regulatory Commission (Payment of Fees) Regulations,
2012, as amended from time to time or any statutory re-enactment
thereof.
(b) Copies of the annual reports in case of the persons incorporated
under the Companies Act, 1956 or Companies Act, 2013 including
audited accounts along with the Directors' Report, Auditors' Report, the
Schedules and notes to accounts for one Year immediately preceding
the Year in which the application has been made and the audited
special balance sheet as on any date falling within 30 days immediately
preceding the date of filing the application.
(2) The Applicant shall post complete application along with annexures and
enclosures on its website so as to facilitate access to the application by any
person through internet and shall keep them on the website till the disposal of
the application.
(3) The Applicant shall within 7 days after making such application, publish a
notice of its application, in two daily newspapers in Form II, with the following
particulars, namely:
************
(4) The Applicant shall within 7 days from the date of publication of the notice
as aforesaid submit to the Commission on affidavit the details of the notice
published and shall also file the original complete page of the newspaper in

electrical energy, enter into demand side management contracts, energy-
conservation contracts including energy performance contracts, megawatt

ORDER
Petition No. 216/MP/2024 pertaining to ReNew Solar Power Pvt. Ltd. (RSPPL),
ReNew Surya Aayan Pvt. Ltd. (RSAPL), ReNew Surya Roshni Pvt. Ltd. (RSRPL) and
ReNew Surya Vihaan Pvt. Ltd. (RSVPL) (hereinafter to be referred to as “Petitioners
RSPPL, RSAPL, RSRPL and RSVPL”), Petition No. 242/MP/2024 pertaining to Adani
Renewable Energy Holding Seventeen Limited (AREHSL) and Adani Solar Energy
Barmer One Private Limited (ASEBOPL) (hereinafter to be referred as “Petitioners
AREHSL and ASEBOPL”) and Petition No. 271/MP/2024 pertaining to Altra Xergi
Power Private Limited (hereinafter to be referred as “AXPPL”) have been filed
challenging the invoices raised by Central Transmission Utility of India Ltd. levying
bilateral/ transmission charges under the CERC (Sharing of Inter-State Transmission
Charges and Losses) Regulations, 2020 (hereinafter referred to as ‘2020 Sharing
Regulations’).
2. The Petitioners RSPPL, RSAPL, RSRPL and RSVPL have made the following
prayers in Petition No. 216/MP/2024:
(a) Set aside the Impugned Invoices dated 22.03.2024, 02.04.2024 and 01.05.2024
issued by CTUIL to the Petitioners levying Transmission / Bilateral Charges on the
Petitioners.
(b) Injunct CTUIL from taking any coercive and/or precipitative steps towards recovery
of the transmission charges during pendency of the present petition.
(c) Pass such other order or orders which are deemed fit and proper in the facts and
circumstances of the case.
3. The Petitioners AREHSL and ASEBOPL have made the following prayers in
Petition No. 242/MP/2024:
(a) Quash/ Set aside the impugned bills/ invoices dated (i) 22.03.2024; (ii) 22.03.2024
and (iii) 02.04.2024 issued by the Central Transmission Utility of India Limited
(CTUIL), cumulatively of Rs. 2,62,71,559/-, in terms as stated in the present petition;
(b) Consequently, hold and declare that no form of transmission charges can be imposed
upon the Petitioners, in terms as stated in the present petition; and
Order in Petition Numbers 216/MP/2024, 242/MP/2024 and 271/MP/2024 Page 4

(c) Pass any order and/ or any such orders as this Hon’ble Commission may deem
appropriate.
4. The Petitioner AXPPL has made the following prayers in Petition 271/MP/2024:
(a) Quash the Impugned Invoice dated 22.03.2024 for the Month of February 2024,
Impugned Invoice dated 22.03.2024 for the month of March, 2024 and Impugned
Invoice dated 02.04.2024 issued for the month of April, 2024 by CTUIL;
(b) Direct the CTUIL to not issue any coercive direction/ backdown/curtailment
instructions to NRLDC with respect to the Petitioner’s Project;
(c) Pass any further order(s)/direction(s) that this Hon’ble Court may deem fit in nature
of the facts and circumstances of the present case.
5. The Petitioners RSPPL, RSAPL, RSRPL and RSVPL have also filed an IA being
No. 66/IA/2024 in Petition No. 216/MP/2024 and made the following prayers:
(a) Allow the present Application and urgently list and hear the Petition No. 216/MP/2024
on 08.08.2024 or at any earliest date convenient to this Hon’ble Commission;
(b) Direct the CTUIL to not take any coercive steps against the Petitioners, including but
not limited to, issuance of directions for backdown / curtailment of power from the
Petitioners’ Project;
(c) Pass any such other order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission deems just in the facts and
circumstances of the present case.
6. The Petitioner AREHSL and ASEBOPL have also filed an IA, being No.
57/IA/2024, in Petition No. 242/MP/2024 and made the following prayers in
57/IA/2024:
(a) Allow and admit the present application;
(b) Stay the operation of the impugned bills as the same are against the extant regulations
and the mandate of EA 2003;
(c) Direct the Respondent No. 1/ CTUIL to not issue any further invoices qua transmission
charges till the pendency of the petition;
(d) Direct the Respondent No. 1/ CTUIL to not take coercive measures against the
Applicants/ Petitioners, in any manner whatsoever, till the pendency of the petition; and
(e) Pass any order, as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the light of
facts and circumstances of the instant case.
7. The Commission vide RoP for hearing dated 13.08.2024 in Petition No.
216/MP/2024 along with IA No. 66/2024, directed that, CTUIL, is not to take any
coercive steps against the Petitioners, including the issuance of directions for
backdown/ curtailment of power from their projects, provided the Petitioners
deposit an amount of Rs. 1 crore against such invoices within a week subject to
the outcome of the present case.
Order in Petition Numbers 216/MP/2024, 242/MP/2024 and 271/MP/2024 Page 5

8. The Commission vide RoP for hearing dated 08.11.2024 in Petition No.
242/MP/2024 along with IA No. 57/2024, directed that, the Petitioners will deposit
an amount of Rs. 1 crore on a lump sum basis against the Bilateral Transmission
charges invoices raised and subject to such payment, the CTUIL will not take any
coercive measures against the Petitioners until further directions.
9. The issues raised in Petition No. 216/MP/2024, 242/MP/2024 and Petition No.
271/MP/2024 are identical. Hence, pleadings in Petition No. 216/MP/2024 are
covered in detail, and additional submissions (apart from those already covered in
Petition No. 216/MP/2024) in Petitions 242/MP/2024 and 271/MP/2024 are
covered in brief. Analysis and decision are applicable to all three cases.

(g) Invoices for transmission charges have been issued by CTUIL in contravention of
the GNA Regulations 2022, and the 2020 Sharing Regulations, since the GNA /
Connectivity has not been made effective till date. In the absence of the GNA
having been made effective and the same having been intimated to the
Petitioners, the actions of CTUIL in issuing the said invoices are patently illegal.
(h) Petitioners are generating stations based on renewable sources of energy and
are, as such, exempt from payment of transmission charges in accordance with
the 2020 Sharing Regulations and the extant MoP orders. The only scenario in
which a renewable energy-based generating station is required to pay
transmission charges is as per Regulation 13(3) of the 2020 Sharing Regulations.
Regulation 13(3) of the 2020 Sharing Regulations as amended by the CERC
Sharing Regulations (First Amendment) 2023 and CERC Sharing Regulations
(Second Amendment) 2023 deals with a scenario where COD of a Connectivity
Grantee has not been achieved on or before the start date of connectivity and the
Associated Transmission System has achieved COD, then the Connectivity
Grantee shall pay Yearly Transmission Charges for the Associated Transmission
System corresponding to Connectivity capacity which has not achieved COD. It is
submitted that the prerequisite for attributing liability to a connectivity grantee is
that the ATS has achieved COD, which is not earlier than the start date of
connectivity. The trigger for the application of Regulation 13(3) of the amended
Sharing Regulations is that:
(i) Connectivity Grantee (Petitioner in this case) have not achieved COD
before the start date of connectivity; AND
(ii) The ATS has achieved COD, which is not earlier than the start date of
connectivity.

been no delay by the Petitioners in attaining the COD. All the Petitioners have
attained COD as below:
(i) Renew Surya Pratap, wholly owned subsidiary of RSVPL: attained COD for
175 MW capacity on 22.02.2024 and the balance 22 MW on 02.04.2024.
(ii) RSVPL (100 MW): attained COD for 98 MW capacity on 31.03.2024.
(iii) RSAPL: attained COD for 290 MW capacity on 31.03.2024.
(iv) RSRPL: attained COD for 285 MW capacity.
(j) CTUIL vide Impugned Invoices has sought to levy transmission charges for the
months of December 2023, January 2024, February 2024 and March 2024 upon
the Petitioners, allegedly for the delay in commencement of generation and supply
of power from the Projects. However, without all elements of the transmission
system being ready, the issuance of the transmission invoices is completely
unlawful and contrary to the extant Regulations and decisions of this Commission.
In this regard, the Petitioners' liability to pay transmission charges accrues only
when the last element of the transmission asset is operationalised, and the bays
at both ends of the transmission line are put to use.
(k) Regulation 2(1)(g) of the 2020 Sharing Regulations, defined ‘COD of the ATS’ to
mean the COD of the last transmission element of the ATS. Admittedly, all the
elements of the ATS/ Common Transmission System as specified in the grant of
LTA to the Petitioners are not ready as of the date, and therefore, there is no basis
for CTUIL to impose any transmission / bilateral charges.
(l) Regulation 22.4 of the GNA Regulations 2022 provides that the start date of
connectivity will be the effective date of GNA. Since the Petitioners have not
received any letter/ intimation from CTUIL for operationalisation of GNA, it
emerges that the start date of connectivity and effective date of GNA have not
been achieved. No transmission charges are payable before the Effectiveness of
the GNA/ Connectivity.
(m) The intimation of grant of LTA to the Petitioners categorically states that liability
to pay transmission charges shall start from the start date of LTA as requested by
the applicant or from the date of commissioning of the transmission system
identified for LTA, whichever is later. Admittedly, the last element of the

Projects are yet to be commissioned as per data obtained from the CEA Monthly
Progress Report for the month of March 2024 and the Joint Co-ordination

Submissions of Petitioners AREHSL and ASEBOPL in Petition 242/MP/2024:
11. The Petitioners AREHSL and ASEBOPL have submitted as under:
(a) Petitioner ASEBOPL has executed two different PPAs with NHPC Limited, both
dated 10.09.2020, for the supply of 280 MW and 320 MW, respectively, on a long
term basis for a period of 25 years from COD. Under the said PPAs, the Original
Scheduled Commercial Operation Date (SCOD) was 10.03.2022, which was later
revised progressively up to 31.08.2024 through multiple SCOD extensions
granted by NHPC. Thus, once the SCOD under the aforesaid PPAs stood
extended, there can clearly be no allegation of a mismatch in COD by the
generator qua the ATS or that the COD has not been achieved. This is because
the COD cannot be before the SCOD under the PPAs mentioned in Regulation
13(1).
(b) As per Regulation 6.2 of GNA Regulations 2022, an ATS has been defined to mean
the augmentation, which is required for immediate evacuation of power, excluding
terminal bay(s). However, post the transition from LTA to GNA (vide letter dated
25.09.2023 issued by CTUIL), till date, CTUIL has never communicated any
revised ATS to the Petitioner. Thus, without such intimation/ communication, it can
be assumed that the transmission system as was identified at the time of grant of
LTA to the Petitioner, is the ATS under the GNA of the said Petitioner as well,
whose elements/ system has till date not achieved commissioning.
Order in Petition Numbers 216/MP/2024, 242/MP/2024 and 271/MP/2024 Page 13

(c) Regulation 13(3) of 2020 Sharing Regulations can only apply if the generator is
not able to achieve SCOD/ COD in terms of the PPAs mentioned under Regulation
13(1), while the transmission infrastructure required for immediate evacuation of
power (i.e., ATS) achieves COD.
(d) As per Regulation 13(3) read with Regulation 2(1)(g) of the 2020 Sharing
Regulations, Regulation 22.4 of the GNA Regulations 2022 and Clause 7 of the
Conditions to the Grant of LTA the liability to pay transmission charges only
accrues upon a connectivity grantee from the date of commissioning of all
elements identified in the LTA forming part of the Common Transmission System.
(e) RE Power Plants are exempted from payment of transmission charges under the
2020 Sharing Regulations. Therefore, by imposing such penalty qua transmission
charges, CTUIL is in effect acting in contravention to the above Regulations, as
well as against the intent of the EA 2003, qua promotion of the RE generation.
Hence, on this count also, the impugned invoices deserve to be quashed/ set
aside.

Reply of CTUIL in Petition No. 216/MP/2024:
21. The Respondent, CTUIL vide affidavit dated 09.10.2024 in its reply has mainly
submitted as under:
(a) The clear regulatory position is that, irrespective of any delay in achieving the
project COD, the connectivity grantee is liable to pay transmission charges for the
ATS corresponding to the connectivity capacity which has not achieved COD.
(b) The Petitioners have placed reliance on Regulation 19.1 of the 2020 Sharing
Regulations to assert that CTUIL is obligated to provide notice to the Designated
ISTS Customer (DIC) at least three months prior to the operationalisation date of
LTA. The requirement for notice pertains specifically to the establishment of a
Letter of Credit as part of the payment security mechanism, which is not applicable
to the Petitioners, who are renewable energy generators for whom transmission
charges are waived once their projects are commissioned.
(c) The bilateral transmission charges bills are raised by CTUIL on behalf of the
transmission licensees who submit the required data to the Implementing Agency,
and the Implementing Agency, in turn, intimates the claims of the licensees to the
concerned RPC for their incorporation in the RTAs issued to CTUIL.
(d) A GNA grantee, under the GNA Regulations 2022, is placed in a similar position
as an LTA grantee under the Connectivity Regulations and, as such, is liable to
pay the transmission charges as per the Sharing Regulations; waiver for
transmission charges can only be availed by a generating station from the date of
its actual COD.
(e) In the context of the provisions under the GNA regulations, the Commission has
notified an amendment in the 2020 Sharing Regulations, wherein ATS is now

defined to have the same meaning as defined in the GNA Regulations and
Regulation 13(3) of the 2020 Sharing Regulations was amended. However, since
the Petitioner’s connectivity and LTA grants (since then transitioned to deemed
GNA) had been made under the provisions of the Connectivity Regulations, a
subsequent amendment in the Sharing Regulations brought about in view of the
fresh grants under the GNA Regulations could not be made applicable to them,
more so retrospectively.
(f) The Petitioners have relied upon Regulation 22.4 of the GNA Regulations to
contend that the start date or effective date of connectivity can only occur after
operationalisation of GNA, or the start date of connectivity is to be the effective
date of GNA. The above provision is necessarily to be read in conjunction with
Regulation 13(3) of the 2020 Sharing Regulations, which makes an LTTC liable
for transmission charges if the ATS has achieved COD, which is the position in the
instant case.
(g) Elements of Rajasthan SEZ Ph-II Part-A (S. No. A in Annexure-II of the LTA

to the grid for generation projects connected or to be connected at Fatehgarh-III
PS (Section-I). This covers the Petitioners and two other Renewable energy
developers – Altra Xergi Power Private Limited (380 MW) and Adani Renewable
Energy Holding Seventeen Ltd. (600 MW). Accordingly, the elements of Rajasthan
SEZ Ph-II Part-A are to be considered as ATS for all these developers (ReNew,
Altra Xergi, and Adani).
Order in Petition Numbers 216/MP/2024, 242/MP/2024 and 271/MP/2024 Page 37

(d) The Common Transmission System identified for the Petitioners were part of the
larger scheme – either the Phase I scheme related to 8.9 GW or the Phase II
scheme related to 8.1 GW. Whereas Part A is identified only for the generation
projects connected/ proposed to be connected at Fatehgarh-III PS (Sec-I).
(e) In the present case, the applications and grant letters were prior to the GNA
Regulations. The provisions of GNA Regulations cannot be made applicable
retrospectively to these aspects. While the Petitioners exercised the option to
convert their LTAs into GNAs deemed to have been granted under the GNA
Regulations, the deemed GNA is not a fresh grant under the GNA Regulations.
This is also clear from the letter dated 25.09.2023. There was no change in start
date or transmission system requirements from the earlier grant.
(f) The contention of the Petitioner that both Part A and Part B be identified as ATS
would render the entire purpose of the division into two categories, both in the LTA
letters and Regulation 6 of GNA Regulations, redundant, besides being contrary
to the definition of ATS.
(g) The fact that the ATS is only Part A, which was already commissioned on
24.12.2023, can also be clear from the fact that the Petitioners’ generating stations
were able to declare COD utilising the Part A system mentioned under LTA and, in
fact, were able to evacuate power under T-GNA. Therefore, ATS was clearly
sufficient for the immediate evacuation of power, as per Regulation 6.2 of the GNA
Regulations. The Petitioners were undoubtedly able to commission and evacuate
power from the generating station, indicating that the ATS was ready. If the
Petitioners had been ready on 24.12.2023, they could also have commissioned
the generating station on that day.
(h) Petitioners have sought to refer to Regulation 22.4 of GNA Regulations 2022,
which refers to the effective date of GNA. However, Regulation 13(3) of 2020
Sharing Regulations is not with reference to the effective date of GNA, and
therefore, the reliance is misconceived. The provision is necessarily to be read in
conjunction with Regulation 13(3) of the 2020 Sharing Regulations, which makes
the Generator liable for transmission charges if the ATS has achieved COD.
Written submissions of Petitioners RSPPL, RSAPL, RSRPL and RSVPL in
Petition No.216/MP/2024 dated 29.08.2025:
Order in Petition Numbers 216/MP/2024, 242/MP/2024 and 271/MP/2024 Page 38

35. Petitioners RSPPL, RSAPL, RSRPL and RSVPL, in their written submission, re-
iterated its earlier submissions and mainly submitted as under:
(a) No distinction has been made at the time of granting the LTA as to whether Part A
or Part B or both constitute the ATS.
(b) The Commission has itself observed that COD can be declared only after a
successful trial run of the last element of the ATS, and there can be no relaxation,
as commercial liability starts soon after COD of all elements of the ATS. Therefore,
CTUIL and PRTL cannot hold Petitioners liable to pay transmission charges before
COD of the last element of the ATS (being the Annexure specified in the grant of
LTA).
(c) Instead of raising a bilateral bill upon the Petitioners, PRTL is entitled to recover
its amounts in terms of Regulation 13(12) of the 2020 Sharing Regulations, which
provides the modalities for a transmission licensee to recover its Transmission
Charges.
Written submissions of Petitioners AREHSL and ASEBOPL in Petition No.
242/MP/2024 dated 25.08.2025:
36. Petitioners in their written submission re-iterated its earlier submissions and
mainly submitted as under:
(a) The right to impose bilateral bills by CTUIL, on behalf of transmission licensees
such as PRTL, under Regulation 13(3) of the 2020 Sharing Regulations, is
contingent upon the CTUIL being able to offer effectiveness of GNA to the
generator, while the said generator has not commissioned. In the event that GNA
cannot be said to be effective, PRTL is not entitled to recover its transmission
charges from the generators through CTUIL, in terms of the above Regulations.
In such an event, the transmission charges for PRTL must be passed on to the
POC Pool in terms of regulation 13(12) of the 2020 Sharing regulations.
(b) The Petitioner’s GNA became effective/ operationalised only from 22.01.2025, i.e.,
after the commissioning of the 765/400 kV Sikar-II S/s, Bhadla-II – Sikar-II –
Neemrana 400 kV D/c line. Until then, whatever system/ elements were made
ready were not sufficient for the desired transfer of power on a long term basis, in
terms of the LTA grant.

evacuation of power; however, the GNA itself is not operationalised, meaning
thereby that there cannot be any flow of power to intended beneficiaries on a long
term basis even after commissioning the transmission system.
(d) Only 3 elements out of the elements covered under Schedule III of the TSA
executed with PRTL are covered under the LTA/ GNA of the Petitioners.
Therefore, transmission charges qua only these elements can be levied upon the
Petitioner. The total capacity of PRTL’s transmission system comprises the
