Sector– 29, Gurgaon, Haryana - 122 001
3. Southern Regional Load Dispatch Centre (SRLDC)
29, Race Course Cross Road,
Bangalore- 560009 ……. Respondent(s)
Order in Petition No. 183/MP/2021 1

Parties Present:
Shri Sidhant Kumar, Advocate, APTRANSCO
Ms. Manya Chandok, Advocate, APTRANSCO
Ms. Ekssha Kashyap, Advocate, APTRANSCO
Shri Shubham Arya, Advocate, CTUIL
Ms. Reeha Singh, Advocate, CTUIL
Ms. Kaavya Madaan, Advocate, CTUIL
Ms. Kavya Bhardwaj, CTUIL
Ms. Muskan Agarwal, CTUIL
Shri Alok Mishra, SRLDC
Shri Ashok Rajan, SRLDC
ORDER
Transmission Corporation of Andhra Pradesh Ltd has filed this Petition seeking
directions to the Southern Regional Power Committee to provide necessary information
regarding intra-State transmission lines falling under Regulation 2(1)(ee) CERC (Sharing
of Inter-State Transmission Charges And Losses) Regulations, 2020 (hereinafter
‘Sharing Regulations, 2020’).
2. The Petitioner has made the following prayers in the Petition:
(a) Direct the Respondent to provide necessary information to the Petitioner as sought under
Para 3 of the present Petition, for the year 2020-21 any other relevant information to
enable the Petitioner to recover transmission charges under the Sharing Regulations
2020;
(b) Grant liberty to the Petitioner to file an Application for determining the transmission tariff
under Regulation 13 (13) of the Sharing Regulations, 2020, read with CERC Tariff
Regulations, 2019, on the basis of the information sought under prayer (a) in the present
proceedings;
(c) Pass any other or further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper
in the interest of justice
(Para 3 mentioned in prayer is at para 4 of this order)
Submissions of Petitioner
3. The Petitioner owns and controls various intra-state transmission lines in the State of
Andhra Pradesh. These intra-state transmission lines are frequently used for the
transmission of inter-state power for utilisation outside AP. Petitioner is entitled to
recover Yearly Transmission Charges (YTC) for such inter-state transmission, using
Order in Petition No. 183/MP/2021 2

these intra-state transmission lines under the Sharing Regulations, 2020. Petitioner,
however, has been prevented from recovering the YTC for the FY 2020-21, solely due
to the failure on the part of the Respondent No. 1 to provide the requisite information.
4. The recovery of YTC under the Sharing Regulations, 2020, necessarily requires the
Petitioner to furnish details pertaining to (i) the identification of the intra-state
transmission lines carrying inter-state power and (ii) the percentage of inter-state
power transmitted through these lines.
5. The domain of the Petitioner, under Section 39 of the Act, is restricted only to the
transmission of electricity within the State and does not encompass the inter-state
power system operation. Petitioner cannot, therefore, itself identify such intra-state
lines that carry inter-state power and whether they are eligible for claiming
transmission charges under the Sharing Regulations, 2020. Such identification can
only be done by the Respondent No. 1, using the appropriate software and information
within its authority.
6. Intra-state lines owned and operated by the Petitioner have been used to carry inter-
state power for many years, depending on conditions arising from system parameters,
configuration, composition of different lines and incidental situations. Due to such
inter-state transmission, these intra-state transmission lines have been accorded
annual certification as Natural/ Deemed Inter-State Transmission System by the
Respondent No. 1 under the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Sharing of
Inter-State Transmission Charges and Losses) Regulations, 2010 (‘Sharing
Regulations, 2010’/ ‘former Sharing Regulations’).
7. On the basis of such certification by the Respondent No. 1, and the consequent tariff
approval granted by the APERC, the Petitioner has been able to recover the YTC for
inter-state transmission for the past five years.
8. From the definition of YTC under Regulation 2(1)(ee) of the Sharing Regulations,
2020, recovery of YTC is permitted on the basis of a tariff approved by the Commission
for both the inter-State Transmission System (‘ISTS’) and the Intra-State Transmission
System used for inter-state transmission of electricity (‘InSTS’). The Petitioner is
entitled to recover YTC on account of:
i. Transmission elements of ISTS, which have achieved COD up to the last day of a
billing period (For ISTS); or
ii. Intra-state transmission lines used for inter-State transmission of electricity. (For
InSTS).
Order in Petition No. 183/MP/2021 3

9. Regulation 13(3), the Petitioner is entitled to recover YTC only on the satisfaction of
the following conditions:
i. The tariff for the InSTS must be approved by the Central Commission; and
ii. Such a tariff must be approved for the entire period for which recovery of
transmission charges is sought.
10. Petitioner addressed a letter dated 12.05.2021 to the Respondent No. 1, seeking
identification and/or certification of intra-state transmission lines owned by the
Petitioner, which carried inter-state power during 2020-2021. Petitioner also
addressed a letter dated 12.05.2021 to the Implementing Agency under the
Regulations, i.e. the National Load Dispatch Centre, seeking a detailed procedure to
be followed by the STUs for claiming YTC charges in respect of InSTS under the
Sharing Regulations, 2020. However, the Petitioner has not received any clarification
or reply from the Implementing Agency.
11. Respondent No. 1, in its letter dated 13.05.2021, refused to furnish the requisite
certification of intra-state lines carrying inter-state electricity. Respondent No. 1 merely
stated that such certification was not envisaged under the Sharing Regulations, 2020.
Respondent No. 1 also directed the Petitioner to approach this Commission directly
for approval of a tariff for such intra-state transmission lines forming part of InSTS
carrying inter-state power, to recover transmission charges.
12. Petitioner issued a letter dated 17.05.2021 to the Commission seeking from the
Respondent No. 1 the inter-state lines carrying inter-state power for the purpose of
filing the requisite tariff petition before the Commission in compliance with Regulation
13(13).
13. Petitioner sought such information and details from the Respondent No. 1, vide letter
and email dated 17.06.2021. By way of an email dated 18.06.2021, the Respondent
No. 1 has merely sent a document containing ‘Minutes of Special Meeting on
certification of non-ISTS transmission lines and on NEA held on 11.01.2019.
14. This has caused grave prejudice and loss to the Petitioner and the Andhra Pradesh
State Distribution Companies (‘APDISCOMs’), who will have to bear the transmission
charges of such inter-state power, despite its utilisation by other state utilities.
15. If appropriate directions as sought in the present Appeal are not passed against the
No. 1 herein, the intent behind Regulation 2(1)(ee) r/w Regulation 13(13) for allowing
recovery of YTC, will be defeated and would render the said Regulations otiose qua
the intra-state transmission lines carrying inter-state power.
Order in Petition No. 183/MP/2021 4

16. It is incumbent on the Respondent No. 1 to provide such identification and/or
certification of intra-state transmission lines owned by the Petitioner which carried
inter-state power during 2020-2021, to enable the Petitioner to file an appropriate
petition for determining tariff under the Sharing Regulations, 2020. Consequently,
such information is crucial to ultimately enable the Petitioner to avail of its entitlements
under the Sharing Regulations, 2020.
Hearing dated 12.10.2021
17. The Relevant extract of RoP dated 12.10.2021 is as below:
Case was called out for virtual hearing.
2. Leaned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner owns intra-State
transmission lines in Andhra Pradesh which are used for transmission of inter-State power
and is entitled to recover YTC for such transmission lines. Accordingly, it has approached
SRPC on 12.5.2021 to certify the intra-State lines owned by the Petitioner which carried inter-
State power during 2021 for claiming tariff for the year 2021. SRPC vide letter dated 13.5.2021
has refused to issue the requisite certification stating that such certification is not envisaged
in the 2021 Sharing Regulations and directed the Petitioner to approach the Commission
directly for approval of tariff for such intra-State transmission lines.
3. The Commission observed that it is the responsibility of APTRANSCO to give the details of
the intra-State transmission lines which in its view are used for transmission of inter-State
power.
4. In response, the learned counsel for the Petitioner sought two weeks’ time to get
instructions from APTRANSCO in this regard.
5. The Petition shall be listed for hearing in due course for which separate notice will be issued.
Submission of Petitioner
18. Petitioner, vide affidavit 17.11.2021, has submitted as below:
(a) Petitioner, by letter dated 20.10.2021, provided the Respondent No. 1 a list of
all intra-state transmission lines (40 Lines are EHT lines, 232 lines are 220KV
and 2 lines are 132KV) which are likely to incidentally carry Inter-state power.
Accordingly, the Petitioner requested the Respondent No. 1 to provide the
necessary certification/identification for such intra-state lines. Respondent
No. 1, in its reply dated 22.10.2021, has yet again refused to provide the
necessary certification/ identification of such intra-state lines.
(b) The Respondent No. 1 SRPC, in its 31st Meeting held on 25.02.2017,
approved the methodology for certification for non-ISTS lines having more
than 50% utilization for carrying inter-state power transmission. As per the
said methodology, the base case of each quarter submitted by DIC to the
validation Committee for PoC computation of the previous financial year
would be examined for certification in the current year. If in each base case,
Order in Petition No. 183/MP/2021 5

the usage of state-owned lines is greater by other states than the home state,
then those lines would be certified as non-ISTS line carrying interstate power.
The usage of lines was agreed to be obtained through the Webnet software.
(c) The Petitioner does not have the means or access to the Webnet software
and therefore cannot itself identify the intra-state transmission lines which
carry inter-state power.
Submission of Respondent No. 1
19. The Respondent No. 1, Southern Regional Power Committee, vide affidavit dated
08.02.2024 have submitted as follows:
a) APTRANSCO, vide letter dated 12.05.2021, requested SRPC to provide
certification/identification of intra-state lines carrying inter-state power which have
more than 50% utilization for carrying inter-state power during 2020-21. SRPC, vide
response letter dated 13 May 2021, had clarified that the certification of intra-state
lines carrying inter-state power by RPCs was not envisaged in the Sharing
Regulations 2020 and suggested that APTRANSCO may approach the Commission
directly for approval of the tariff of intra state lines carrying interstate power for
recovery of transmission charges.
b) Further, APTRANSCO, vide letter dated 20.10.2021, had again sought the above
details, and SRPC vide letter dated 22.10.2021 clarified that there is no provision for
RPC Certification for non-ISTS in the Sharing Regulation 2020. Hence, APTRANSCO
furnished details of the intra-State transmission lines, which in its view are used for
transmission of inter-state power, to CERC, as directed by CERC in RoP dated
12.10.2021.
Hearing dated 15.03.2024
20. The Relevant extract of RoP is as below:
The instant petition has been filed by the Petitioner seeking directions to Southern Regional
Power Committee (SRPC) to provide necessary information regarding the intra-State
transmission lines falling under Regulation 2(1)(EE) Central Electricity Regulatory
Commission (Sharing of inter-State Transmission Charges and Losses) Regulations, 2020.
2. The learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner is a State Transmission
Utility (STU) of Andhra Pradesh, and some of the transmission lines owned by it are carrying
inter-State power. The Petitioner is entitled to recovery of Yearly Transmission Charges (YTC)
as per Regulation 13 of the 2020 Sharing Regulations. After the enforcement of the 2020
Sharing Regulations, identification of intra-State transmission lines carrying inter-state power
is a pre-requisite for recovery of YTC. The Petitioner does not have the facility to measure the
percentage of power flowing through the intra-State lines to declare them as natural/ deemed
inter-State transmission lines Therefore, the Petitioner approached the SRPC for identification
Order in Petition No. 183/MP/2021 6

of its intra-State transmission lines, which are carrying more than 50% inter-State power
during the year 2020-21, using the webnet software. However, SRPC refused to furnish the
requisite information. As the Petitioner does not have the webnet software to measure the
percentage of load factor and load-flow analysis, it is unable to file a tariff petition before the
Commission. He submitted that SRPC may be directed to provide the load flow analysis of
the lines so that the Petitioner could file a petition for recovery of transmission charges for
such lines. He further submitted that all the available information with the Petitioner has
already been furnished to SRPC.
3. The Commission directed the Petitioner to implead CTUIL and SRLDC as a party to the
petition and serve a copy of the petition on them. The Commission further directed the
Petitioner to file the amended ‘Memo of Parties’ by 1.4.2024.
4. The Commission further observed that the Petitioner has provided a summary of about 272
intra-State transmission lines, which are claimed to be carrying inter-State power, without
explaining the details regarding how these transmission lines are being used as ISTS lines.
The Petitioner is directed to provide the details of how these 272 numbers of transmission
lines are being used as ISTS lines on an affidavit, by 1.4.2024, with an advance copy to the
Respondents.
5. The Commission directed SRLDC to submit the details of the monthly percentage utilization
of the intra-State lines of APTRANSCO claimed to be carrying inter-State power in 2020-21
in its reply.
Submission of Respondent No 3
21. Respondent No.3 Southern Regional Load Despatch Center, vide affidavit dated
19.04.2024 has submitted as below:
a) During FY 2020-21, there were two regulations of CERC on Sharing of Inter-State
Transmission Charges and Losses for different time periods that were in force as
mentioned below:
i. Sharing of Transmission Charges and Losses, Regulations, 2010 till 31.10.2020
ii. Sharing of Inter-State Transmission Charges and Losses Regulations, 2020,
effective from 01.11.2020
As per the 2010 regulation on Sharing of Inter-State Transmission Charges and
Losses, the PSS/E Base case was prepared Quarterly, whereas the PSS/E base
case is prepared monthly as per the 2020 regulation w.e.f 01.11.2020.
b) SRLDC has performed the simulation in the Web Net Use software, which is used for
the determination of the sharing of Inter-State Transmission Charges.
c) In the present petition, Andhra Pradesh has claimed 274 transmission lines; however,
considering circuit-wise, the total number of transmission lines would be as given
below:

Submission of Petitioner
22. Petitioner vide additional affidavit dated 22.04.2024 has reiterated its earlier
submission and has additionally submitted as under:
a) It is imperative to clarify that Petitioners do not have the requisite software or expertise
to identify the inter-state transmission lines carrying inter-state power. It is for this
reason that the Petitioners on 20 October 2021 submitted a list of 272 transmission
lines to Respondent No.1, which are likely to carry the interstate power since lines are
connected to inter-state lines in a meshed network. It is not the submission or pleading
of the Petitioner that all of these 272 intra state transmission lines qualify the criteria
for recovering YTC. It is stated that out of this list, only some intra-state lines may
carry more than 50% interstate power.
b) Respondent No.1 is the appropriate technical body having the requisite information
concerning intra-state transmission lines carrying ISTS power.
c) The Petitioner has analyzed the prior certifications issued by Respondent No.1. The
number of qualified intrastate lines year wise is as below-

state transmission lines which are likely to carry inter-state power for FY 2020-21.

Hearing dated 13.05.2025
23. The Relevant extract of RoP is as below:
At the outset, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that, in compliance with the
directions given by the Commission vide RoP dated 15.3.2024, the Southern Region Load
Despatch Centre (SRLDC) had filed an affidavit dated 19.4.2024, providing the relevant

25. Respondent No. 3 SRLDC vide affidavit dated 02.06.2025 has submitted information

a) Query 1: Clarify what value was taken for the denominator when calculating the
percentage utilisation of the respective transmission lines. For a sample in the 400 kV
Nunna -Vemagiri line on actual loading of 69 MW, the % utilization in ISTS has been
given as 82.75%, which is to be explained.
GRID-INDIA/NLDC/SRLDC is using the WebNetUse software application for the
determination of Transmission usage cost and loss allocation. The aforesaid software
does not utilise the denominator component for determining the percentage utilisation
of the transmission lines. Further, WebNetUse software performs Load Flow Analysis
(LFA), which computes bus voltages (magnitude and angle) for a given network
topology and load-generation schedule. Once voltages are known, power flows are
also computed. Based on the power flow results, the transmission usage cost
allocation will be computed by the WebNetUse software as per the Transmission
usage cost allocation algorithm. This algorithm computes the recovery of the
embedded or fixed cost of the transmission system from multiple users, such as loads
and generators. WebNetUse software uses a hybrid method for the computation of
transmission usage based on the following two methods:
i. Average Participation: In this method, power flow is traced from the injection
nodes to the withdrawal nodes using assumptions. Power flow tracing is based on
the equi-proportionality principle. It is possible to identify and measure the
responsibility of each injection and withdrawal nodes for the power flows on each
network element.
ii. Marginal Participation: Marginal participation method analyses the modified
flows in the transmission lines when marginal (minor) changes are introduced in
Order in Petition No. 183/MP/2021 12

Generation and Loads. The marginal participation sensitivities of each entity are
calculated as a product of its net injection and marginal participation. The cost of
each line is allocated pro-rata to different agents according to their total
participation in the corresponding line
Based on the two methods, WebNetUse software traces the power flow in each line
and accounts for all loads and generators present in the load flow scenario. The

Analysis and Decision
Order in Petition No. 183/MP/2021 20

31. Petitioner has filed the instant petition seeking directions to SRPC to provide
necessary information to the Petitioner for the year 2020-21. Petitioner has prayed
that SRPC should identify the intra-state lines owned and operated by Petitioner in its
capacity as STU (APTRANSCO), which have been used for inter-state power for
2020-2021, to enable Petitioner to seek a tariff from this Commission.
32. Petitioner in the instant Petition filed on 11.08.20201 stated that it is seeking YTC for
the year 2020-2021. However, Petitioner has referred to the letter dated 12.05.2021
by Petitioner to Respondent SRPC vide which petitioner requested SRPC to certify
intra-state lines basis data of 2020-2021 so that it can claim YTC for the year 2021-
2022. Petitioner vide Affidavit dated 17.11.2021 stated that it is seeking YTC for the
year 2021-2022. We note that Petitioner has relied on data for the year 2020-2021.
Accordingly, the analysis has been made for data for the year 2020-2021 which would
cover YTC for the year 2020-2021 and 2021-2022 covered under the Sharing
Regulations 2020.
33. The issue that arises for our consideration is as under
Whether any directions are required to be issued to SRPC (Respondent No 1) to
identify such intra-state lines in light of pleadings under the instant Petition, and
consequently, whether Petitioner is required to be granted liberty to file an
Application for determining the transmission tariff under Regulation 13 (13) of
the Sharing Regulations?
The issue is dealt with in subsequent paragraphs.
34. The Petitioner, Transmission Corporation of Andhra Pradesh Ltd. (APTRANSCO),
submitted that its intra-state transmission lines are used to carry inter-state power,
and therefore it is entitled to recover Yearly Transmission Charges (YTC) under the
Sharing Regulations, 2020. APTRANSCO emphasised that recovery of YTC requires
identification of which intra-state lines carried inter-state power and the percentage of
such usage. Since this information can only be determined through data available with
the Southern Regional Power Committee (SRPC) and Southern Regional Load
Dispatch Centre (SRLDC), SRPC should be directed to identify such lines.
35. APTRANSCO submitted that under the Sharing Regulations, 2010, SRPC had
consistently certified its lines as “deemed inter-state” based on usage, enabling
recovery of charges for several years. However, after the Sharing Regulations, 2020
came into force, SRPC refused to provide certification.
Order in Petition No. 183/MP/2021 21

36. On a query from the Commission on intra-state lines as per the Petitioner, which
carried inter-state power, the Petitioner initially submitted a list of 272 transmission
lines.
37. Commission, vide ROP for hearing dated 15.03.2024, directed SRLDC to submit the
details of the monthly percentage utilization of the intra-State lines of APTRANSCO
claimed to be carrying inter-State power in 2020-21 in its reply, SRLDC in its reply
furnished the details of all lines (except 9 lines not available in PSSE case) and
submitted that the majority of lines do not utilize more than 50 % to carry ISTS power
in all quarters, however, some of the lines are getting utilized for more than 50% to
carry ISTS power in all quarters.
38. Respondent SRPC submitted that the certification of intrastate lines carrying interstate
power by RPCs was not envisaged in the Sharing Regulations, 2020. Therefore,
Petitioner is requested to approach CERC directly for approval of the tariff of
intra-state lines carrying interstate power for recovery of transmission charges.
39. Petitioner, vide Affidavit dated 22.04.2024, submitted that it is not the submission or
pleading of the Petitioner that all of these 272 intra-state transmission lines qualify the
criteria for recovering YTC and stated that out of this list, only some intra-state lines
may carry more than 50% interstate power. Accordingly, Petitioner submitted a list of
42 intra-state transmission lines, that are likely to carry inter-state power for FY 2020-
21 as under: Petitioner categorically stated that it is not pressing for load flow details
for 9 lines which were not in the PSSE case.
Order in Petition No. 183/MP/2021 22

40. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and Respondents.
41. We note that Petitioner is seeking identification of intra-state lines used for carrying
inter-state power for FY 2020-21. In this regard Snap of the SRPC letter dated
30.04.2020 for certification of non-ISTS line carrying ISTS power for the period 2020-
21, which were having more than 50% utilization for Interstate Power Transmission
during the year 2019-20, is as under:
Order in Petition No. 183/MP/2021 23

Order in Petition No. 183/MP/2021 24

Order in Petition No. 183/MP/2021 25

As per above, SRPC already provided certification for FY 2020-2021 on 30.4.2020.
Based on the above certification, SRPC also issued an Availability Certificate for
these lines, and Petitioner has confirmed that it has recovered YTC for identified
lines for the period April 2020-October 2020.
42. The Commission, vide Order dated 17.05.2024 in Petition No. 25/MP/2022, filed by
the APTRANSCO, has allowed the recovery of the transmission charges of the non-
ISTS lines carrying ISTS power till 30.10.2020, quoted as under:
“Issue No.1: Whether the petitioner is entitled to inclusion of transmission charges
determined by the APERC for non-ISTS lines certified by SRPC to be carrying inter-state
power for the period from 2015-16, 2016-17 and 2020- 21 (up to 31.10.2020) in the PoC
mechanism as per the Sharing Regulations, 2010?
…………….
40. We observe that though the above-claimed lines by the Petitioner are certified by
the SRPC and carry more than 50% inter-State power at the same time, we also
observe from the CTUIL submission that power flow on ISTS line as well STU lines
varies significantly based on the load demand and power generation and further on
some of the transmission lines, the power flow also changes in reverse direction. We
also observe that the methodology followed by RPCs for certification of IntraState
lines carrying Inter-State Power is not identical; NRPC certification is based on the
power flow during 2nd and 4th quarters and is valid for one year, SRPC certification
is based on the power flow in all four quarters and is valid for one year and in case of
WRPC once the line is certified as deemed ISTS based upon the study, it shall retain
the status of deemed ISTS.
41. We are of the view that due to laws of physics and the meshed network of ISTS
and STU lines, ISTS power may flow through the intra-State lines; similarly, intra-State
power may also flow through the ISTS network. We also observe that there is a defined
process of executing a line under ISTS under the Guidelines issued by MoP. Any line
envisaged as an ISTS should be constructed as an ISTS line only, following due
process. Hence, an intra-State line planned as an intra-State and executed as an intra-
State should remain as an intra-State line unless it becomes inter-State due to the
bifurcation of the State. However, a mechanism was included in the 2010 Sharing
Regulations to include intra-state lines under the ISTS pool based on certification of
respective RPC as quoted in paragraphs 32 and 33 of this Order. Such mechanism of
certification has been discontinued in the 2020 Sharing Regulations, keeping in view
these aspects.
42.Considering the certification carried out by SRPC under provisions of the Sharing
Regulations 2010 and the determination of line-wise tariff by APERC, we are of the view that
the specified lines, as per details in paragraph 24 of this Order, shall be considered under
PoC under the Sharing Regulations 2010 for the period 2015-16, 2016-17 and 2020-21 (up
to 30.10.2020). Accordingly, we direct the implementing agency/CTUIL to include the lines
as per details in paragraph 24 under POC for the period 2015-16, 2016-17, and 2020-21 (up
to 30.10.2020) and raise bills accordingly. Accordingly, the liabilities of DICs for arrears of
transmission charges shall be recovered from the concerned DICs through Bills under
Regulation 15(2)(b) of the 2020 Sharing Regulations. We observe that once the transmission
charges of non-ISTS lines are included in the ISTS pool, the availability of such lines needs
to be verified by the respective RPC, and recovery of tariff should be linked with its
availability, for which necessary mechanisms may be put in place by RPC. We direct that
YTC of such intra-State lines shall be included in the PoC Pool based on the availability of
each of the lines to be certified by the SRPC in terms of the provisions under the CERC
Order in Petition No. 183/MP/2021 26

(Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2014 and CERC (Terms and Conditions of
Tariff) Regulations, 2019, as applicable.
……
Issue No.2: Whether the petitioner is entitled to include transmission charges determined by
the APERC for non-ISTS lines certified by SRPC to carry inter-state power for the period
01.11.2020 to 31.12.2020 in the PoC mechanism as per the Sharing Regulations, 2010?
45.Petitioner has claimed to include the non-ISTS lines under the PoC pool under the
Sharing Regulations 2010 till 31.12.2020, citing Regulation 22 of the Sharing Regulation
2020, which provides that during the transition period between the former of 2010 and the
new Sharing Regulations, the bills raised for the first two billing periods after 01.11.2020,
i.e., till 31.12.2020, shall be as per the Sharing Regulations 2010. Petitioner further
submitted that this has been further clarified by the Commission, vide Removal of Difficulties
Order dated 14.02.2021.
…………….
As per the above, the Commission vide order dated 14.02.2021 vide Order No.
L1/250/2019/CERC has clarified that the bills raised in the months of November 2020 and
December 2020 shall be based on the notified PoC rates for October 2020 and November
2020, respectively. The Commission clarified that bills raised “in the month of November
2020 and December 2020” shall be as per notified POC rates and not that Sharing
Regulations 2010 was applicable for the period of November 2020 and December 2020. The
Commission explained that bills for the billing period of November 2020 and December 2020
could be raised by CTU only in the billing month of January 2021 and February 2021,
respectively, based on the computation carried out in December 2020 and January 2021 in
terms of the Sharing Regulations 2020. Accordingly, the Commission directed that the bills
raised in January 2021 onwards, which shall be for the billing period of November 2020 and
onwards, shall be as per the Sharing Regulations 2020.
48. Considering the above, we don’t agree with the Petitioner’s claim that it is entitled to the
inclusion of non-ISTS lines certified by SRPC for the period from 1.11.2020 to 31.12.2020
when the Sharing Regulations 2020 became effective. The Petitioner shall be entitled to
include the non-ISTS Lines under POC for FY 2020-21 as directed in Issue No.1 for the
period up to 31.10.2020. Therefore, we reject the petitioner’s claim to include the YTC of the
intra-State lines used for carrying ISTSPower in the PoC Pool for the period from 01.11.2020
to 31.12.2020.”
As per the above transmission tariff for the period 1.4.2020-31.10.2020, it was allowed
to be recovered, and for the period 1.11.2020-31.12.2020, based on the 2010 Sharing
regulations, it was not accepted.
43. We note that the Sharing Regulations 2020 became effective from 1.11.2020, which
provides as under:
“2. Definitions
1.
ee) ‘Yearly Transmission Charges’ or ‘YTC’ means the annual transmission charges as
determined or adopted by the Commission for the transmission elements of ISTS which have
achieved COD upto the last day of a billing period, and for intra-State transmission lines
used for inter-State transmission of electricity as approved by the Commission
….
13
(13) An intra-State transmission system for which tariff is approved by the Commission shall
be included for sharing of transmission charges of DICs in accordance with Regulations 5 to
8 of these regulations, only for the period for which such tariff has been approved.”
Order in Petition No. 183/MP/2021 27

44. Statement of Reasons under the Sharing Regulation, 2020 states the following:
“39. Clause (12) of Draft Regulation 11
39.1 The draft Regulation provided as under: “(12) An Intra-State Transmission System
already certified by the respective Regional Power Committees being used for inter-State
transmission of electricity and for which tariff has already been approved by the Commission,
shall be covered under these Regulations: Provided that such intra-State Transmission
System shall be included under these Regulations only for the tariff period for which tariff
has already been approved by this Commission.”
39.2 Comments have been received from ATL, L&T IDPL, HPPTCL, SRPC, TANGEDCO,
GUVNL and APPCC.
39.2.1 SRPC has suggested that a new proviso may be added as under: ‘Incentive for Intra-
state lines will be considered by CTU based on the Availability certificate issued by
respective SLDC within a month, else no incentive will be considered. RPCs to follow 50%
criteria for certification of Intra-state lines as ISTS lines. RPC shall certify the Non-ISTS lines
with the above criteria for a year based on the base case furnished by NLDC for the peak
ISTS drawal for the previous year.’
39.2.2 SRPC has also suggested that certification of intra-State lines needs to be carried out
by respective SLDCs. No post facto inclusion of intra-State lines should be allowed. If a
region is following 50% criteria while other regions are following 10% criteria, more lines of
10% criteria would be included in AC-UBC and other regions would be burdened with
additional usage component. Therefore, uniform criterion need to be specified by the
Commission.
39.3 Analysis and Decision
39.3.1 The rationale for the proposed Clause was provided in the Explanatory Memorandum
issued along with the Draft 2019 Sharing Regulations. Such intra-State systems that have
already been certified by RPC as being used for inter-State use and for which tariff has
already been approved by the Commission shall be covered under these Regulations.
39.3.2 Approval of tariff for intra-State system is done by SERCs. However, in circumstances
where an intra-State system is used for inter-State flow of power, its tariff is required to be
approved by CERC, if such system is to be considered for recovery of transmission charges
under the 2020 Sharing Regulations.”
45. In the Explanatory Memorandum dated 3.12.2019 for Draft Sharing Regulations, the
following was mentioned regarding Intra-state lines certified by RPC:
“2.7 Intra-state lines certified by RPC
(ii) Jha Committee has observed regarding inclusion of intra-state lines certified by RPC
under ISTS pool as follows:
“Intra-state transmission lines certified by respective Regional Power Committee being used
for inter-State transmission: Intra-state system is generally planned for transfer of power
within the State. Similarly adequate inter-state system has generally been planned for
transfer of inter-state power. Under this situation, if intra-state system carries inter-state
power or vice versa it is basically due to meshed network. Further, it is observed that such
assets are already being included in ARR of the State system. As such, it is not appropriate
to include such intrastate system under ISTS on the basis of load flow. Further since AC
system has been divided into “AC-UBC” and “AC-BC” and as per simulations, only a portion
of lines shall be included under “AC-UBC”. Hence it would not be appropriate to allocate
charges of such system under “balance component” on other DICs. It is suggested that such
systems should be included for recovery under these Regulations only for the tariff period
Order in Petition No. 183/MP/2021 28

for which tariff has already been approved by this Commission as on date of notification of
these Regulations. No intra-state transmission system other than the one already included
that too for the period for which tariff has already been approved shall be considered for
allocation of transmission charges under ISTS.”
Accordingly, it is proposed at regulation 11(12) as follows:
“An Intra-State Transmission System already certified by the respective Regional Power
Committees being used for inter-State transmission of electricity and for which tariff has
already been approved by the Commission, shall be covered under these Regulations:
Provided that such intra-State Transmission System shall be included under these
Regulations only for the tariff period for which tariff has already been approved by this
Commission.”
46. The Commission, vide order dated 04.05.2023 in Petition No. 57/MP/2022, filed by
the H.P. Power Transmission Corporation Limited (HPPTCL) for a similar issue, has
held that the intra-State line of HP cannot be considered as an Inter-State line and it
continues to be an intra-State line under the jurisdiction of the State. Relevant extract
of the order dated 04.05.2023 in Petition No. 57/MP/2022 are as under:
“22. The Electricity Act 2003 lays down the framework of transmission system development
in our Country as divided into intra-State transmission and inter-State transmission. The
responsibility of development of inter-State transmission system lies with CTU, while the
development of intra-State transmission system with STU. Inter-State transmission system
is planned by CTU for evacuation and transmission of interstate power after consultation
with CEA and the concerned RPC, and mode of implementation of inter-state transmission
system is either Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) route or Regulated Tariff
Mechanism (RTM) route, as decided by the committee constituted by MOP, Govt. of India.
However, there are some transmission lines connecting the systems of two neighboring
states which have been constructed over the years by concerned States under bilateral
arrangement or the intra-state lines converted into inter-state lines due to bifurcation of a
State. Such transmission lines connecting two states are eligible as inter-State lines under
Section 36(i) of the Act and they are being approved by the Commission as inter-State
transmission system upon application by the Concerned States. Commission had also
introduced identification of intra-State transmission lines as inter-State based on load flow
under Sharing Regulations, 2010. However, load flow varies in a transmission system on
continuous basis depending on the load-generation balance scenarios. A transmission
system planned as intra-State transmission system cannot be termed as inter-State for one
month and then intra-State for another month. There are cases where intrastate power flows
through inter-State lines where such inter-State lines cannot be declared as intra-State.
Since the network is meshed, it is not appropriate to identify an intra-State transmission
system as inter-State and levy its transmission charges on beneficiaries of other States.
23. We have considered both the planning aspect of subject transmission line as well as
load flow data submitted by NRLDC. As far as planning is concerned, the subject
transmission line has been planned as intra-State transmission line on insistence of
Petitioner which is STU of Himachal Pradesh keeping in view of potential development of
intra-state hydro projects. Petitioner has not submitted anything on record to substantiate
that what has changed from the day of planning, when this transmission line was envisaged
and constructed as Intra-State, that now it is being proposed as Inter-State. It is observed
from the power flow data submitted by NRLDC that the power flow on the instant line reduces
during the winter months while the power flow is maximum during the summer months and
% utilisation by H.P. for the said line is also varying over the months from 11% to 98%.
Order in Petition No. 183/MP/2021 29

Further for the Period July Sept. 2021 (2nd quarter) and January-March 2022 (4th Quarter),
the average % utilization by H.P. works out to be 53% which is more than 50% within the
State:
……………..
24. In view of the above discussions, the instant line cannot be considered as InterState line
and it continues to be an intra-State line under jurisdiction of the State Commission.
Accordingly, the prayers of the petitioner are rejected.”
47. We have perused the details of the utilisation of 42 lines claimed by the Petitioner for
carrying inter-state power as furnished by SRLDC. A sample of data is produced
below:

As per the above, it is observed that the GAZUWAKA2-KALPAKKA1 line has an actual
flow of 76 MW out of its thermal limit of 874 MW. Out of 76 MW, ~97% power is going
outside the state, showing a % utilisation of ISTS as 97%. Whether the tariff for such
a line, which was planned as an intra-state line, is to be recovered from all India DICs
on the basis of 76 MW of power, is required to be decided in the instant case.
48. We note that the Electricity Act 2003 lays down the framework of transmission system
development in our Country as divided into intra-State transmission and inter-State
transmission. The responsibility for the development of the inter-State transmission
system lies with CTU, while the development of the intra-State transmission system
lies with STU. Inter-State transmission system is planned by CTU for evacuation and
transmission of interstate power after consultation with CEA and the concerned RPC,
and the mode of implementation of the inter-state transmission system is either Tariff
Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) route or Regulated Tariff Mechanism (RTM) route,
as decided by the committee constituted by MOP, Govt. of India. The Commission
had also introduced the identification of intra-State transmission lines as inter-State
based on load flow under the Sharing Regulations, 2010. However, load flow varies
in a transmission system on a continuous basis depending on the load-generation
balance. A transmission system planned as an intra-State transmission system cannot
be termed as inter-State for one month and then intra-State for another month. As
quoted in Para 44 of this Order vide the Explanatory Memorandum dated 3.12.2019,
in case intra-state power flows through inter-State lines, it is due to the meshed
network and such inter-State lines are not declared as intra-State with charges of such
inter-state systems levied entirely on a particular state (as intra-state network).
49. We have also noted in the sample case above that an intra-state line being utilised for
as low as 9% is being proposed to be qualified as interstate with charges on all INDIA
DICs, since out of 9% utilization, 97% power was going outside the state.
50. In light of the above discussions, about data for load flow of 2020-21 which reveals
low utilisation vis a vis the capacity of intra-state lines proposed to be used as inter-
state, and the fact that since the network is meshed an intra-State transmission system
may qualify as inter-State based on load flow for one year which may get disqualified
next year due to changing load flow, the provisions of the Act on clear segregation of
ISTS and intra-state as detailed in Para 48 of this Order, we are of the considered
Order in Petition No. 183/MP/2021 31

view that the lines proposed by the Petitioner cannot be considered as inter-state and
its charges cannot be levied on beneficiaries of other States.
51. On the issue of submission of Petitioner regarding annual mechanism requiring
SRLDC to provide yearly load flow data for intra-State transmission lines, we note that
under Tariff Regulations, 2024, a methodology has been provided to identify such
intra-state lines where such a nature of flow of power has become permanent to be
certified by CEA based on recommendations and consultations with RPC, STU, RLDC
and CTU. In case any of Petitioner’s intra-state lies qualify under such criterion, it may
follow due process in accordance with the Tariff Regulations, 2024, for the period
beyond 1.4.2024.
52. In light of the above, all prayers of the Petitioner stand rejected.
53. Petition No. 183/MP/2021 is disposed of in terms of the above.

(1) The additional capital expenditure in respect of a new project or an existing

(a) Undischarged liabilities recognized to be payable at a future date;

(c) Procurement of initial capital spares within the original scope of work, in
accordance with the provisions of Regulation 23 of these regulations;
(d) Liabilities to meet award of arbitration or for compliance of the

(c) Deferred works relating to ash pond or ash handling system in the

admitted by the Commission, after making necessary adjustments in the

the energy bills raised by the Petitioner on the basis of the scheduled energy to be
certified at point D by Gujarat SLDC which is the delivery point in terms of the RfS and
PPA provisions.
And in the matter of:
SJVN Green Energy Limited
Corporate Office Complex
Shakti Sadan, Shanan, Shimla -171006
……Petitioner

Sardar Patel Vidyut Bhawan,

2. Gujarat Energy Transmission Corporation Limited (GETCO),
State Load Despatch Centre,
Gotri Road, Gotri, Vadodara-3900021
3. State Load Dispatch Centre (SLDC), Gujarat
132kV Gotri Sub Station Compound, Gotri Road
Vadodara, Gujarat-3900021 … Respondent(s)
Parties Present: Ms. Anushree Bardhan, Advocate, SJVNGEL
Ms. Ritika Singh, Advocate, SJVNGEL

Shri Utkarsh Singh, Advocate, GUVNL & GSLDC
Ms. Sneha Singh, Advocate, GUVNL & GSLDC
Order in Petition No. 548/MP/2025 Page 1

ORDER
SJVN Green Energy Limited (hereinafter referred to as ‘Petitioner’/ ‘SGEL’) has
filed the present Petition seeking adjudication of a dispute regarding the delivery point for
the scheduled energy in terms of the RfS, PPA, Implementation and Support Agreement
and the Tripartite Connection Agreement. The Petitioner has also sought direction to the
Gujarat SLDC to amend the monthly State Energy Account from April 2024 onwards, and
to GUVNL to make payments on the basis of the revised monthly State Energy Account
from April 2024 onwards, along with interest/carrying costs. The Petitioner has made the
following prayers:
(a) Hold and declare that point D in the above line diagram is the delivery point for the scheduled
energy in terms of the RfS, PPA, Implementation and Support Agreement and the Tripartite
Connection Agreement. Furthermore, hold and declare that point D is also the GETCO
periphery i.e. point of interconnection between CTU Grid and Gujarat STU Grid for all intent
and purposes;
(b) Hold and Declare that GUVNL ought to make payment towards the energy bills raised by the
Petitioner on the basis of the scheduled energy to be certified at point D by Gujarat SLDC;
(c) Direct Gujarat SLDC to amend the monthly State Energy Account from April 2024 onwards
on the basis of Point D as the delivery point and direct GUVNL to make payment on the basis
of the revised monthly State Energy Account from April 2024 onwards along with
interest/carrying cost till the final discharge of the outstanding balance amount;
(d) Pass such other Order(s) and this Hon’ble Commission may deem just and proper in the
circumstances of the case.
The line diagram, as mentioned in the prayer, is at Para No. 1(h) of this Order.
Submissions of the Petitioner:
1. The Petitioner has mainly submitted as follows:
(a) On 15.03.2021, GUVNL issued a Request for Selection (‘RfS’) for the procurement
of power from 100 MW Solar Projects to be developed in the 700 MW Raghanesda
Solar Park through a competitive bidding process. The Petitioner was declared the
successful bidder at the tariff of Rs. 2.64/unit.
(b) On 03.01.2022, GUVNL entered into a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) with the
Petitioner for the 100 MW Solar PV project to be developed at 700 MW Raghanesda
Solar Park. Thereafter, on 16.01.2023, GUVNL entered into a Supplementary PPA
with the Petitioner.
Order in Petition No. 548/MP/2025 Page 2

(c) On 19.06.2023, the Petitioner entered into an Implementation and Support
Agreement (ISA) with the Gujarat Power Corporation Limited (GPCL) (i.e. the Solar
Power Park Developer for the facilitation and implementation of the 700 MW
Raghanesda Solar Park).
(d) On 20.07.2023, the Petitioner entered into a Connection Agreement with GETCO and
GPCL for establishing connectivity of the 700 MW solar power park project with the
GETCO 220 kV Raghanesda Substation.
(e) The Commercial Operation Date of the Petitioner’s 100 MW project was achieved on
02.04.2024 for 75 MW, and the residual 25 MW was commissioned on 20.09.2024.
(f) A schematic diagram of the Project is as under: -
(g) As per PPA dated 03.01.2022, the Petitioner at its own cost laid the 33 kV cables
from the 100 MW project up to the low voltage side of the 33 kV/220 kV internal
Pooling Substation of GETCO. Thereafter, from the 33 kV/ 220 kV GETCO Pooling
Substation, a 220-kV line under the scope of GETCO connects to the 220 kV/400 kV
Khimnawas Substation of CTU, which is the metering point.
(h) Section 2.1 of the PPA mentions that the Delivery Point shall be the point of inter-
connection between CTU Grid and Gujarat STU Grid, i.e. GETCO Periphery, at which
Electricity shall be delivered. The PPA further provides that GUVNL will pay to the
Order in Petition No. 548/MP/2025 Page 3

Solar Power Developer (SPD) for the delivered energy (which is the electricity actually
scheduled at the delivery point as certified by Gujarat SLDC in the State Energy
Account in accordance with provisions of the supplemental PPA, based on energy
certified by WRPC under the Regional Energy Account).
(i) The Clause 3(k) of the ISA provides that the “Inter-connection point or Delivery Point”
shall mean the 220/400 kV Sub-station of CTU and that all line losses up to Delivery
point as per PPA will be on account of the Solar Power Developers (SPDs); Clause
6.5(a) provides that Inter-connection point or Delivery Point shall mean the point at
220 kV side of 220/400 kV Sub-station of CTU and the Clause 8.8 provides that
Metering shall be at 33 kV side of 220/33 kV Substation where the power from the
solar power project is injected and at the 220 kV Side of 400/220 kV Substation of
CTU. Further, the 5th point of Clause 8.8 provides that both sets of meters are used
for billing purposes and to measure the transmission losses up to the interconnection
point.
(j) A conjoint reading of the RfS, PPA, ISA and the Tripartite Connection Agreement
shows that the low voltage bus-bar point (i.e. 220 kV) of 220 kV/400 kV Khimnawas
sub-station of CTU is the delivery point for the scheduled energy from the 100 MW
project of the Petitioner and is the GETCO periphery, i.e. point of interconnection
between CTU Grid and Gujarat STU Grid for all intents and purposes. Thus, the
interconnection Point, the Metering Point (at the 220 kV side of 220 kV/400 kV
Substation) and the Delivery Point, as dealt with in the above documents, are the
same point.
(k) In view of the terms of the RfS, PPA, ISA and the connection agreement, the payment
of charges at the tariff of Rs. 2.64/unit by GUVNL for the delivered energy is at Point
D in the above diagram (to be certified by Gujarat SLDC, in accordance with
provisions of PPA, based on energy certified by WRPC under Regional Energy
Account).
(l) Upon supply of power from the commercial operation date on 02.04.2024 from the
100 MW project, the Petitioner raised an invoice dated 03.05.2024 on GUVNL based
on the scheduled energy as per the Regional Energy Account issued by WRPC
(issued in terms of the CERC (Terms and Conditions of Tariff), Regulations, 2024)
for the period from 03.04.2024 to 30.04.2024 amounting to Rs. 3.44 Crores.
Order in Petition No. 548/MP/2025 Page 4

(m) GUVNL raised the issue that payment to the Petitioner will be made for the delivered
energy as certified in the State Energy Account by Gujarat SLDC- GETCO.
Thereafter, a revised bill was raised on 29.05.2024 for the period from 03.04.2024 to
30.04.2024, corresponding to the delivered energy as certified in the State Energy
Account by Gujarat SLDC- GETCO, amounting to Rs. 3.32 Crores.
(n) The Petitioner has been raising bills on GUVNL for the energy certified in the State
Energy Account by Gujarat SLDC- GETCO.
(o) Upon analysing the delivered energy as certified in the State Energy Account by
Gujarat SLDC- GETCO, and as there was a difference of Rs.12.19 Lacs in the total
billed amount for the power supplied from the period from 03.04.2024 to 30.04.2024,
the Petitioner concluded that the same was on account of a mismatch in the
consideration of the delivery point.
(p) Evidently, the units recorded in the State Energy Account issued by Gujarat SLDC-
GETCO are not at Point D, which is the interconnection Point, the Metering Point (at
the 220 kV side of 220 kV/400 kV Substation) and the Delivery Point in terms of the
RfS, PPA, Implementation and Support Agreement and the Tripartite Connection
Agreement.
(q) On 04.12.2024, the Petitioner sent an email to Gujarat SLDC - GETCO requesting
clarification on the losses, along with an Excel sheet detailing the incurred losses. On
23.01.2025, the Petitioner wrote a letter to Gujarat SLDC – GETCO with a copy
marked to GUVNL requesting an amendment of the Energy Accounts from April
2024.
(r) On 28.01.2025, Gujarat SLDC – GETCO replied to the above letter and as per the
Gujarat SLDC, the delivery points are Point H1, H2 and H3 in the above line diagram.
(s) The delivery point (H1, H2 and H3) for the scheduled energy in the energy bills on
the basis of the State Energy Account generated by Gujarat SLDC- GETCO does not
align with the meaning of delivered energy as per the supplemental PPA which is the
energy scheduled at the delivery point as certified by Gujarat SLDC in State Energy
Account in accordance with provisions of PPA, based on energy certified by WRPC
under Regional Energy Account.
Order in Petition No. 548/MP/2025 Page 5

(t) Due to the mismatch of the delivery point and delivered energy, the Petitioner has
suffered financially to the tune of Rs 1.24 Crore till December 2024.
(u) On 10.02.2025 & 04.03.2025, the Petitioner wrote to GUVNL, to which No Response
has been received from GUVNL to date.
(v) A dispute has arisen between the Petitioner and GUVNL as GUVNL is not making
payments to the Petitioner in terms of the power scheduled at point D, which is the

A) The applicant has applied to the STU-GETCO for connectivity of 700 MW

C) The parties have entered into this Connection Agreement to record the terms

resulting in financial losses to the GETCO will be as per GERC Regulations for
this Agreement. Similarly, for the regular O&M of the connection equipment's
owned by the applicant and located in the STU premises / switchyard and line the
parties shall separately take up the O& M agreement on mutually agreed terms
and conditions. Indemnification of each other against losses incurred in this
regards, and form a part of this agreement.

5.0 Site Access
5.1 Being restricted area the STU may give permission or allow access to GPCL (being
SPPD will ensure that Solar Power Developers will get this access) employees in the
GETCO's 220Kv Raghanesda substation premises to carry out preliminary site
investigation works, the Connection works modification works inspections, etc. based on
a written request by the GPCL (being SPPD will ensure that Solar Power Developers will
make a written request) as deemed fit. All such actions are to be carried out under the
strict supervision of the STU's authorized representative to safeguard the safety and
security, requirements of STU's installations and safety of the representatives of the
applicant or State transmission licensee.
Similarly, the GPCL being SPPD will ensure that Solar Power Developers shall also allow,
on prior permission, site access to the STU's employees to carryout preliminary site
Investigation works, inspections, etc. in the connection site of the GPCL (being SPPD will
ensure that Solar Power Developers shall allow such access) as deemed fit.
5.2 Conditions of access
Site access at 220KV Raghanesda Substation of GETCO shall include the right to bring
such vehicles, plant, machinery and construction materials as shall be reasonably
necessary to carry out the function in respect of which the permission of access is granted.
Being a restricted area, any individual to whom access is given under the Agreement shall
comply with all reasonable directions given by the GPCL being SPPD will ensure that
Solar Power Developers/ STU (GETCO) and its appropriately authorized employees and
agents to safe guard the Interest of safety and security requirements of personnel and
equipment. All such access shall be exercisable without payment of any kind.”
As per above, it is noted that the internal 33 kV/220 kV substation of GPCL-SPPD
has been established by GETCO, and accordingly, GETCO is also a signatory to this
connection agreement as the Petitioner is connecting to the Pooling station owned
by GETCO.
25. Respondent, GUVNL, has submitted that the 33/220 kV Pooling Substation at
Raghanesda is not the STU system, but is a pooling substation of the park developer.
GETCO undertook the construction of the said sub-station.
26. It is noted that the ISA dated 19.6.2023 between Petitioner and SPPD-GPCL
provides for payment of one-time charges for the 33/220 kV internal Pooling station
of GPCL. The ISA nowhere mentions that such a 33/220 kV Pooling station is owned
and operated by GETCO. At the same time, the Connection Agreement dated
20.6.2023 (the next day to ISA) provides 33/220 kV pooling s/s as that of GETCO.
27. We have perused the RFS, PPA, ISA and the Connection Agreement. We are of the
considered view that the liability of payment of the charges by GUVNL is governed
as per the PPA and the definition of delivered energy as per PPA, which is “energy
Order in Petition No. 548/MP/2025 Page 22

scheduled at the delivery point as certified by Gujarat SLDC in State Energy Account
in accordance with provisions of PPA, based on energy certified by WRPC under
Regional Energy Account.” Mere construction of an internal pooling station of SPPD-
GPCL by GETCO does not shift the delivery point of energy agreed upon between
Petitioner and GUVNL.
28. We do not agree to the contention of the Petitioner that since the 33 kV/220 kV
Pooling Substation, along with the 220 kV transmission line, is owned and operated
by the GETCO, point D is the delivery point as well as the GETCO Periphery. The
aforesaid submissions of the Petitioner are contrary to the provisions of the PPA as
well as the ISA, which provides that the 33 kV / 220 kV PS and 220 kV Transmission
lines up to 220 kV/400 kV Khimanawas Pooling Substation were under the scope of
GPCL.
29. In view of the above discussions, we are of the considered view that the 33 kV / 220
KV PS and 220 kV Transmission lines up to 220 kV/400 kV Khimanawas Pooling
Substation is an internal system of GPCL-SPPD for transmission of electricity up to
the 220 kV/400 kV Khimanawas Pooling Substation, which is the inter-connection
point of the Petitioner’s project with the CTU grid in terms of the PPA. The scheduled
energy is to be worked out as ‘delivered energy’ under the PPA, in terms of the State
Energy Account, by Gujarat SLDC. Accordingly, the prayer of the Petitioner to declare
point D as the delivery point is not acceded to. All other prayers are accordingly
addressed as not acceded to.
30. The Petition No. 548/MP/2025 is disposed of in terms of the above.

ORDER
This Petition has been filed by the Petitioner, NHPC Limited, for truing-up of
the tariff of Dulhasti Power Station (390 MW) (in short “the generating station”) for the
period 2019-24, in accordance with the provisions of the Central Electricity Regulatory
Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2019 (in short, ‘the 2019
Tariff Regulations”) and for determination of the tariff of the generating station for the
period 2024-29, in accordance with the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission
(“Terms and Conditions of Tariff”) Regulations, 2024 (in short “the 2024 Tariff
Regulations”). The generating station with a total capacity of 390 MW comprises three
units of 130 MW each and is located in the UT of Jammu & Kashmir. All three units of
the generating station were declared under commercial operation on 7.4.2007.

“19. Capital Cost:
(1) The Capital cost of the generating station or the transmission system, as the case may be,
as determined by the Commission after prudence check in accordance with these Regulations
shall form the basis for determination of Tariff for existing and new projects.
(2) The Capital Cost of a new project shall include the following:
(a) The expenditure incurred or projected to be incurred up to the date of commercial operation
of the project;
(b) Interest during construction and financing charges, on the loans
(i) being equal to 70% of the funds deployed, in the event of the actual equity in excess of 30%
of the funds deployed, by treating the excess equity as normative loan, or
(ii) being equal to the actual amount of loan in the event of the actual equity less than 30% of
the funds deployed;
(c) Any gain or loss on account of foreign exchange risk variation pertaining to the loan amount
availed during the construction period;
(d) Interest during construction and incidental expenditure during construction as computed in
accordance with these Regulations;
(e) Capitalised initial spares subject to the ceiling rates in accordance with these Regulations;
(f) Expenditure on account of additional capitalization and de-capitalisation determined in
accordance with these Regulations;
(g) Adjustment of revenue due to sale of infirm power in excess of fuel cost prior to the date of
commercial operation as specified under Regulation 7 of these Regulations;
(h) Adjustment of revenue earned by the transmission licensee by using the assets before the
date of commercial operation;
(i) Capital expenditure on account of ash disposal and utilization including handling and
transportation facility;
(j) Capital expenditure incurred towards railway infrastructure and its augmentation for
transportation of coal upto the receiving end of the generating station but does not include the
transportation cost and any other appurtenant cost paid to the railway;
(k) Capital expenditure on account of biomass handling equipment and facilities, for co-firing;
(l) Capital expenditure on account of emission control system necessary to meet the revised
emission standards and sewage treatment plant;
(m) Expenditure on account of fulfilment of any conditions for obtaining environment clearance
for the project;
(n) Expenditure on account of change in law and force majeure events; and
(o) Capital cost incurred or projected to be incurred by a thermal generating station, on account
of implementation of the norms under Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme of
Government of India shall be considered by the Commission subject to sharing of benefits
accrued under the PAT scheme with the beneficiaries.
(3) The Capital cost of an existing project shall include the following:
(a) Capital cost admitted by the Commission prior to 1.4.2019 duly trued up by excluding
liability, if any, as on 1.4.2019;
(b) Additional capitalization and de-capitalization for the respective year of Tariff as determined
in accordance with these Regulations;
(c) Capital expenditure on account of renovation and modernisation as admitted by this
Commission in accordance with these Regulations;
(d) Capital expenditure on account of ash disposal and utilization including handling and
transportation facility;

(e)Capital expenditure incurred towards railway infrastructure and its augmentation for
transportation of coal upto the receiving end of generating station but does not include the
transportation cost and any other appurtenant cost paid to the railway;
(f) and Capital cost incurred or projected to be incurred by a thermal generating station, on
account of implementation of the norms under Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme of
Government of India shall be considered by the Commission subject to sharing of benefits
accrued under the PAT scheme with the beneficiaries.
(4) The capital cost in case of existing or new hydro generating station shall also include:
(a) cost of approved rehabilitation and resettlement (R&R) plan of the project in conformity with
National R&R Policy and R&R package as approved; and
(b) cost of the developer’s 10% contribution towards Rajiv Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran
Yojana (RGGVY) and Deendayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY) project in the
affected area.
(5) The following shall be excluded from the capital cost of the existing and new projects:
(a) The assets forming part of the project, but not in use, as declared in the Tariff petition;
(b) De-capitalised Assets after the date of commercial operation on account of replacement or
removal on account of obsolescence or shifting from one project to another project: Provided
that in case replacement of transmission asset is recommended by Regional Power
Committee, such asset shall be decapitalised only after its redeployment; Provided further that
unless shifting of an asset from one project to another is of permanent nature, there shall be
no de-capitalization of the concerned assets.
(c) In case of hydro generating stations, any expenditure incurred or committed to be incurred
by a project developer for getting the project site allotted by the State Government by following
a transparent process;
(d) Proportionate cost of land of the existing project which is being used for generating power
from generating station based on renewable energy; and
(e) Any grant received from the Central or State Government or any statutory body or authority
for the execution of the project which does not carry any liability of repayment.”
9. Clause (1) of Regulation 19 of the 2019 Tariff Regulations provides that the
capital cost as determined by the Commission, after a prudence check, in accordance
with the Regulation, shall form the basis of the determination of the tariff of existing
and new projects. The Commission vide its order dated 9.5.2022 in Petition No.
146/GT/2020, had approved the capital cost of Rs. 522037.61 lakh, as on 31.3.2019.
Accordingly, in terms of Regulation 19(1) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations, the capital
cost of Rs. 522037.61 lakh has been considered as the opening capital cost, as on
1.4.2019, for the purposes of truing up the tariff of the generating station, for the period
2019-24.

Additional Capital Expenditure
10. Clauses (1) and (2) of Regulation 25 and clause (1) of Regulation 26 of the 2019
Tariff Regulations provide as under:
“25. Additional Capitalisation within the original scope and after the cut – off date:
(1) The additional capital expenditure incurred or projected to be incurred in respect of an
existing project or a new project on the following counts within the original scope of work and
after the cut-off date may be admitted by the Commission, subject to prudence check:
(a) Liabilities to meet award of arbitration or for compliance of the directions or order of any
statutory authority, or order or decree of any court of law;
(b) Change in law or compliance of any existing law;
(c) Deferred works relating to ash pond or ash handling system in the original scope of work;
(d) Liability for works executed prior to the cut-off date;
(e) Force Majeure events;
(f) Liability for works admitted by the Commission after the cut-off date to the extent of
discharge of such liabilities by actual payments; and
(g) Raising of ash dyke as a part of ash disposal system.
(2) In case of replacement of assets deployed under the original scope of the existing project
after cut – off date, the additional capitalisation may be admitted by the Commission, after
making necessary adjustments in the gross fixed assets and the cumulated depreciation,
subject to prudence check on the following grounds:
(a) The replacement of the assets or equipment is necessary on account of change in law or
Force Majeure conditions;
(b) The replacement of such assets or equipment is necessary on account of obsolescence of
technology; and
(c) The replacement of such assets or equipment has otherwise been allowed by the
Commission.
26. Additional Capitalisation beyond the original scope
(1) The capital expenditure, in respect of existing generating station or the transmission system
including communication system, incurred or projected to be incurred on the following counts

(a) Liabilities to meet award of arbitration or for compliance of order or directions of any
statutory authority, or order or decree of any court of law;
(b) Change in law or compliance of any existing law;
(c) Force Majeure events;
(d) Need for higher security and safety of the plant as advised or directed by appropriate Indian
Government Instrumentality or statutory authorities responsible for national or internal security;
(e) Deferred works relating to ash pond or ash handling system in additional to the original
scope of work, on case-to-case basis:
Provided also that of any expenditure has been claimed under Renovation and Maintenance
(R&M) or repairs and maintenance under O&M expenses, the same shall not be claimed under
these Regulations;
