Parties present:
Shri Hemant Singh, Advocate, GTPL
ORDER
The Petitioner, Greennsure Trading Private Limited (hereinafter referred to
as ‘the Petitioner’), incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013, read with Regulation
6 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions
for the Grant of Trading Licence and other related matters) Regulations, 2020
(hereinafter referred to as “the Trading Licence Regulations”), amended from time to
time, has filed the present Petition for the grant of a Category ‘V’ trading licence for
inter-State trading in electricity in all over India.
Order in Petition No. 46/TD/2026
Page 1 of 8

Hearing Dated 3.2.2026
2. During the course of the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner
submitted that the Petitioner company has complied with the requirements of the
Trading Licence Regulations and requested the trading licence be granted. The
Petitioner, vide Record of Proceedings (hereinafter referred to as “RoP’) for the
hearing dated 3.2.2026, was directed to submit the details of engagement of full-time
professional(s) with qualification in Finance, Commerce and Accounts, i.e.
CA/ICWA/MBA (Finance) with a minimum of five years’ experience, with all supporting
details, including resumes, qualification certificates, and proof of full-time engagement
of the concerned professional(s) in terms of Regulation 3(2) of the Trading Licence
Regulations, 2020.
3. In compliance with the RoP dated 3.2.2026, the Petitioner vide its affidavit dated
10.2.2026 has furnished the information regarding full-time professional(s).
4. We have perused the documents available on record. Regulation 6 of the
Trading Licence Regulations provides for the procedure for the grant of a trading
licence as under:
“6. Procedure for grant of licence
(1) Any person desirous of undertaking inter-State trading in electricity shall
make an application to the Commission for grant of licence in the manner
specified in Form-I appended to these regulations and such application shall be
accompanied by-
(a) Such application fee as prescribed by the Central Government from
time to time and shall be paid as per the procedure specified in Central
Electricity Regulatory Commission (Payment of Fees) Regulations,
2012, as amended from time to time or any statutory re-enactment
thereof.
Order in Petition No. 46/TD/2026
Page 2 of 8

(b) Copies of the annual reports in case of the persons incorporated
under the Companies Act, 1956 or Companies Act, 2013 including
audited accounts along with the Directors' Report, Auditors' Report, the
Schedules and notes to accounts for one Year immediately preceding
the Year in which the application has been made and the audited special
balance sheet as on any date falling within 30 days immediately
preceding the date of filing the application.
(2) The Applicant shall post complete application along with annexures and
enclosures on its website so as to facilitate access to the application by any
person through internet and shall keep them on the website till the disposal of
the application.
(3) The Applicant shall within 7 days after making such application, publish a
notice of its application, in two daily newspapers in Form II, with the following
particulars, namely:
************
(4) The Applicant shall within 7 days from the date of publication of the notice
as aforesaid submit to the Commission on affidavit the details of the notice
published and shall also file the original complete page of the newspaper in
which the notice has been published.
(5) The Applicant shall allow a period of 30 days to the public to file objections
or suggestions to the notice of application published in the newspapers.
(6) The Applicant shall file its reply before the Commission within 30 days from
the last date of receipt of objections or suggestions from the public.

of the five regions, in addition to publications from Delhi, including one economic daily.

21(5) of 2019 Tariff Regulations provide as follows:
“21. Interest During Construction (IDC) and Incidental Expenditure during
Construction (IEDC)
---
(4) If the delay in achieving the COD is not attributable to the generating company or
the transmission licensee, IDC and IEDC beyond SCOD may be allowed after prudence
check and the liquidated damages, if any, recovered from the contractor or supplier or
agency shall be adjusted in the capital cost of the generating station or the transmission
system, as the case may be.
(5) If the delay in achieving the COD is attributable either in entirety on in part to the
generating company or the transmission licensee or its contractor or supplier or agency,
in such cases, IDC and IEDC beyond SCOD may be disallowed after prudence check
either in entirety or on pro-rata basis corresponding to the period of delay not condoned
and the liquidated damages, if any, recovered from the contractor or supplier or agency
shall be retained by the generating company or the transmission licensee, as the case
may be.”

disallowed the IDC & IEDC on account of time overrun in respect of Asset-B1, Asset-

Capital Cost
64. Regulation 19 of the 2024 Tariff Regulations provides as follows:
“19. Capital Cost: (1) The Capital cost of the generating station or the transmission
system, as the case may be, as determined by the Commission after prudence checks
in accordance with these regulations shall form the basis for the determination of tariff
for existing and new projects.
(2) The Capital Cost of a new project shall include the following:
(a) The expenditure incurred or projected to be incurred up to the date of
commercial operation of the project;
(b) Interest during construction and financing charges, on the loans (i) being equal
to 70% of the funds deployed and, in the event actual equity is in excess of 30%
on a pari-passu basis, by treating the excess equity over and above 30% of the
funds deployed as a normative loan, or (ii) being equal to the actual amount of the
loan in the event of actual equity being less than 30% of the funds deployed;
(c) Any gain or loss on account of foreign exchange risk variation pertaining to the
loan amount availed during the construction period;
(d) Interest during construction and incidental expenditure during construction as
computed in accordance with these regulations;
(e) Capitalised initial spares subject to the ceiling rates in accordance with these
regulations;
(f) Expenditure on account of additional capitalization and de-capitalisation
determined in accordance with these regulations;
(g) Adjustment of revenue due to the sale of infirm power in excess of fuel cost
prior to the date of commercial operation as specified under Regulation 6 of these
regulations;
(h) Adjustment of revenue earned by the transmission licensee by using the assets
before the date of commercial operation;
(i) Capital expenditure on account of ash disposal and utilization including handling
and transportation facility;
(j) Capital expenditure incurred towards railway infrastructure and its augmentation
for transportation of coal up to the receiving end of the generating station but does
not include the transportation cost and any other appurtenant cost paid to the
railway;
(k) Capital expenditure on account of biomass handling equipment and facilities,
for co-firing;
(l) Capital expenditure on account of emission control system necessary to meet
the revised emission standards and sewage treatment plant;
(m) Expenditure on account of the fulfilment of any conditions for obtaining
environment clearance for the project;
(n) Expenditure on account of change in law and force majeure events; and
(o) ……..
(p) ……..

(b) Additional capitalization and de-capitalization for the respective year of tariff as

29. We have considered the Petitioner and MPPMCL’s submissions and have also
gone through the record. We observe that the entities covered under the MAT regime are
paying Income Tax as per the MAT rates notified for the respective financial year under
the IT Act, 1961, which is levied on the book profit of the entity computed as per Section
115 JB of the IT Act, 1961. Section 115 JB (2) defines book profit as net profit in the
Statement of Profit and Loss prepared in accordance with Schedule-II of the Companies
Act, 2013, subject to some additions and deductions as mentioned in the IT Act, 1961.
Since the Petitioner has been paying the MAT rates of the respective financial year, the
notified MAT rates for the respective financial year shall be considered as an effective tax
rate for the purpose of grossing up the RoE for truing up the 2019-24 tariff period in terms
of the provisions of the 2019 Tariff Regulations. Interest imposed on any additional income
tax demand as per the Assessment Order of the Income Tax Authorities shall be
considered on the actual payment. However, the penalty (for default on the part of the

The instant Petition has been filed by Power Grid Corporation of India Limited
(hereinafter referred to as the “PGCIL / the Petitioner”), a deemed transmission
licensee, for truing up of the transmission tariff for the 2019-24 tariff period under the
Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff)
Regulations, 2019 (hereinafter referred to as “the 2019 Tariff Regulations”) and the
determination of the transmission tariff under the Central Electricity Regulatory
Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2024 (hereinafter referred to
as “the 2024 Tariff Regulations”) for the 2024-29 tariff period for the Combined Asset
under “Sipat-I Transmission System” (hereinafter referred to as the “the transmission
project”) in the Western Region.
2. The Petitioner has made the following prayers in the instant Petition:

Charges, on account of Return on Equity due to change in applicable Minimum
Alternate/Corporate Income Tax rate as per the Income Tax Act, 1961 (as amended
from time to time) of the respective financial year directly without making any application
before the Commission as provided in Tariff Regulations 2019 and Tariff Regulations,
2024 as per para 15 and 16 above for respective block.

fee, and expenditure on publishing of notices in newspapers in terms of Regulation 94
(1) Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff)
Regulations, 2024, and other expenditure (if any) in relation to the filing of petition.
e) Allow the petitioner to bill and recover RLDC fees & charges and License fee
separately from the respondents in terms of Regulation 94 (3) and (4) Central Electricity
Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff Regulations, 2024).
f) Allow the petitioner to bill and adjust impact on Interest on Loan due to change in
Interest rate on account of floating rate of interest applicable during 2024-29 period, if
any, from the respondents.
g) Allow the petitioner to file a separate petition before the Commission for claiming the
overall security expenses and consequential IOWC on that security expenses as
mentioned at para 21 above.
h) Allow the petitioner to file a separate petition before the Commission for claiming the
overall insurance expenses and consequential IOWC on that insurance expenses as
mentioned at para 21 above.
i) Allow the petitioner to file a separate petition before the Commission for claiming the
overall capital spares at the end of tariff block as per actual as mentioned at Para 21

j) Allow the Petitioner to claim expenses of CTUIL borne by POWERGRID through a
separate petition as mentioned at para 22 above.

ORDER
The Petitioner, Power & Electricity Department (in short ‘PEDM’), has filed the
present petition seeking the following relief(s):
Order in Petition No. 484/MP/2024 along with IA No. 98/2024 Page 1 of 4

a) Admit the Present Petition;
b) Set aside the impugned Invoice dated 30.04.2024, for being unsustainable in law;
c) Hold and declare that the alleged demand of shortfall charges vide the Impugned
Invoice is in absolute contradiction of the contractual construct of the PPA as well
as the applicable law; and
d) Pass such further Order(s) as this Commission may deem fit in the facts and
circumstances of the present case.”
Background
2. The Petitioner had entered into a Power Purchase Agreement dated 2.7.2010
(PPA I) with the Respondent, North Eastern Electric Power Corporation Limited
(NEEPCO), for the procurement of power from the Tuirial Hydro Electric Project
situated in Kolasib district of Mizoram for a period of five years. Upon expiry of the
PPA I, the parties executed a fresh Power Purchase Agreement dated 19.4.2023 (PPA
II) to continue power supply for a further period of five years.
3. The present Petition was filed on 27.11.2024, inter alia, challenging Invoice No.
NEEPCO/MIZO/2024-25/1500/SHRTFL/01 dated 30.4.2024 raised by the
Respondent towards recovery of shortfall in energy charges for the tariff period 2019-
24. The Petitioner has also filed Interlocutory Application No. 98/2024 seeking interim
relief in the nature of a stay on the operation of the impugned invoice and restraining
the Respondent from taking any coercive action during the pendency of the Petition.
4. The dispute pertains to the Respondent’s claim for recovery of Rs. 102.07 crore
towards shortfall energy charges under Regulations 65 (7) and 65 (8) of the Central
Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2024.
The Respondent has attributed the shortfall to factors beyond its control, including
variations between maximum possible generation based on available inflows and
design energy, transmission constraints leading to energy losses, and lower
Order in Petition No. 484/MP/2024 along with IA No. 98/2024 Page 2 of 4

scheduling vis-à-vis declared capacity. The Petitioner has contested the invoice on
grounds of discrepancies in billing, absence of certified data, and alleged violation of
the PPA provisions and applicable CERC regulations. The issue has also been
deliberated in various forums, including meetings of the Commercial Sub-Committee
of the North Eastern Regional Power Committee (NERPC) under the Ministry of
Power. Subsequently, during a reconciliation meeting held on 4.10.2024, the amount
was revised to Rs. 101.21 crore.
5. The Petition was admitted on 28.11.2024, and in compliance with the directions
of the Commission, the Petitioner commenced payment of instalments as per the
impugned invoice. Subsequently, the matter was listed for hearing on 26.12.2024,
28.1.2025, 25.3.2025, 8.7.2025, 26.9.2025, 10.11.2025, and 2.1.2026, during which
the Commission directed the Petitioner to liquidate the balance of the monthly tariff
instalment payment within the stipulated trigger dates.
Hearing dated 10.2.2026
6. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that all
fifteen instalments under the impugned invoices have been paid to the Respondent,
which was duly acknowledged by the learned counsel for the Respondent. In light of
these developments, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the reliefs
sought in the present Petition no longer survive and, accordingly, sought permission
to withdraw the Petition. The learned counsel for the Respondent did not object to the
said request.
7. In view of the above submissions, the present Petition is disposed of as
‘withdrawn’.
Order in Petition No. 484/MP/2024 along with IA No. 98/2024 Page 3 of 4

8. Petition No. 484/MP/2024, along with IA No. 98/2024, is disposed of in terms
of the above.
Sd/- sd/- sd/-

Member Member Chairperson

(d) On relinquishment of full quantum of GNA by entity covered under clause (iii) of
Regulation 17.1 of these regulations, such entity shall be disconnected from the grid.
(e) Relinquishment charges shall be paid one month prior to effective date of
relinquishment failing which relinquishment shall not be effective.”
From above, in case of relinquishment of GNA, prior to the date of
effectiveness, connectivity Bank Guarantees are to be encashed.
23. CTUIL has submitted that regulatory provisions are unambiguous and Conn BGs
of Petitioner are liable to be encashed, even if it wants to continue with the same
grants. Petitioner has argued and pleaded that it should be allowed to continue
with 700 MW GNA, without any financial implication under the power to relax/
remove difficulties, as:
a) Initially, due to demand projections by hyperscale customers focusing on
expanding AI capacity in India, much ahead of schedule, it applied for the
withdrawal of GNA applications. However, the release of DeepSeek aimed
to provide capabilities similar to those of modern LLM-based AI models,
and the AI sector experienced global disruptions, also leading to demand
recalculations. Further, demand for data centres in Mumbai is encouraging,
which led SPPL to decide to withdraw the relinquishment of GNA, with the
request that Conn BGs submitted earlier may be considered as sufficient
and valid.
Order in Petition No. 451/MP/2025 along with IA 36/2025 Page 16

b) Transmission system required for SPPL’s GNA had never been
constructed; therefore, relinquishment has not resulted in any loss to
CTUIL or burden to DICs.
c) Withdrawal of relinquishment does not constitute a fresh grant of GNA, but
continuation of its existing rights.
24. We have taken note of the aforesaid arguments of parties, the stipulations under
Regulations 25.1 of 2022 GNA Regulations are unequivocal and mandate
encashment of Conn BGs, in case GNA is relinquished prior to effectiveness.
25. We have also considered Petitioner’s proposition that the new generation AI data
centres are highly specialised infrastructure and relatively nascent technology.
Petitioner has withdrawn its request for relinquishment on 04.04.2025, about two
and a half months of relinquishment on 22.01.2025.
26. We note that CTUIL has not encashed the Bank Guarantees since the Petitioner
requested to pay cash in lieu of such BGs, and subsequently the Petitioner was
advised to withdraw its withdrawal request.
27. We note that once relinquishment has been requested by an entity and accepted
by the Nodal Agency, the vacant capacity is considered for allocation to another
entity. In case an entity requests relinquishment, which is accepted by the CTUIL,
but at a later point in time requests such withdrawal, it would lead to an anomalous
situation where such vacated capacity has already been granted to another entity.
Petitioner should have been more cautious prior to requesting the relinquishment
of GNA. Petitioner has requested that its original GNA be restored with the same
date, and in the event the start date is postponed due to the transmission system,
it has no objections to revised dates.
28.In the instant matter, we note that the Nodal Agency-CTUIL has not indicated if
such withdrawal would affect the priority of any other GNA applicant at South
Kalamb S/s or if there is any other GNA applicant at South Kalamb who has
requested the vacated capacity. We are of the considered opinion that if Petitioner
is allowed to withdraw its relinquishment request, this would not take away any
other entity’s rights, and it may not only facilitate the development of nascent
Order in Petition No. 451/MP/2025 along with IA 36/2025 Page 17

demand technologies but also lead to optimal utilisation of the transmission
system. Accordingly, we are of the considered view that the case is fit for
consideration. We note that the provision of Conn-BGs under the GNA
Regulations has been made to ensure that utilisation of the GNA grant
commences as per the stipulated timeline. As per regulation, relinquishment
would have caused encashment of BG amount of Rs 21 crore; however, in this
case Commission allows the withdrawal request of Relinquishment of the
petitioner with notional charge of 10% of BG amount, relaxing Regulatory
provisions in order to encourage this emerging sector of Data Centres.
29. As discussed above, we are of the view that Petitioner should be allowed to
continue with 700 MW GNA granted vide different 14 GNA grants by CTUIL, with
subsisting Conn BGs already furnished in terms of such grants. Accordingly,
CTUIL is directed to reinstate/ restore the GNA of the Petitioner in accordance
with the revised SCOD of the transmission system after the Petitioner deposits a
notional charge of 10% of the BG amount.
30.We also note that the Petitioner was granted and allowed to continue 700 MW
GNA as a bulk consumer under Regulation 17.1(iii) of the 2022 GNA Regulations,
in terms of the paragraph above, the relevant extracts of the 2022 GNA
Regulations are as under:
“17. Eligibility for GNA
17.1. The following entities shall be eligible as Applicants to apply for
grant of GNA or for enhancement of the quantum of GNA:
(i)State Transmission Utility on behalf of intra-State entities including
distribution licensees;
(ii)A drawee entity connected to intra-State transmission system;
(iii)A distribution licensee or a Bulk consumer, seeking to connect
to ISTS, directly, with a load of 50 MW and above;
(iv)Trading licensees engaged in cross border trade of electricity in terms
of the Cross Border Regulations;
(v)Transmission licensee connected to ISTS for drawal of auxiliary
power.”
Further, the Regulations 12.5 of the 2022 GNA Regulations provides as under:
“12. Dedicated Transmission Lines and Bay(s)
Order in Petition No. 451/MP/2025 along with IA 36/2025 Page 18

….
12.5. In case of an entity covered under Regulation 17.1(iii), the line to
connect such an entity to the ISTS and the necessary augmentation for
providing connection to the ISTS, shall be constructed and maintained
by a licensee at the cost of such entity:
As per the above Regulation 12.5 read with Regulation 17.1(iii) of the GNA
Regulations, if a distribution licensee or a bulk consumer is seeking GNA with
direct connectivity to ISTS, the line to connect such an entity to the ISTS and the
necessary augmentation for providing the connection to the ISTS, shall be
constructed and maintained by a licensee at the cost of such entity.
31. To summarise, considering the discussions above, we are of the view that
Petitioner is allowed to continue with its 700 MW GNA with a revised start date,
subject to submission of an amount equivalent to 10% of the total ConnBG amount
and compliance with the GNA Regulations.
31. The Petition 451MP2025, along with IA 36/2025, is disposed of in terms of the
above.

Purchase Agreement (PPA) dated 20.08.2019 (effective date of the PPA is 03.07.2019).
It is pertinent to mention that, as per Clause 4.9 of the PSA, the agreements are
enforceable only when they are granted regulatory approval by the Delhi Electricity
Regulatory Commission (DERC). On 31.12.2020, DERC passed an order in Petition
No. 65/2019, thereby approving the PSA executed between TPDDL and SECI.
However, SECI's trading margin was reduced from Rs. 0.07 per unit to Rs. 0.02 per
unit. The above order was challenged by SECI before the APTEL in Appeal No. 52 of
2021. On 23.02.2021, APTEL passed an interim order, thereby staying the DERC order.
On 02.07.2021, APTEL passed the final judgment in Appeal No. 52 of 2021, wherein
it set aside the decision of DERC to the extent of reduction in trading margin of SECI
from Rs. 0.07 per unit to Rs. 0.02 per unit. Further, BSES Yamuna Power Limited
(BYPL) and SECI executed the PSA on 17.06.2019. On 17.07.2021, DERC conveyed
to BYPL in-principle approval for the procurement of 150 MW Solar power, subject to
compliance with the competitive bidding process. BYPL filed the petition for approval
of PSA (Petition No. 22/2021) before the DERC in February 2021, and the same was
listed for the first time before DERC only in September 2021, i.e., after a span of almost
two years post-signing of the PSA, and since then, the said petition has been adjourned
on a continuous basis. DERC finally approved the tariff on 04.02.2025.
c) As per the PPA, the Scheduled Commissioning Date (SCoD) was 03.01.2021, i.e. 18
months from the effective date of the PPA (viz. 03.07.2019). SECI extended the SCoD
up to 20.11.2021 on account of the disruption caused by the COVID-19 outbreak and
the delay in the operationalisation of LTA, vide its letters dated 11.09.2020, 10.08.2021,
and 22.09.2021. On 30.07.2021, SBSR issued a letter to SECI, thereby invoking the
force majeure clause under Article 11 of the PPA, on the ground that PSAs were to be
approved by the DERC and that, therefore, SCoD shall be extended by at least 14
months from the date of receipt of PSA approval. On 10.08.2021, CTUIL granted an
extension for the operationalisation of LTA, up to 03.09.2021 or until the
commissioning of the transmission network, whichever is later. On 24.08.2021, CTUIL
informed SBSR that LTA will take effect on 03.09.2021. SBSR achieved part
commissioning of 150 MW, viz. 50 MW on 15.08.2021, 50 MW on 04.04.2022 and 50
MW on 11.04.2022. The long-stop date as per the PPA is 20.05.2022.
d) On 26.08.2021, SBSR filed the original petition seeking an extension of SCoD under
the PPA, in terms of the PPA, till 02.07.2022. On 31.08.2022, SECI has informed SBSR
that “In response to your request dated 23.08.2022, this is to inform that, insofar as
Order in Petition No. 192/MP/2021& Petition No. 235/MP/2023 Page 4 of 68

SECI is concerned, SBSR may self-commission the 62.5 MW capacity and decide on the
sale of power in view of the non-extension of time sought for by SBSR notified by SECI
vide its communication dated 30.06.2022 and in the absence of any mutual resolution
as mentioned above. As such, SBSR had self-commissioned the 62.5 MW (part project)
on 20.06.2022.
e) On 11.07.2022, SBSR filed an I.A. 52 of 2022 seeking direction to SECI not to take any
coercive actions against SBSR, including taking steps towards encashment/ invocation
of the Performance Bank and also to direct SECI to accept and issue Commissioning
Certificate for 62.50 MW as intimated to it by SBSR vide email dated 20.06.2022, or
alternatively, direct SECI to issue NOC for 62.5 MW for third-party sale in open
market/Exchange etc. On 17.10.2022, SBSR filed I.A. No. 62 of 2022, seeking to
amend its pending Petition No. 192/MP/2021. On 12.12.2022, after hearing the parties,
the Commission allowed SBSR to amend the petition and I.A. No. 52 of 2022 and I.A.
No. 62 of 2022 were also disposed of.
f) On 0.9.01.2023, TPDDL filed I.A. No. 3 of 2023 to direct SBSR to supply the
commissioned capacity of 62.5 MW forthwith to TPDDL on a pro-rata basis under the
terms and conditions as stipulated under the PPA dated 20.08.2019 and the PSA dated
26.06.2019. The matter was reserved on 02.05.2023, and the Commission passed the
order on 05.06.2023. TPDDL preferred an appeal (I.A. No. 1730 in Appeal No. 625 of
2023) before the APTEL against the Commission’s order dated 05.06.2023 in I.A. No.
3 of 2023 in Petition No. 192/MP/2021. APTEL disposed of the said Appeal vide order
dated 31.07.2023, wherein the APTEL observed that TPDDL could not have sought
relief through an I.A. in a Petition filed by SPCEPL. APTEL permitted TPDDL to
withdraw the I.A. filed by it before this Commission, with liberty to file an independent
petition before the Commission seeking appropriate relief.
Vide amended petition SBSR is now seeking that SBSR is not liable to pay any liquidated
damages or any other penalties corresponding to the PPA capacity of 150 MW, which stands
commissioned, and the balance capacity of 150 MW not commissioned as the delays are not
attributable to SBSR for both capacities, in terms as stated in the present petition.
TPDDL (in Petition No 235/ MP/2023) is seeking adjudication of a dispute against SBSR
Power Cleantech Eleven Private Limited (SBSR) and SECI. TPDDL is the beneficiary of the
entire Contracted Capacity installed/commissioned by SBSR. The SBSR diverted 62.5 MW of
Order in Petition No. 192/MP/2021& Petition No. 235/MP/2023 Page 5 of 68

its installed capacity to third parties, depriving TPDDL of its share of Renewable Power. SBSR
sought an extension from SECI, but SECI denied it. SECI on 31.08.2022, granted No Objection
Certificate (NOC) to SBSR to self-commission 62.5 MW and further granted NOC for the sale
in respect thereof to a third party. SBSR then proceeded to tie up its power sale with the
Electricity Department of Goa through a trader, namely Manikaran Power Limited, under an
umbrella arrangement of the parent company, where 50 MW (out of the commissioned 62.5
MW power Subject Capacity) is being supplied to Goa under a bilateral arrangement through
open access. SBSR, by its actions, seeks to benefit from its own inaction and has altered the
scheme of the PPA/PSA. TPDDL has also filed I.A. 56 of 2023, seeking directions to direct
SBSR to forthwith supply the commissioned capacity of 62.5 MW to TPDDL on a pro-rata
basis and to direct SECI to encash PBG & to pay the Liquidated Damages to TPDDL.
2. The Respondent No. 1, Solar Energy Corporation of India Limited (SECI) (in petition no.
192/MP/2021 & 235/MP/2023), is a designated Nodal Agency for developing and facilitating
the establishment of the grid-connected Solar Power capacity in India.
3. The Respondent No. 3, BSES Yamuna Power Limited (BYPL) (in petition no. 192/MP/2021 &
235/MP/2023) is a joint venture company between Government of NCT of Delhi and Reliance
Infrastructure Limited with the majority of the stake being held by Reliance Infrastructure
Limited and is engaged in the business of distribution of electricity in Eastern and Central parts
of Delhi.
4. SBSR has made the following prayers:
SBSR in petition no. 192/MP/2021:
Original Prayers:
a) Grant extension of Scheduled Commercial Operation Date (SCoD) to the Petitioner in
terms of the Power Purchase Agreement dated 20.08.2019, till 02.07.2022, in light of
the submissions made in the present petition;
b) Direct the Respondent No. 1/ SECI to issue a formal letter to the Petitioner for extension
of SCoD, till 02.07.2022;
c) Consequently, direct the Respondent Nos. 2 and 3 to extend/ defer the
operationalization of the Long-Term Access (LTA) granted to the Petitioner vide the
Order in Petition No. 192/MP/2021& Petition No. 235/MP/2023 Page 6 of 68

LTA Agreement dated 26.11.2019, till the actual SCoD/ COD is achieved by the
Petitioner, or till 02.07.2022, whichever is earlier;
d) Quash the letter dated 24.08.2021 (Annexure P-38) issued by the Respondent No. 2
upon the Petitioner;
e) In the interim, direct as follows:
i. Stay the operation of the letter dated 24.08.2021 issued by the Respondent No.
2, till the pendency of the present petition;
ii. Direct Respondent Nos. 2 and 3 not to operationalize the LTA of the Petitioner
and levy any transmission charges, till the pendency of the present petition;
iii. Direct the Respondents not to take any coercive actions under the PPA, back-
to-back TPDDL-PSA & BYPL-PSA, and the LTA Agreement against the
Petitioner, till the pendency of the present petition; and
f) pass any other order as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit in the facts and
circumstances of the present case and in the interest of justice.
Prayers in the Amended Petition as allowed through ROP dated 12.12.2022:
a) Declare that the Petitioner is not liable to pay any liquidate damages or any other
penalties corresponding to PPA capacity of 150 MW which stands commissioned, and
the balance capacity of 150 MW not commissioned as the delays are not attributable to
the Petitioner for both capacities, in terms as stated in the present petition;
b) Direct SECI to return the Performance Bank Guarantee(s) [as detailed in Annexures P-
46 and P-47] furnished by the Petitioner on its behalf;
c) In the interim, direct the Respondents not to take any coercive actions against the
Petitioner, including taking steps towards encashment/ invocation of the Performance
Bank Guarantee No. 2158IGP001515321 dated 16.06.2021 read with Amendment
dated 16.06.2022 furnished by the Petitioner on behalf of SECI, till the pendency of the
present petition; and
d) pass any other order as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit in the facts and
circumstances of the present case and in the interest of justice.
Prayers by TPDDL in Petition No 235/MP/2023:
a) Hold and declare that the Respondent No. 1 having defaulted to supply 100 MW to the
Petitioner, is obligated to supply 62.5 MW Subject to Petitioner in terms of the binding
obligations of the PSA/PPA;

b) Hold and declare that Respondent No. 1 cannot sell the commissioned 62.5MW power
to third party to the exclusion of the Petitioner; and
c) Direct SECI to proceed with invocation of contractual rights against the Respondent
No.1 for blatant breach of the PPA, PSA provisions without further delay
d) Direct SECI to take steps under Article 13 of the PPA to take over the Project.;

capacity/38.5 MW capacity as the case may be.
f) Pass any such other direction (s)/order (s) as may be deemed fit and in the interest of
justice and equity.
Prayers in I.A. 56 of 2023:
a) Direct the Respondent No. 1 to forthwith supply the commissioned capacity of 62.5 MW
to the Applicant on pro-rata basis as per the terms and conditions of the PPA and PSA.
b) Direct the Respondent No. 2 to encash Performance Bank Guarantee in terms of Article
4.6.1 (a) r/w Article 4.6.2 and 4.6.3 of the PPA, to pay the Liquidated Damages to the
Applicant.
c) Pass any other appropriate Orders/Directions as this Hon’ble Commission may deem

6. The petition no. 192/MP/2021 was filed on 22.09.2021. During the hearing held on 06.10.2021,
the Petition was admitted by the Commission. The Commission further directed the SBSR to
implead TPDDL and BYPL and to file a revised Memo of Parties. The Commission also
observed that the extension of SCoD and the deferment of operationalisation of LTA are two
distinct and independent actions arising from two separate and independent
contracts/agreements. Therefore, these issues must be dealt with separately and independently.
Interlinking these two issues will only complicate and delay the matter. The Commission
suggested that SBSR may consider filing a separate petition on the issue of deferment of the
operationalisation of LTA. The Commission further directed SBSR to submit (i) the status of
PPA with SBSR and whether it has reduced its contracted capacity and encashed any
Performance Bank Guarantee (PBG); (ii) CTU to submit whether it has operationalized the
LTA and, if so, from which date and whether the Petitioner was granted Stage-II connectivity
Order in Petition No. 192/MP/2021& Petition No. 235/MP/2023 Page 11 of 68

under Clause 9.2.1 or Clause 9.2.2 of the RE detailed procedure. SBSR to submit a copy of the
grant of stage-II connectivity, if any and the status of the commissioning of the balance 250
MW capacity of its generating project. During the hearing held on 09.03.2022, the Commission
directed CTUIL and NLDC regarding billing and compliance with Regulation 13(3) of the 2020
Sharing Regulations on affidavit by 29.3.2022. On 12.04.2022, the matter was adjourned on
the request of the contracting parties. During the hearing held on 22.08.2022, CTUIL submitted
that as the issue involved is the extension of SCoD, there is no requirement for CTUIL to be a
party to the present proceedings. Accordingly, it requested the Commission to delete CTUIL as
a party to the Petition. The request was allowed, and the Commission accordingly directed the
Petitioner to file a revised “Memo of Parties” deleting CTUIL from the array of Respondents.
After hearing the parties, the Commission directed the Respondents to file their reply to the
I.A. No. 52/2022. On the request of SBSR to allow commissioning of 62.5 MW, the
Commission observed that there should not be any impediment in allowing SBSR to
commission 62.5 MW capacity to prevent idling of capacity during the pendency of the present
petition.
Submissions of NLDC dated 29.03.2022
7. Briefly, NLDC has submitted as under:
i. In response to para 6(a) of RoP dated 09.03.2022, CTU vide email dated 21.06.2021
had furnished details required to implement the Regulation 13(3) for billing period May,
2021.
ii. The transmission charges of 765kV D/C Ajmer (PG) - Phagi transmission line had not
been included in the details provided by CTU to be recovered under Regulation13(3).
iii. CTU had included the transmission charges of the above transmission line to be
recovered under the National component RE in line with Regulation 5 of the Sharing
Regulations, 2020. Accordingly, Monthly Transmission Charges for the above

consequence of the same, the TPDDL-PSA will also stand automatically terminated to
that extent. The aforesaid provisions are unambiguous and clear, and therefore, since
the PPA is on a higher pedestal (as evident from a reading of the afore-quoted articles),
there is a privity of contract between SBSR and SECI, thereby resulting in no right
being conferred upon TPDDL to enforce its contract (TPDDL-PSA).
Re. Contention of TPDDL that SECI vide its letter dated 31.08.2022 while permitting
SBSR to self-commission its project, has also given due regards to the rights available
to TPDDL, and therefore, the letter dated 30.06.2022 and 31.08.2022 has no bearing
n) TPDDL has contended that under para 11.5 of its reply has alleged that SECI vide its
letter dated 31.08.2022 while permitting SBSR to self-commission its project, has also
given due regard to the rights available to TPDDL, and therefore, the letter dated
30.06.2022 and 31.08.2022 has no bearing. The above argument is bereft of any merit

Petitioner, vide affidavits dated 20.11.2025 and 25.11.2025, has filed the revised
memo of parties and the compliance affidavit in terms of Regulations 5(8) and 5(10)
of the Transmission Licence Regulations, 2024, respectively.
4. Vide RoP dated 13.11.2025, CTUIL was directed to clarify the reasons for not
planning the instant transmission line as a dedicated transmission line for the

iii. In view of the above, Alternative-1 was found to be a techno-economic

generation project.
b. As per the Act, “dedicated transmission lines" means any electric supply-
line for point to point transmission which are required for the purpose of
connecting electric lines or electric plants of a captive generating plant referred
to in Section 9 or generating station referred to in Section 10 to any
transmission lines or sub-stations or generating stations, or the load centre,
as the case may be.
c. In the instant case, the power flow in the LILO of both circuits of Angul -
Sundergarh-A (Jharsuguda) 765 kV 2xS/c lines at Talabira is not completely
dedicated in nature. i.e. apart from the injection from Talabira generation,
power of various other generations and load centers shall also flow on the
LILO portion. Moreover, the LILO is also not envisaged for point-to-point
transmission. In view of the above, the LILO portion was proposed to be
implemented under ISTS as an ATS and connectivity was planned to be
provided at the generation switchyard. Regulation 9.1(a) provides that the
ISTS Connectivity point is the generation switchyard. Nevertheless, the line
bays and switchable line reactors in the said LILO lines at the generation
switchyard have been kept in the scope of the generation project developer.
As the establishment of the LILO is to be carried out for providing the ISTS
connectivity solely to NLCIL, the entire system has been considered as ATS
of the said generation project in terms of the GNA Regulations. Accordingly,
for the ATS applicable Conn-BG2 equivalent to the cost of the identified ATS,
the applicant has already submitted it in accordance with the GNA
Regulations, 2022.
Order in Petition No. 824/TL/2025

d. Regulation 12.1 of the GNA Regulations provides that “In case the
connectivity grantee is a generating station or a captive generating plant or a
standalone ESS, the dedicated transmission lines shall be established,
operated and maintained by such Connectivity grantee.”
e. In the instant case, there is no dedicated transmission line for the subject
project. Therefore, no transmission line is to be established, operated, or
maintained by NLCIL. Considering the techno-economics of the entire power
system requirement, connectivity was planned to be granted at the generation
switchyard through ATS, namely, Eastern Region Generation Scheme-I
(ERGS-I).
f. The ERGS-I scheme was deliberated and agreed in the 16th meeting of
the National Committee on Transmission (NCT) held on 30.11.2023, wherein
it was inter alia recorded that subject connectivity is planned at the generation
switchyard.
g. Considering the site challenges and optimising the entire power system
development cost, etc., connectivity to ISTS is being planned for other entities
also through LILO arrangements of ISTS lines with LILOs to be implemented
under ISTS as an ATS.
7. Vide Record of Proceedings dated 3.12.2025, the Petitioner was again directed
to implead all the beneficiaries of power from the 2400 MW Talabira TPP, including
WBSEDCL, as respondents and to file a revised memo of parties. In compliance with
the RoP dated 3.12.2025, the Petitioner vide affidavit dated 12.12.2025 has filed the
revised memo of parties by impleading all the beneficiaries of power from the 2400
MW Talabira TPP.
Hearing dated 2.1.2026
8. During the course of the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner
submitted that the Petitioner has complied with the directions issued vide RoP dated
3.12.2025 and filed an amended memo of Parties impleading all the beneficiaries of
Order in Petition No. 824/TL/2025
Page 9

2400 MW Talabira TPP and WBSEDCL as parties to the Petitions. He further
submitted that CTUIL has also filed its compliance affidavit dated 9.12.2025 as per the
directions vide RoP dated 13.11.2025. After hearing the parties to the Petition, the
matter was reserved for order.
9. The Petitioner has submitted that in accordance with the “Guidelines for
Encouraging Competition in Development of Transmission Projects” and “Tariff Based
Competitive Bidding Guidelines for Transmission Service” (hereinafter referred to as
“the Guidelines”) issued by the Ministry of Power, Government of India, under Section
63 of the Act, PFC Consulting Limited (hereinafter referred to as “PFCCL”) was notified
by the Ministry of Power, Government of India, vide Gazette Notification. No. CG-DL-
E-23012024-251570 dated 23.1.2024 as the Bid Process Coordinator (hereinafter
referred to as “BPC”) for the purpose of selection of bidder as the Transmission
Service Provider (hereinafter referred to as “TSP”) to establish an Inter-State
transmission system for “Eastern Region Generation Scheme-I (ERGS-I)” on a Build,
Own, Operate and Transfer basis.
10. PFCCL, in its capacity as the BPC, initiated the first bid process on 29.3.2024.
However, the said bid process for the subject transmission scheme was annulled
because the tariff quoted by one of the bidders was higher than the levelised tariff
estimated in accordance with the CERC norms. Accordingly, the re-bidding was
carried out on 21.1.2025 and completed on 28.7.2025 in accordance with the
Guidelines. H.G. Infra Engineering Limited was selected as the successful bidder,
having quoted the lowest transmission charges of Rs. 431.11 million per annum to
provide the transmission services to the beneficiaries of the transmission system.
Order in Petition No. 824/TL/2025
Page 10

three bidders, namely, (i) H G Infra Engineering Limited; (ii) The Tata Power Company

RfP (Technical) bids were opened by the Bid Opening Committee at the Central
Electricity Authority on 23.3.2025 in the presence of a representative of the bidders.
Based on the recommendation of the Bid Evaluation Committee (“BEC”), the RfP
(Financial) Bids-Initial Price Offer of the bidders were opened on 10.6.2025. The
Lowest Initial Price Offer discovered (Best Deal) on the MSTC portal was Rs. 431.11
million per annum. The details of the quoted transmission charges by the bidders are
as under:

14. As per Clause 3.6.1 of RFP, " if no bid is received during the e-reverse bidding
stage, then the Bidder with the lowest quoted initial transmission charges during the
e-bidding stage shall be declared as the Successful Bidder. Since no bidder

15. As per the Bid Evaluation Report dated 12.6.2025, H G Infra Engineering
Limited emerged as the successful bidder with the lowest quoted transmission charges
of Rs. 431.11 million per annum. BEC, vide its certificate dated 12.6.2025, has certified

issued by the Ministry of Power under Section 63 of the Act. BEC has further certified

acceptable.
16. Consequent to its selection as the lowest bidder, a Letter of Intent (hereinafter
referred to as “LoI”) was issued to H G Infra Engineering Limited on 19.6.2025, which
Order in Petition No. 824/TL/2025
Page 12

was accepted by H G Infra Engineering Limited. Under the terms of RfP and the Letter
of Intent, the successful bidder is obligated to accomplish the following tasks:
a) Provide Contract Performance Guarantee in favour of Central Transmission
Utility of India Limited (CTUIL);
b) Execute Share Purchase Agreement and Transmission Service Agreement;
c) Acquire, for the Acquisition Price, 100% equity share of Angul Sundargarh
Transmission Limited from PFCCL along with all its related assets and
liabilities;
d) Make an application to this Commission for the adoption of transmission
charges, as required under Section 63 of the Act; and
e) Apply to this Commission for the grant of a transmission licence.
17. H G Infra Engineering Limited has furnished the Contract Performance
Guarantee (hereinafter referred to as “CPG”) in favour of the Nodal Agency, i.e.,
CTUIL, for Rs. 10.00 crore on 26.6.2025 and has acquired a hundred per cent equity
holding in Angul Sundargarh Transmission Limited on 28.7.2025. The Petitioner
entered into a Transmission Service Agreement (the TSA) with CTUIL on 28.7.2025.
18. Section 14 of the Act provides that the Appropriate Commission may, on an
application made under Section 15 of the Act, grant a licence to any person to transmit
electricity as a transmission licensee in any area as may be specified in the licence.
The word “person” has been defined in Section 2 (49) of the Act to include any
company or body corporate or association or body of individuals, whether incorporated
or not, or artificial juridical person. The Petitioner has been incorporated under the
Companies Act, 2013. The main objective of the Petitioner Company is as under:
Order in Petition No. 824/TL/2025
Page 13

“To develop Power System Network, To plan, promote and develop an
integrated and efficient power transmission system network in all its aspects
including planning, investigation, research, design and engineering, preparation
of preliminary, feasibility and definite project reports, construction, operation
and maintenance of transmission lines, sub-stations, load dispatch stations
and communication facilities and appurtenant works, coordination of integrated
operation of state, regional and national grid system, execution of turn-key jobs
for other utilities/organizations and wheeling of power in accordance with the
policies, guidelines and objectives laid down by the Central Government from
time to time”
19. Section 15 (1) of the Act provides that every application under Section 14 of
the Act shall be made in such manner and in such form as may be specified by the
Appropriate Commission and shall be accompanied by such fees as may be
prescribed by the Central Government. The Commission has specified Transmission
Licence Regulations in this regard. Regulation 4 (1) of the Transmission Licence
Regulations provides that eligibility for the grant of a licence for inter-State
transmission of electricity is contingent upon the entity being selected either through
the competitive bidding process under Section 63 of the Electricity Act, 2003 or by the
Central Government or its authorised agency to implement a project under the
regulated tariff mechanism. Regulation 10 (1) of the Transmission Licence Regulations
provided that, in case the licensee has been selected for implementation of the project
in accordance with the competitive bidding guidelines, the transmission tariff in terms
of the Transmission Service Agreement shall be adopted by the Commission under
Section 63 of the Act. The Project under consideration has been identified for
development under competitive bidding by a competent authority, and the selection of
the Project developer has been certified to have been made in accordance with the
Guidelines for competitive bidding.
20. Regulation 5 of the Transmission Licence Regulations, 2024 provides for the
Order in Petition No. 824/TL/2025
Page 14

procedure for granting of a transmission licence as under:
“(1) The application for the grant of licence shall be made to the Commission
in Form-I appended to these regulations and shall be accompanied by such
fee as may be prescribed by the Central Government from time to time under
sub-section (1) of section 15 of the Act.
(2) The application shall be supported with an affidavit in accordance with
Regulation 17 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of
Business) Regulations, 2023.
(3) The applicant shall submit the original application in electronic form along
with enclosures on the e-filing portal of the Commission and electronically
serve a copy of such application on all the concerned DICs of the project and
the Central Transmission Utility. The application shall be served through e-
mail on the concerned DICs of the project who are not registered on the e-
filing portal of the Commission.
(4) The applicant shall also upload the complete application along with
annexures on its website, in English. The applicant shall also upload on its
website, the details as per Form-I and Form-II appended to these regulations
in the Indian language of the State or the Union Territory where an element of
the project or concerned transmission line is situated or proposed to be
situated. The application shall be kept posted on the website of the applicant
till such time the application is disposed of by the Commission.
(5) The applicant shall, within 3 working days of filing the application, publish
a notice of its application in Form-II appended to these regulations in at least
two leading daily digital newspapers, one in English language and another in
the Indian language of the State or Union Territory where an element of the
project or concerned transmission line is situated or proposed to be situated,
inviting comments from the general public. The notice shall also be kept
posted on the website of the applicant.
(6) The Registry of the Commission shall carry out a preliminary scrutiny of
the application and convey the defects, if any, as far as possible within 7 days
of receipt of the application. The defects shall be rectified by the applicant
within a period of 7 days from the date of such intimation from the Registry of

25. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner, BPC, and CTUIL. The
proviso to Clause 2.15.2 of the RfP provides that “if for any reason attributable to the
BPC, the said activities are not completed by the Selected Bidder within the above
period of ten (10) days as mentioned in this clause, such period of 10 days shall be
extended, on a day-to-day basis till the end of the Bid validity period”. As per the above
Order in Petition No. 824/TL/2025
Page 20

provision, the selected bidder was required to complete all the activities, including the
acquisition of the SPVs by 30.6.2025. Though LoI was issued on 19.6.2025, BPC, vide
its letter dated 28.7.2025 in terms of Clause 2.15.2 of the RfP, extended the date up
to 28.7.2025 for completion of all activities by the successful bidder. The selected
bidder furnished the Contract Performance Guarantee in favour of the Nodal Agency
(CTUIL) for Rs. 10.00 crore on 26.6.2025 and acquired a hundred per cent equity-
holding in the applicant company on 28.7.2025 after execution of the Share Purchase
Agreement. As per clause 2.15.4 of the RfP, TSP is required to apply to the
Commission for the grant of a transmission licence within five working days of the
issuance of the acquisition of the SPV to the successful bidder. The successful bidder,
namely H G Infra Engineering Limited, acquired the SPV on 28.7.2025. Accordingly,
the TSP filed the instant Petition through e-filing for the grant of a transmission licence
on 4.8.2025.
26. Vide ROP dated 13.11.2025 CTUIL was directed to clarify, as to why the
impugned LILO was not planned as a Dedicated Transmission Line (DTL) under the
scope of the generator, NLC Talabira TPP, in terms of Section 10 of the Electricity Act,
2003, read with Regulation 12.1 of the Connectivity and General Network Access
Regulations, 2022.
27. In response CTUIL has submitted that based on the 2000 MW connectivity
application by the NLC India Limited a detailed system study was carried out, and
amongst the proposed alternatives, connectivity through LILO of both circuits of Angul
- Sundergarh-A (Jharsuguda) 765 kV 2xS/c lines at NLC Talabira TPP was considered
to be the most feasible techno economic option. Accordingly, the instant scheme has
been planned as a part of the ISTS.
Order in Petition No. 824/TL/2025
Page 21

28. We note the regulatory provision for the evacuation of power from the
generating stations connecting to the ISTS is defined under the Act and the 2022 GNA
Regulations. The relevant extracts of Sections 2(16) and 10(1) of the Electricity Act,
2003 are as under:
“2 (16) “dedicated transmission lines" means any electric supply-line for point to
point transmission which are required for the purpose of connecting electric lines
or electric plants of a captive generating plant referred to in section 9 or
generating station referred to in section 10 to any transmission lines or sub-
stations or generating stations, or the load center, as the case may be;
…..”
Section10. (Duties of generating companies):
(1) Subject to the provisions of this Act, the duties of a generating company shall
be to establish, operate and maintain generating stations, tie-lines, sub-stations
and dedicated transmission lines connected therewith in accordance with the
provisions of this Act or the rules or regulations made thereunder.”
****
The relevant extracts of Regulation 12.1 of the 2022 GNA Regulations are as
under:
“12. Dedicated Transmission Lines and Bay(s)
12..1 In case Connectivity grantee is a generating station or a captive generating
plant or a standalone ESS, the dedicated transmission lines shall be established,
operated and maintained by such Connectivity grantee”.
The combined reading of the above provisions reveals that the Dedicated
Transmission Line (DTL) is any supply line connecting generating plants to any
transmission line or sub-station. The Dedicated Transmission Line (DTL) emanating
from a generating station is required to be established, operated, and maintained by
such generating station.
29. CTUIL has sought to submit that the impugned LILO at NLC Talabira TPP is
not completely a dedicated in nature as power of various other generators and load
Order in Petition No. 824/TL/2025
Page 22

centres apart from the NLC Talabira TPP should also flow in the LILO portion;
moreover, the LILO is also not envisaged for point-to-point transmission. Since there
is no DTL in the instant case, no transmission line to be established, operated, and
maintained by the generator.
30. We note that the requirement of the LILO has arisen solely to carry power for
the instant generating station and not to carry power of other generating stations. The
definition of “DTL” under clause 16 of Section (2) of the Act states that any electric
supply line, herein impugned LILO, connecting a power plant (herein NLC Talabira
TPP) to any transmission lines (herein Angul- Sundergarh A (Jharsuguda) 765kV D/c
line). Accordingly, DTL is not only a sub-station to sub-station inter-connection, but it
also includes interconnection of a sub-station to a transmission line, as the impugned
LILO is an arrangement connecting a generating switchyard to an ISTS line, securing
a dedicated path for power flow. We note that the since Act and the regulations put
the responsibility of construction and maintenance of such DTL on the generating
station, the same should have been considered accordingly by CTUIL.
31. We note that LILOs in the past have been planned as dedicated lines in a
number of cases by CTUIL; a number of such interim LILOs have been listed in the
Order dated 28.09.2016 in Petition No. 30/MP/2014.
32. As discussed above, we are of the view that the instant transmission line ought
to have been established as the DTL of NLC Talabira TPP. If the said DTL had been
constructed and maintained by the generating station, the transmission charges in
terms of GNA Regulation, 2022 would have been borne by the Generating Station.
Order in Petition No. 824/TL/2025
Page 23

33. It is pertinent to mention that the instant transmission scheme has been
approved by the NCT on the premise that the present transmission scheme is an ISTS
Scheme to be implemented through the TBCB route. In the case of a dedicated
transmission line, such approval would not have been required. However, the
applicant has approached the Commission for the grant of a transmission licence after
being a successful bidder under transparent TBCB guidelines. The transmission
charges for the instant transmission line are discovered through competitive bidding.
The instant transmission system is required for evacuating power from the NLC-
Talabira Generation Station, and timely execution is important to ensure power
evacuation and prevent it from getting stranded. Since the bidding process under
Section 63 of the Act has already been completed, and the TSA has been signed, the
transmission system is required to be constructed for evacuation of power from the
generating station. Considering the material on record, we are constrained to propose
the grant of the transmission licence to the Petitioner company. However, the
transmission charges shall be recovered from the generating station. The parties are
directed to submit their comments on the proposal for the grant of a transmission
licence along with the recovery of transmission charges as proposed above, within two
weeks. Accordingly, we, therefore, direct that a public notice in two daily digital
newspapers and on the Commission`s website under clause (a) of sub-section (5) of
Section 15 of the Act be published to invite suggestions or objections to the grant of a
transmission licence aforesaid. The objections or suggestions, if any, shall be filed by
any person before the Commission by 24.2.2026.

provisions of the TSA, the applicable provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003, and the
Order in Petition No. 824/TL/2025
Page 24

Transmission Licence Regulations, as framed and notified by the Commission.

expense, shall be responsible for designing, constructing, erecting, testing, and
commissioning each element of the Project by scheduled COD in accordance with the
various regulations of the Central Electricity Authority regarding Technical Standards
and Grid Standards, Prudent Utility Practices and other applicable laws. Further,
Article 5.4 of the TSA provides that the TSP shall ensure that the Project is designed,
built and completed in a good workman-like manner using sound engineering and
construction practices and using only materials and equipment that are new and of
international utility-grade quality such that the useful life of the Project will be till the
expiry date. Further, the design, construction, and testing of all equipment, facilities,
components, and systems of the Project shall be in accordance with Indian Standards
and Codes issued by the Bureau of Indian Standards. In this regard, the Petitioner has
submitted that it will implement the Project in accordance with the provisions of the
TSA. It is expected that while carrying out the survey, the Petitioner has complied with
the provisions of clause 2.5.7.3, clause 2.5.7.4, and clause 2.5.7.5 of the RfP. The
Petitioner will comply with the provisions of the bidding documents and the TSA for
the commissioning of the Project within the SCOD.
37. The Petition shall be listed for hearing on 26.2.2026.

instant Petition under Section 27(1) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms

5. CTUIL, in compliance with the Order dated 18.12.2025, vide affidavit dated
12.1.2026, has submitted as under:
(a) The estimated cost of the Inter-State transmission system, which is
implemented under the TBCB route, is carried out by the Cost Committee of

Order in Petition No. 73/TL/2025 Page 6

on a half-yearly/ yearly basis. Accordingly, the estimated cost of the ICTs
along with the associated bays is being regularly updated and would vary for
the different applicants, based on the timelines of application. Therefore, if the
estimated cost is calculated for each applicant based on their application
timelines, different costs would be levied for the various applicants. This may
lead to discrimination among applicants and to future disputes and litigations.
Therefore, it would be prudent to specify a single cost figure (in Lacs/MW)
applicable for all the entities under Regulation 17.1 (iii), like Green Hydrogen/
Green Ammonia, and Data Centre, etc.
(b) The matter was placed before the National Committee on Transmission
(NCT) for deliberations towards a uniform cost to be levied on the entities
under Regulation 17.1 (iii), like Green Hydrogen / Green Ammonia, and Data
Centre, etc. The matter was deliberated in the 36th meeting of NCT held on

(c) The pooling stations presently identified are GIS stations as they are
located near coastal areas in view of the CEA’s report on “Cyclone Resilient
Robust Electricity Transmission & Distribution Infrastructure in the Coastal
Areas”. These pooling stations are of different capacities in the initial phase
like at Navinal: 4500 MW, Kandla: 3000 MW, Kakinada GH: 3000 MW,

capacities may lead to different levies on the costs on the GNA/GNA-RE

4500 MW in the first phase and subsequent ICT augmentations are carried

out based on the receipt of the applications. In some cases where applications

765/400 kV ISTS GIS S/s with necessary augmentation including N-1

(g) The Commission`s order dated 18.12.2025 does not give any general

other ISTS schemes of a similar nature [i.e. those identified for the entities
